description: BRIEF SUMMARY: THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS 5-YEAR FDA AWARD IS TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT STRATEGIES TO ASSESS, EVALUATE, AND MONITOR MEDICAL COUNTERMEASURE SAFETY, PERFORMANCE, AND PATIENT COMPLIANCE IN RESPONSE TO A PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY. CLINICAL SITES FOR THE UNITED STATES CRITICAL ILLNESS AND INJURY TRIALS GROUP PROGRAM FOR EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS (USCIITG-PREP) HAVE BEEN RECRUITED TO PERFORM THIS WORK. THE WORK IS DIVIDED INTO A BASE PERIOD AND 4 ONE-YEAR OPTION PERIODS. Â€¢ UTILIZE PRE-ESTABLISHED INFRASTRUCTURE FOR BROAD COVERAGE OF CLINICAL TRIAL SITES ACROSS THE UNITED STATES Â€¢ UTILIZE RAPID DATA COLLECTION TOOL/MECHANISM FOR COLLECTION OF SAFETY (ADVERSE EVENTS) AND EFFECTIVENESS (PERFORMANCE) DATA Â€¢ COLLABORATE WITH BARDA AND BARDA-FUNDED COMPANY SPONSORS OF MEDICAL COUNTERMEASURES ON PATHWAY FOR FDA APPROVAL/LICENSURE UNDER THE ANIMAL RULE TO MEET POST-MARKETING REGULATORY COMMITMENTS THE BULK OF THIS WORK WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED IN YEAR 1 OF THE BASE PERIOD; MINOR ITERATIONS OF THE WORK ARE REQUIRED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER. COLLABORATORS IN THE USCIITG-PREP NETWORK ARE TASKED WITH COORDINATING REPORTS AND COMPLETING THE WORK REQUIRED AT THEIR RESPECTIVE SITES. DELIVERABLES SPECIFIC FOR THE BASE PERIOD INCLUDE: 1. MONTHLY - PROGRESS REPORTS TO INCLUDE FINANCIAL INFORMATION AND RESEARCH UPDATES, DUE THE 15TH OF EACH MONTH WITH THE FIRST REPORT DUE ON NOVEMBER 15, 2014 2. YEARLY - PROGRESS REPORT FOR THE PAST YEAR'S WORK TO INCLUDE BOTH RESEARCH FINDINGS, FINANCIAL UPDATE, AND PUBLICATIONS AND SPEAKING ENGAGEMENTS, DUE NOVEMBER 15TH OF EACH YEAR 3. YEARLY - OPERATIONS PLAN FOR THE BARDA-SPONSORED PHASE 4 FIELD STUDIES, DUE SEPTEMBER 30TH OF EACH YEAR IF APPLICABLE 4. JANUARY 31, 2015 - FINAL TREATMENT PROTOCOL FOR TREATING CRITICALLY ILL INFLUENZA PATIENTS WITH IV ZANAMIVIR 5. JULY 30, 2015 - A COPY OF THE ECRF TO BE USED DURING THE 2015-2016 INFLUENZA SEASON

description: "OBJECTIVE 1: DEVELOPMENT AND LAUNCH OF EFFECTIVE BREAST CANCER GENETIC EPIDEMIOLOGY CHALLENGE. IN THE PROPOSED WORK, SAGE BIONETWORKS WORK WITH NCI AND NCI PRIZE ADVISORY COMMITTEE TO DEVELOP AN EFFECTIVE CHALLENGE. THIS WORK WILL INCLUDE PREPARATION OF CHALLENGE DESCRIPTION, RULES, AND EVALUATION CRITERIA. IN ADDITION, SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL PREPARE THE CHALLENGE HUB USING THE SYNAPSE INFRASTRUCTURE FOR THE CHALLENGE, INCLUDING POSTING ALL RULES, DESCRIPTIVE INFORMATION, FAQS, AND INSTRUCTIONS FOR CHALLENGE PARTICIPATION. SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL ALSO PROVIDE DATA SCIENTIST SUPPORT TO WORK WITH THE CHALLENGE LEADER AND OTHER DATA SCIENTISTS AS PART OF THE CHALLENGE ORGANIZATIONAL TEAM. THE SAGE APPOINTED DATA SCIENTIST WILL HELP GUIDE THE TEAM IN CHALLENGE Â€˜BEST PRACTICESÂ€™, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO PRE-CHALLENGE DRY-RUN AND SUPPORT FOR THE SYNAPSE PLATFORM. SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL WORK WITH NCI TO ANNOUNCE LAUNCHING OF THE CHALLENGE. OBJECTIVE 2: MANAGEMENT AND PROMOTION OF BREAST CANCER GENETIC EPIDEMIOLOGY CHALLENGE. IN THE PROPOSED WORK, SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL PERFORM DISSEMINATION ACTIVITIES FOR THE CHALLENGE AND POST CHALLENGE ON THE SAGE/SYNAPSE PLATFORM. THEY WILL DEVELOP A CHALLENGE HUB TO FACILITATE PARTICIPATION IN THE CHALLENGE. THIS HUB WILL INCLUDE REGISTRATION AND TRACKING OF CHALLENGE PARTICIPANTS, PROVIDING SUPPORT FOR DATA ACCESS REQUESTS, SUPPORT FOR PARTICIPANTS REQARDING INQUIRES, TRANSLATION SERVICES, COMMUNITY FORUM AND MANAGEMENT OF SUBMISSIONS OF CHALLENGE SOLUTIONS. OBJECTIVE 3: EVALUATION, AWARD AND DISSEMINATION OF BREAST CANCER GENETIC EPIDEMIOLOGY CHALLENGE SOLUTIONS. IN THE PROPOSED WORK, SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL MANAGE EVALUATIONS OF CHALLENGE SUBMISSIONS, ANNOUNCE WINNER OF THE PRIZE, PROVIDE THE CHALLENGE AWARD AND PARTICIPATE IN DISSEMINATION OF THE CHALLENG SOLUTION AND NARRATIVE DESCRIPTION OF THE CHALLENGE PROCESS. FINALLY, SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL PROVIDE POST-CHALLENGE INFRASTRUCTURE SUPPORT BY STORING SUMMARY OF SUBMISSIONS AND SOURCE CODE, AS APPROPRIATE, FOR THE CHALLENGE. "

description: ACCORD FOLLOW-ON STUDY IS A PROSPECTIVE, OBSERVATIONAL FOLLOW-UP STUDY OF APPROXIMATELY 8,000 PARTICIPANTS WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED IN THE ACTION TO CONTROL CARDIOVASCULAR RISK IN DIABETES (ACCORD) TRIAL. IT IS DESIGNED TO FURTHER ELUCIDATE AND CLARIFY THE LONG-TERM EFFECT OF THE ACCORTD TREATMENT STRATEGIES AND PROVIDE ADDITIONAL DATA ON THE LONG-TERM RELATIONSHIPS AMONG VARIOUS CARDIOVASCULAR AND DIABETIC RISK FACTORS. ACCORD WAS A RANDOMIZED CARDIOVASCULAR CLINICAL TRIAL IN PEOPLE WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED FOR AN AVERAGE OF APPROXIMATELY 5 YEARS FROM 2001 THROUGH MID-2009. ACCORD PARTICIPANTS WHO AGREE TO PARTICIPATE IN THE FOLLOW-ON STUDY WILL CONTINUE TO BE FOLLOWED THROUGH CLINIC AND PHONE VISITS FOR AN AVERAGE OF 3.5 YEARS IN THE PERIOD 2011 THROUGH 2014. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE SEEN IN 76 CLINICS ACROSS THE UNITED STATES AND CANADA. THE PRIMARY OUTCOME WILL BE THE FIRST OCCURRENCE OF A MAJOR CARDIOVASCULAR EVENT. SECONDARY OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE ALL CAUSE MORTALITY, OTHER MACRO VASCULAR SECONDARY OUTCOMES, AND DISEASE-FREE SURVIVAL TIME. LAB AND ECG MEASUREMENTS WILL ALSO BE TAKEN PERIODICALLY DURING THE STUDY.

description: THE SICKLE CELL DISEASE TREATMENT DEMONSTRATION PROGRAM (SCDTDP) PROVIDES GRANTS TO REGIONAL NETWORKS THAT WILL WORK WITH PRIMARY CARE PRACTICES THAT TREAT SICKLE CELL DISEASE, COMPREHENSIVE SICKLE CELL DISEASE CENTERS, AND COMMUNITY-BASED SUPPORT ORGANIZATIONS TO PROVIDE COORDINATED, COMPREHENSIVE, CULTURALLY COMPETENT, AND FAMILY-CENTERED CARE TO FAMILIES WITH SICKLE CELL DISEASE. TO ADDRESS THESE BARRIERS TO ACCESS TO SICKLE CELL DISEASE CARE, THE MATERNAL AND CHILD HEALTH BUREAU (MCHB) IS ADJUSTING THE SCDTDP TO A REGIONAL MODEL. THE REGIONAL APPROACH HAS BEEN USED BY MCHB WITH OTHER PROGRAMS AND WILL INCREASE THE REACH OF THE PROGRAM TO PROVIDE ACCESS TO A GREATER NUMBER OF PATIENTS. THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROCUREMENT FOR THE SCDTDP COORDINATING CENTER IS TO OBTAIN SERVICES TO GATHER DATA FROM AND EVALUATE THE PERFORMANCE OF THE SCDTDP GRANTEES IN ADDRESSING THE THREE GOALS OF THE PROGRAM, INCLUDING: 1) INCREASING THE NUMBER OF PROVIDERS TREATING PERSONS FOR SICKLE CELL DISEASE FOR SICKLE CELL RELATED ISSUES; 2) INCREASING THE NUMBER OF PROVIDERS PRESCRIBING DISEASE MODIFYING THERAPIES SUCH AS HYDROXYUREA; AND 3) INCREASING THE NUMBER OF SICKLE CELL PATIENTS THAT ARE RECEIVING REGULAR CARE WITH PROVIDERS KNOWLEDGEABLE ABOUT TREATING SICKLE CELL DISEASE. THE CONTRACTOR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SUPPORTING DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING RESULTS OF THE SCDTDP AS FOLLOWS DURING THE COURSE OF THE BASE YEAR AND OPTION YEARS 1 AND 2: Â€¢ CREATE A DATABASE WITH DATA ELEMENTS AND A DATA DICTIONARY THAT ALLOWS HRSA TO COLLECT AND EVALUATE DATA FROM MULTIPLE REGIONS ON MEETING THE GOALS OF THE PROGRAM Â€¢ CONTRIBUTE TO AND IMPLEMENT FROM AND INFORMATICS PERSPECTIVE REPORTING STRATEGIES THAT ALLOW HRSA TO REPORT RESULTS OF THE PROGRAM TO THE GENERAL PUBLIC Â€¢ CONTRIBUTE TO A REPORT TO CONGRESS ON THE SCDTDP

description: THE OBJECTIVES OF THIS CONTRACT ARE TO CONDUCT PHASE 2 AND EARLY CLINICAL TRIALS OF NCI-SPONSORED AGENTS, TO EVALUATE BIOLOGIC EFFECTS OF THESE AGENTS ON THEIR MOLECULAR TARGETS, TO EVALUATE OTHER RELEVANT BIOLOGIC EFFECTS AND TO DETERMINE CLINICALLY RELEVANT OUTCOMES/CORRELATES. MAJOR EMPHASIS SHALL BE ON PHASE 2 STUDIES, PILOT PROTOCOLS THAT EXPLORE PROMISING COMBINATION THERAPIES, AND HIGH PRIORITY STUDIES THAT ARE PIVOTAL FOR DRUG DEVELOPMENT AND REQUIRE RAPID INITIATION, COMPLETION, AND DATA REPORTING. THE NCI-IND AGENTS TO BE STUDIED SHALL INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING: A) AGENTS DEVELOPED BY THE PHARMACEUTICAL INDUSTRY AND PROVIDED TO THE NCI FOR COLLABORATIVE DEVELOPMENT; AND AGENTS DEVELOPED BY ACADEMIC INVESTIGATORS AND/OR THE DEVELOPMENTAL THERAPEUTICS PROGRAM (DTP), DCTD, NCI; B) AGENTS WHICH HAVE COMPLETED SOME OR ALL PHASE I TESTING, AND: C) COMBINATIONS OF AGENTS FOR WHICH THE INDIVIDUAL TOXICITIES ARE KNOWN.

description: THE AMERICAN INSTITUTES FOR RESEARCH (AIR) HAS IN PLACE THE NECESSARY ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE AND EXPERIENCE TO COMPLETE THE WORK ASSIGNED UNDER THIS AGREEMENT. WE HAVE BUDGETED THE TASKS AS DESCRIBED BELOW TO ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF THE BAYLOR COLLEGE OF MEDICINE EISENBERG CENTER (E.G., ENSURING GEOGRAPHIC DIVERSITY, AND HIGH-QUALITY RECRUITS). WE CAN ADJUST PRODUCT TESTING OR FORMATIVE RESEARCH ACTIVITIES THROUGHOUT THE CONTRACT TO ADDRESS CHANGING NEEDS OF THE EC-BCM. MANAGEMENT. AIR AND BCM WILL WORK COLLABORATIVELY TO DISSEMINATE FINDINGS FROM THE EISENBERG CENTER TESTING AND FORMATIVE RESEARCH ACTIVITIES. WE HAVE BUDGETED HOURS FOR MANAGEMENT OF THE CONTRACT, WHICH INCLUDES TIME FOR MONTHLY MONITORING OF THE PROJECTÂ€™S BUDGET, COORDINATING STAFFING ACROSS PROJECT ACTIVITIES, WEEKLY MEETINGS WITH THE EISENBERG CENTER, AND INTERNAL PROJECT MEETINGS ACROSS TRANSLATION TOPICS. WHILE LEVEL OF EFFORT REMAINS ROUGHLY EQUAL ACROSS ALL YEARS FOR THIS TASK, WE ESTIMATE AN INCREASE OF ABOUT $2,800 PER YEAR FOR AIRÂ€™S ANNUAL COST OF LIVING SALARY INCREASES. AIR WILL CONDUCT CLINICIAN TESTING FOR SIX TRANSLATION PRODUCTS AND CONSUMER TESTING FOR SIX TRANSLATION PRODUCTS EACH YEAR. CLINICIAN TESTING INCLUDES SEVEN CLINICIAN ONE-HOUR COGNITIVE INTERVIEWS WITH FIVE GENERAL PRACTITIONERS AND TWO SPECIALISTS. CONSUMER TESTING INCLUDES NINE 90-MINUTE IN-PERSON INTERVIEWS WITH CONSUMERS AT PROFESSIONAL FACILITIES OR AN AIR OFFICE LOCATION (I.E., WASHINGTON, DC, CHAPEL HILL, NC, OR SAN MATEO, CA) BELOW, WE DESCRIBE OUR OVERALL PROCESS AND ASSUMPTIONS FOR THE PRODUCT TESTING AND FORMATIVE RESEARCH ACTIVITIES. THESE ASSUMPTIONS APPLY ACROSS ALL YEARS OF THE PROJECT. RECRUITMENT. CLINICIANS AND CONSUMERS WILL BE RECRUITED THROUGH PROFESSIONAL RECRUITMENT FIRMS, DEPENDENT ON PRODUCT TESTING LOCATION. FOR RESEARCH WITH CONSUMERS, AIR WILL OVER-RECRUIT TO OBTAIN THE DESIRED NUMBER OF RESPONDENTS (RECRUIT 12 TO GET 9). BASED ON OUR RECENT EXPERIENCES ON THE PREVIOUS CONTRACT, WE HAVE BUDGETED RECRUITMENT COSTS OF $160 FOR CONSUMERS AND $150 FOR CLINICIANS. DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS. ALL INTERVIEWERS WILL WORK COLLABORATIVELY UNDER THE GUIDANCE OF DR. FIRMINGER TO CONDUCT THE INTERVIEWS, ANALYZE THE RESULTS, PREPARE THE TOPLINE REPORTS, AND PRESENT THE RESULTS TO THE EC-BCM. FOR THE CONSUMER RESEARCH, INTERVIEWERS AND NOTETAKERS WILL BE DETERMINED BY LOCATION AND AVAILABILITY. INCENTIVES. BASED ON OUR RECENT EXPERIENCES ON THE PREVIOUS CONTRACT, WE HAVE BUDGETED INCENTIVES OF $100 FOR CONSUMERS. FOR CLINICIANS, WE HAVE BUDGETED $150 INCENTIVES FOR GENERAL PRACTITIONERS AND $250 INCENTIVES FOR SPECIALISTS. WE WILL WORK WITH THE EC-BCM IF PRODUCT TRANSLATION TOPICS REQUIRE SPECIALIZED POPULATIONS THAT REQUIRE HIGHER INCENTIVES. TASK 8: CONSUMER AND PATIENT ACTIVATION AND ENGAGEMENT IN EHC ACTIVITIES AIR WILL LEAD THE EFFORTS TO ENGAGE CONSUMER AND PATIENT ORGANIZATIONS THROUGHOUT THE FIVE YEARS. IN YEARS 1 THROUGH 5, THE EC-BCM WILL MEET WITH AHRQ TO DISCUSS EXPECTATIONS AND POTENTIAL ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES; DEVELOP AN ENGAGEMENT PLAN FOR THE YEAR; MEET AND WORK WITH 15 PATIENT AND CONSUMER ORGANIZATIONS; PLAN AND FACILITATE 4 TO 5 TELECONFERENCES WITH PATIENT AND CONSUMER ORGANIZATIONS AND AHRQ STAFF; AND DISSEMINATE INFORMATION TO PATIENTS AND CONSUMERS TO HIGHLIGHT AHRQ ACTIVITIES AND ENGAGEMENT OPPORTUNITIES. IN YEAR 1, THE EC-BCM WILL RECRUIT 15 CONSUMER AND PATIENT ORGANIZATIONS; DEVELOP PROCESSES FOR MATCHING PATIENT AND CONSUMER REPRESENTATIVES WITH AHRQ AND EHC PROGRAM RESEARCH PROJECTS; ESTABLISH STANDARDIZED APPROACHES AND GUIDANCE ON HOW TO SUCCESSFULLY INVOLVE PATIENT AND CONSUMER PARTICIPANTS; DEVELOP A PASSWORD PROTECTED ONLINE RESOURCE CENTER FOR PATIENTS AND CONSUMERS ENGAGED IN SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES; CREATE AND HOST THREE MULTIMEDIA PRESENTATIONS AND ENSURE THEY ARE 508 COMPLIANT TO POST ON THE EHC WEB SITE; AND DEVELOP FEEDBACK FORMS TO COLLECT FEEDBACK ABOUT THE ENGAGEMENT PROCESS AND OUTCOMES.

description: JOHNS HOPKINS SCOPE OF WORK A. INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES EMERGING INSIGHT INTO TUMOR GENOMES MAKES IT CLEAR THAT CHROMOSOMAL TRANSLOCATIONS OCCUR RELATIVELY COMMONLY AND IN A NON-RANDOM FASHION (1-3). FUSION PROTEINS THAT FORM AS A RESULT OF THESE TRANSLOCATIONS TYPICALLY HAVE ALTERED FUNCTIONS RELATIVE TO THE INDIVIDUAL SOURCE PROTEINS AND, IN SOME CASES, APPEAR TO DRIVE THE MALIGNANT PHENOTYPE. SINCE THE FUSION PROTEINS ARISE DURING TUMOR DEVELOPMENT, AND ARE NOT EXPRESSED IN NORMAL TISSUES, THEY REPRESENT TUMOR-SPECIFIC ANTIGENS AND PROVIDE POTENTIAL TARGETS FOR TUMOR VACCINES. THERAPEUTIC BREAKPOINT PEPTIDE VACCINES WITH EVIDENCE OF CLINICAL ACTIVITY WERE FIRST DEVELOPED AGAINST THE BCRABL FUSIONS OBSERVED IN CML (4-6). WHILE THE SIZE OF THE TRIALS CONDUCTED HAVE BEEN MODEST AND THE EXACT CONTENT OF THE VACCINES VARIABLE, THE BODY OF THE DATA SUPPORTS THE POTENTIAL FOR CLINICAL ACTIVITY OF THE PRODUCTS. MORE MODEST PROGRESS HAS BEEN MADE USING THERAPEUTIC BREAKPOINT VACCINES AGAINST CHARACTERISTIC FUSIONS OBSERVED IN SARCOMAS (7-9). GIVEN THAT VACCINATION AGAINST HPV, THE VIRUS THAT INDUCES CERVICAL CANCER, IS CAPABLE OF PROTECTING WOMEN FROM THE DEVELOPMENT OF CERVICAL CANCER WHEN GIVEN PRIOR TO VIRUS EXPOSURE, YET INEFFECTIVE IN THE TREATMENT SETTING AFTER THE CANCER HAS ALREADY DEVELOPED (10), BREAKPOINT VACCINES MAY ALSO BE MORE EFFECTIVE AS A PREVENTATIVE THERAPY. HOWEVER, SO FAR, NO BREAKPOINT-SPECIFIC VACCINES HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED FOR CANCER PREVENTION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT A MULTIVALENT VACCINE DIRECTED AGAINST FUSION PROTEINS OBSERVED IN SOLID TUMORS COULD GENERATE AN IMMUNE RESPONSE CAPABLE OF PREVENTING SOLID TUMORS IN HIGH-RISK GROUPS OF PATIENTS. IN ADULT SOLID TUMORS, FUSIONS INVOLVING SOME OF THE SAME AND SOME DIFFERENT SOURCE GENES AS THOSE IDENTIFIED IN SARCOMAS HAVE BEEN OBSERVED. SINCE THE SAME SET OF TRANSLOCATIONS AND CORRESPONDING FUSION PROTEINS ARE NOT OBSERVED IN ALL TUMORS OF A GIVEN HISTOLOGIC TYPE, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT A STRATEGY THAT TARGETS MULTIPLE, FREQUENTLY OBSERVED FUSIONS HAS THE BEST CHANCE OF GENERATING EFFECTIVE ANTITUMOR IMMUNITY AND PROTECTION. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS STUDY IS TO DEFINE ONE OR MORE PRECLINICAL MODELS TO DEVELOP THIS APPROACH AND EVALUATE ITS POTENTIAL FOR THE PREVENTION OF SOLID TUMORS. OBJECTIVES 1. TO IDENTIFY T CELL TARGETABLE GENE FUSION ANTIGENS EXPRESSED BY THE MURINE LEWIS LUNG CANCER AND MC38 COLON CANCER CELL LINES. 2. TO EVALUATE THE IMMUNOGENICITY OF AN EML4-ALK GENE FUSION THAT DRIVES TUMOR DEVELOPMENT IN A TRANSGENIC LUNG CANCER MODEL. 3. TO DEVELOP PEPTIDE AND LISTERIA-BASED IMMUNIZATION STRATEGIES FOR INDUCING ROBUST GENE FUSION-SPECIFIC EFFECTOR T CELL RESPONSES. 4. TO EVALUATE THE PRECLINICAL EFFICACY OF GENE FUSION-SPECIFIC IMMUNIZATION STRATEGIES FOR PREVENTING TUMOR DEVELOPMENT.

description: OPTION 15A (09/15/14-02/29/16): 0258-0516-4609 THE ROLES OF SPECIFIC SIALIC ACID VARIANTS IN INFLUENZA-HOST CELL INTERACTIONS. WE ARE FOCUSING ON BETTER UNDERSTANDING THE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN INFLUENZA VIRUSES AND DIFFERENT HOSTS BY DEFINING THE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN INFLUENZA HA AND NA AND SPECIFICALLY MODIFIED SIALIC ACIDS (WITH ADDITIONAL ACETYLATIONS, HYDROXYLATIONS, AND/OR LINKAGES) DISPLAYED ON THE VARIOUS TARGET CELLS AND TISSUES FROM DIFFERENT HOSTS. THESE LIKELY MODIFY THE SPECIFIC PROCESSES OF VIRUS CELL BINDING, INFECTION AND SHEDDING AND WILL THEREFORE ADD TO OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE VIRUS-HOST INTERACTION, AND PROVIDE INSIGHTS INTO POTENTIAL NEW INTERVENTION STRATEGIES. IN THE FIRST PART OF THE PROJECT WE WILL DEVELOP TOOLS FOR DETECTING THE PRESENCE OF MODIFIED FORMS OF SA ON CELLS AND TISSUES. WE WILL PREPARE PROBES FOR QUANTITATIVELY ASSAYING FOR THE PRESENCE OF NEU5AC AND NEU5GC ON CELLS AND TISSUES USING PARVOVIRUS CAPSIDS, ANTIBODIES RECOGNIZING NEU5GC, AND BACTERIAL TOXIN SUBUNITS. PROBES FOR 4-O-ACETYLATED SAS WILL BE DERIVED FROM THE MOUSE HEPATITIS VIRUS (MHV) HEMAGGLUTININ-ESTERASE (HE), AND THE MHV-S HE ESTERASE WOULD BE USED TO REMOVE THE 4-O-ACETYL GROUP FROM THE SA ON CELLS OR TISSUES. PROBES FOR 9-O-ACETYLATED SA WILL BE DERIVED FROM THE BOVINE CORONAVIRUS HE PROTEIN OR INFLUENZA C HE PROTEIN, AND ESTERASE ACTIVE FORMS WOULD BE USED AS MODIFYING ENZYMES. OTHER PROBES THAT WE WILL DEVELOP FOR THIS TESTING INCLUDE SPECIFIC INFLUENZA HA DOMAINS LINKED TO THE FC PORTION OF HUMAN IGG1. IN THE SECOND PART OF THE PROJECT WE WILL DEFINE THE SPECIFIC SA FORMS AND LINKAGES EXPRESSED ON THE RESPIRATORY EPITHELIAL AND OTHER CELLS OF NATURAL HOSTS OF INFLUENZA, SO AS TO UNDERSTAND THE CORRELATIONS BETWEEN HA BINDING AND NA CLEAVAGE AND NATURAL VIRUS SUSCEPTIBILITY. WE WILL ALSO EXAMINE THE EXPRESSION OF THE MODIFIED SIALIC ACIDS ON CELLS IN TISSUE CULTURE, AND THEN WILL TEST FOR THE EFFECTS OF SA MODIFICATIONS ON VIRUS BINDING, INFECTION, AND RELEASE, OR INTERACTIONS WITH HOST PROTEINS. OPTION 22D (09/10/16-12/09/17): 0258-0578-4609 DR. COLIN R. PARRISH (CORNELL UNIVERSITY) WILL COORDINATE STUDIES TO DEFINE THE ROLES OF MODIFIED SIALIC ACIDS (SIAS) IN CONTROLLING THE HOST RANGES AND TROPISMS OF INFLUENZA A VIRUSES. INFLUENZA VIRUSES ALL BIND AND CLEAVE SPECIFIC SIAS DURING MANY INTERACTIONS WITH THEIR HOSTS, AND IN THIS PROPOSAL THE PARRISH LABORATORY WILL DEFINE THE EXPRESSION OF MODIFIED SIA RECEPTORS, AND EXPLAIN THEIR ROLES IN THE CONTROL OF INFLUENZA VIRUS INTERACTIONS WITH HOST CELLS AND TISSUES. PRIMARY GOALS OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO PREPARE SPECIFIC PROBES THAT RECOGNIZE THE DIFFERENT MODIFIED FORMS OF SIALIC ACID THAT ARE EXPRESSED ON CELLS, AND THEN TO DEFINE THEIR EFFECTS ON VIRUS INFECTION. THE SPECIFIC PROJECT INVOLVES THE PREPARATION OF A VARIETY OF PROBES BY EXPRESSION OF PROTEINS IN BACULOVIRUS SYSTEMS WHERE THE PROTEIN IS SECRETED AND PURIFIED. THE DIFFERENT PROBES ARE BEING USED TO DETECT THE PRESENCE OF DIFFERENT MODIFIED SIALIC ACIDS ON PROTEINS, CELLS, OR TISSUES OBTAINED FROM DIFFERENT HOSTS, USING A VARIETY OF DETECTION METHODS. WE WOULD ALSO USE VARIOUS ENZYMES TO ALTER THE EXPRESSION OF DIFFERENT SIALIC ACIDS, TO MODIFY THE SIALIC ACIDS ON THE SURFACE OF CELLS, AND WOULD USE CRSP/CAS9 EDITING OF GENES IN CELLS TO ALTER THE SIALIC ACID EXPRESSION. THE MODIFIED SIALIC ACID FORMS WOULD THEN BE TESTED FOR THEIR INTERACTIONS WITH INFLUENZA VIRUSES, OR THEIR EXPRESSED PROTEINS. DR. PARRISH WILL OVERSEE THE LOCAL MANAGEMENT OF THIS RESEARCH PROJECT AT CORNELL, AND WILL ASSIST IN THE PREPARATION OF MONTHLY, SEMI-ANNUAL, AND ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS. HE WILL ALSO OVERSEE THE WRITING OF SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS DESCRIBING THE RESULTS OF THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM. THIS WORK DIRECTLY REFLECTS BOTH THE SPECIFIC AND OVERALL GOALS OF THE CEIRS PROGRAM, AND IS HIGHLY COMPLEMENTARY TO A NUMBER OF PROJECTS WITHIN THE CEIRS NETWORK, PARTICULARLY THOSE EXAMINING THE HOST AND TISSUE TROPISMS OF THE VARIOUS INFLUENZA VIRUSES IN MAMMALS AND IN DIFFERENT AVIAN HOSTS. WE WILL GAIN A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN INFLUENZA VIRUSES AND THEIR HOSTS BY DEFINING THE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN INFLUENZA HA AND NA AND THE SPECIFICALLY MODIFIED RECEPTORS ON HOST CELLS AND TISSUES, WHICH LIKELY CONTROL THE SPECIFIC PROCESSES OF VIRUS INFECTION OF CELLS AND TISSUES OF DIFFERENT HOSTS, INTERACTIONS WITH MUCUS, AND VIRUS SHEDDING. THE RESULTS WILL ALSO PROVIDE NEW INSIGHTS INTO POTENTIAL INTERVENTIONS

description: BRIEF SUMMARY: THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS 5-YEAR FDA AWARD IS TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT STRATEGIES TO ASSESS, EVALUATE, AND MONITOR MEDICAL COUNTERMEASURE SAFETY, PERFORMANCE, AND PATIENT COMPLIANCE IN RESPONSE TO A PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY. CLINICAL SITES FOR THE UNITED STATES CRITICAL ILLNESS AND INJURY TRIALS GROUP PROGRAM FOR EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS (USCIITG-PREP) HAVE BEEN RECRUITED TO PERFORM THIS WORK. THE WORK IS DIVIDED INTO A BASE PERIOD AND 4 ONE-YEAR OPTION PERIODS. BASE PERIOD (YEARS 1-4): THERE ARE FOUR DELIVERABLES IDENTIFIED FOR THE BASE PERIOD: Â€¢ IN YEAR 1, DEVELOP AN INTRAVENOUS ANTIVIRAL TREATMENT PROTOCOL TO ASSESS THE USE OF INTRAVENOUS (IV) ANTIVIRALS (E.G., IV ZANAMIVIR) UNDER AN EXPANDED ACCESS IND FOR CRITICALLY ILL PATIENTS WITH CONFIRMED INFLUENZA USING ELECTRONIC CASE REPORT FORMS (ECRFS) AND A DATA ENTRY USER MANUAL. Â€¢ UTILIZE PRE-ESTABLISHED INFRASTRUCTURE FOR BROAD COVERAGE OF CLINICAL TRIAL SITES ACROSS THE UNITED STATES Â€¢ UTILIZE RAPID DATA COLLECTION TOOL/MECHANISM FOR COLLECTION OF SAFETY (ADVERSE EVENTS) AND EFFECTIVENESS (PERFORMANCE) DATA Â€¢ COLLABORATE WITH BARDA AND BARDA-FUNDED COMPANY SPONSORS OF MEDICAL COUNTERMEASURES ON PATHWAY FOR FDA APPROVAL/LICENSURE UNDER THE ANIMAL RULE TO MEET POST-MARKETING REGULATORY COMMITMENTS THE BULK OF THIS WORK WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED IN YEAR 1 OF THE BASE PERIOD; MINOR ITERATIONS OF THE WORK ARE REQUIRED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER. COLLABORATORS IN THE USCIITG-PREP NETWORK ARE TASKED WITH COORDINATING REPORTS AND COMPLETING THE WORK REQUIRED AT THEIR RESPECTIVE SITES. DELIVERABLES SPECIFIC FOR THE BASE PERIOD INCLUDE: 1. MONTHLY - PROGRESS REPORTS TO INCLUDE FINANCIAL INFORMATION AND RESEARCH UPDATES, DUE THE 15TH OF EACH MONTH WITH THE FIRST REPORT DUE ON NOVEMBER 15, 2014 2. YEARLY - PROGRESS REPORT FOR THE PAST YEAR'S WORK TO INCLUDE BOTH RESEARCH FINDINGS, FINANCIAL UPDATE, AND PUBLICATIONS AND SPEAKING ENGAGEMENTS, DUE NOVEMBER 15TH OF EACH YEAR 3. YEARLY - OPERATIONS PLAN FOR THE BARDA-SPONSORED PHASE 4 FIELD STUDIES, DUE SEPTEMBER 30TH OF EACH YEAR IF APPLICABLE 4. JANUARY 31, 2015 - FINAL TREATMENT PROTOCOL FOR TREATING CRITICALLY ILL INFLUENZA PATIENTS WITH IV ZANAMIVIR 5. JULY 30, 2015 - A COPY OF THE ECRF TO BE USED DURING THE 2015-2016 INFLUENZA SEASON

description: 1.TO RAPIDLY INITIATE AND COMPLETE LABORATORY-BASED PHASE II TRIALS EVALUATING THE SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF NEW NCI-SPONSORED ANTINEOPLASTIC AGENTS MY MAXIMIZING THE PATIENT AND SCIENTIFIC RESOURCES AND CLINICAL RESEARCH EXPERTISE OF AN ESTABLISHED CONSORTIUM WITH DEMONSTRATED EXPERTISE IN EARLY THERAPEUTICS DEVELOPMENT 2. TO EMPLOY A SYSTEMATIC APPROACH TO COLLECTION, PROCESSING, AND STORAGE OF BLOOD, NORMAL AND TUMOR TISSUE, AND OTHER RELEVANT BIOLOGIC SAMPLES FOR MOLECULAR AND CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGIC STUDIES. 3. TO EVALUATE THE BIOLOGIC EFFECTS OF NEW NCI-SPONSORED ANTINEOPLASTIC AGENTS ON THEIR MOLECULAR TARGETS BY INVESTIGATING POTENTIAL LABORATORY, PHARMACOKINETIC AND PHARMACODYNAMIC CORRELATIONS, INCLUDING EVALUATION OF SPECIAL PATIENT POPULATIONS, SUCH AS THOSE WITH IMPAIRED END-ORGAN FUNCTION, THE ELDERLY, AND RACIAL AND/OR ETHNIC GROUPS IN WHOM DIFFERENCES ARE ANTICIPATED. 4. TO IDENTIFY NEW PREDICTIVE MARKERS OF RESPONSE AND/OR SURVIVAL TO NOVEL THERAPEUTICS, INCLUDING CYTOSTATIC AGENTS, TO DEVELOP APPROPRIATE STUDY DESIGNS AND STATISTICAL METHODOLOGIES TO ASSESS SURROGATE MOLECULAR AND BIOLOGIC ENDPOINTS, AND TO CORRELATE FINDINGS WITH CLINICALLY RELEVANT OUTCOMES IN ASSOCIATED CLINICAL TRIALS. 5. TO UTILIZE SPECIAL SCIENTIFIC EXPERTISE WITHIN THE CALIFORNIA CANCER CONSORTIUM IN THE AREAS OF A) DNA METHYLATION, B) DNA REPAIR, C) SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION AND CELL CYCLE REGULATION, D) TUMOR ANGIOGENESIS, AND E) FUNCTIONAL IMAGING TO ASSESS DRUG-TARGET INTERACTIONS, TO ESTABLISH POTENTIAL SURROGATE STUDY ENDPOINTS, AND TO OPTIMIZE DESIGN OF LABORATORY-CLINICAL CORRELATIVE STUDIES.

description: THIS STUDY SHALL PROVIDE A CLINICAL TRIAL COMPARING TWO APPROACHES FOR THE PREVENTION OF CMV I.E., PROPHYLAXIS VERSUS PREEMPTIVE THERAPY IN CMV RECIPIENT NEGATIVE/DONOR POSITIVE (R-/D+) LIVER TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS. THE STUDY ADDRESSES AN IMPORTANT BIOLOGIC CONCEPT, I.E. ALLOWING CONTROLLED ANTIGEN EXPOSURE TO OCCUR AS OPPOSED TO ITS COMPLETE SUPPRESSION MIGHT BETTER FACILITATE PROTECTIVE IMMUNITY NECESSARY FOR LONG-TERM PROTECTION AGAINST CMV. THUS, THE TARGETED APPROACH OF USING PREEMPTIVE THERAPY UPON DETECTION OF VIREMIA MAY INCUR A LOWER RISK OF CMV DISEASE AND LEADS TO GREATER DEVELOPMENT OF CMV-SPECIFIC IMMUNE RESPONSE COMPARED TO PROPHYLAXIS. OVER THE LIFE OF THE CONTRACT, SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL RECRUIT AND RETAIN APPROXIMATELY 67 CMV R-/D+ LIVER TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS TO COMPLETE THE FINAL PROTOCOL. description: ACCORD FOLLOW-ON STUDY IS A PROSPECTIVE, OBSERVATIONAL FOLLOW-UP STUDY OF APPROXIMATELY 8,000 PARTICIPANTS WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED IN THE ACTION TO CONTROL CARDIOVASCULAR RISK IN DIABETES (ACCORD) TRIAL. IT IS DESIGNED TO FURTHER ELUCIDATE AND CLARIFY THE LONG-TERM EFFECT OF THE ACCORTD TREATMENT STRATEGIES AND PROVIDE ADDITIONAL DATA ON THE LONG-TERM RELATIONSHIPS AMONG VARIOUS CARDIOVASCULAR AND DIABETIC RISK FACTORS. ACCORD WAS A RANDOMIZED CARDIOVASCULAR CLINICAL TRIAL IN PEOPLE WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED FOR AN AVERAGE OF APPROXIMATELY 5 YEARS FROM 2001 THROUGH MID-2009. ACCORD PARTICIPANTS WHO AGREE TO PARTICIPATE IN THE FOLLOW-ON STUDY WILL CONTINUE TO BE FOLLOWED THROUGH CLINIC AND PHONE VISITS FOR AN AVERAGE OF 3.5 YEARS IN THE PERIOD 2011 THROUGH 2014. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE SEEN IN 76 CLINICS ACROSS THE UNITED STATES AND CANADA. THE PRIMARY OUTCOME WILL BE THE FIRST OCCURRENCE OF A MAJOR CARDIOVASCULAR EVENT. SECONDARY OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE ALL CAUSE MORTALITY, OTHER MACRO VASCULAR SECONDARY OUTCOMES, AND DISEASE-FREE SURVIVAL TIME. LAB AND ECG MEASUREMENTS WILL ALSO BE TAKEN PERIODICALLY DURING THE STUDY.

description: I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. OF THE SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS TO BE STUDIED, TWO ARE MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). THE PARASITE STUDIES WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS (UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH FLORIDA), KING (CASE WESTERN RESERVE UNIVERSITY) AND TOLIA (WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). IN ADDITION TO THE EPITOPE MAPPING TO BE PERFORMED BY DR. TOLIA, A SECOND MAJOR GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF CORRELATES RELATING B CELL EPITOPES WITH AB NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY AND AG BINDING THAT WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS AND KING. B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT. HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS AND MURINE MABS FROM IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. MALARIA NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED USING ASSAYS INTERROGATING BOTH SPOROZOITE AND MEROZOITE STAGES OF DEVELOPMENT. QUANTITATIVE ASSAYS WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE AB/AG INTERACTION STRENGTH, SPECIFICITY, AND VALENCY TO FURTHER DEVELOP CORRELATES OF PROTECTION. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION WILL BE INTERROGATED FOR OUR MOST POTENT MABS, WHERE THE STAGE OF THE INFECTION PROCESS BLOCKED BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED. ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION. II. SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.) ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT. B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. MAB GENERATION. LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. DR. ADAMS WILL COORDINATE OBTAINING EXISTING MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. description: THIS STUDY SHALL PROVIDE A CLINICAL TRIAL COMPARING TWO APPROACHES FOR THE PREVENTION OF CMV I.E., PROPHYLAXIS VERSUS PREEMPTIVE THERAPY IN CMV RECIPIENT NEGATIVE/DONOR POSITIVE (R-/D+) LIVER TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS. THE STUDY ADDRESSES AN IMPORTANT BIOLOGIC CONCEPT, I.E. ALLOWING CONTROLLED ANTIGEN EXPOSURE TO OCCUR AS OPPOSED TO ITS COMPLETE SUPPRESSION MIGHT BETTER FACILITATE PROTECTIVE IMMUNITY NECESSARY FOR LONG-TERM PROTECTION AGAINST CMV. THUS, THE TARGETED APPROACH OF USING PREEMPTIVE THERAPY UPON DETECTION OF VIREMIA MAY INCUR A LOWER RISK OF CMV DISEASE AND LEADS TO GREATER DEVELOPMENT OF CMV-SPECIFIC IMMUNE RESPONSE COMPARED TO PROPHYLAXIS. OVER THE LIFE OF THIS SUBCONTRACT AGREEMENT, SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL RECRUIT AND RETAIN APPROXIMATELY THIRTY-SIX (36) CMV R-/D+ LIVER TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS TO COMPLETE THE FINAL PROTOCOL.

description: PURPOSE: TO SERVE AS A DESIGNATED OUTREACH LIBRARY FOR THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION OF THE NATIONAL NETWORK OF LIBRARIES OF MEDICINE. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: OUTREACH LIBRARIES AGREE TO PERFORM THE FOLLOWING FUNCTIONS ON BEHALF OF THE NETWORK: 1. DESIGNATE A LIBRARIAN TO SERVE AS OUTREACH LIBRARY LIAISON TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION; 2. PARTICIPATE IN OUTREACH LIBRARY WEBINARS AND OTHER COLLABORATIVE ACTIVITIES PROVIDED FOR OUTREACH LIBRARIANS; 3. ASSIST THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY IN THE IDENTIFICATION OF UNDERSERVED GROUPS OF HEALTH PROFESSIONALS AND CONSUMERS WITHIN THE STATE; 4. PROVIDE UNAFFILIATED HEALTH PROFESSIONALS WITHIN THE STATE WITH REFERENCE SERVICES AND ACCESS TO COLLECTIONS, INCLUDING ACCESS TO ELECTRONIC RESOURCES TO THE EXTENT PERMITTED BY LICENSE AGREEMENTS; 5. PROVIDE DOCUMENT DELIVERY SERVICE TO UNAFFILIATED HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, CONSUMERS AND NN/LM AFFILIATE MEMBERS IN THE STATE; 6. PROVIDE TRAINING IN NLM RESOURCES AND DATABASES TO HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, LIBRARIANS AND CONSUMERS IN THE STATE. THIS MAY BE DONE AT THE LIBRARY'S OWN INITIATIVE OR IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY; 7. SUPPORT THE NLM AND NN/LM EXHIBIT PROGRAMS BY ASSISTING IN AND/OR SUPPORTING STAFFING AT STATE EXHIBITS COORDINATED BY THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY, BY INFORMING THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY ABOUT POSSIBLE EXHIBIT OPPORTUNITIES IN THE STATE, AND BY EXHIBITING AT LOCAL COMMUNITY EVENTS; 8. ENTER NLM AND NN/LM RELATED OUTREACH ACTIVITIES INTO THE APPROPRIATE DATABASE WITHIN 30 DAYS OF THE ACTIVITY 9. SUBMIT TALLY SHEETS TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION WITHIN 30 DAYS AFTER AN EXHIBIT EVENT 10. SUBMIT AN ANNUAL REPORT TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION, SUMMARIZING OUTREACH ACTIVITIES UNDERTAKEN BY THE OUTREACH LIBRARY DURING THE CONTRACT PREVIOUS YEAR *NOTE: IN THE FALL, NLM PLANS TO COMBINE THESE THREE REPORTING OPTIONS INTO THE "NLM OUTREACH APPLICATION AND ONLINE CONTACT REPORTING SYSTEM" WHICH WILL REPLACE THE OARF DATABASE. ALL OUTREACH ACTIVITIES, EXHIBITING EVENTS AND ANNUAL REPORTS WILL BE ENTERED INTO THAT SYSTEM WHEN IT BECOMES AVAILABLE. MEASUREMENT OF PROGREY: PROGRESS WILL BE MEASURED BY MONITORING INPUT FROM THE DESIGNATED OUTREACH LIBRARIAN DURING QUARTERLY WEBINARS AND OTHER MEETINGS, LEVEL OF ACTIVITY REPORTED IN THE NLM OUTREACH ACTIVITY DATABASE, AND CONTENT OF THE ANNUAL REPORT.

description: I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS OF HUMAN WILL BE STUDIED: TWO FLAVIVIRUSES (DENGUE VIRUS SEROTYPE 4 AND JAPANESE ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS), TWO BUNYAVIRUSES (RIFT VALLEY FEVER AND OROPOUCHE VIRUSES) AND TWO MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). WE HAVE DEVELOPED A STRONG PLAN FOR THE GENERATION OF HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS OR IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS. B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT. LARGE PANELS OF NEUTRALIZING MABS AGAINST TARGET VIRUSES WILL BE GENERATED BY DR. JAMES CROWE. HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS OR VACCINE TRIALS WILL BE DEVELOPED AGAINST RIFT VALLEY FEVER VIRUS (RVFV), DENGUE VIRUS SEROTYPE 4 (DENV-4), JAPANESE ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS (JEV) AND OROPOUCHE VIRUS. ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION. II. SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.) ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT. B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. A CRITICAL ELEMENT OF OUR PROPOSAL IS THE GENERATION OF LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST OUR TARGET PATHOGENS. HUMAN MABS AGAINST FLAVIVIRUS AND BUNYAVIRUS TARGETS WILL BE DEVELOPED IN THE CROWE LAB. THE MABS FOR RVFV THAT WILL BE MAPPED IN THIS CONTRACT ARE BEING ISOLATED AS PART OF ONGOING RESEARCH IN COLLABORATION OF TED ROSS, PHD OF VGTI IN FLORIDA. THE DENV-4 HUMAN MABS WILL BE ISOLATED FROM PBMCS OF SUBJECTS IMMUNIZED WITH A LIVE-ATTENUATED MONOVALENT DENV-4 VACCINE THAT HAS BEEN USED SUCCESSFULLY IN HUMAN TRIALS IN COLLABORATION WITH A. DURBIN AND S. WHITEHEAD. THE JEV HUMAN MABS WILL BE ISOLATED FROM PBMCS OF VOLUNTEERS WHO HAVE RECEIVED A LIVE-ATTENUATED OR INACTIVATED JEV VACCINE IN COLLABORATION WITH S. THOMAS AND FROM CONVALESCENT PBMCS FROM SUBJECTS INFECTED WITH JEV IN THE FIELD IN COLLABORATION WITH C. SIMMONS. FOR THIS CONTRACT, THE CROWE LABORATORY WILL SUPPLY HIGHLY PURIFIED IGG PREPARATIONS OF HUMAN MABS WITH KNOWN FUNCTIONAL ACTIVITY. THE TEXT BELOW DESCRIBES A PLAN FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THESE MABS. SOURCE OF HUMAN B CELLS. NATURAL INFECTION. FOR SOME OF THE VIRUSES TARGETED FOR HUMAN MAB PRODUCTION (JEV, RVFV), SOME OF THE SAMPLES WILL BE OBTAINED FROM PERIPHERAL BLOOD CELLS OF OTHERWISE HEALTHY DONORS WHO SUFFERED ACUTE AND CONFIRMED VIRAL INFECTION. THIS WILL BE COORDINATED BY DR. CROWE AND COLLABORATORS (RVFV: DR. MARIETJIE VENTER, UNIVERSITY OF PRETORIA; JEV: DR. CAMERON SIMMONS, OXFORD UNIVERSITY CLINICAL RESEARCH UNIT, VIETNAM). CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS FROM SEVERAL IMMUNE DONORS WILL BE TRANSFERRED IN A COMPLETELY DE-IDENTIFIED FASHION TO THE VANDERBILT VACCINE CENTER IN THE U.S. FOR THESE STUDIES. IMMUNIZATION. PBMCS ARE AVAILABLE FROM A LARGE NUMBER OF VACCINE RECIPIENTS WHO HAVE RECEIVED EITHER THE INACTIVATED RVFV VACCINE OR THE LIVE ATTENUATED MP-12 STRAIN AT USAMRIID IN MARYLAND, A LIVE ATTENUATED MONOVALENT DENV-4 VACCINE (NIH AND JOHNS HOPKINS), OR INACTIVATED OR LIVE-ATTENUATED JEV (WRAIR). WITH THE HELP OF OUR COLLABORATORS, SUBJECTS WITH HIGH TITER NEUTRALIZING POLYCLONAL ABS WILL BE IDENTIFIED AND, DR. CROWE WILL OBTAIN DE-IDENTIFIED CELLS FROM VACCINEES. THE USE OF CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS FROM MONOVALENTLY IMMUNIZED INDIVIDUALS IS ESPECIALLY IMPORTANT FOR DENV-4 AND JEV, AS IN ENDEMIC REGIONS THESE VIRUSES CO-CIRCULATE WITH OTHER FLAVIVIRUSES (E.G., OTHER DENV SEROTYPES AND YELLOW FEVER VIRUS), WHICH CAN SKEW THE ANTIBODY REPERTOIRE TOWARDS MORE CROSS-REACTIVE AND LESS NEUTRALIZING ABS. MAB TECHNOLOGIES. THE CROWE LAB HAVE SEVERAL B CELL TECHNOLOGIES THAT WILL BE USED IN THIS PROJECT. ONE STRATEGY IS TO GENERATE HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS FROM CIRCULATING B CELLS USING AN ELECTROFUSION TECHNIQUE THAT HAS BEEN VALIDATED AND OPTIMIZED. ARGUABLY, THIS APPROACH IS THE HIGHEST EFFICIENCY TECHNIQUE FOR ISOLATING HUMAN CLONES WITH NATURALLY MATCHED HEAVY AND LIGHT CHAIN GENES EVER REPORTED. THE CROWE LAB HAS GENERATED THOUSANDS OF VIRUS-SPECIFIC B CELL LINES AND MABS TO INFLUENZA, DENV, RSV, MPV, HIV, WEST NILE VIRUS AND OTHERS. THE EFFICIENCY OF THIS METHOD ALLOWED FOR GENERATION OF HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS TO THE 1918 H1N1 PANDEMIC INFLUENZA VIRUS FROM ~ 100 YEAR OLD SURVIVORS, IN WHOM THE AVERAGE CIRCULATING FREQUENCY OF SPECIFIC B CELLS SPECIFIC WAS 1 IN 4 X 106 CELLS. HYBRIDOMA FORMATION. THE CROWE LAB WILL THAW CRYOPRESERVED PBMC AND ISOLATE CELLS USING A FICOLL-HYPAQUE DENSITY GRADIENT METHOD. HUMAN LYMPHOCYTES WILL BE STIMULATED AND TRANSFORMED AFTER INCUBATION WITH EBV SUBSTRAIN B95.8, THE TLR AGONIST CPG ODN 2006 (2.5 ÂΜG/ML; INVIVOGEN), 10 ÂΜM OF CHK2 INHIBITOR II (SIGMA C3742), AND 1 ÂΜG/ML CYCLOSPORIN A. CELLS ARE PLATED IN 384-WELL TISSUE CULTURE PLATES AND MONITORED FOR TRANSFORMATION. TYPICALLY, 50 TO 80 COLONIES FORM PER WELL, WITH ROBUST AB SECRETION. SCREENING FOR VIRUS-SPECIFIC AB LINES. SUPERNATANTS FROM WELLS CONTAINING EBV-TRANSFORMED LYMPHOBLASTOID CELL LINES (LCL) ARE SCREENED IN THE CROWE LABORATORY FOR VIRUS (RVFV, DENV-4, JEV) NEUTRALIZATION (ATTENUATED STRAINS ONLY) OR BINDING ACTIVITY IN ELISAS AGAINST A PANEL OF VIRAL ANTIGENS (RECOMBINANT SOLUBLE PROTEINS (GC, GN, E PROTEINS), OR INACTIVATED WHOLE VIRUS (RVFV STRAIN MP-12, DENV-4 STRAIN 1036, OR JEV STRAIN 14-14-2). CONCURRENTLY, THE CROWE LAB WILL SEND BY OVERNIGHT EXPRESS SHIPPING AN ALIQUOT OF SUPERNATANT FOR TESTING THE NEXT DAY IN A VIRUS NEUTRALIZATION ASSAY USING LIVE VIRULENT WILD-TYPE RVFV (AT VGTI IN THE ROSS LABORATORY) DENV-4 (DIAMOND LABORATORY) AND JEV (DIAMOND LABORATORY). POSITIVE WELLS IN ANY OF THE ASSAYS ARE SELECTED FOR EXPANSION AND FUSION. ELECTROFUSION. EBV-TRANSFORMED LCL SECRETE HUMAN ABS, BUT ARE QUITE UNSTABLE AND DIFFICULT TO CLONE. LCLS SECRETING VIRUS-SPECIFIC MABS ARE FUSED WITH HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS TO FORM HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS, WHICH ARE CONSIDERABLY MORE STABLE. THE SYSTEM USED IS A PROGRAMMABLE ELECTROFUSION SOURCE (CYTOPULSE PA-4000/PA-101). HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS AND EBV-TRANSFORMED HUMAN B CELLS ARE WASHED WITH RPMI-1640 AND CYTOFUSION MEDIUM. LARGE VOLUME FUSION CHAMBERS ARE COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE AND INTERFACE WELL WITH THIS UNIT. THE KEY TO THE FUSION IS BRINGING THE TWO CELL TYPES INTO CLOSE PHYSICAL CONTACT. AFTER FUSION, CELLS ARE ALLOWED TO RECOVER IN THE FUSION ELECTRODE FOR 30 MINUTES, HARVESTED, AND THEN WASHED ONCE WITH RPMI-1640 AT ROOM TEMPERATURE PRIOR TO PLATING IN SELECTION PLATES. HYBRIDOMA SELECTION AND CLONING. FUSED CELLS ARE SEEDED INTO 384-WELL PLATES IN COMPLETE MEDIUM CONTAINING HAT AND OUABAIN. AFTER FIVE DAYS OF CULTURE, CELLS ARE FED WITH FRESH MEDIUM CONTAINING HYPOXANTHINE/THYMIDINE OR HT. WE USED A SERIES OF STEMCELL TECHNOLOGIES MEDIA FOR THESE PROCEDURES, MOST IMPORTANTLY THE CLONACELLÂ®-HY MEDIUM E FOR GROWTH AND EXPANSION. AFTER INITIAL SCREENING FOR HUMAN AB PRODUCTION BY ELISA, THE HYBRIDOMA CELLS FROM POSITIVE WELLS ARE EXPANDED INTO 96- AND THEN 24-WELL PLATES AND CULTURED IN COMPLETE MEDIUM AND THEN HYBRIDOMA CELLS ARE SEEDED IN 96-WELL PLATES AT 0.3 CELL-PER-WELL DENSITY. LIMITING DILUTION IS PERFORMED TWICE TO ENSURE THAT HYBRIDOMA CLONES ARE GENERATED. ALTERNATIVELY, WE CAN SINGLE-CELL SORT THE LINES ON A FACSARIA III FLOW OR USE A CLONEPIX INSTRUMENT. CULTURE SUPERNATANTS ARE SCREENED BY ELISA FOR HUMAN IGG AND ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC ABS. THE COATING ANTIGENS INCLUDE INACTIVATED VIRUSES, LIVE ATTENUATED VIRUS PARTICLES, AND RECOMBINANT ENVELOPE GLYCOPROTEINS. MAB PREPARATIONS. HYBRIDOMA CELL LINES WILL BE ADAPTED TO SERUM-FREE MEDIUM. SUPERNATANTS OF HIGH-DENSITY CULTURES WILL BE PRODUCED IN CELLINE DEVICES (BD BIOSCIENCES). PURIFIED AND CONCENTRATED PREPARATIONS OF EACH MAB WILL BE PREPARED BY FPLC USING PROTEIN G RESIN ON AN AKTA INSTRUMENT FOLLOWED BY BUFFER EXCHANGE USING ULTRA CENTRIFUGAL FILTER DEVICES. FOR LARGER SCALE PREPARATIONS (E.G., 50 TO 100 MG LOTS), WE WILL SCALE THE CELL CULTURE UP TO 25 L USING A WAVE BIOREACTOR. VOLUME WILL BE INITIALLY REDUCED USING A GE QUIXSTAND LABORATORY-SCALE SEPARATION SYSTEM THAT USES CROSS-FLOW FILTRATION CARTRIDGES. THIS PROCEDURE IS FOLLOWED BY FPLC PURIFICATION. WE WILL USE QUANTITATIVE ELISAS TO DEFINE THE FINAL CONCENTRATION OF MABS. C. HUMAN SUBJECTS AND/OR ANIMALS IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. description: THE OVERARCHING LONG-TERM GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO CHARACTERIZE IMMUNE MARKERS AND MECHANISMS IN THE ELDERLY THAT DETERMINE THEIR VULNERABILITY TO INFECTIONS AND BIOTERRORISM AGENTS, SPECIFICALLY WEST NILE VIRUS (WNV). ELDERLY HUMANS ARE HIGHLY SUSCEPTIBLE TO WNV COMPARED TO IMMUNOCOMPETENT ADULTS, AND WNV READILY INFECTS MICE, WHERE THE DISEASE IS HIGHLY LETHAL TO OLD ANIMALS AND RECAPITULATES MANY ESSENTIAL FEATURES OF THE HUMAN DISEASE. PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR AT OREGON HEALTH AND SCIENCE UNIVERSITY (OHSU) WILL OVERSEE WNV MICRORNA EXPERIMENTS AND THE WORK COMPLETED BY THE CO-PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATORS, POSTDOCTORAL RESEARCHER, SENIOR RESEARCH ASSISTANT, AND RESEARCH ASSISTANT 2. OHSU WILL IDENTIFY MICRO RNAS WITHIN SPECIFIED CELL TYPES FROM ADULT AND OLD ORGANISMS USING MASSIVELY (“DEEP”) SEQUENCING-BASED TECHNIQUES. THESE METHODS ARE EXPECTED TO PROVIDE BOTH SEQUENCE AND QUALITY INFORMATION FOR EACH MIRNA, REGARDLESS OF WHETHER THE MIRNA HAS BEEN PREVIOUSLY IDENTIFIED. SPECIFICALLY, THE CO-PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATORS WILL ANALYZE MIRNA EXPRESSION IN DCS AND T-CELLS FROM AND ADULT MICE AND HUMANS, WORK WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF ARIZONA LAB TO DETERMINE THE CONTRIBUTION OF THESE MIRNAS TO FUNCTIONAL DEFECTS OBSERVED IN THESE CELLS AND WORK WITH POSTDOCTORAL RESEARCHER TO DETERMINE MRNA TARGEST OF AGE-MISREGULATED MIRNAS AND THUS HELP PROVIDE A MECHANISTIC BASIS FOR AGE-RELATED MULTIFUNCTION OF CELLS OF THE IMMUNE SYSTEM AND PROVIDE STATISTICAL OVERSIGHT AND ASSIST WITH EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN AND OVERSEE ACTIVITIES OF SENIOR RESEARCH ASSISTANT AND RESEARCH ASSISTANT. THE POSTDOCTORAL RESEARCHER WILL IDENTIFY TARGETS AFFECTED BY AGE-MISREGULATED MIRNAS AND DETERMINE THE ROLES THESE TARGETS PLAY IN AGE-RELATED DEFECTS IN IMMUNITY. THE SENIOR RESEARCH ASSISTANT WILL LEAD THE MIRNA AND PATHWAY ANALYSIS. THE RESEARCH ASSISTANT 2 WILL OVERSEE ALL DATA DISSEMINATION FOLLOWING THE DATA SHARING PLAN. ADDITIONALLY, OHSU WILL PARTICIPATE IN MEETINGS WITH UNIVERSITY OF ARIZONA AS PROJECT PROGRESSES, INCLUDING TRAVELING TO UNIVERSITY OF ARIZONA.

description: I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. OF THE SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS TO BE STUDIED, TWO ARE MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). THE PARASITE STUDIES WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS (UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH FLORIDA), KING (CASE WESTERN RESERVE UNIVERSITY) AND TOLIA (WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). IN ADDITION TO THE EPITOPE MAPPING TO BE PERFORMED BY DR. TOLIA, A SECOND MAJOR GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF CORRELATES RELATING B CELL EPITOPES WITH AB NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY AND AG BINDING THAT WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS AND KING. B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT. HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS AND MURINE MABS FROM IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. MALARIA NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED USING ASSAYS INTERROGATING BOTH SPOROZOITE AND MEROZOITE STAGES OF DEVELOPMENT. QUANTITATIVE ASSAYS WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE AB/AG INTERACTION STRENGTH, SPECIFICITY, AND VALENCY TO FURTHER DEVELOP CORRELATES OF PROTECTION. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION WILL BE INTERROGATED FOR OUR MOST POTENT MABS, WHERE THE STAGE OF THE INFECTION PROCESS BLOCKED BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED. ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION. II. SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.) ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT.   B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. MAB GENERATION. LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. DR. KING WILL GENERATE HUMAN ANTI-MALARIA MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES TO TWO ANTIGENS PER YEAR WILL BE GENERATED. EPITOPE VALIDATION. A PRIMARY GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A FRAMEWORK RELATING B CELLS EPITOPES WITH AB BINDING AND NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY. TO ASSESS NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX, DR. KING HAS DEVELOPED NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING MALARIA MEROZOITES. DR. ADAMS WILL PERFORM P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX BLOOD-STAGE MEROZOITE NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING ESTABLISHED ASSAYS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR NEUTRALIZATION IN PER YEAR. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION. A KEY QUESTION FOR PARASITES IS AT WHAT STAGE OF INFECTION/DEVELOPMENT AB NEUTRALIZATION IS ACHIEVED. DIRECT MALARIA PARASITE ANTIGEN BINDING ASSAYS TO EXAMINE MAB BLOCKADE OF AG BINDING TO HOST-CELLS AND/OR COGNATE RECEPTORS, AND THE EFFECT OF MABS ON MEROZOITE DEVELOPMENT WILL BE CARRIED OUT BY DR. KING. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED IN THESE ASSAYS PER YEAR. DATA MANAGEMENT AND EPITOPE SUBMISSION. THIS CONTRACT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. A DATABASE AT WU WILL CATALOG THE DATA GENERATED IN ALL OF THE CONTRACT GROUPS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: AB POTENCY IN NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS; AB VARIABLE DOMAIN SEQUENCES; AG RECOGNIZED; EXPRESSION VECTORS CONSTRUCTED; PROGRESS OF AB AND AG PRODUCTION; AB/AG BINDING AFFINITY AND KINETICS; PROGRESS OF YEAST SURFACE DISPLAY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF MASS SPECTROMETRY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF CRYSTALLOGRAPHY EXPERIMENTS; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY CORE STRATEGIES; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY ALTERNATE STRATEGIES; AND RESULTS FROM AB MECHANISM OF PROTECTION STUDIES. DR. KING WILL PROVIDE ALL DATA FOR DEPOSITION TO THE WU DATABASE. C. HUMAN SUBJECTS AND/OR ANIMALS IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. I Â€“ O. OPTION 15B - PATHOGENESIS PROJECT (0258-0517-4609) COLLABORATION BETWEEN UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA RESEARCH FOUNDATION, INC. - UNIVERSIDAD NACIONAL DE CORDOBA, ARGENTINA AS PART OF THE CENTER FOR RESEARCH ON INFLUENZA SURVEILLANCE AND PATHOGENESIS (CRIP) OUR MANDATE IS TO ADD TO THE CURRENT BODY OF KNOWLEDGE ON INFLUENZA VIRUS PATHOGENESIS, HOST RESTRICTION AND TRANSMISSION THROUGH CONDUCTING NOVEL RESEARCH AIMED AT PUBLICATION IN PEER-REVIEWED JOURNALS. 1) TO INVESTIGATE WHETHER SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION SYSTEMS OF S. PNEUMONIAE SENSE IAV-INDUCED ALTERATIONS IN ALVEOLAR AND BRONCHIAL CELLS WE WILL. 2) TO DETERMINE WHICH VIRAL FACTORS ARE INVOLVED IN THE SYNERGISTIC MECHANISM BETWEEN IAV AND S. PNEUMONIAE CELLS WE WILL. 3) TO DEFINE THE SYNERGISM BETWEEN AVIAN/HUMAN INFLUENZA STRAINS AND S. PNEUMONIAE IN DIFFERENTIATED HUMAN AIRWAY CELLS (HAE). OPTION 11B - 400 ANIMAL SURVEILLANCE SAMPLES (0258-0572-4609) FERRETS (MUSTELA PUTORIUS FURO) ARE NATURALLY SUSCEPTIBLE TO HUMAN INFLUENZA VIRUSES A AND THEIR DISEASE RESPONSE TO INFECTION WIDELY RESEMBLES THAT OF HUMANS INCLUDING CLINICAL SIGNS, PATHOGENESIS AND IMMUNITY (1-6). FERRETS ARE ALSO SUSCEPTIBLE TO AVIAN, EQUINE AND SWINE INFLUENZA A VIRUSES, ALTHOUGH ONLY SWINE AND HUMAN A VIRUSES INDUCE FEBRILE ILLNESSES IN FERRETS (7, 8). THE FERRET ALSO DISPLAYS PHYSICAL CHARACTERISTICS THAT ALLOW EASY IDENTIFICATION AND CHARACTERIZATION OF CLINICAL SYMPTOMS. THE UNUSUALLY LONG TRACHEA ALLOWS EASY COMPARTMENTALIZATION OF THE UPPER AND LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACTS (9, 10). THE FERRET IS LARGE ENOUGH TO MONITOR CLINICAL PARAMETERS SUCH AS TEMPERATURE, PULSE AND RESPIRATORY RATE WHILE ALSO BEING THE ONLY SMALL ANIMAL TO DEVELOPS A FEBRILE RESPONSE TO NATURALLY OCCURRING INFLUENZA A VIRUSES (10). ANTIGENIC CHARACTERIZATION OF INFLUENZA VIRUSES IS TYPICALLY BASED ON HEMAGGLUTINATION INHIBITION (HI) ASSAY DATA FOR VIRAL ISOLATES TESTED AGAINST STRAIN-SPECIFIC POST-INFECTION FERRET ANTISERA. THE GOAL OF THIS SUBCONTRACT IS TO PREPARE FERRET SERA AGAINST HUMAN INFLUENZA VIRUSES. FERRETS WILL BE INOCULATED WITH A HIGH DOSE (≥106 TCID50) OF HUMAN INFLUENZA VIRUS IN 1 ML INOCULUM (TABLE 1). TWO FERRETS/VIRUS WILL BE USED. FERRETS WILL BE MONITORED FOR CLINICAL SIGNS OF DISEASE. AT 14 DAYS-POST-INOCULATION (DPI), 2-3 ML OF BLOOD ARE COLLECTED TO TEST HI TITER AGAINST HOMOLOGOUS VIRUS, IF THE ANTIBODY TITER HAS REACHED ≥ 640, THEN COLLECT FULL BLOOD. SACRIFICE. IF THE ANTIBODY TITER HAS NOT YET REACHED THE EXPECTED TITER, PERFORM ADDITIONAL IMMUNIZATION, FOOTPAD SQ INJECTION OF 0.4 ML (INACTIVATED VIRUS+ADJUVANT)*/FOOTPAD. AT 14 DAYS-POST-BOOST, BLEED OUT AND TEST HI TITERS AGAINST HOMOLOGOUS VIRUS. description: PURPOSE: TO SERVE AS A DESIGNATED OUTREACH LIBRARY FOR THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION OF THE NATIONAL NETWORK OF LIBRARIES OF MEDICINE. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: OUTREACH LIBRARIES AGREE TO PERFORM THE FOLLOWING FUNCTIONS ON BEHALF OF THE NETWORK: 1. DESIGNATE A LIBRARIAN TO SERVE AS OUTREACH LIBRARY LIAISON TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION; 2. PARTICIPATE IN OUTREACH LIBRARY WEBINARS AND OTHER COLLABORATIVE ACTIVITIES PROVIDED FOR OUTREACH LIBRARIANS; 3. ASSIST THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY IN THE IDENTIFICATION OF UNDERSERVED GROUPS OF HEALTH PROFESSIONALS AND CONSUMERS WITHIN THE STATE; 4. PROVIDE UNAFFILIATED HEALTH PROFESSIONALS WITHIN THE STATE WITH REFERENCE SERVICES AND ACCESS TO COLLECTIONS, INCLUDING ACCESS TO ELECTRONIC RESOURCES TO THE EXTENT PERMITTED BY" LICENSE AGREEMENTS; 5. PROVIDE DOCUMENT DELIVERY SERVICE TO UNAFFILIATED HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, CONSUMERS AND NN/LM AFFILIATE MEMBERS IN THE STATE; 6. PROVIDE TRAINING IN NLM RESOURCES AND DATABASES TO HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, LIBRARIANS AND CONSUMERS IN THE STATE. THIS MAY BE DONE AT THE LIBRARY'S OWN INITIATIVE OR IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY; 7. SUPPORT THE NLM AND NN/LM EXHIBIT PROGRAMS BY ASSISTING IN AND/OR SUPPORTING STAFFING AT STATE EXHIBITS COORDINATED BY THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY, BY INFORMING THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY ABOUT POSSIBLE EXHIBIT OPPORTUNITIES IN THE STATE, AND BY EXHIBITING AT LOCAL COMMUNITY EVENTS; 8. ENTER NLM AND NN/LM RELATED OUTREACH ACTIVITIES INTO THE APPROPRIATE DATABASE WITHIN 30 DAYS OF THE ACTIVITY *; 9. SUBMIT TALLY SHEETS TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION WITHIN 30 DAYS AFTER AN EXHIBIT EVENT ..; 10. SUBMIT AN ANNUAL REPORT TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION, SUMMARIZING OUTREACH ACTIVITIES UNDERTAKEN BY THE OUTREACH LIBRARY DURING THE CONTRACT PREVIOUS YEAR*. *NOTE: IN THE FALL, NLM PLANS TO COMBINE THESE THREE REPORTING OPTIONS INTO THE "NLM OUTREACH APPLICATION AND ONLINE CONTACT REPORTING SYSTEM" WHICH WILL REPLACE THE OARF DATABASE. ALL OUTREACH ACTIVITIES, EXHIBITING EVENTS AND ANNUAL.REPORTS WILL BE ENTERED INTO THAT SYSTEM WHEN IT BECOMES AVAILABLE. MEASUREMENT OF PROGRESS: PROGRESS WILL BE MEASURED BY MONITORING INPUT FROM THE DESIGNATED OUTREACH LIBRARIAN DURING QUARTERLY WEBINARS AND OTHER MEETINGS, LEVEL OF ACTIVITY REPORTED IN THE NLM OUTREACH ACTIVITY DATABASE, AND CONTENT OF THE ANNUAL REPORT.

description: BIOSCIENCE WRITERS (BSW) WILL PROVIDE WRITERS/EDITORS TO SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF CLINICIAN SUMMARIES USING THE METHODS AND PROTOCOLS DEVELOPED BY THE EISENBERG CENTER. BSW WILL SERVE AS PART OF THE TRANSLATION TEAM BY CONTRIBUTING TO THE PREPARATION OF, AND WRITING AND EDITING OF, UP TO 10 CLINICIAN SUMMARIES, PROVIDING BETWEEN 60 AND 85 HOURS OF SERVICES FOR OUR COMPONENTS OF THE WORK ON EACH TOPIC AT $100 PER HOUR, TOTALING $85,000 IN DIRECT LABOR COSTS PER YEAR. BSW COSTS ALSO INCLUDE A FIXED FEE OF $1,500 PER TOPIC ($15,000 FOR 10 TOPICS ANNUALLY) FOR A TOTAL OF $100,000 PER YEAR FOR UP TO 5 YEARS. TASKS THAT BSW WILL ASSIST UNDER EISENBERG CENTER GUIDANCE AND PROTOCOLS INCLUDE ONE OR MORE OF THE FOLLOWING: 1) PRE-REVIEWING EPC DRAFTS USING THE EISENBERG CENTER CHECKLIST; 2) REVIEWING AND SUPPLEMENTING (AS NEEDED) FORMATIVE FINDINGS; 3) PREPARING PROJECT PLANS SPECIFIC TO CLINICIAN TARGET AUDIENCE(S), AND CONTRIBUTING TO DRAFTING THE KEY MESSAGE DOCUMENTS; 4) PREPARING, IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE MEDICAL CONTENT EXPERT (MCE) AND THE EISENBERG CENTER DIRECTOR OR HIS DESIGNEE, DRAFT CLINICIAN SUMMARIES; 5) CONTRIBUTING TO PREPARATION OF TESTING PROTOCOLS; 6) PARTICIPATING IN ANALYZING TESTING RESULTS; 7) MODIFYING SUMMARIES AS A RESULT OF TESTING AND REVIEWS BY EXPERTS, EXTERNAL ORGANIZATIONS, AND AHRQ; AND 8) PREPARING THE DISPOSITION REPORT AND THE CONTENT PROOF FOR FINAL INTERNAL EISENBERG CENTER REVIEW FOR SUBMISSION TO AHRQ.

description: DRS. MARK GLADWIN AND TAMIR KANIAS WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE STUDY DESIGN, PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT, HUMAN SUBJECT RESEARCH COMPLIANCE, PERFORM RATE OF HEMOLYSIS ASSAYS AND DATA ANALYSIS, SHIP REPOSITORY SAMPLES TO BLOOD SYSTEMS RESEARCH INSTITUTE (BSRI) AND REPORT RESULTS TO BSRI AND RESEARCH TRIANGLE INTERNATIONAL (RTI). TRAINING/MOP DR. GLADWINÂ€™S LAB WILL PROVIDE TRAINING TO BSRI STAFF IN PERFORMING THE SELECTED HIGH-THROUGHPUT ASSAYS MEASURING UP TO 4 FORMS OF STRESS: OXIDANT-INDUCED STRESS, SHEAR OR MECHANICAL STRESS, OSMOTIC STRESS AND STORAGE HEMOLYSIS. DR. GLADWINÂ€™S LAB WILL SHARE ALL PROTOCOLS RELATED TO ASSAYS AND INFORMATION REQUIRED TO SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE MANUAL OF PROCEDURES FOR THE STUDY WITH BSRI IN COLLABORATION WITH RTI, THE REDS-III DATA COORDINATING CENTER. PILOT/QC DR. GLADWINÂ€™S LAB WILL PARTICIPATE IN A PILOT STUDY WITH BSRI TO COMPARE HEMOLYSIS PARAMETERS DURING STORAGE IN THE MANUFACTURED LEUKO-REDUCED PACKED RED BLOOD CELLS AND TRANSFER BAGS FROM EACH OF THE 4 HUBS, AND COMPARE THE REPRODUCIBILITY OF THE ASSAYS ACROSS THE TWO TESTING LABS (UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH (UP) AND BSRI). SCREENING FOR EXTREME HEMOLYSIS PHENOTYPES A TOTAL OF 14,000 RBC DONORS WILL BE ENROLLED ACROSS FOUR REDS-III HUBS IN A MULTI-CENTER STUDY TO IDENTIFY NOVEL POLYMORPHISMS IN HEMOGLOBIN AND IRON REGULATORY PROTEINS, TO DEFINE THE GENETIC AND METABOLIC BASES FOR DONOR SPECIFIC DIFFERENCES IN STORAGE HEMOLYSIS AND TO ESTABLISH A SHARABLE REPOSITORY OF RED BLOOD CELLS (RBC), PLASMA, WHITE BLOOD CELLS, AND DNA SAMPLES FROM DONORS WHO WERE CHARACTERIZED FOR HEMOGLOBIN PARAMETERS, IRON METABOLISM, RBC STORAGE HEMOLYSIS PROPENSITY, AND GENETIC AND METABOLOMIC PROFILES. DR. GLADWINÂ€™S LAB AT UP WILL RECEIVE LEUKOCYTE REDUCED-PACKED RED BLOOD CELL (LR-PRBC) SAMPLES IN SMALLER VOLUME BLOOD BAGS FROM THREE (3) OF THE REDS-III BLOOD CENTERS (APPROX.10,500 DONORS). DURING THE INITIAL SCREENING, THE BAGS WILL BE ACCESSED USING STERILE TECHNIQUES TO ACQUIRE SAMPLES CORRESPONDING TO LR-RBC COMPONENTS STORED FOR 42 DAYS OF STORAGE. SAMPLES (~120/WEEK) FROM EACH BAG AT THE 40-42 DAY STORAGE TIME POINT WILL BE TESTED WITH SELECTED HIGH-THROUGHPUT ASSAYS (SPONTANEOUS HEMOLYSIS AND OSMOTIC STRESS). THIS COHORT OF REDS-III DONORS WITH LINKED RBC DONATION-DERIVED SAMPLES WILL ENABLE ANALYSIS OF KEY RBC STORAGE PARAMETERS AS A FUNCTION OF DONOR CHARACTERISTICS INCLUDING DEMOGRAPHICS, SMOKING HISTORY, AND FIRST-TIME/REPEAT AND ABO BLOOD GROUP STATUS. THE DATA WILL BE ANALYZED AND REPORTED TO IDENTIFY 1000 DONORS WITH EXTREME RATES OF HEMOLYSIS PHENOTYPES TO BE RECALLED IN THE SECOND PHASE OF THE STUDY. IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT 800 WILL BE ENROLLED IN THE RECALL STUDY AND WILL PROVIDE DONATION OF ONE FULL LR-PRBC UNIT ALLOWING FOR AMPLE VOLUME TO TEST 3 OR MORE STORAGE TIME POINTS USING EXPANDED TESTING MEASURING UP TO 4 FORMS OF STRESS: OXIDANT-INDUCED STRESS, SHEAR OR MECHANICAL STRESS, OSMOTIC STRESS AND STORAGE HEMOLYSIS. UP WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE FOLLOW UP TESTING ON Â¾ (600) OF THE RECALLED DONORS. BIOSPECIMEN REPOSITORY/BIOLINCC DOCUMENTATION DR. GLADWINÂ€™S LAB WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE STORAGE (-86 DEGREE CELSIUS MECHANICAL FREEZER PROVIDED BY BSRI) OF MULTIPLE ALIQUOTS OF CONCENTRATED RED-BLOOD CELLS AND SUPERNATANT FLUID (ADDITIVE SOLUTION AND LEFT OVER PLASMA) AT EACH TIME POINT TESTED, DURING BOTH THE INITIAL SCREENING AND RECALL STUDY. THE LAB WILL USE VALIDATED SPECIMEN ACQUISITION AND STORAGE SOPS, AND WILL HAVE AN ACTIVE QA/QC PROGRAM TO ENSURE THAT THE SOPS ARE BEING FOLLOWED. SHIPMENT VMI WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SHIPMENT OF SPECIFIC ALIQUOTS TO DR. ZIMRINGÂ€™S LAB AT PUGET SOUND BLOOD CENTER (PSBC) FOR FURTHER METABOLOMIC TESTING AND QUARTERLY SHIPMENT OF FINAL REPOSITORY ALIQUOTS TO BSRI.

PURCHASE EQUIPMENT AS NEEDED D. TRAVEL TO AN AREA LIBRARY/ARCHIVES FOR ADVISE AND EXPERTISE 4. STRIVE TO INCREASE COMMUNITY PATRONAGE OF LIBRARY SERVICES. A. PARTNERSHIP WITH TECHNOLOGY AND MEDIA DEPARTMENTS WILL BE FORMED TO RECORD PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENTS AND DESIGN POSTERS UTILIZING LIBRARY INTERNS, COMMUNITY YOUTH, AND COLLEGE STUDENTS. C. CONTINUED GROWTH OF HEALTH ACQUISITIONS TO INCREASE HOLDINGS ON HEALTH TOPICS FOR THEVMML. D. PROVIDE A MONTHLY PARENT'S NIGHT AND CHILDREN'S NIGHT TO EDUCATE DAKOTA CULTURE, VALUES, COMMON HEALTH RISKS/PREVENTION, AND ACTIVITIES. description: ACCORD FOLLOW-ON STUDY IS A PROSPECTIVE, OBSERVATIONAL FOLLOW-UP STUDY OF APPROXIMATELY 8,000 PARTICIPANTS WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED IN THE ACTION TO CONTROL CARDIOVASCULAR RISK IN DIABETES (ACCORD) TRIAL. IT IS DESIGNED TO FURTHER ELUCIDATE AND CLARIFY THE LONG-TERM EFFECT OF THE ACCORTD TREATMENT STRATEGIES AND PROVIDE ADDITIONAL DATA ON THE LONG-TERM RELATIONSHIPS AMONG VARIOUS CARDIOVASCULAR AND DIABETIC RISK FACTORS. ACCORD WAS A RANDOMIZED CARDIOVASCULAR CLINICAL TRIAL IN PEOPLE WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED FOR AN AVERAGE OF APPROXIMATELY 5 YEARS FROM 2001 THROUGH MID-2009. ACCORD PARTICIPANTS WHO AGREE TO PARTICIPATE IN THE FOLLOW-ON STUDY WILL CONTINUE TO BE FOLLOWED THROUGH CLINIC AND PHONE VISITS FOR AN AVERAGE OF 3.5 YEARS IN THE PERIOD 2011 THROUGH 2014. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE SEEN IN 76 CLINICS ACROSS THE UNITED STATES AND CANADA. THE PRIMARY OUTCOME WILL BE THE FIRST OCCURRENCE OF A MAJOR CARDIOVASCULAR EVENT. SECONDARY OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE ALL CAUSE MORTALITY, OTHER MACRO VASCULAR SECONDARY OUTCOMES, AND DISEASE-FREE SURVIVAL TIME. LAB AND ECG MEASUREMENTS WILL ALSO BE TAKEN PERIODICALLY DURING THE STUDY.

description: THE OVERALL OBJECTIVES OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO 1) APPLY HIGH THROUGHPUT GENOMIC TECHNOLOGIES ON THE WELL-CHARACTERIZED WOMEN'S HEALTH INITIATIVE BIO RESOURCE AND TO 2) INTEGRATE THE DATA GENERATED WITH EXISTING CLINICAL, GENETIC, AND BIOMARKER DATA IN ORDER TO CONFIDENTLY IDENTIFY NOVEL DETERMINANTS OF CORONARY HEART DISEASE AND RELATED PHENOTYPES IN AGING POST-MENOPAUSAL WOMEN" WE PROPOSE TO CAREFULLY PROFILE THE DNA AND PLASMA OF CHD CASES AS WELL AS AN APPROPRIATE SET OF CONTROLS USING TWO COMPLEMENTARY BUT WELL-VALIDATED GENOMIC TECHNOLOGIES AT BASELINE .. THESE GENOMIC TECHNOLOGIES ARE EXPECTED TO GENERATE HIGH QUALITY AND HIGH-RESOLUTION GENOME WIDE DNA METHYLATION PROFILE AS WELL AS A COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT OF CIRCULATING MICRORNA LEVELS. WE WILL THEN COMPREHENSIVELY ANALYZE AND INTEGRATE THIS GENOMIC DATA WITH EXISTING CLINICAL, GENETIC, AND BIOMARKER DATA USING STATE OF THE ART STATISTICAL METHODOLOGIES DEVELOPED BY MEMBERS OF THE INVESTIGATIVE TEAM TO IDENTIFY GENOMIC SIGNATURES AND PATHWAYS RELEVANT TO CHD AND ITS RISK FACTORS. THIS PROPOSAL WILL ALLOW US AND OTHERS 1) TO IDENTIFY GENOMIC BIOMARKERS OF CHD EVENTS, 2) TO INTEGRATE THESE BIOMARKERS INTO DIAGNOSTIC AND PROGNOSTIC PREDICTORS OF CHD AND RELATED PHENOTYPES, 3) TO ELUCIDATE THE BIOLOGY OF CHD AND RELATED PHENOTYPES, 4) TO TEST WHETHER AGING RELATED CPGS FOUND IN OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES MEDIATE THE RISK OF AGE ON CHD, AND 5) TO REVISIT THE GWAS STUDIES OF CHD BASED ON MOLECULARLY REFINED PHENOTYPES AND SNP SET ANALYSIS INFORMED BY OUR NEW GENOMIC DATA. THESE OBJECTIVES ARE ACHIEVABLE IN THE CONTEXT OF OUR PRIOR EXPERIENCE PRODUCING AND ANALYZING SIMILAR DATA IN OTHER SAMPLES SETS AS EXTENSIVELY DESCRIBED IN THE "TECHNICAL PLAN" SECTION OF THIS PROPOSAL. THESE OBJECTIVES ARE ALSO ACHIEVABLE IN THE CONTEXT OF THE NUMEROUS UNIQUE STATISTICAL TOOLS WE HAVE DEVELOPED SPECIFICALLY FOR INTEGRATING GENOMIC DATA GENERATED FROM VARIOUS SOURCES.

description: THE CONTRACTOR SHALL UNDERTAKE THE FOLLOWING TASKS IN COMPLETING THIS WORK: PROVIDE OVERALL LEADERSHIP AND ADMINISTRATIVE OVERSIGHT FOR THE PROPOSED PROJECT, INVOLVING CO-INVESTIGATORS RABIN AND DAVIES. PROVIDE EXPERT INPUT ON A LITERATURE REVIEW AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN AIMED AT DEVELOPING AN INVENTORY OF EXISTING CPMS FOR BOTH USE-CASES, AS WELL AS A SET OF PRELIMINARY CRITERIA FOR JUDGING THE QUALITY AND CLINICAL APPLICABILITY OF CPMS. THIS WORK WILL BE LED BY DR. RABIN, BUILDING ON PRIOR WORK BY HER TEAM AND OTHERS (EPROGNOSIS.ORG RESEARCH GROUP, CPM DEVELOPERS) TO PRODUCE CLINICAL TOOLS AIMED AT MAKING CPMS ACCESSIBLE TO CLINICIANS AND PATIENTS. THE CONTRACTOR WILL FOCUS ON CPMS FOR PROSTATE CANCER AND HEAD AND NECK CANCER TREATMENT OUTCOMES. OTHER CANDIDATE CPMS FOR BOTH USE CASES WILL BE IDENTIFIED THROUGH FURTHER LITERATURE REVIEW. LEAD DEVELOPMENT OF A PROTOTYPE MODEL OF USE FOR INCORPORATING CPMS RELEVANT TO TREATMENT DECISIONS FOR PROSTATE CANCER, AND REFINE THIS MODEL BASED ON ITERATIVE FEEDBACK OF EXPERT ADVISORY PANEL (EAP) MEMBERS, CONSISTING OF PRACTICING CLINICIANS (UROLOGISTS, MEDICAL ONCOLOGISTS), CANCER SURVIVORS WITH FOCUSED CONTENT EXPERTISE AND EXPERIENCE IN PROSTATE CANCER, AND CPM DEVELOPERS. THE MODEL OF USE WILL 1) IDENTIFY EXISTING CPMS OF SUFFICIENT QUALITY AND RELEVANCE TO THE TREATMENT DECISION, 2) CLARIFY THE VALUE AND LIMITATIONS OF EACH CPM, AND 3) SPECIFY THE APPROPRIATE MANNER AND SEQUENCE OF USE OF EACH CPM IN THE PATIENT COUNSELING AND DECISION-MAKING PROCESS. THE TEAMS WILL USE LOGIC MODELS AND STORYBOARDING TO DEPICT THE INFORMATION NEEDS OF CLINICIANS AND PATIENTS WHO ARE ENGAGING IN DECISION MAKING, AND TO REFINE THE PROTOTYPE MODELS OF USE. PROVIDE EXPERT INPUT ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF A PROTOTYPE WEB-BASED CLINICAL META-TOOL THAT OPERATIONALIZES THE USE OF PROGNOSTIC MODELS IN CANCER CARE DECISIONS. THE META-TOOL PROTOTYPE WILL UTILIZE INTERACTIVITY AND INNOVATIVE VISUALIZATION TECHNIQUES TO ENHANCE THE UNDERSTANDABILITY AND USABILITY OF INFORMATION, AS WELL AS LANGUAGE SCRIPTS FOR EXPLAINING THE VALUE AND LIMITATIONS OF PROGNOSTIC ESTIMATES. THE TOOL WILL INCORPORATE EXPLANATORY LANGUAGE AND SCRIPTS DEVELOPED WITH THE ASSISTANCE OF EAP MEMBERS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL NOT BE INVOLVED IN WRITING ANY SPECIFIC FUNDING OPPORTUNITIES THAT MIGHT DEVELOP FROM THIS WORK. HOWEVER, THE OUTPUT OF THIS CONTRACT IS EXPECTED TO INFORM THE DEVELOPMENT OF POTENTIAL FUNDING OPPORTUNITIES IN THIS AREA, AND WILL BE USED. FOR EXAMPLE, PRESENTATIONS TO SENIOR NCI LEADERSHIP AND TO OTHER INTERESTED RESEARCHERS, TO CONTINUE THE DEVELOPMENT OF THIS AREA AS A RESEARCH PROGRAM FOR NCI.

description: DR. SHARPE'S GROUP IS ANALYZING AGED-RELATED CHANGES IN CD8 T CELL RESPONSES IN CLOSE COLLABORATION WITH DRS. MARCIA HAIGIS AND E. JOHN WHERRY. DR. HAIGIS' GROUP STUDIES THE ROLE OF SIRTUINS IN THE METABOLIC REGULATION OF T CELL RESPONSES IN YOUNG AND AGED MICE. THE MAIN GOALS OF THEIR STUDIES ARE TO UNDERSTAND HOW SITUINS REGULATE (1) THE ROLE OF KEY METABOLIC PATHWAYS IN IMMUNE REGULATIONS, AND (2) TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT IMMUNE SENESCENCE CAN BE ATTRIBUTED, AT LEAST PARTIALLY, TO METABOLIC FUNCTION.

description: UCSF SUBCONTRACT TO PROVIDE GENETIC EXPERT CONSULTATION, EXOME SEQUENCING, GWAS GENOTYPING, AND RAW DATA CLEANING TO PREPARE FOR DATA ANALYSIS. IN COLLABORATION WITH THE KPVSC, CDC AND FDA, PROVIDED EXPERT INPUT INTO THE DESIGN OF THE CURRENT APPROVED PROTOCOL CURRENTLY BEING CONDUCTED. AS A SUB-CONTRACTOR TO KPNC FOR THIS PROJECT, THE UCSF WILL COLLABORATE WITH THE FDA AND CONTRIBUTE EXPERTISE IN GENETIC STATISTICAL DESIGN, DNA ANALYSES, INTERPRETATION OF EXOME AND GWAS ANALYSES, AND CONSTRUCT A REPOSITORY DATABASE OF GENES IDENTIFIED BY DNA SEQUENCE ANALYSES REVEALED BY LITERATURE SEARCH. description: THE GOALS OF THE ATR PROGRAM CENTER ON THE PROVISION OF SUBSTANCE ABUSE CLINICAL AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES TO THOSE IN NEED. THIS GRANT PROGRAM IS DESIGNED TO BE A SYSTEMS- CHANGE INITIATIVE THROUGH THE INTRODUCTION OF A VOUCHER-BASED SYSTEM OF PAYMENT INTO THE CLINICAL TREATMENT DELIVERY SYSTEM, ENCOURAGING INDIVIDUAL CHOICE BY EMPOWERING THE INDIVIDUAL TO CHOOSE HIS/HER PROVIDER OF SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS CLINICAL TREATMENT AND/OR RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES. THROUGH THIS CONTRACT, TA WILL BE PROVIDED TO STATE/T~IBES TO IMPLEMENT A LARGE-SCALE VOUCHERS SYSTEM THAT SUPPORTS THE CONTINUUM OF RECOVERY FROM SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS. ADDITIONALLY, THIS CONTRACT WILL SUPPORT PEER PROVIDERS WHO RECEIVE FEDERAL FUNDING TO BOTH PROVIDE PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES THROUGH RECOVERY CENTERS, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, ETC. AND INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT AND CAPACITY-BUILDING FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A STATEWIDE NETWORK OF RECOVERY COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS THAT SERVE TO PROMOTE THE INVOLVEMENT OF INDIVIDUALS IN RECOVERY FROM ADDICTION, AND THEIR FAMILY MEMBERS AS PARTNERS IN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND OTHER ALLIED HEALTH SYSTEMS. SCOPE: THE MAJOR OBJECTIVE OF A SUBCONTRACT TO THE C-BCSC SCC DATA RESOURCE IS TO ASSIST IN THE SHARING OF DATA STORED WITHIN THE CURRENT BCSC DATABASE AND IMPROVE ITS CAPACITY TO SUPPORT USE OF THE DATA BY THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. TO ENSURE VALID DATA INTERPRETATION THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL MAINTAIN DATA USE AGREEMENTS WITH THE C-BCSC SCC TO AID IN CLARIFYING SITE SPECIFIC DATA IN THE POOLED DATABASE. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS: PROJECT AREA 1. PARTICIPATION IN BCSC POOLED DATABASE THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL PARTICIPATE IN THE SCSC POOLED DATABASE THROUGH THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES: A. PROVIDE ACCESS TO THE EXISTING SITE-SPECIFIC DATA. B. ENSURE THAT PROPER ADMINISTRATIVE AUTHORIZATIONS AND CERTIFICATIONS ARE IN PLACE WHICH MAY INCLUDE, BUT MAY NOT BE LIMITED TO, IRS APPROVALS, CERTIFICATES OF CONFIDENTIALITY, HIPAA CERTIFICATIONS, AND CERTIFICATIONS FOR RESEARCH ON HUMAN SUBJECTS. RECORDS OF THESE APPROVALS, CERTIFICATIONS, AND OR TRAININGS SHALL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE C-SCSC SCC UPON REQUEST. C. WITHIN THE LIMITS OF THE SUBCONTRACTOR BUDGET AND THE AVAILABILITY OF THE DATA, ASSIST THE C-SCSC SCC IN UNDERSTANDING PREVIOUSLY UNUSED VARIABLES, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO: CORRECTING DATA ELEMENTS THAT ARE INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT, CONTAIN IMPOSSIBLE VALUES, OR ARE MISSING. IT IS UNDERSTOOD THAT THE SUBCONTRACTORS MAY NOT BE ABLE TO COLLECT NEW DATA FROM THEIR RADIOLOGY FACILITIES TO ADDRESS PROBLEMS THAT MAY EXIST IN A VARIABLE, BUT THAT THEY WILL PURSUE THE BEST AVAILABLE REMEDY. PROJECT AREA 2. PARTICIPATE IN REGULAR 1.5 HOUR MONTHLY CONFERENCE CALLS FOR STEERING COMMITTEE MEMBERS AND PROVIDE MEETING MATERIALS AS REQUESTED BY THE C-SCSC SCC FOR DOCUMENTATION OF THE DATA AT OR BEFORE THE MEETING. B. PARTICIPATE IN DECISIONS REGARDING DATA REQUESTS, PROPOSED ANALYSES, DATA ISSUES AND MEETINGS, ON THE CONFERENCE CALLS. PROJECT AREA 3. COLLABORATION WITH THE STATISTICAL COORDINATING CENTER A. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL WORK WITH THE C-8CSC SCC TO ENSURE THAT EXTERNAL INVESTIGATORS ARE AWARE OF THIS RESEARCH RESOURCE AND ITS POTENTIAL TO AID THEM IN THEIR RESEARCH. B. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL COMPLY WITH THE REQUIREMENTS FOR TRANSITION-IN AND TRANSITION-OUT OF THE C-8CSC SCC. SUBCONTRACTORS SHALL PARTICIPATE IN TRANSITION-IN REQUIREMENTS BY PARTICIPATING IN THE C-BCSC SCC'S EVALUATION OF DATA COLLECTION PROCEDURES. PROJECT AREA 4. SECURITY AND PRIVACY THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST THE C-BCSC SCC'S IN MEETING THE SYSTEM SECURITY PROCEDURES TO ENSURE DETAILED PHYSICAL AND DATA SECURITY OF THE POOLED BCSC DATABASE AND PRIVATE WEBSITE, AS WELL AS TO ENSURE CONFIDENTIALITY OF PERSONAL INFORMATION OF LIMITED DATA SETS, INCLUDING LIMITS ON CELL SIZES IN ANALYSES. A. ALL SUBCONTRACTOR EMPLOYEES WITH ACCESS TO THE BCSC DATA SHALL TAKE SECURITY TRAINING COMMENSURATE WITH THEIR RESPONSIBILITIES FOR PERFORMING WORK UNDER THE TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF THEIR CONTRACTUAL AGREEMENTS. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL ENSURE THAT EACH SUBCONTRACTOR EMPLOYEE HAS COMPLETED THE ONLINE TRAINING LABELED "ENTIRE INFORMATION SECURITY AWARENESS COURSE" WITHIN THE NIH COMPUTER SECURITY AWARENESS TRAINING MODULE LOCATED AT: HTTP://IRTSECTRAINING.NIH.GOV/ WITHIN THIRTY (30) CALENDAR DAYS OF COMMENCING WORK ON THE CONTRACT, AND THEREAFTER COMPLETING THE NIH-SPECIFIED FISCAL YEAR REFRESHER COURSE DURING EACH PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE OF THE CONTRACT. B. description: UWNMR SHALL PERFORM NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR)-BASED METHODS TO DETERMINE AT LEAST THREE (3) SOLUTION STRUCTURES FROM TARGETS APPROVED BY NIAID FOR ENTRY INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE, FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASES. THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25-30 KDA THAT FAIL TO PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL BE IDENTIFIED BY THE CENTER FOR INFECTIOUS DISEASE RESEARCH TARGET SELECTION GROUP. CANDIDATES SUITABLE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION WILL BE IDENTIFIED FROM 1H-15N HSQC SPECTRA COLLECTED ON 15N-LABELED PROTEIN PREPARED BY UW-NMR. STANDARD TRIPLE RESONANCE EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PERFORMED TO ASSIGN THE BACKBONE AND THE SIDE CHAIN RESONANCES OF THE PROTEIN. ONCE THE RESONANCE ASSIGNMENTS ARE COMPLETE, NOE DATA CRUCIAL FOR OBTAINING DISTANCE RESTRAINS WILL BE COLLECTED. NOE ASSIGNMENTS AND STRUCTURE CALCULATIONS WILL BE PERFORMED ITERATIVELY USING COMBINED AUTOMATED AND MANUAL METHODS. THE QUALITY OF THE FINAL SET OF STRUCTURES WILL BE ASSESSED AND ONCE THE FINAL ENSEMBLE OF STRUCTURES IS FOUND TO BE SATISFACTORY, THE COORDINATES OF THE ENSEMBLE AND THE MEAN STRUCTURE WILL BE DEPOSITED IN THE PROTEIN DATA BANK (PDB; HTTP://WWW.PDB.ORG) AND IMMEDIATELY RELEASED TO THE WORLD. AT THE SAME TIME, ALL 1H, 13C AND 15N CHEMICAL SHIFT DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED WITH THE BIOMAGNETIC RESEARCH BANK (BMRB; HTTP://WWW.BMRB.WISC.EDU/). MANUSCRIPTS THAT INCLUDE A DESCRIPTION OF THESE STRUCTURES WILL BE PUBLISHED IN AS TIMELY A FASHION AS IS POSSIBLE. UW NMR SHALL LEAD FUNCTIONAL STUDY (FUN_11) ENTITLED, "FUNCTIONAL CHARACTERIZATION OF PFHMGB2 AND DEVELOPMENT AS A DRUG TARGET FOR THE TREATMENT OF CEREBRAL MALARIA." THE AIM OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DISCOVER AND LATER DEVELOP A LEAD INHIBITOR COMPOUND AGAINST PFHMGB2 THAT IS EFFECTIVE IN REDUCING BRAIN SWELLING AND INCREASING THE SURVIVAL OF CHILDREN WITH CEREBRAL MALARIA.

description: UNIV OF KENTUCKY WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE HIGHLY COLLABORATIVE FUNCTIONAL STUDY (FUN_12) ENTITLED, Â€ŒTHE ROLE OF MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS IN NONRIBOSOMAL PEPTIDE SYNTHETASE (NRPS) ASSEMBLY-LINES Â€“ TOOLS FOR BIOSYNTHESIS/ BIOENGINEERING OF NOVEL ANTIBIOTICS.Â€? THE ROLE OF MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS IN NONRIBOSOMAL PEPTIDE SYNTHETASE (NRPS) ASSEMBLY-LINES Â€“ TOOLS FOR BIOSYNTHESIS/BIOENGINEERING OF NOVEL ANTIBIOTICS. MANY OF THE NATURALLY DERIVED ANTIBIOTICS IN CURRENT USE ARE COMPLEX SECONDARY METABOLITES BIOSYNTHESIZED ON NONRIBOSOMAL PEPTIDE SYNTHETASE (NRPS) Â€ŒASSEMBLY-LINESÂ€? BY BACTERIA. UNIV OF KY HAS SHOWN THAT THREE SMALL PROTEINS (MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS) IN THE NPRS SYSTEM WERE ESSENTIAL FOR THE ACTIVATION OF CONGOCIDINE, KUTZNERIDE, AND THIOCORALINE NRPS SYSTEMS, RESPECTIVELY, IN S. COELICOLOR. FURTHERMORE, UNIV KY RECENTLY FOUND THAT CO-EXPRESSION OF ONE OF THESE SMALL PROTEINS (TIOT) WITH HOMOLOGUES FROM OTHER NRPS SYSTEMS RESULTED IN A DRASTIC CHANGE IN THE BIOCHEMICAL FUNCTION OF THE COMPLEX. BY COMBINING A VARIETY OF MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS WITH DIFFERENT OTHER NRPS PARTNERS, IT MAY BE POSSIBLE TO CREATE A TOOLBOX FOR THE BIOENGINEERING OF NOVEL PHARMACEUTICALS. THE AIM OF THIS FUNCTIONAL STUDY IS TO USE MTBH-LIKE PROTEINS FROM M. TUBERCULOSIS AND PURIFIED BY THE SSGCID TO EXPAND THE NRPS TOOLBOX AND DETERMINE THE STRUCTURAL BASIS DRIVING THE FUNCTIONAL VARIABILITY. SPECIFIC AIMS OF THE PROJECT ARE AS FOLLOWS: SPECIFIC AIM 1: CONSTRUCT HETEROLOGOUS NRPS CO-EXPRESSION SYSTEMS: GENES FOR THE MTBH-LIKE PROTEINS FROM SSGCID AND CSGID RELEVANT BACTERIAL PATHOGENS WILL BE CO-EXPRESSED WITH THE S. ALBUS NRPS PROTEINS TIOK AND TION AND THE CO-EXPRESSED COMPLEXES ASSAYED FOR A WIDE RANGE OF NRPS ACTIVITIES. THIS WORK WILL BE PERFORMED IN THE GARNEAU-TSODIKOVA LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY. SPECIFIC AIM 2: DETERMINE CRYSTAL STRUCTURE OF TIOK AND TION IN COMPLEX WITH VARIOUS MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS: PURIFIED CO-EXPRESSED COMPLEXES OF PROTEINS WILL BE SHIPPED BY GARNEAU-TSODIKOVA TO SSGCID FOR PLACEMENT INTO CRYSTALLIZATION SCREENS AT BERYLLIUM. IF NECESSARY, ADDITIONAL PROTEIN EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION WILL BE DONE BY DR. BUCHKO AT PNNL. THIS WORK WILL BE PERFORMED BY BOTH THE GARNEAU-TSODIKOVA LABORATORY AND SSGCID. SPECIFIC AIM 3: DETERMINE A CRYSTAL STRUCTURE FOR A MBTH-MBTB COMPLEX AND ASSAY ACTIVITY: MBTH WILL ALSO BE CO-EXPRESSED WITH THE M. TUBERCULOSIS PROTEIN (MBTB) HOMOLOGOUS TO TION WITH THE AIM OF OBTAINING A STRUCTURE OF THE PROTEIN-PROTEIN COMPLEX. CLONING, PROTEIN PURIFICATION, AND ASSAY WORK WILL BE PERFORMED IN THE GARNEAU-TSODIKOVA LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY. CRYSTALLIZATION SCREENS AND STRUCTURE DETERMINATION WILL BE PERFORMED AT BERYLLIUM AND ANY ADDITIONAL PROTEIN EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION NEEDED WILL BE DONE BY DR. BUCHKO AT PNNL. OUTCOMES: THE ULTIMATE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT, A TOOLBOX FOR THE BIOENGINEERING OF NOVEL PHARMACEUTICALS, ALIGNS WITH NIAIDÂ€™S MISSION OF USING STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY TO ASSIST THE STRUCTURE-BASED DESIGN OF NOVEL ANTIMICROBIAL AGENTS. THE ACTIVITY ASSAYS WITH MULTIPLE MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS AND TIOK AND TION WILL EXPAND THE AVAILABLE BIOENGINEERING TOOLBOX AND THE COMPLEMENTARY CRYSTAL STRUCTURES OF THE MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS WITH TIOK AND TION WILL PROVIDE A STRUCTURAL BASIS TO EXPLAIN THE MOLECULAR REACTIONS THESE COMPLEXES PERFORM AND THE ROLE OF MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS IN INFLUENCING THE BIOCHEMISTRY. NOT ONLY WILL THE STRUCTURES OF THESE MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS WITH TIOK AND TION ASSIST THE STRUCTURE BASED DESIGN OF NOVEL BIOSYNTHESIZED ANTIBIOTICS, THE CO-EXPRESSION PROTOCOL WITH MTBH-LIKE PROTEINS MAY BE THE ONLY METHOD OF DETERMINING A STRUCTURE FOR M. TUBERCULOSIS MBTB AND SOME OF THE OTHER PROTEINS IN THE M. TUBERCULOSIS NRPS ASSEMBLY-LINE THAT ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR PRODUCING SIDEROPHORES. THE STRUCTURES OF THESE LATER COMPLEXES WILL ASSIST THE STRUCTURE-BASED DESIGN OF ANTIBIOTICS BASED ON COMPOUNDS THAT PREVENT THE FORMATION OF THESE COMPLEXES AND THE CONSEQUENTIAL IRON-STARVATION OF M. TUBERCULOSIS FOLLOWING INFECTION.

description: BERYLLIUM SHALL PREPARE SAMPLES FOR X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY STRUCTURE DETERMINATION STUDIES AND CONDUCT HIGH THROUGHPUT (HTP) CRYSTALLIZATION EXPERIMENTS, IN WHICH CRYSTALLIZATION TRIALS, OPTIMIZATION, DATA COLLECTION AND INTERPRETATION MUST BE AUTOMATED, WITH LIMITED HUMAN INTERVENTION.
