description: I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. OF THE SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS TO BE STUDIED, TWO ARE MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). THE PARASITE STUDIES WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS (UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH FLORIDA), KING (CASE WESTERN RESERVE UNIVERSITY) AND TOLIA (WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). IN ADDITION TO THE EPITOPE MAPPING TO BE PERFORMED BY DR. TOLIA, A SECOND MAJOR GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF CORRELATES RELATING B CELL EPITOPES WITH AB NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY AND AG BINDING THAT WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS AND KING. B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT. HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS AND MURINE MABS FROM IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. MALARIA NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED USING ASSAYS INTERROGATING BOTH SPOROZOITE AND MEROZOITE STAGES OF DEVELOPMENT. QUANTITATIVE ASSAYS WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE AB/AG INTERACTION STRENGTH, SPECIFICITY, AND VALENCY TO FURTHER DEVELOP CORRELATES OF PROTECTION. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION WILL BE INTERROGATED FOR OUR MOST POTENT MABS, WHERE THE STAGE OF THE INFECTION PROCESS BLOCKED BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED. ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION. II. SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.) ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT. B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. MAB GENERATION. LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. DR. ADAMS WILL COORDINATE OBTAINING EXISTING MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX ANTIGENS THROUGH COLLABORATION WITH DRS. P. DUFFY, D. KASLOW AND A. HOLDER (SEE LETTERS OF SUPPORT). MURINE PANELS OF MABS WILL BE GENERATED DR. ADAMS (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). A MINIMUM OF TEN MURINE ANTIBODIES TO TWO ANTIGENS PER YEAR WILL BE OBTAINED THROUGH COLLABORATIONS OR GENERATED. EPITOPE VALIDATION. A PRIMARY GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A FRAMEWORK RELATING B CELLS EPITOPES WITH AB BINDING AND NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY. TO ASSESS NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX, DR. ADAMS HAS DEVELOPED NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING MALARIA SPOROZOITES OR MEROZOITES. NEUTRALIZATION OF P. FALCIPARUM SPOROZOITES WILL BE EXAMINED BY DR. ADAMS IN ONE OF THREE ASSAYS. DR. ADAMS WILL PERFORM P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX BLOOD-STAGE MEROZOITE NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING ESTABLISHED ASSAYS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR NEUTRALIZATION IN SPOROZOITE OR MEROZOITE ASSAYS PER YEAR. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION. A KEY QUESTION FOR PARASITES IS AT WHAT STAGE OF INFECTION/DEVELOPMENT AB NEUTRALIZATION IS ACHIEVED. DIRECT MALARIA PARASITE ANTIGEN BINDING ASSAYS TO EXAMINE MAB BLOCKADE OF AG BINDING TO HOST-CELLS AND/OR COGNATE RECEPTORS, AND THE EFFECT OF MABS ON MEROZOITE AND SPOROZOITE DEVELOPMENT WILL BE EVALUATED BY DR. ADAMS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED IN THESE ASSAYS PER YEAR. DATA MANAGEMENT AND EPITOPE SUBMISSION. THIS CONTRACT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. A DATABASE AT WU WILL CATALOG THE DATA GENERATED IN ALL OF THE CONTRACT GROUPS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: AB POTENCY IN NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS; AB VARIABLE DOMAIN SEQUENCES; AG RECOGNIZED; EXPRESSION VECTORS CONSTRUCTED; PROGRESS OF AB AND AG PRODUCTION; AB/AG BINDING AFFINITY AND KINETICS; PROGRESS OF YEAST SURFACE DISPLAY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF MASS SPECTROMETRY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF CRYSTALLOGRAPHY EXPERIMENTS; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY CORE STRATEGIES; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY ALTERNATE STRATEGIES; AND RESULTS FROM AB MECHANISM OF PROTECTION STUDIES. DR. ADAMS WILL PROVIDE ALL DATA FOR DEPOSITION TO THE WU DATABASE. ALTERNATE EPITOPE MAPPING STRATEGIES. IN ADDITION TO THE CORE EPITOPE MAPPING STRATEGIES TO BE PERFORMED BY DRS. FREMONT, GROSS AND TOLIA, OUR COLLABORATIVE TEAM HAS EXPERTISE WITH A VARIETY OF COMPLEMENTARY METHODS THAT CAN BE USED AS NEEDED. B CELL EPITOPES MAY BE MAPPED BY PHAGE DISPLAY TECHNOLOGY, A TECHNIQUE SUCCESSFULLY APPLIED BY DR. ADAMS. C. HUMAN SUBJECTS AND/OR ANIMALS IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. I Â€“ O. OF THE PHS SOLICITATION FOR FURTHER GUIDANCE. PBMCS ARE AVAILABLE FROM A LARGE NUMBER OF VACCINE RECIPIENTS WHO HAVE RECEIVED EITHER THE INACTIVATED RVFV VACCINE OR THE LIVE ATTENUATED MP-12 STRAIN AT USAMRIID IN MARYLAND, A LIVE ATTENUATED MONOVALENT DENV-4 VACCINE (NIH AND JOHNS HOPKINS), OR INACTIVATED OR LIVE-ATTENUATED JEV (WRAIR). WITH THE HELP OF OUR COLLABORATORS, SUBJECTS WITH HIGH TITER NEUTRALIZING POLYCLONAL ABS WILL BE IDENTIFIED AND, DR. CROWE WILL OBTAIN DE-IDENTIFIED CELLS FROM VACCINEES. THE USE OF CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS FROM MONOVALENTLY IMMUNIZED INDIVIDUALS IS ESPECIALLY IMPORTANT FOR DENV-4 AND JEV, AS IN ENDEMIC REGIONS THESE VIRUSES CO-CIRCULATE WITH OTHER FLAVIVIRUSES (E.G., OTHER DENV SEROTYPES AND YELLOW FEVER VIRUS), WHICH CAN SKEW THE ANTIBODY REPERTOIRE TOWARDS MORE CROSS-REACTIVE AND LESS NEUTRALIZING ABS. MAB TECHNOLOGIES. THE CROWE LAB HAVE SEVERAL B CELL TECHNOLOGIES THAT WILL BE USED IN THIS PROJECT. ONE STRATEGY IS TO GENERATE HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS FROM CIRCULATING B CELLS USING AN ELECTROFUSION TECHNIQUE THAT HAS BEEN VALIDATED AND OPTIMIZED. ARGUABLY, THIS APPROACH IS THE HIGHEST EFFICIENCY TECHNIQUE FOR ISOLATING HUMAN CLONES WITH NATURALLY MATCHED HEAVY AND LIGHT CHAIN GENES EVER REPORTED. THE CROWE LAB HAS GENERATED THOUSANDS OF VIRUS-SPECIFIC B CELL LINES AND MABS TO INFLUENZA, DENV, RSV, MPV, HIV, WEST NILE VIRUS AND OTHERS. THE EFFICIENCY OF THIS METHOD ALLOWED FOR GENERATION OF HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS TO THE 1918 H1N1 PANDEMIC INFLUENZA VIRUS FROM ~ 100 YEAR OLD SURVIVORS, IN WHOM THE AVERAGE CIRCULATING FREQUENCY OF SPECIFIC B CELLS SPECIFIC WAS 1 IN 4 X 106 CELLS. HYBRIDOMA FORMATION. THE CROWE LAB WILL THAW CRYOPRESERVED PBMC AND ISOLATE CELLS USING A FICOLL-HYPAQUE DENSITY GRADIENT METHOD. HUMAN LYMPHOCYTES WILL BE STIMULATED AND TRANSFORMED AFTER INCUBATION WITH EBV SUBSTRAIN B95.8, THE TLR AGONIST CPG ODN 2006 (2.5 ÂΜG/ML; INVIVOGEN), 10 ÂΜM OF CHK2 INHIBITOR II (SIGMA C3742), AND 1 ÂΜG/ML CYCLOSPORIN A. CELLS ARE PLATED IN 384-WELL TISSUE CULTURE PLATES AND MONITORED FOR TRANSFORMATION. TYPICALLY, 50 TO 80 COLONIES FORM PER WELL, WITH ROBUST AB SECRETION. SCREENING FOR VIRUS-SPECIFIC AB LINES. SUPERNATANTS FROM WELLS CONTAINING EBV-TRANSFORMED LYMPHOBLASTOID CELL LINES (LCL) ARE SCREENED IN THE CROWE LABORATORY FOR VIRUS (RVFV, DENV-4, JEV) NEUTRALIZATION (ATTENUATED STRAINS ONLY) OR BINDING ACTIVITY IN ELISAS AGAINST A PANEL OF VIRAL ANTIGENS (RECOMBINANT SOLUBLE PROTEINS (GC, GN, E PROTEINS), OR INACTIVATED WHOLE VIRUS (RVFV STRAIN MP-12, DENV-4 STRAIN 1036, OR JEV STRAIN 14-14-2). CONCURRENTLY, THE CROWE LAB WILL SEND BY OVERNIGHT EXPRESS SHIPPING AN ALIQUOT OF SUPERNATANT FOR TESTING THE NEXT DAY IN A VIRUS NEUTRALIZATION ASSAY USING LIVE VIRULENT WILD-TYPE RVFV (AT VGTI IN THE ROSS LABORATORY) DENV-4 (DIAMOND LABORATORY) AND JEV (DIAMOND LABORATORY). POSITIVE WELLS IN ANY OF THE ASSAYS ARE SELECTED FOR EXPANSION AND FUSION. ELECTROFUSION. EBV-TRANSFORMED LCL SECRETE HUMAN ABS, BUT ARE QUITE UNSTABLE AND DIFFICULT TO CLONE. LCLS SECRETING VIRUS-SPECIFIC MABS ARE FUSED WITH HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS TO FORM HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS, WHICH ARE CONSIDERABLY MORE STABLE. THE SYSTEM USED IS A PROGRAMMABLE ELECTROFUSION SOURCE (CYTOPULSE PA-4000/PA-101). HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS AND EBV-TRANSFORMED HUMAN B CELLS ARE WASHED WITH RPMI-1640 AND CYTOFUSION MEDIUM. LARGE VOLUME FUSION CHAMBERS ARE COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE AND INTERFACE WELL WITH THIS UNIT. THE KEY TO THE FUSION IS BRINGING THE TWO CELL TYPES INTO CLOSE PHYSICAL CONTACT. AFTER FUSION, CELLS ARE ALLOWED TO RECOVER IN THE FUSION ELECTRODE FOR 30 MINUTES, HARVESTED, AND THEN WASHED ONCE WITH RPMI-1640 AT ROOM TEMPERATURE PRIOR TO PLATING IN SELECTION PLATES. HYBRIDOMA SELECTION AND CLONING. FUSED CELLS ARE SEEDED INTO 384-WELL PLATES IN COMPLETE MEDIUM CONTAINING HAT AND OUABAIN. AFTER FIVE DAYS OF CULTURE, CELLS ARE FED WITH FRESH MEDIUM CONTAINING HYPOXANTHINE/THYMIDINE OR HT. WE USED A SERIES OF STEMCELL TECHNOLOGIES MEDIA FOR THESE PROCEDURES, MOST IMPORTANTLY THE CLONACELLÂ®-HY MEDIUM E FOR GROWTH AND EXPANSION. AFTER INITIAL SCREENING FOR HUMAN AB PRODUCTION BY ELISA, THE HYBRIDOMA CELLS FROM POSITIVE WELLS ARE EXPANDED INTO 96- AND THEN 24-WELL PLATES AND CULTURED IN COMPLETE MEDIUM AND THEN HYBRIDOMA CELLS ARE SEEDED IN 96-WELL PLATES AT 0.3 CELL-PER-WELL DENSITY. LIMITING DILUTION IS PERFORMED TWICE TO ENSURE THAT HYBRIDOMA CLONES ARE GENERATED. ALTERNATIVELY, WE CAN SINGLE-CELL SORT THE LINES ON A FACSARIA III FLOW OR USE A CLONEPIX INSTRUMENT. CULTURE SUPERNATANTS ARE SCREENED BY ELISA FOR HUMAN IGG AND ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC ABS. THE COATING ANTIGENS INCLUDE INACTIVATED VIRUSES, LIVE ATTENUATED VIRUS PARTICLES, AND RECOMBINANT ENVELOPE GLYCOPROTEINS. MAB PREPARATIONS. HYBRIDOMA CELL LINES WILL BE ADAPTED TO SERUM-FREE MEDIUM. SUPERNATANTS OF HIGH-DENSITY CULTURES WILL BE PRODUCED IN CELLINE DEVICES (BD BIOSCIENCES). PURIFIED AND CONCENTRATED PREPARATIONS OF EACH MAB WILL BE PREPARED BY FPLC USING PROTEIN G RESIN ON AN AKTA INSTRUMENT FOLLOWED BY BUFFER EXCHANGE USING ULTRA CENTRIFUGAL FILTER DEVICES. FOR LARGER SCALE PREPARATIONS (E.G., 50 TO 100 MG LOTS), WE WILL SCALE THE CELL CULTURE UP TO 25 L USING A WAVE BIOREACTOR. VOLUME WILL BE INITIALLY REDUCED USING A GE QUIXSTAND LABORATORY-SCALE SEPARATION SYSTEM THAT USES CROSS-FLOW FILTRATION CARTRIDGES. THIS PROCEDURE IS FOLLOWED BY FPLC PURIFICATION. WE WILL USE QUANTITATIVE ELISAS TO DEFINE THE FINAL CONCENTRATION OF MABS. C. HUMAN SUBJECTS AND/OR ANIMALS IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. description: I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. OF THE SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS TO BE STUDIED, TWO ARE MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). THE PARASITE STUDIES WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS (UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH FLORIDA), KING (CASE WESTERN RESERVE UNIVERSITY) AND TOLIA (WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). IN ADDITION TO THE EPITOPE MAPPING TO BE PERFORMED BY DR. TOLIA, A SECOND MAJOR GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF CORRELATES RELATING B CELL EPITOPES WITH AB NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY AND AG BINDING THAT WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS AND KING. B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT. HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS AND MURINE MABS FROM IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. MALARIA NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED USING ASSAYS INTERROGATING BOTH SPOROZOITE AND MEROZOITE STAGES OF DEVELOPMENT. QUANTITATIVE ASSAYS WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE AB/AG INTERACTION STRENGTH, SPECIFICITY, AND VALENCY TO FURTHER DEVELOP CORRELATES OF PROTECTION. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION WILL BE INTERROGATED FOR OUR MOST POTENT MABS, WHERE THE STAGE OF THE INFECTION PROCESS BLOCKED BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED. ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION. II. SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.) ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT.   B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. MAB GENERATION. LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. DR. KING WILL GENERATE HUMAN ANTI-MALARIA MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES TO TWO ANTIGENS PER YEAR WILL BE GENERATED. EPITOPE VALIDATION. A PRIMARY GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A FRAMEWORK RELATING B CELLS EPITOPES WITH AB BINDING AND NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY. TO ASSESS NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX, DR. KING HAS DEVELOPED NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING MALARIA MEROZOITES. DR. ADAMS WILL PERFORM P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX BLOOD-STAGE MEROZOITE NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING ESTABLISHED ASSAYS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR NEUTRALIZATION IN PER YEAR. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION. A KEY QUESTION FOR PARASITES IS AT WHAT STAGE OF INFECTION/DEVELOPMENT AB NEUTRALIZATION IS ACHIEVED. DIRECT MALARIA PARASITE ANTIGEN BINDING ASSAYS TO EXAMINE MAB BLOCKADE OF AG BINDING TO HOST-CELLS AND/OR COGNATE RECEPTORS, AND THE EFFECT OF MABS ON MEROZOITE DEVELOPMENT WILL BE CARRIED OUT BY DR. KING. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED IN THESE ASSAYS PER YEAR. DATA MANAGEMENT AND EPITOPE SUBMISSION. THIS CONTRACT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. A DATABASE AT WU WILL CATALOG THE DATA GENERATED IN ALL OF THE CONTRACT GROUPS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: AB POTENCY IN NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS; AB VARIABLE DOMAIN SEQUENCES; AG RECOGNIZED; EXPRESSION VECTORS CONSTRUCTED; PROGRESS OF AB AND AG PRODUCTION; AB/AG BINDING AFFINITY AND KINETICS; PROGRESS OF YEAST SURFACE DISPLAY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF MASS SPECTROMETRY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF CRYSTALLOGRAPHY EXPERIMENTS; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY CORE STRATEGIES; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY ALTERNATE STRATEGIES; AND RESULTS FROM AB MECHANISM OF PROTECTION STUDIES. DR. KING WILL PROVIDE ALL DATA FOR DEPOSITION TO THE WU DATABASE. C. HUMAN SUBJECTS AND/OR ANIMALS IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. I Â€“ O. description: BREAST CANCER SURVEILLANCE CONSORTIUM DATA RESOURCE INDEPENDENTLY AND NOT AS AN AGENT OF THE BREAST CANCER SURVEILLANCE CONSORTIUM (BCSC) DATA RESOURCE STATISTICAL COORDINATING CENTER (BCSC-SCC), THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL BE REQUIRED TO FURNISH ALL THE NECESSARY SERVICES, QUALIFIED PERSONNEL, MATERIAL, EQUIPMENT, AND FACILITIES , NOT OTHERWISE PROVIDED BY THE BCSC-SCC, AS NEEDED TO PERFORM THE STATEMENT OF WORK. SCOPE: THE MAJOR OBJECTIVE OF THIS SUBCONTRACT IS TO ASSIST IN THE SHARING OF EXISTING DATA STORED WITHIN THE CURRENT BCSC POOLED DATABASE AND IMPROVE ITS CAPACITY TO SUPPORT USE OF THIS POOLED DATA BY THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL DO THIS BY PROVIDING APPROVAL FOR DATA SHARING, AND BY RESPONDING TO QUERIES FROM THE BCSC-SCC DATA RESOURCE TO HELP THEM CLEAN THE POOLED DATA. IF THE SUBCONTRACTOR IS COVERED UNDER HIPAA, IT WILL MAINTAIN DATA USE AGREEMENTS (DUAS) TO ENSURE VALID DATA INTERPRETATION WITH THE BCSC-SCC. THE DUAS ARE REQUIRED IN THE EVENT THAT THE SUBCONTRACTOR NEEDS TO ACCESS ITS SITE-SPECIFIC DATA IN ORDER TO SEND A CORRECTED DATASET BACK TO THE BCSC-SCC DATA RESOURCE IN ORDER TO IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF THE POOLED DATABASE. THERE ARE THREE DATA SOURCES FOR THIS CONTRACT: 1} THE POOLED DATA; 2) THE SITE-SPECIFIC DATA; 3) THE CORRECTED SITE-SPECIFIC DATA. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL NEVER HAVE ACCESS TO THE DATABASE CONTAINING THE POOLED DATA. THIS CONTRACT DOES NOT COVER THE SITE-SPECIFIC DATA, BUT DOES COVER CORRECTIONS (I.E., CORRECTED DATASETS) OF SITE-SPECIFIC DATA, WHICH WILL BE SENT BACK TO THE BCSC-SCC, AND THE BCSC-SCC STAFF WILL REPLACE THE ERRONEOUS DATA ELEMENTS WITH THE CORRECT DATA. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS: PROJECT AREA 1. PARTICIPATION IN MAINTAINING DATA QUALITY OF THE BCSC POOLED DATABASE THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL PARTICIPATE IN IMPROVING THE DATA QUALITY OF THE BCSC- POOLED DATABASE THROUGH THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES: A. ACCESSING SITE-SPECIFIC DATA TO SUPPLY CORRECTIONS TO THE BCSC-SCC POOLED DATASET, AS NEEDED. THIS CONTRACT DOES NOT COVER COLLECTION OF ADDITIONAL SITE-SPECIFIC DATA, BUT DOES COVER SUBMISSION OF CORRECTED SITE-SPECIFIC DATA TO THE BCSC-SCC. THE SUBCONTRACTOR ONLY WILL ACCESS SITE-SPECIFIC DATA THAT IS ALREADY IN THEIR POSSESSION. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL NEVER ACCESS THE DATABASE CONTAINING THE POOLED DATA. B. ENSURE THAT PROPER ADMINISTRATIVE AUTHORIZATIONS AND CERTIFICATIONS ARE IN PLACE WHICH MAY INCLUDE, BUT MAY NOT BE LIMITED TO, IRB APPROVALS, HIPAA CERTIFICAT IONS, AND CERTIFICATIONS FOR RESEARCH ON HUMAN SUBJECTS. RECORDS OF THESE APPROVALS, CERTIFICATIONS, AND OR TRAININGS SHALL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE BCSC-SCC UPON REQUEST. SUBCONTRACTORS WILL COOPERATE WITH THE CONTRACTOR IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF CERTIFICATES OF CONFIDENTIALITY , WITHIN THE LIMITS OF THE SUBCONTRACTOR BUDGET AND THE AVAILABILITY OF THE SITE-SPECIFIC DATA ASSIST THE BCSC-SCC IN UNDERSTANDING PREVIOUSLY UNUSED VARIABLES, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO: CORRECTING DATA ELEMENTS THAT ARE INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT, CONTAIN IMPOSSIBLE VALUES, OR ARE MISSING. IT IS UNDERSTOOD THAT THE SUBCONTRACTORS MAY NOT BE ABLE TO PROVIDE CORRECTIONS FOR APPARENTLY ERRONEOUS DATA, BUT THAT THEY WILL, TO THE BEST OF THEIR ABILITY, ATTEMPT TO DETERMINE NECESSARY MODIFICATIONS. PROJECT AREA 2. BCSC STEERING COMMITTEE THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT THE WORK WITH THE BCSC STEERING COMMITTEE COMPOSED OF BCSC INVESTIGATORS THE BCSC-SCC, AND THE NCI COTR IN THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES: A. description: "NOVA PROPOSED KEY PERSONNEL SUPPORT PROJECT MANAGER/CORPORATE MONITOR: DANA M. YOUNG, JD. MS. YOUNG WILL OVERSEE AND MANAGE CONTRACTING MATTERS, PARTICIPATE IN COMMUNICATIONS WITH NCI DCCPS, ASSIST DR. MILLIKEN AS NEEDED IN PRIORITIZING AND PROVIDING CORPORATE RESOURCES, ATTEND CANCER CENTER MEETING IN HOUSTON, TX IN NOVEMBER TO ASSIST IN DOCUMENTING DISCUSSIONS AND NETWORKING WITH KEY CANCER CENTER REPRESENTATIVES, AND PROVIDE INPUT ON AND PERFORM QC REVIEW OF DRAFT AND FINAL REPORTS. SENIOR SCIENCE WRITER: ERIN MILLIKEN, PHD. DR. MILLIKEN WILL BE THE LEAD WRITER PREPARING THE SYNTHESIS REPORT. SHE WILL COMMUNICATE WITH NCI DCCPS AS NEEDED, REVIEW CANCER CENTER SUPPLEMENT FINAL REPORTS, ATTEND CANCER CENTER MEETING IN HOUSTON, TX IN NOVEMBER, IDENTIFY KEY QUESTIONS/ISSUES REQUIRING FOLLOW-UP, CONDUCT NECESSARY FOLLOW-UP DISCUSSIONS WITH CANCER CENTER REPRESENTATIVES AND/OR GATHER ADDITIONAL INFORMATION, PREPARE SYNTHESIS REPORT OUTLINE, PREPARE DRAFT AND FINAL SYNTHESIS REPORTS FOR DELIVERY TO NCI DCCPS. NOVA TECHNICAL SUPPORT COMMUNICATE WITH NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD AS NEEDED THROUGHOUT THE PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE. PREPARE A WORK PLAN/TIMELINE FOR TASK PERFORMANCE, TO BE APPROVED BY NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD. SUBMIT MONTHLY REPORTS ON PROGRESS TO NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD. UPON RECEIPT, REVIEW EACH OF THE 18 CANCER CENTERS SUPPLEMENT FINAL REPORTS (APPROXIMATELY 20 PP EACH) AND IDENTIFY COMMON THEMES, ISSUES, AND OTHER VARIABLES OF INTEREST. IDENTIFY ANY QUESTIONS AND/OR GAPS IN INFORMATION REQUIRING FOLLOWUP. ATTEND MEETING ON NOVEMBER 5-6, 2015 IN HOUSTON, TEXAS WHERE THE 18 CANCER CENTERS AWARDED SUPPLEMENTS WILL REPORT OUT ON FINDINGS. TAKE NOTES AT THE MEETING FOR PURPOSES OF ASSISTING IN PREPARATION OF THE SYNTHESIS REPORT. IDENTIFY ANY ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS OR INFORMATION REQUIRED TO PREPARE A SUBSTANTIVE SYNTHESIS OF THE CANCER CENTER SUPPLEMENTS AND APPROPRIATE PERSONS TO FOLLOW UP WITH AT CANCER CENTERS. OBTAIN APPROVAL FROM NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD TO INITIATE CONTACT WITH APPROPRIATE PERSONS AT CANCER CENTERS. DOCUMENT DISCUSSIONS. USING INFORMATION GATHERED FROM REVIEW OF SUPPLEMENT FINAL REPORTS, ATTENDANCE AT HOUSTON MEETING, AND DISCUSSIONS WITH CANCER CENTER REPRESENTATIVES, PREPARE AN OUTLINE OF REPORT FOR APPROVAL BY NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD. FOLLOWING APPROVAL OF SYNTHESIS REPORT OUTLINE BEGIN WRITING OF DRAFT REPORT. DELIVER DRAFT REPORT TO NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD ON OR ABOUT JANUARY 15, 2016. A NOVA EDITOR/PROOFREADER WILL EDIT THE DRAFT REPORT FOR CORRECT GRAMMAR, SPELLING, PUNCTUATION, AND TONE, AND ENSURE THAT THE DOCUMENT IS PRESENTED IN THE FORMAT AND LEVEL OF DETAIL CONSISTENT WITH AGREED-UPON REQUIREMENTS. NOVA WILL REVISE THE REPORT AS DEEMED NECESSARY BY NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD. WITHIN THE AGREED-UPON SCHEDULE, NOVA WILL DELIVER A FINAL SYNTHESIS REPORT AND ASSOCIATED SLIDE DECK TO THE NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD FOR FINAL REVIEW AND APPROVAL. "

description: TEAM IS POSITIONED TO EXECUTE AN AMBITIOUS PROJECT THAT WILL FUNDAMENTALLY ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF NONHUMAN PRIMATE (NHP) MAJOR HISTOCOMPATIBILITY COMPLEX (MHC) GENETICS AND IMPROVE THE UTILITY OF THESE IMPORTANT ANIMAL MODELS FOR BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH (FIGURE SOW.1). THE TEAM MEMBERS ARE UNIQUELY QUALIFIED FOR THIS PROJECT; TOGETHER WE HAVE ALREADY DEVELOPED THE LEADING NHP MHC ALLELE DISCOVERY, GENOTYPING, NOMENCLATURE, AND ANNOTATION RESOURCES FOR THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. IN THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL DEFINE MHC CLASS I AND MHC CLASS II -DRB CDNA SEQUENCES FROM 715 ANIMALS: CYNOMOLGUS MACAQUES OF Ã¢Â‚¬ËŒCHINESEÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ (120)- AND VIETNAMESE (120)-ORIGINS; PIG-TAILED MACAQUES (120); AND CHINESE (120)- AND INDIAN (120)-ORIGIN RHESUS MACAQUES, PLUS 115 ANIMALS OF NIAIDÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S CHOOSING. THE ADVENT OF ROCHE/454 DNA PYROSEQUENCING ENABLES NOVEL MHC CLASS I AND CLASS II -DRB ALLELES TO BE DETERMINED AT THE SAME TIME AS ANIMALS ARE GENOTYPED FOR PREVIOUSLY DESCRIBED ALLELES, ESSENTIALLY UNIFYING THESE TWO PREVIOUSLY DISPARATE GOALS INTO A SINGLE HIGH-RESOLUTION AND COST-EFFECTIVE ASSAY. THIS STATE-OF-THE-ART ASSAY IS AVAILABLE TODAY AND WILL BE IMPROVED DURING THE CONTRACT. MHC CLASS II -DPA, -DPB, -DQA, -DQB, AND -DRA ALLELES WILL BE SANGER SEQUENCED FROM 415 OF THE 715 MACAQUES. CDNA LIBRARIES FROM 15 OF THE 715 ANIMALS WILL BE CONSTRUCTED FROM HIGH-PRIORITY ANIMALS TO FACILITATE IDENTIFICATION OF NON-CODING REGIONS OF MHC GENES AND TO PROVIDE A RESOURCE FOR OTHERS INTERESTED IN CHARACTERIZING GENES WITHIN THE EXTENDED MHC. ALLELES WILL BE CHARACTERIZED USING CRITERIA ESTABLISHED FOR HLA NOMENCLATURE, WHICH WILL RESULT IN CHARACTERIZATION OF BOTH FULL-LENGTH AND PARTIAL TRANSCRIPTS USING TECHNOLOGY AVAILABLE TODAY. WE STRONGLY BELIEVE, HOWEVER, THAT FULL-LENGTH TRANSCRIPT ALLELE DISCOVERY IS PREFERABLE AND ATTAINABLE AND WILL AGGRESSIVELY DEVELOP TECHNOLOGIES THAT WILL ENABLE HIGH-THROUGHPUT, FULL-LENGTH TRANSCRIPT SEQUENCING DURING THE CONTRACT PROPOSAL. 300 MHC CLASS I AND 300 MHC CLASS II PLASMID CLONES WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. ALL 715 MACAQUES WILL BE EXAMINED WITH DNA MICROSATELLITE MARKERS TO DEFINE HAPLOTYPES, WHILE AT LEAST 20 NEW MHC MICROSATELLITE MARKERS WILL BE DEFINED. SUCH MARKERS WILL ENABLE ANY MOLECULAR BIOLOGY LABORATORY TO MHC HAPLOTYPE NHPS WITHOUT REQUIRING THE SOPHISTICATED SEQUENCING AND INFORMATICS SKILLS NECESSARY FOR HIGH-THROUGHPUT DNA SEQUENCING. IN ADDITION, IMMORTALIZED B CELL LINES FROM 250 OF THE 715 ANIMALS WILL BE PRODUCED AND MADE AVAILABLE TO THE COMMUNITY TO SERVE AS CONTROLS FOR LABORATORIES INTERESTED IN DEVELOPING GENOTYPING AND HAPLOTYPING EXPERTISE. THE COMMUNITY WILL ALSO BENEFIT FROM THE PRODUCTION OF 50 STABLE TRANSFERENT CELL LINES EXPRESSING INDIVIDUAL MHC CLASS I OR COMBINATIONS OF MHC CLASS II A AND B ALLELES, AS WELL AS 15 MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES SPECIFIC FOR INDIVIDUAL MHC ALLELES. ALLELE DISCOVERY, MHC GENOTYPING, AND MHC HAPLOTYPING PROTOCOLS, ALONG WITH QUALITY CONTROL PRECAUTIONS, AND BIOLOGICAL REAGENTS WILL BE PUBLISHED TO AN MHC CONTRACT WEB PORTAL BUILT ON THE LABKEY SERVER PLATFORM AND HOSTED BY THE PI. description: TASK 1: RECEIVE AND REVIEW MATERIALS ABOUT THE NPSD - TRUVEN HEALTH WILL HAVE NO HOURS ALLOCATED TO THIS TASK. TASK 2: ANALYZE NON-IDENTIFIABLE PSO DATA - FOR THIS TASK, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL PREPARE TO RECEIVE EVENT-LEVEL DATA AND CONSULT WITH THE PPC ON VARIABILITY ANALYSIS FOR NON-IDENTIFIABLE EVENTS. IN COLLABORATION WITH STANFORD UNIVERSITY, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL REVIEW, REVISE OR DEVELOP NEW TABLE LAYOUTS FOR AGGREGATED DATA, AND DESIGN ANALYTIC PLANS FOR EVENT LEVEL ANALYSES (ESTIMATED 500 TABLES). TRUVEN HEALTH WILL REVIEW DISSEMINATION STRATEGY, DRAFT RECOMMENDATIONS FOR CHANGES TO THE AHRQ COMMON FORMATS BASED ON ANALYSES. TRUVEN HEALTH WILL PARTICIPATE IN ONE HOUR INTERNAL WEEKLY CALLS AND ADDITIONAL CALLS AS REQUIRED. TASK 3: ANALYZE DATA ON TRENDS IN PATIENT SAFETY EVENTS AND PATTERNS OF HEALTH CARE ERROR - FOR THIS TASK, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL DESIGN ANALYTIC PLAN FOR TASK 3, DEVELOP 160 PROVIDER TABLES, DEVELOP GRAPHICS FOR TABLES, AND CREATE BULLET TEXT FOR 160 TABLES. TRUVEN HEALTH WILL DEVELOP TRENDS FROM EXISTING EXTERNAL PATIENT SAFETY DATA, SUCH AS THE HCUP DATABASES, OASIS, MDS, NSQUIP, OR QSRS. FOR THESE SOURCES, THEY WILL DEVELOP APPROXIMATELY 70 TABLES, WITH BULLETS. TRUVEN HEALTH WILL DEVELOP MULTIVARIATE TRENDS ANALYSES AND CREATE BULLETED TEXT FOR TABLES. TRUVEN HEALTH WILL REVIEW TABLES, GRAPHICS AND BULLETS CREATED BY OTHER SUBCONTRACTOR(S). TASK 4: REPORT ON PATIENT SAFETY EVENTS IN THE NATIONAL HEALTHCARE QUALITY AND DISPARITIES REPORTS - FOR THIS TASK TRUVEN HEALTH WILL LEAD WORK EFFORTS, AS STATED ABOVE, INCLUDING ANALYSES, PRESENTING FINDINGS TO THE INTERAGENCY WORK GROUP AS REQUESTED, AND CONDUCT FURTHER DISSEMINATION AS AGREED UPON WITH STANFORD AND AHRQ. TASK 5: MONITOR EFFECTIVE STRATEGIES FOR REDUCING MEDICAL ERRORS AND INCREASING PATIENT SAFETY - FOR THIS TASK, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL CONSULT ON THE WORK PLAN AND REVIEW WORK MATERIALS. TASK 6: DISSEMINATE FINDINGS FROM ANALYSES - FOR THIS TASK TRUVEN HEALTH WILL CREATE THE DISSEMINATION PLAN. TRUVEN HEALTH WILL PROVIDE TWO INDIVIDUALS TO ATTEND THE PSO ANNUAL MEETING, AND CREATE 2 EDUCATIONAL BRIEFS. TASK 7: ADMINISTER TASK ORDER - THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DELIVER A MONTHLY PROGRESS REPORT TO THE STANFORD. OPTIONAL TASK 8: ASSESS FEASIBILITY OF THE CREATION OF AN INTERACTIVE EVIDENCE-BASED MANAGEMENT RESOURCE FOR NETWORK OF PATIENT SAFETY DATABASES - FOR THIS TASK, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL LEAD ALL WORK DESCRIBED ABOVE AND CREATE THE FINAL FEASIBILITY REPORT. OPTIONAL TASK 9: ANALYZE NON-IDENTIFIABLE PSO DATA Â€“ PRODUCE ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLET RESULTS - OPTIONAL TASK 9A: ANALYZE NON-IDENTIFIABLE PSO DATA Â€“ PRODUCE 500 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLET RESULTS. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 6 MONTHS. THIS OPTIONAL TASK WILL BE AWARDED ON A TIME AND MATERIALS BASIS TO PRODUCE 500 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLETED RESULTS. OPTIONAL TASK 9B: ANALYZE NON-IDENTIFIABLE PSO DATA Â€“ PRODUCE 750 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLET RESULTS. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 6 MONTHS. THIS OPTIONAL TASK WILL BE AWARDED ON A TIME AND MATERIALS BASIS TO PRODUCE 750 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLETED RESULTS. OPTIONAL TASK 9C: ANALYZE NON-IDENTIFIABLE PSO DATA Â€“ PRODUCE 1000 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLET RESULTS PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 6 MONTHS. THIS OPTIONAL TASK WILL BE AWARDED ON A TIME AND MATERIALS BASIS TO PRODUCE 1000 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLETED RESULTS. FOR EACH OF THE OPTION 9A-9C, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL CREATE 50% OF THE TABLES AND ASSOCIATED DOCUMENTATION.

description: THE PURPOSE OF THIS SUBAWARD IS TO STUDY HOW THE BASELINE STATE AND FUNCTION OF ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES CAN BE ALTERED BY VACCINATION AND DISEASE STATE, IN THE CONTEXT OF MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL INVESTIGATE THE MECHANISMS THAT DRIVE INNATE CELL REPROGRAMMING BY VACCINATION AND BACTERIAL EXPOSURE AS WELL AS THE IMPACT ON THE HOST IMMUNE RESPONSE AND BACTERIAL CONTROL. THE SUBAWARD WILL PERFORM EPIGENETIC ANALYSIS OF HUMAN AND MOUSE ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES AND COLLABORATE WITH OTHER LABORATORIES IN THE CONSORTIUM TO LINK MACROPHAGE EPIGENETIC STATES TO TRANSCRIPTIONAL RESPONSES. 1) PERFORM ATAC-SEQ EPIGENETIC PROFILING AND ANALYSIS ON ADDITIONAL FROZEN HUMAN ADHERENT BAL SAMPLES FROM ACTIVE TB, RESISTER, HEALTHY CONTROLS, AND ASYMPTOMATIC TB INDIVIDUALS. PROFILING INCLUDES: CELL PREPARATION, TRANSPOSITION REACTION AND PURIFICATION, PCR AMPLIFICATION, LIBRARY PURIFICATION, AND LIBRARY QC. ANALYSIS INCLUDES: SEQUENCING FILTERING AND ALIGNMENT, DIFFERENTIAL EXPRESSION ANALYSIS, PATHWAY ANALYSIS, AND MOTIF ENRICHMENT ANALYSIS. 2) ANALYZE LINKAGE BETWEEN HUMAN ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGE EPIGENETIC PROFILES AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL RESPONSES (IN COLLABORATION WITH WALZL/DU PLESSIS LABS). 3) COMPARE HUMAN ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGE EPIGENETIC PROFILES TO EPIGENETIC PROFILES OF MURINE ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES TRAINED BY TYPE I OR TYPE II INTERFERONS. 4) TRANSCRIPTIONAL ANALYSIS OF SINGLE-CELL RNA-SEQUENCING DATA FROM HUMAN MACROPHAGES PROFILED FROM NONADHERENT BAL SAMPLES (IN COLLABORATION WITH WALZL/DU PLESSIS/LEWINSOHN LABS). 5) COMPLETE STUDIES COMPARING INNATE RESPONSES AND PRODUCTION OF IFN-BETA FOR WT, SP140-/-, IFNAR-/-, AND SP140-/-IFNAR-/- MEXAMS AND BMDMS FOLLOWING STIMULATION WITH LPS OR INFECTION WITH MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS TO CHARACTERIZE MACROPHAGE SUBSET-SPECIFIC REGULATION OF TYPE I IFN AND CYTOKINE RESPONSES.

description: STATEMENT OF WORK – YEAR 7 (BASE) – BAROUCH LAB DURING THE PRECEDING YEARS OF THE AWARD, WE FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING AN INNOVATIVE AND PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT MOUSE CHALLENGE MODEL THAT UNDERGOES REPEATED ULTRA-LOW DOSE MTB EXPOSURES TO ASSESS THE PROTECTIVE EFFICACY OF TB VACCINES. IN YEAR 6, WE SUCCESSFULLY ESTABLISHED AND VALIDATED A HIGHLY REPRODUCIBLE MURINE REPEATED ULTRA-LOW DOSE CHALLENGE MODEL WITH REDUCED STRINGENCY. USING THIS MODEL, WE TESTED THE PROTECTIVE EFFICACY OF BCGS AND ΔLPRG VACCINES. UNDER THE REPEATED ULTRA-LOW DOSE EXPOSURE MODEL, ΔLPRG IMMUNIZATION CONFERRED ~65% PROTECTION AGAINST ACQUISITION OF INFECTION, COMPARED WITH ~45% PROTECTION OBSERVED WITH THE SINGLE ULTRA-LOW DOSE CHALLENGE, REPRESENTING A SIGNIFICANT IMPROVEMENT IN VACCINE-INDUCED PROTECTION. WE ALSO EXPANDED OUR CORRELATES OF PROTECTION ANALYSES TO IDENTIFY CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH PROTECTION FROM THE ACQUISITION OF INFECTION. A MANUSCRIPT DESCRIBING THESE FINDINGS IS CURRENTLY IN PREPARATION. IN YEAR 7, BASED ON THE DATA COLLECTED DURING THE PRECEDING YEAR, OUR RESEARCH WILL FOCUS ON EXTENDING CORRELATES OF PROTECTION STUDIES AND CONDUCTING MECHANISTIC ANALYSES TO DEFINE THE CELLULAR SUBSETS AND PATHWAYS UNDERLYING VACCINE-MEDIATED PROTECTION. WE WILL FURTHER CHARACTERIZE INFECTION KINETICS AND IMMUNE RESPONSES TO REPEATED ULTRA-LOW DOSE MTB EXPOSURE MODEL TO BETTER UNDERSTAND HOW LOW-LEVEL MTB EXPOSURE SHAPES HOST IMMUNITY AND SUBSEQUENT INFECTION OUTCOMES. TO PERFORM THESE STUDIES, WE WILL UTILIZE A BARCODED MTB STRAIN TO MONITOR INFECTION DYNAMICS UNDER REPEATED ULTRA-LOW DOSE AEROSOL CHALLENGES. FINALLY, WE WILL ALSO APPLY THIS PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT CHALLENGE MODEL TO EVALUATE THE PROTECTIVE EFFICACY OF EMERGING TB VACCINES, INCLUDING SUBUNIT MRNA, PROTEIN-BASED, AND LIVE-ATTENUATED VACCINES.

description: STATEMENT OF WORK – YEAR 7 (BASE) – HAWN THE HAWN LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) WILL HAVE SEVERAL ROLES IN THIS SUBCONTRACT IN YEAR 7. EACH ACTIVITY FROM YEARS 1-6 IS ONGOING. 1) UW WILL OVERSEE GENOTYPING AND ANALYSIS OF CANDIDATE GENE POLYMORPHISMS IN HEALTHY CONTROLS IN SEATTLE. GENOTYPING IS COMPLETED EXCEPT FOR NEW ENROLLEES. ANALYSIS IS ONGOING WITH NEW CANDIDATE GENES THAT HAVE RECENTLY BEEN SELECTED FOR WORK IN YEAR 6. POLYMORPHISMS WILL BE ANALYZED FOR THEIR ASSOCIATION WITH MTB-INFECTED MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES. CANDIDATE GENES WILL BE SELECTED BASED ON STUDIES FROM DRS. URDAHL, PICKER, LEWINSOHN, AND WALZL. 2) UW WILL ORGANIZE AND FACILITATE THE ISOLATION OF PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONOCYTES AND MONOCYTE-DERIVED MACROPHAGES FOR EX VIVO MTB INFECTION FROM HEALTHY CONTROLS IN SEATTLE. MONOCYTES WILL BE ISOLATED FROM CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS, WHICH ARE AVAILABLE FROM AN ESTABLISHED SEATTLE COHORT OF HEALTHY SUBJECTS. ANALYSES ARE UNDERWAY TO EXAMINE THE ASSOCIATION OF GENETIC VARIANTS IN CANDIDATE GENES WITH MTB-INDUCED MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES IN A COHORT OF 100 HEALTHY DONORS. 3) CELLULAR GWAS: UW WILL PERFORM CELLULAR GWAS EXPERIMENTS TO DISCOVER GENETIC REGULATORS OF MTB-INDUCED MYELOID CELL PHENOTYPES. LEAD FINDINGS WILL BE ASSESSED FOR ASSOCIATION WITH CLINICAL PHENOTYPES WITH AN OVERALL GOAL TO DISCOVER MAJOR GENETIC DETERMINANTS OF TB CLINICAL PHENOTYPES. 4) UW WILL OVERSEE THE MACROPHAGE EXPERIMENTS INCLUDING CRISPR/CAS9 GENE SILENCING IN THP1 AND U937 CELLS AND STUDIES OF PRIMARY MONOCYTES FROM SEATTLE AND CAPE TOWN. STUDIES WILL INCLUDE INFECTION OF MACROPHAGES WITH MTB AND ANALYSIS OF IMMUNE PATHWAYS AND CONTROL OF MTB REPLICATION. CELL SUPERNATANTS WILL BE HARVESTED FOR CYTOKINE/CHEMOKINE ELISA AND RNA EXTRACTED FROM CELLS, QUANTIFIED, AND ANALYZED. 5) UW WILL COLLABORATE WITH INVESTIGATORS ON THE ANALYSIS OF WHETHER POLYMORPHISMS IN CANDIDATE GENES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES AND PREPARE IT FOR PUBLICATION WITH OTHER INVESTIGATORS.

description: STATEMENT OF WORK – YEAR 7 (BASE) THE DU PLESSIS/WALZL LABORATORY AT STELLENBOSCH UNIVERSITY (SU) WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE CLINICAL AND IMMUNOLOGICAL WORK (INCLUDING ON-SITE DATA MANAGEMENT) OF THE PROJECT. SU WILL COORDINATE THE STUDY DESIGN, PARTICIPANT SCREENING AND ENROLLMENT FOR THE CASCADE HOUSEHOLD CONTACT STUDY, PERFORM BRONCHOSCOPIES AND MANAGE SAMPLE SHARING TO PARTICIPATING SITES. SU WILL PROVIDE INPUT IN THE DESIGN, EXECUTION AND DATA ANALYSIS OF IMMUNOLOGICAL STUDIES AND PARTICIPATE IN THE LEADERSHIP TEAM OF “CASCADE IMPAC-TB” CENTER. SU WILL INTERACT AND COORDINATE ALL PROJECT ACTIVITIES WITH THE PI OF THE PROJECT. DR. DU PLESSIS AND DR. WALZL, THE SU CO-PI’S WILL REVIEW ALL RAW DATA GENERATED BY THE SU TEAM, AND SUPERVISE THE LABORATORY WORK, AND THE RESEARCH TECHNICIANS. SPECIFIC DELIVERABLES FOR YEAR 7 OF THE CONTRACT AT SU INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING: A. RECRUITMENT: SU WILL CONDUCT PET/CT, BRONCHOSCOPY AND PHLEBOTOMY IN ALL COHORTS TO COVER THE FULL SPECTRUM OF INFECTION AND OBTAIN BAL AND PBMC SAMPLES FROM EACH. RECRUITMENT HAS BEEN COMPLETED, AND NO NEW PARTICIPANTS ARE BEING ENROLLED. HOWEVER, WE ARE FOLLOWING UP SELECTED PARTICIPANTS TO SCREEN FOR TB PROGRESSION WITH LONGITUDINAL SAMPLING, REQUIRING ETHICS APPROVAL AND LIMITED CONTINUED CLINICAL INVOLVEMENT. B. END-ASSAYS: IMMUNOPHENOTYPING EXPERIMENTS – ONE OF THE DELIVERABLES AT SU IS TO CONDUCT DEEP PHENOTYPING OF PAIRED BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE (BAL) AND PBMC FROM THE VARIOUS CASCADE HOUSEHOLD CONTACT STUDY CLINICAL GROUPS. SU HAS EVALUATED THE ASSAY PRIORITY LIST, AS WELL AS THE BAL AND PBMC SAMPLES COLLECTED FROM PARTICIPANTS ENROLLED IN THE CASCADE HOUSEHOLD CONTACT STUDY, TO ENUMERATE THE NUMBER OF STORED SAMPLES AVAILABLE FOR THE OBJECTIVES RELATED TO THE PROPOSED PLANS FOR THIS END-ASSAY. OF ALL MAIN STUDY PARTICIPANTS FROM WHICH PAIRED BAL AND PBMC HAVE BEEN COLLECTED, SUFFICIENT CELL NUMBERS WERE OBTAINED FROM 88% OF PARTICIPANTS, WHICH INCLUDES MAKING USE OF RESIDUALLY STORED BAL CELLS. WE WILL PERFORM MULTIPARAMETER FLOW CYTOMETRY ANALYSES ON UNFRACTIONATED BAL CELLS AND PBMC SAMPLES FROM A SUBSET OF INDIVIDUALS FROM THE CASCADE CLINICAL GROUPS ALL COHORTS TO DEFINE THE PHENOTYPE OF LUNG RESIDENT AND CIRCULATING LYMPHOCYTE POPULATIONS. IMMUNE PHENOTYPING OF THESE SU HHC PBMC SAMPLES FOR THE LYMPHOID FLOW CYTOMETRY PANEL WILL BE COMPLETED BY MARCH 2026. GRANULOMA MODEL/KILLING ASSAYS – SU WILL MAKE USE OF THE IN VITRO GRANULOMA MODEL ALONG WITH PARALLEL ASSESSMENTS IN MONOLAYER CULTURE AND UNFRACTIONATED PBMC AND BAL, TO ASSESS MTB KILLING AMONGST THE VARIOUS CLINICAL GROUPS. INTERESTING FINDINGS RELATED TO MTB CONTROL WILL BE TESTED IN FUTURE IN GRANULOMA MODEL EXPERIMENTS. BY USING CLINICAL SAMPLES FROM PARTICIPANTS NOT ELIGIBLE ACCORDING TO THE CASCADE HHC STUDY CRITERIA, SU HAS OPTIMIZED THE MODEL AND ALSO IMPLEMENTED CHANGES TO STREAMLINE BACTERIAL LOAD ASSESSMENT THROUGH MGIT CULTURE. SU HAS COMPLETED THE KILLING ASSAY EXPERIMENTS FOR A QUARTER OF ALL SU HHC SAMPLES FROM 4 CLINICAL GROUPS BY THE END OF PERIOD 6 AND WILL REVIEW FINDINGS FROM THIS SUBSET OF THE COHORT PRIOR TO CONTINUING THE KILLING ASSAYS IN THE FINAL YEAR (PERIOD 7 ONWARDS). C. OTHER LABORATORY WORK: THE RNASEQ DATA FROM THE BAL AM AND PAX SAMPLES COLLECTED FROM THE SU CASCADE HHC STUDY, ARE BEING GENERATED IN THREE RANDOMIZED BATCHES. DATA FROM ALL 3 BATCHES HAVE BEEN RECEIVED AND ARE BEING ANALYZED BY LOCAL BIOINFORMATICIANS, IT HAS BECOME EVIDENT THAT THE COMPLEXITY OF THE DATA REQUIRES MORE ADVANCED COMPUTATIONAL ANALYSES TO ACHIEVE RELIABLE AND FAST RESULTS. DUE TO THE REDUCED CLINICAL ACTIVITIES AT SU DURING PERIOD 6, THE SCOPE OF THE SU BUDGET WILL ALLOW THE STELLENBOSCH TEAM TO INVOLVE MORE EXPERIENCED/HIGH LEVEL ANALYSTS TO ASSIST WITH RNASEQ ANALYSES AND OMICS DATA INTEGRATION. description: STATEMENT OF WORK – YEAR 7 (BASE) – GALE THE GALE LABORATORY WILL PERFORM RNA-SEQ ASSAYS FOR THE NHP IMMUNOLOGIC STUDIES IN YEAR 7. WHOLE BLOOD AND TISSUE SAMPLES WILL BE RECEIVED AT THE GALE LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MINNESOTA FROM LOUIS PICKER (OHSU). RNA-SEQ ASSAYS WILL BE CONDUCTED BY UNIVERSITY OF MINNESOTA GENOME CENTER (UMGC). RNA-SEQ ASSAY TASKS INCLUDE 1) RNA ISOLATION AND RNA QC, 2) RNA-SEQ LIBRARY CONSTRUCTION AND LIBRARY QC, AND 3) GENERATION OF RNA SEQUENCE DATA FROM THE RESULTING MRNA-SEQ LIBRARIES ON A UG 100 PLATFORM. THE GALE LABORATORY WILL CONDUCT COMPUTATIONAL DATA ANALYSIS AND MODELING ON THE RNA-SEQ DATA SETS. IN YEAR 7, THE GALE LAB WILL ANALYZE NHP WHOLE BLOOD AND TISSUE RNA-SEQ DATA SETS THAT WERE GENERATED IN YEAR 7 AND PRIOR PERIODS. THIS ANALYSIS WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO INITIAL DATA QC, GENERATION OF NORMALIZED EXPRESSION MATRICES, DIFFERENTIAL GENE EXPRESSION ANALYSIS, FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS, CO-EXPRESSION ANALYSIS AND WHEN APPROPRIATE RULE-BASED MODELING.

description: STATEMENT OF WORK – YEAR 7 (BASE) – GERNER THE GERNER LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) SCHOOL OF MEDICINE DEPARTMENT OF IMMUNOLOGY HAS A MAJOR ROLE IN THE IMPAC-TB MICROSCOPY, HIGH-DIMENSIONAL FLOW CYTOMETRY AND SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING ANALYSIS STUDIES. THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF HOW IMMUNE CELL HETEROGENEITY AND LOCALIZATION IN INFECTED LUNGS AND DRAINING LYMPH NODES INFLUENCES VACCINE EFFICACY AND MEDIATES PROTECTION AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (MTB), THUS ALLOWING FOR IMPROVED VACCINE DESIGN. IN PARTICULAR, UW WILL STUDY THE CORRELATES OF IMMUNE PROTECTION DURING INFECTION WITH MTB SPECIFICALLY REGARDING THE ROLE OF CELLULAR RESPONSE HETEROGENEITY, IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION AND TISSUE MICROENVIRONMENTS IN LYMPHOID AND NON-LYMPHOID INFECTED TISSUES. UW WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE THE DIVERSIFICATION OF MTB STATES AND EXPRESSION OF DIFFERENT ANTIGENS IN DIFFERENT TISSUE MICROENVIRONMENTS AND CELL TYPES, AND STUDY HOW THIS CORRESPONDS TO LOCAL IMMUNE ACTIVITY BY MTB-SPECIFIC T CELLS. IN YEAR 7, THE GERNER LABORATORY AT UW WILL: I. CONTINUE IMPLEMENTATION OF MICROSCOPY STUDIES AIMED TO UNDERSTAND THE SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF IMMUNE CELLS IN MTB INFECTED ANIMALS WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION, INCLUDING: TISSUE PROCESSING, MULTIPARAMETER CONFOCAL IMAGING, IMAGE ANALYSIS AND DATA STORAGE, AS WELL AS DATA INTEGRATION WITH OTHER RELATED STUDIES WITHIN THE IMPAC-TB PROJECT. SUBSTANTIAL EFFORT WILL BE PLACED ON FINALIZING STUDIES DESCRIBING MTB DISSEMINATION TO LUNG-DRAINING LYMPH NODES AND MECHANISMS OF HOW VACCINATION PREVENTS LOCAL GENERATION OF MYELOID NICHES FOR MTB PERSISTENCE. SPECIFIC EFFORTS WILL BE PLACED ON FINALIZING THE MANUSCRIPT FOR PUBLICATION AND PERFORMING REVIEWER REQUESTED STUDIES. II. CONTINUE EVALUATING THE DISTRIBUTION OF MTB ANTIGENS WITH RESPECT TO DISTINCT BACILLARY STATES WITHIN TISSUES. WE HAVE IDENTIFIED THAT MAJOR IMMUNODOMINANT ANTIGENS DO NOT APPEAR PHYSICALLY COUPLED WITH MTB BACILLI AND ARE OFTEN EXPORTED TO NEIGHBORING CELLS. THIS INDICATES THAT VACCINE EFFORTS AIMED AT ELICITING ADAPTIVE RESPONSES TO THOSE ANTIGENS WILL LARGELY FAIL TO AFFECT CELLS WHICH ARE ACTUALLY INFECTED WITH MTB – RATHER THE BYSTANDER CELLS CONTAINING ANTIGENS. UNDERSTANDING THESE PROCESSES WILL HELP IDENTIFY MECHANISMS OF VACCINE SUCCESS VS. FAILURE ALLOWING FOR CURBING MTB INFECTION AND ITS EVENTUAL PERSISTENCE. III. IMPLEMENT ESTABLISHED HUMAN IMAGING PANELS TO STUDY IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION IN HUMAN INFECTED TISSUES (LUNG AND LYMPH NODE) OBTAINED FROM THE UGANDA POST-MORTEM STUDY, WITH DR STEVE COSE. PREVIOUS EFFORTS IDENTIFIED DIVERSE GRANULOMA STRUCTURES IN LUNGS FROM DECEASED INDIVIDUALS WITH ADVANCED DISEASE. WE HAVE ALSO DEVELOPED EXTENSIVE ANTIBODY PANELS AGAINST MAJOR IMMUNE POPULATIONS OF INTEREST AS WELL AS IMPLEMENTED AN HIGHLY-MULTIPLEX ITERATIVE IMAGING TECHNIQUE, IBEX. UPCOMING WORK WILL USE THESE ADVANCED METHODS TO ELUCIDATE MAJOR STRUCTURAL FEATURES OF THESE LESIONS. WE WILL ALSO CONTINUE TO DISSECT HOW MTB INFECTION OCCURS WITHIN HUMAN LUNG-DRAINING LNS, DIRECTLY RELATING TO THE MURINE STUDY DESCRIBED ABOVE. IV. CONTINUE WITH ANALYSIS OF THE SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS DATA FOR LUNG GRANULOMAS OVER THE EARLY COURSE OF INFECTION WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION. WE HAVE COLLECTED LARGE NUMBERS OF SAMPLES OF EARLY LUNG LESIONS FOR THE SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS STUDY AND HAVE BEGUN ANALYSIS. MAJOR SLOWDOWNS IN WORK RESULTED DUE TO MICHAEL GALE’S LAB RELOCATING, BUT WE HAVE NOW BEGUN ANALYSIS WORK WITH JOHN AITCHINSON AND FERGUL DUFFY AT SCRI. IN THE COMING YEAR, THE GERNER LAB WILL FINALIZE ANALYSIS OF THE COLLECTED DATASET. V. ASSIST WITH MULTIOMICS ANALYSIS AND DATA INTERPRETATION FOR FLOW CYTOMETRY, SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING, SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS DATA OBTAINED BY THE GERNER LAB AND OTHER GROUPS WITHIN THE IMPACTB CONSORTIUM. THIS WILL INVOLVE ANALYSIS OF CHEMOTACTIC AND ADHESION MOLECULES THAT MAY REGULATE CELLULAR POSITIONING, AS WELL AS HELPING IDENTIFY POTENTIA

description: THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT STATENS SERUM INSTITUT (SSI) WILL BE PERFORMING. NOTE THAT THE TASK NUMBERS BELOW REFLECT THE NUMBERING OF THE OVERALL ACTIVITIES IN THE PRIME CONTRACT. THROUGH THE EXECUTION OF THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL EXAMINE BASIC INDUCTION OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY FROM VACCINATION, INCLUDING STUDIES THAT ADDRESS NONTUBERCULOUS MYCOBACTERIA (NTM) INTERFERENCE, RNA DELIVERY, PRIME-BOOST REGIMENS (INCLUDING BCG PRE-EXPOSURE), TRANSCRIPTOMIC HOST SIGNATURES, , SYSTEMS BIOLOGY AND DURABLE IMMUNE MEMORY FOR THE FURTHER ADVANCEMENT OF THE EFFORT TO DESIGN AND EVALUATE AN EFFICACIOUS VACCINE AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (M.TB). THE WORK UNDER THIS CONTRACT MAY INCLUDE THE POSSIBLE DISTRIBUTION OF DE-IDENTIFIED HUMAN SUBJECT PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMC), SERUM, AND OTHER CLINICAL SAMPLES TO SCRI AND THE PHOENIX PARTNERS. NHP SAMPLES AND/OR DOWNSTREAM DATA MAY BE SHARED WITH THE PARTNERS ON THIS CONTRACT. OPTION 3 ACTIVITIES: EVALUATE OPTIMIZED M.TB VACCINE CANDIDATES FOR SAFETY, IMMUNOGENICITY AND EFFICACY IN THE NHP MODEL OF TB TASK 3.1: NHP SAFETY AND EFFICACY AGAINST ULTRA-LOW DOSE AEROSOL (ULDA) M.TB ERDMAN TO ENSURE THAT BIOLOGICAL RESULTS GENERATED IN THE VARIOUS CONSORTIUM LABS ARE COMPARABLE, WE WILL STANDARDIZE THE PRIMARY ASSAYS USED IN IMMUNOGENICITY ASSESSMENTS FOR EACH SPECIES. IN LINE WITH THE PROJECT GOALS TO DEVELOP A CROSS-SPECIES INTERROGATION PLATFORM, WE WILL HARMONIZE KEY ASSAYS ACROSS MULTIPLE SPECIES. SCRI WILL APPOINT AN OVERALL TASK LEADER TO COORDINATE AND OVERSEE THE WORK. ALL ASSAY STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES (SOP) WILL BE SHARED WITH A PRECLINICAL LABORATORY LEAD, DESIGNATED FOR EACH ASSAY, WHO WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR HARMONIZING. THESE REGENTS WILL BE INCLUDED IN AN OPTIMIZED MULTICOLOR IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE PANEL (OMIP). FURTHERMORE, SSI WILL ASSIST IN THE ANALYSIS OF REACTIVITY OF PEPTIDES IN HUMAN AND ANIMAL MODELS IN ANTIGENICITY ASSAYS PRIOR TO IMPLEMENTATION IN OPTIONS 1-4. A POOL OF 15-MER T CELL EPITOPES WHICH ARE FOUND IN DIVERSE NTMS BUT ABSENT FROM M.TB (PMID: 25548174) WILL BE SUPPLIED BY SSI IN THE OPTION 3 PERIOD TO COLLABORATOR LABS THAT REQUIRE THEM FOR IMMUNE PHENOTYPING ASSAYS. TAKING ADVANTAGE OF THE RECENTLY DEVELOPED APPROACH OF COMBINING A LARGE NUMBER OF EPITOPES IN ONE SINGLE POOL AS A "MEGAPOOL" (PMID: 27409590) WE COMBINE ALL EPITOPES IDENTIFIED IN THE PNAS STUDY TOGETHER WITH PEPTIDES IDENTIFIED BY OTHER MEMBERS OF OUR GROUP (PMID: 22046285). IN SUMMARY, LJI AND/OR SSI WILL PROVIDE: A. MEGAPOOL OF 15-MER T CELL EPITOPES WHICH ARE FOUND IN DIVERSE NTMS BUT ABSENT FROM M.TB B. MEGAPOOL OF M.TB -DERIVED EPITOPES (MTB300). C. description: THE KEY GOAL OF THIS PROGRAM IS TO DEVELOP A DESIGN-LOCKED VERSION OF STI SCOUT, AN IN VITRO DIAGNOSTIC (IVD) FOR THE DETECTION OF GONORRHEA AND CHLAMYDIA FROM MALE URINE AND FEMALE VAGINAL SWAB SAMPLES. THE TARGET PATHOGENS ARE NEISSERIA GONORRHOEAE AND CHLAMYDIA TRACHOMATIS. STI SCOUT WILL ENABLE PCR-LEVEL ACCURACY WITH THE CONVENIENCE AND COST OF RAPID ANTIGEN TESTING. COSTS OF GOODS SOLD ARE PROJECTED TO BE FAR LOWER THAN COMPETITIVE PRODUCTS, MAKING IT FINANCIALLY VIABLE TO ENTER GLOBAL LOW RESOURCE MARKETS. THE SCOUT PLATFORM INCLUDES A SCOUT HUB—A LOW-COST REUSABLE DEVICE—AND THE SCOUT CONNECT MOBILE APPLICATION FOR IOS AND ANDROID OS. TOGETHER, THESE ENABLE TESTING FOR A DEVELOPING MENU OF INDICATIONS, NOT JUST STIS, AND PERMIT RESULT TRACKING, SECURE SHARING, AND FOLLOW-ON CARE VIA TELEHEALTH. SCOUT WAS PREVIOUSLY AWARDED A CARB-X SEED AWARD CONTRACT TO DEMONSTRATE LOOP-DE-LOOP (LDL) CHEMISTRY WITH CRUDE PATIENT SAMPLES (URINE, VAGINAL SWABS). SCOUT SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETED ALL MILESTONES WITHIN THE SEED CONTRACT AND DEMONSTRATED ANALYTICAL PERFORMANCE IN POSITIVE AND PATIENT SPIKED SAMPLES THAT EXCEEDED THE TARGETS SET WITHIN THE CONTRACT. IN THIS DEVELOPMENT STAGE WORK, SCOUT WILL GENERATE ROBUST DATA AND DOCUMENTATION TO REACH DESIGN LOCK FOR STI SCOUT IN ADVANCE OF DOWNSTREAM FORMAL VERIFICATION AND VALIDATION ACTIVITIES THAT WILL EVENTUALLY SUPPORT A WHO PREQUALIFICATION AND US FDA 510(K) CLEARANCE. SCOUT WILL COMPLETE ASSAY DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES TO ENHANCE BOTH PERFORMANCE AND REGULATORY ALIGNMENT WITH WHO DRAFT TECHNICAL GUIDANCE. STI SCOUT PERFORMANCE AGAINST DESIGN INPUT REQUIREMENTS WILL BE ASSESSED ON THE INTEGRATED SCOUT SYSTEM (SCOUT HUB, SCOUT CONNECT APP) USING CONTROLLED TEST PROTOCOLS TO PROVIDE A SCIENTIFICALLY SOUND AND STATISTICALLY RIGOROUS EVALUATIONS. THE OUTCOME OF THIS PHASE WILL BE A CLEAR, DE-RISKED PATH TO INTERNATIONAL AND US COMMERCIALIZATION OF STI SCOUT, WITH SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION AND EARLY PERFORMANCE AND USABILITY DATA TO INFORM FUTURE PIVOTAL STUDIES. IN ALIGNMENT WITH CARB-X’S MISSION TO COMBAT THE GROWING THREAT OF ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE, SCOUT WILL ALSO ASSESS THE FEASIBILITY OF EXPANDING THE STI SCOUT PLATFORM TO DETECT NUCLEIC ACID MARKERS OF ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE (AMR) ALONGSIDE PATHOGEN IDENTIFICATION.

description: THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON CRYO-EM GROUP (UW-CRYOEM), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF DAVID VEESLER, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT. UW-CRYOEM WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING CRYOEM STRUCTURES DURING THIS CONTRACT YEAR (SEPT 1, 2025 THROUGH AUG 31, 2026). UW-CRYOEM WILL ALSO MANAGE (SHEPHERD) A PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS PROJECT AND WILL SUPPORT OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES AS NEEDED. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES BY CRYOEM: UW-CRYOEM (DR. VEESLER) WILL DETERMINE THE STRUCTURE OF PROTEIN OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES USING CRYOEM AS A PART OF THIS SUBCONTRACT. THESE TARGET(S) WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASE AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE UW-CRYOEM WORK. THE TARGETS SELECTED WILL BE IMPACTFUL AND MAY BE MANAGED AS HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE. PROTEINS FROM VIRAL AND/OR EUKARYOTIC TARGETS WILL BE EXPRESSED IN BACULOVIRUS-INFECTED INSECT CELLS OR MAMMALIAN CELLS (HEK), WHILE BACTERIAL TARGETS (IF SELECTED FOR CRYOEM) WILL BE EXPRESSED IN E. COLI. THE MOLECULAR WEIGHT AND STOICHIOMETRY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL BE CONFIRMED USING ANALYTICAL SEC COUPLED WITH MULTI-ANGLE LIGHT SCATTERING (SEC-MALS). THE HOMOGENEITY AND STRUCTURAL STABILITY OF THE PURIFIED PROTEINS WILL ALSO BE ASSESSED BY HIGH-THROUGHPUT NEGATIVE STAIN ELECTRON MICROSCOPY USING AN AUTOMATED DATA COLLECTION AND PROCESSING PIPELINE. PROMISING SAMPLES WILL BE FURTHER EVALUATED BY COMPUTING LOW-RESOLUTION THREE-DIMENSIONAL RECONSTRUCTIONS THAT DEMONSTRATE THE COMPOSITIONAL AND CONFORMATIONAL HETEROGENEITY OF EACH SAMPLE. THIS INFORMATION CAN ALSO BE USED TO GUIDE FURTHER CONSTRUCT SELECTION AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION CONDITIONS (IF NECESSARY). SAMPLES WILL BE VITRIFIED WITH AN FEI VITROBOT DEVICE TO PLUNGE-FREEZE GRIDS IN LIQUID ETHANE UNDER CAREFULLY CONTROLLED CONDITIONS. THE CRYOEM EXPERIMENTS WILL BE CARRIED OUT ON A TITAN KRIOS ELECTRON MICROSCOPE, EQUIPPED WITH A GATAN GIF ENERGY FILTER AND A K2 SUMMIT DIRECT ELECTRON DETECTOR. AUTOMATED DATA ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING ALLOWS A STREAMLINING OF ALL THE STEPS INVOLVED IN STRUCTURE DETERMINATION BY CRYOEM AT NEAR-ATOMIC RESOLUTION. THE LEGINON DATA COLLECTION SOFTWARE RUNS CONTINUOUSLY; ENABLING AUTOMATED TARGETING AND IMAGE ACQUISITION. LEGINON IS INTEGRATED WITH APPION, A DATA PROCESSING PIPELINE THAT CONNECTS DATA ACQUISITION TO PROCESSING ON A LOCAL CLUSTER, PROVIDING A RELATIONAL DATABASE OF ALL MICROGRAPHS TO EXPEDITE SUBSEQUENT PROCESSING. APPION AUTOMATES MANY IMAGE PROCESSING TASKS AND CREATES A SMOOTH WORKFLOW THAT ALLOWS REAL-TIME ASSESSMENT OF DATA QUALITY DURING ACQUISITION AND PREVENTS ERRORS BY TRACKING ALL THE DETAILS RELATED TO IMAGE ACQUISITION AND PROCESSING. description: THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE IMPAC-TB PROGRAM IS TO INFORM THE RATIONAL DESIGN OF AN EFFECTIVE TB VACCINE BY IDENTIFICATION OF IMMUNE RESPONSES THAT ARE CAPABLE OF CONTROLLING AND POTENTIALLY EVEN ERADICATING MTB. WE WILL ACHIEVE THIS GOAL BY IDENTIFYING AND DISSECTING PROTECTIVE PATHWAYS IN NATURAL AND VACCINE-INDUCED IMMUNITY THROUGH INTEGRATED ANALYSES OF TISSUE-SPECIFIC AND SYSTEMIC IMMUNITY IN MICE, NON-HUMAN PRIMATES (NHP), AND HUMANS. 1. THE GALE LABORATORY WILL CONDUCT RNA-SEQ ASSAYS FOR THE NHP IMMUNOLOGIC STUDIES. IN YEAR 6, THE GALE LABORATORY WILL PERFORM RNA-SEQ ASSAYS ON NHP SAMPLES COLLECTED FROM EXP #1, EXP #2, AND EXP #4. TASKS INCLUDE 1) RECEIVING TISSUE HOMOGENATE SAMPLES RECEIVED AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MINNESOTA FROM LOUIS PICKER (OHSU), 2) ISOLATING RNA FROM THESE SAMPLES AND PERFORMING RNA QC, 3) CONSTRUCTING RNA-SEQ LIBRARIES AND LIBRARY QC USING THE ISOLATED RNA, AND 4) GENERATING RNA SEQUENCE DATA FROM THE RESULTING MRNA-SEQ LIBRARIES. 2. THE GALE LABORATORY WILL CONDUCT COMPUTATIONAL DATA ANALYSIS AND MODELING ON THE RNA-SEQ DATA SETS. IN YEAR 6, THE GALE LAB WILL ANALYZE NHP WHOLE BLOOD RNA-SEQ DATA SETS THAT WERE GENERATED AT UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (GALE LAB) DURING YEAR 5. THIS ANALYSIS WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO INITIAL DATA QC, GENERATION OF NORMALIZED EXPRESSION MATRICES, DIFFERENTIAL GENE EXPRESSION ANALYSIS, FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS, CO-EXPRESSION ANALYSIS AND WHEN APPROPRIATE RULE-BASED MODELING.

description: THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW GERNER) WILL BE PERFORMING. ALTHOUGH THIS SOW DETAILS THE COMPLETE SUITE OF PROPOSED WORK, THE TASKS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CONTRACT ITERATION ARE LIMITED TO THE SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES OUTLINED BELOW, DELIVERABLES FOR THIS CONTRACT PERIOD ARE HIGHLIGHTED. GERNER LAB (YEAR 6 BASE) THE GERNER LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) SCHOOL OF MEDICINE DEPARTMENT OF IMMUNOLOGY HAS A MAJOR ROLE IN THE IMPAC-TB MICROSCOPY, HIGH-DIMENSIONAL FLOW CYTOMETRY AND SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING ANALYSIS STUDIES. THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF HOW IMMUNE CELL HETEROGENEITY AND LOCALIZATION IN INFECTED LUNGS AND DRAINING LYMPH NODES INFLUENCES VACCINE EFFICACY AND MEDIATES PROTECTION AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (MTB), THUS ALLOWING FOR IMPROVED VACCINE DESIGN. IN PARTICULAR, UW WILL STUDY THE CORRELATES OF IMMUNE PROTECTION DURING INFECTION WITH MTB SPECIFICALLY REGARDING THE ROLE OF CELLULAR RESPONSE HETEROGENEITY, IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION AND TISSUE MICROENVIRONMENTS IN LYMPHOID AND NON-LYMPHOID INFECTED TISSUES. UW WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE THE ROLES OF VARIOUS CHEMOTACTIC OR ADHESION MOLECULES IN GUIDING IMMUNE CELLS TO VARIOUS SITES WITHIN THE INFECTED LUNG TISSUES AND LYMPHOID ORGANS, AS WELL AS IN MEDIATING PROTECTION FROM MTB INFECTION. IN YEAR 6, THE GERNER LABORATORY AT UW WILL: I. CONTINUE IMPLEMENTATION OF MICROSCOPY STUDIES AIMED TO UNDERSTAND THE SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF IMMUNE CELLS IN MTB INFECTED ANIMALS WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION, INCLUDING: TISSUE PROCESSING, MULTIPARAMETER CONFOCAL IMAGING, IMAGE ANALYSIS AND DATA STORAGE, AS WELL AS DATA INTEGRATION WITH OTHER RELATED STUDIES WITHIN THE IMPAC-TB PROJECT. SUBSTANTIAL EFFORT WILL BE PLACED ON FINALIZING STUDIES DESCRIBING THE ROLE OF NEUTROPHILS IN SHAPING LUNG GRANULOMA STRUCTURE AND IN IMMUNOREGULATION WITHIN THE GRANULOMA. II. DESIGN AND IMPLEMENT EXPERIMENTS AIMED TO ELUCIDATE THE HETEROGENEITY OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES WITHIN DRAINING LYMPH NODES DURING MTB INFECTION, WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION. SPECIFIC EFFORTS WILL BE PLACED ON ELUCIDATION OF CHANGES OCCURRING WITHIN THE MYELOID COMPARTMENT IN LYMPH NODES WHICH PROMOTE VERSUS INHIBIT FUNCTIONAL T CELL ACTIVATION AT DIFFERENT TIMEPOINTS DURING INFECTION. ADDITIONAL WORK WILL INVESTIGATE HOW BCG VACCINATION INHIBITS THE GENERATION OF MYELOID MICROENVIRONMENTS IN LNS WHICH SERVE AS A NICHE FOR CHRONIC MTB PERSISTENCE. III. CONTINUE DEVELOPMENT OF HUMAN IMAGING PANELS TO STUDY IMMUNE CELL ORGANIZATION IN HUMAN INFECTED TISSUES (LUNG AND LYMPH NODE) OBTAINED FROM THE UGANDA POST-MORTEM STUDY, WITH DR STEVE COSE. PREVIOUS EFFORTS IDENTIFIED DIVERSE GRANULOMA STRUCTURES IN LUNGS FROM DECEASED INDIVIDUALS WITH ADVANCED DISEASE. UPCOMING WORK WILL ELUCIDATE ADDITIONAL IMMUNOLOGICAL FEATURES OF THESE STRUCTURES AND HOW THESE RELATE TO PROCESSES WITHIN THE DRAINING LNS. SPECIFIC GOAL WILL BE TO INVESTIGATE THE MICROANATOMY OF MTB INFECTION IN LUNG-DRAINING LNS, INCLUDING THE CELL TYPES, SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION, AND FUNCTIONAL STATES OF THE INFECTED CELLS. COMPARATIVE ANALYSES WITH MOUSE MODELS OF INFECTION (POINT II ABOVE) WILL BE PERFORMED. IV. PERFORM ANALYSIS OF THE SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS DATA FOR LUNG GRANULOMAS OVER THE EARLY COURSE OF INFECTION WITH AND WITHOUT VACCINATION. IN THE PAST YEAR, WE HAVE COLLECTED LARGE NUMBERS OF SAMPLES OF EARLY LUNG LESIONS FOR THE SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS STUDY. IN THE COMING YEAR, THE GERNER LAB WILL PERFORM ANALYSIS OF THE DATASET, VALIDATE KEY FINDINGS, AND IDENTIFY KEY ACTIONABLE DIRECTIONS FOR FURTHER WORK. V. ASSIST WITH MULTIOMICS ANALYSIS AND DATA INTERPRETATION FOR FLOW CYTOMETRY, SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING, SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS DATA OBTAINED BY THE GERNER LAB AND OTHER GROUPS WITHIN THE IMPACTB CONSORTIUM. description: IN THIS PROJECT, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP A NEW TYPE OF ADJUVANTED VACCINE THAT BOTH ACTIVATES AND LIMITS THE INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSE. IN PRELIMINARY WORK, WE SHOWED THAT ADDING MOLECULES THAT ALTER THE SIGNALING OF THE NF-􀈛􀀥 AND IRF PATHWAY IN COMBINATION WITH A WELL-CHARACTERIZED TLR AGONIST RESULTED IN NEAR-ZERO SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION WHILE MAINTAINING MINIMAL LOCAL INFLAMMATION. AT THE SAME TIME, ADDITION OF THIS COMPOUND, PME-564, INCREASED AND MODIFIED ANTIBODY RESPONSES FOR SEVERAL COMMERCIAL VACCINES – MOST NOTABLY FLUZONE. IN THIS WORK, WE PROPOSE TO FURTHER DEVELOP THIS COMPOUND, PME-564, ALONGSIDE MRNA VACCINES TO FIND A SINGLE ADJUVANT FORMULATION THAT CAN BE USED IN AN IMPROVED H5N1 VACCINE. WE HAVE TWO GOALS: (1) IDENTIFY A FORMULATION CANDIDATE THAT CAN BE RAPIDLY ADMIXED WITH EITHER CURRENT QUADRIVALENT FLU VACCINES OR MRNA VACCINES. PAIRING THESE FORMULATIONS WITH THE HIGHEST PERFORMING VACCINE PLATFORM TO DEVELOP VACCINE CANDIDATES. IMPROVING REACTOGENICITY, REDUCING DOSAGE, AND INCREASING DURABILITY OF EACH VACCINE. (2) RAPIDLY TESTING THESE CANDIDATES FOR COMPATIBILITY WITH COMMERCIAL VACCINE SYSTEMS AND PRE-CLINICAL PANDEMIC FLU VACCINES, DETERMINING AN APPROPRIATE TOXICITY AND SAFETY PROFILE FOR BOTH THE INDEPENDENT AND MIXED FORMULATION. THIS NEW APPROACH ADDRESSES A LIMITATION IN CURRENT ADJUVANT TECHNOLOGY. ADJUVANTS TRANSITIONING OUT OF BASIC DISCOVERY HAVE LIMITED METHODS TO CONTROL EXCESS INFLAMMATION IN THE FORM OF INCREASED CYTOKINES – REPRESENTED BY EXCESS TNF-􀄮􀀃􀁄􀁑􀁇􀀃􀀬􀀯-6 PRODUCTION. THE FOCUS OF THIS SUPPLEMENTAL PROGRAM WILL BE THE COFORMULATION OF THESE MOLECULES WITH MRNA VACCINES, SPECIFICALLY IN THE CONTEXT OF PANDEMIC FLU. FORMULATIONS DO HELP ADDRESS THIS PROBLEM TO SOME EXTENT, BUT THEY DO NOT ADDRESS THE FUNDAMENTAL ACTIVITY OF THE COMPOUND, WHICH GENERATES A LARGE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE AT THE CELLULAR LEVEL. OUR APPROACH DIRECTLY TARGETS THE PATHWAY THAT CAUSES THIS EXCESSIVE AND OFTEN SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION AND REDUCES IT. THE ADDED BENEFIT IS THAT BECAUSE THE MODULATION OCCURS INDEPENDENTLY OF THE AGONIST, IT CAN PROVIDE AN ADDED BENEFIT NOT JUST TO A SPECIFIC AGONIST BUT TO ANY H5N1, QUADRIVALENT, OR MRNA FLU VACCINE. THE RESULT IS COUNTER-INTUITIVE BUT EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED, A BROAD INCREASE IN ANTIBODY RESPONSES FOR THESE VACCINES. AS WELL, EXPERIMENTS IN FORMULATION, DOSAGE, AND CONCENTRATION WILL PROVIDE ESSENTIAL INFORMATION FOR DEFINING HOW IMMUNE-MODULATORS SUCH AS PME-564 ARE CONSIDERED IN USE IN VACCINE FORMULATIONS. WE WILL ALSO EXPLORE THE USE OF OUR IMMUNOMODULATOR IN THE CONTEXT OF DOSE SPARING FOR PANDEMIC FLU VACCINES. IF NEEDED, SEPARATE VIALS OF IMMUNOMODULATOR CAN BE CO-MIXED ON SITE OF VACCINATION WHICH WILL ENABLE DOSE SPARING FOR AVAILABLE VACCINES. WE WILL EXPLORE MAXIMAL AND MINIMAL DOSES OF MRNA IN COMBINATION WITH OUR IMMUNOMODULATORS TO SELECT THE BEST BALANCE BETWEEN DURABILITY, IMMUNOGENICITY, AND REACTOGENICITY. OUR PRIMARY OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP AN ADJUVANT FORMULATION THAT INCREASES THE NEUTRALIZING IGG LEVELS AND DURABILITY OF THOSE LEVELS FOR A PLATFORM OF MRNA VACCINES WITH A FOCUS ON H5N1 FLU SYSTEMS WHILE MINIMIZING THE INFLAMMATORY EFFECTS UPON INJECTION. OUR SECONDARY OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP A NOVEL DERIVATIVE OF IMMUNOMODULATORY COMPOUND PME-564 􀀋􀀥􀁄􀁉􀁈􀁗􀁌􀁑􀁌􀁅􀀌􀀃􀁄􀁖􀀃􀁄􀀃􀁅􀁕􀁒􀁄􀁇-SPECTRUM VACCINE ENHANCING OR DOSE SPARING EXCIPIENT THAT CAN BE USED AS PART OF MULTIPLE FORMULATIONS. TO IMPROVE THE OUTCOME OF THE FORMULATION AND TO DEVELOP A NOVEL DERIVATIVE OF PME-􀀘􀀙􀀗􀀃􀀋􀀥􀁄􀁉􀁈􀁗􀁌􀁑􀁌􀁅􀀌􀀏􀀃􀁚􀁈􀀃 WILL EXPLORE THE MECHANISM OF A SERIES OF CHEMICALLY SYNTHESIZED DERIVATIVES, OPTIMIZE THEIR STRUCTURE AND FORMULATION, AND TEST THEM AS ADJUVANTS WITH MULTIPLE FLU VACCINATION PLATFORMS. THESE VACCINE CANDIDATES WILL THEN BE TESTED FOR SAFETY, TOXICITY, AND THE ABILITY TO PROVIDE PROTECTION IN MOUSE CHALLENGE BEFORE BEING USED IN HIGHER ANIMAL MODELS.

description: DARTMOUTH COLLEGE, UNDER THE DIRECTION OF OLUWATOYIN ASOJO, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT (9/1/2025-8/31/2026). A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES BY X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY: DARTMOUTH WILL TRAIN UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS IN THE USE OF STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY TO CHARACTERIZE THE FUNCTION OF SELECTED TARGETS. THE STUDENTS WILL WRITE MANUSCRIPTS DESCRIBING THE STRUCTURE AND (PREDICTED) FUNCTION OF SELECTED PROTEINS. IF POSSIBLE, ONE OR TWO STUDENTS WILL PARTICIPATE IN RESEARCH PROJECTS FOCUSED ON CHARACTERIZING THE FUNCTION OF TARGET(S) USING A VARIETY OF LABORATORY METHODS. DARTMOUTH WILL SUPPORT HIGH VALUE TARGETS (HVTS), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECTS (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECTS (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM (SLT). B. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: DARTMOUTH WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. DARTMOUTH WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. KEY STAFF MEMBERS FROM DARTMOUTH WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DARTMOUTH STAFF WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION AND WILL CONDUCT THE PROJECT WORK WITH THE AIM OF PRODUCING IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS

description: THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT UK HEALTH SECURITY AGENCY (UKHSA), PREVIOUSLY KNOWN AS PUBLIC HEALTH ENGLAND (PHE), WILL BE PERFORMING. NOTE THAT THE TASK NUMBERS BELOW REFLECT THE NUMBERING OF THE OVERALL ACTIVITIES IN THE PRIME CONTRACT. THROUGH THE EXECUTION OF THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL EXAMINE BASIC INDUCTION OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY FROM VACCINATION, INCLUDING STUDIES THAT ADDRESS NONTUBERCULOUS MYCOBACTERIA (NTM) INTERFERENCE, RNA DELIVERY, PRIME-BOOST REGIMENS (INCLUDING BCG PRE-EXPOSURE), TRANSCRIPTOMIC HOST SIGNATURES, SYSTEMS BIOLOGY AND DURABLE IMMUNE MEMORY FOR THE FURTHER ADVANCEMENT OF THE EFFORT TO DESIGN AND EVALUATE AN EFFICACIOUS VACCINE AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (M.TB). THE WORK UNDER THIS CONTRACT MAY INCLUDE THE POSSIBLE DISTRIBUTION OF DE-IDENTIFIED HUMAN SUBJECT PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMC), SERUM, AND OTHER CLINICAL SAMPLES TO SCRI AND THE PHOENIX PARTNERS. NHP-DERIVED SAMPLES AND/OR DOWNSTREAM DATA MAY BE SHARED WITH THE PARTNERS ON THIS CONTRACT. OPTION 2 ACTIVITIES: OBJECTIVE: EVALUATE OPTIMIZED M.TB VACCINE CANDIDATES FOR SAFETY, IMMUNOGENICITY AND EFFICACY IN GUINEA PIG MODEL OF TB TASK 2.1 EVALUATE IMMUNE RESPONSE OF TB CANDIDATE VACCINES IN GUINEA PIGS GUINEA PIG IMMUNOLOGY THE ABILITY TO STUDY IMMUNE RESPONSES IN GUINEA PIGS IS SLOWLY IMPROVING. METHODOLOGY FOR DETERMINING A VARIETY OF CELL- SURFACE MARKERS, CYTOKINES AND CHEMOKINES HAS BEEN DEVELOPED AND STUDIES HAVE BEEN PERFORMED ON BCG-VACCINATED AND M.TB-INFECTED GUINEA PIGS. RELATED SOPS DEVELOPED AT PARTNER INSTITUTES LIKE CSU WILL BE SHARED WITH UKHSA FOR PERFORMANCE OF GUINEA PIG ENDPOINTS AND ASSAY HARMONIZATION. THE NUMBER OF ANTIBODY REAGENTS REMAINS RESTRICTIVE BUT SOME KEY FEATURES OF THE IMMUNE RESPONSE HAVE BEEN DESCRIBED. USING FLOW CYTOMETRY, IT IS POSSIBLE TO MONITOR CD4 AND CD8 T CELLS IN THE LUNGS AND STAINING WITH CD62L PLUS GATING VERSUS CD45 CAN IDENTIFY ACTIVATED T CELLS. FURTHER DEVELOPMENT OF ANTIBODIES TO DETECT IFN-Γ WILL ENABLE INTRACELLULAR STAINING PROTOCOLS TO BE ESTABLISHED. FLOW CYTOMETRY STUDIES HAVE SHOWN THAT CELL ACCUMULATION PATTERNS CHANGE IN BCG VACCINATED GUINEA PIGS AFTER AEROSOL CHALLENGE AND THAT THESE PATTERNS DIFFER FROM THOSE OF THE UNVACCINATED CONTROLS; FOR EXAMPLE, ACTIVATED CD4+ RESPONSES HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO APPEAR MORE RAPIDLY AND THERE WAS A FASTER AND LARGER MACROPHAGE RESPONSE POST-INFECTION IN BCG VACCINATED ANIMALS THAN IN UNVACCINATED CONTROLS. SUCH FINDINGS OFFER THE POTENTIAL FOR IDENTIFICATION OF IMMUNE CORRELATES OF PROTECTION BOTH PRE- AND POST- CHALLENGE. THERE IS NOW A LARGE PANEL OF CYTOKINES (IL-1, IL-4, IL-10, IL-12P40, IFN-Γ, AND TNFΑ) AND CHEMOKINES (IL- 8, MCP-1, TGFΒ, AND RANTES) THAT CAN BE MEASURED BY PCR. THERE ARE A SMALL NUMBER OF ANTIBODY REAGENTS SPECIFIC FOR SOME OF THESE CYTOKINES BEING DEVELOPED BY OUR GROUP AND OTHERS WHICH WILL INCREASE THE SOPHISTICATION OF THESE STUDIES. WORK BY OTHER GROUPS USED MOUSE ANTIBODIES IN A MULTIPLEX ASSAY TO DETECT GUINEA PIG CYTOKINES AND WE PROPOSE TO EVALUATE THIS SYSTEM ON SERA AND ANTIGEN-STIMULATED CELL SUPERNATANTS. CYTOKINES AND CHEMOKINES: WE HAVE RECENTLY DEVELOPED AN IFN-Γ ELISPOT. INITIATIVES TO FURTHER OPTIMIZE THIS ASSAY ARE ON- GOING. IF SUCH ASSAYS BECOME AVAILABLE, THEY WILL BE USED TO DETECT IFNΓ SECRETION BY CELLS IN WHOLE BLOOD, PMBC OR SPLENOCYTES STIMULATED WITH APPROPRIATE ANTIGENS. OTHER CYTOKINES CAN BE DETECTED USING MOUSE-SPECIFIC ANTIBODIES WHICH CROSS-REACT WITH GUINEA PIG PROTEINS (IL-8 AND TGFΒ), AND GUINEA PIG-SPECIFIC ANTI TNF IS ALSO AVAILABLE. A MULTIPLEX CYTOKINE ASSAY FOR MICE HAS ALSO BEEN SHOWN TO CROSS-REACT WITH GUINEA PIG PROTEINS AND WE WILL INVESTIGATE THESE REAGENTS FOR USE IN A LUMINEX ASSAY FOR GUINEA PIGS. A TNFΑ BIOASSAY HAS ALSO BEEN DESCRIBED TO DETECT ACTIVE TNFΑ, AND THIS ASSAY IS ESTABLISHED AT UKHSA. LUNG AND SPLEEN TISSUE WILL BE COLLECTED FOR HISTOPATHOLOGICAL EXAMINATION AT POST-MORTEM. description: THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON NMR GROUP (UW-NMR), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF GABRIELE VARANI, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT. UW-NMR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING 1 NMR STRUCTURE DURING THIS ONE YEAR SUBCONTRACT PERIOD, 9/1/2025 – 8/31/2026) AND FOR LEADING ONE PROJECT ON PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS AND RAPID RESPONSE TO OUTBREAKS/EPIDEMIC/PANDEMICS. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR RNA MOLECULE BY NMR: UW-NMR WILL DETERMINE THE SOLUTION STRUCTURE OF PROTEINS OR RNA MOLECULES USING NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR)-BASED METHODS. THESE TARGETS WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASES AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE UW-NMR WORK. THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25 KDA THAT FAIL TO PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL PRIMARILY BE IDENTIFIED FROM COMMUNITY REQUESTS AND INTERNAL BATCHES; SPECIFICALLY, THESE WILL BE TARGETS OF INTEREST TO THE CENTER THAT COULD NOT BE DETERMINED USING CRYSTALLOGRAPHY. HOWEVER, DR. VARANI WILL ALSO IDENTIFY RELEVANT COLLABORATORS HIMSELF WHO ARE WILLING TO NOMINATE TARGETS TO THE NMR PIPELINE AND ARE WILLING TO COLLABORATE TO PUBLISH ANY RESULTS PRODUCED BY SSGCID, ESPECIALLY IN THE AREA OF BACTERIAL AND VIRAL NON CODING RNAS. UW-NMR MAY ALSO BE ASKED TO LEAD AND SUPPORT HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM, WHENEVER OPPORTUNITIES ARISE FOR ADVANCING SCIENTIFIC PROBLEMS THAT MIGHT BEST BE ADDRESSED BY NMR. CANDIDATES SUITABLE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION WILL BE IDENTIFIED FROM 1H-15N HSQC SPECTRA COLLECTED ON 15N-LABELED PROTEIN PREPARED BY UW-NMR. STANDARD TRIPLE RESONANCE EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PERFORMED TO ASSIGN THE BACKBONE AND THE SIDE CHAIN RESONANCES OF THE PROTEIN. ONCE THE RESONANCE ASSIGNMENTS ARE COMPLETE, NOE DATA CRUCIAL FOR OBTAINING DISTANCE RESTRAINTS WILL BE COLLECTED. NOE ASSIGNMENTS AND STRUCTURE CALCULATIONS WILL BE PERFORMED ITERATIVELY USING COMBINED AUTOMATED AND MANUAL METHODS. THE QUALITY OF THE FINAL SET OF STRUCTURES WILL BE ASSESSED AND ONCE THE FINAL ENSEMBLE OF STRUCTURES IS FOUND TO BE SATISFACTORY, THE COORDINATES OF THE ENSEMBLE AND THE MEAN STRUCTURE WILL BE DEPOSITED IN THE PROTEIN DATA BANK (PDB; HTTP://WWW.PDB.ORG) AND IMMEDIATELY RELEASED TO THE WORLD. AT THE SAME TIME, ALL 1H, 13C AND 15N CHEMICAL SHIFT DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED WITH THE BIOMAGNETIC RESEARCH BANK (BMRB; HTTP://WWW.BMRB.WISC.EDU/). MANUSCRIPTS THAT INCLUDE A DESCRIPTION OF THESE STRUCTURES WILL BE PUBLISHED IN AS TIMELY A FASHION AS IS POSSIBLE. B. LEAD ONE PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS AND RAPID RESPONSE TO OUTBREAKS/EPIDEMIC/PANDEMICS PROJECT. THE UN-NMR GROUP WILL LEAD A PROJECT ENTITLED “STRUCTURAL CHARACTERIZATION OF AN ESSENTIAL RNA PACKAGING ELEMENT FROM THE INFLUENZA A VIRUS.” C. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-NMR WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH QUALITY DATA ON WELL-DEFINED PROTEIN AND RNA SAMPLES. UW-NMR WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. VARANI WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. VARANI WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION AND WILL CONDUCT THE PROJECT WORK WITH THE AIM OF PRODUCING IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS. UW-NMR IS EXPECTED TO SOLVE AT LEAST 1 NMR STRUCTURE FROM THESE STUDIES DURING THIS CONTRACT YEAR.

description: UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON PROTEIN PRODUCTION GROUP (UW-PPG), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF WESLEY C. VAN VOORHIS, M.D., PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT FROM SEPT 1, 2025 THROUGH AUG 31, 2026. UW-PPG WILL GENERATE TARGET CLONES, PERFORM SMALL- AND LARGE-SCALE SCREENING, UPSCALE EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION OF THE CLONES. UW-PPG WILL ALSO LEAD ONE STRUCTURE-BASED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTIC DEVELOPMENT PROJECT AND SUPPORT OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES AS NEEDED. A. CLONING, EXPRESSION TESTING, UPSCALE AND PURIFICATION OF SSGCID TARGETS: UW-PPG WILL PERFORM CLONING MAINLY USING HTP TECHNOLOGIES AND PCR-BASED LIGATION INDEPENDENT CLONING INTO E. COLI EXPRESSION VECTORS OR DESIGN AND ORDER SYNTHETIC CONSTRUCTS. UW-PPG WILL SCREEN THEIR EXPRESSION AND SOLUBILITY PROPERTIES USING HTP TECHNOLOGIES AND PROTOCOLS, INCLUDING, AS NEEDED, MULTIPLE EXPRESSION SYSTEMS AND CLEAVAGE SYSTEMS. UW-PPG WILL GENERATE LARGE SCALE EXPRESSIONS OF TARGETS FOR HIGHLY PURIFIED TARGET PROTEINS OR PROTEIN FRAGMENTS AND PRODUCE THEM IN SUFFICIENT QUANTITY AND QUALITY FOR STRUCTURE DETERMINATION THROUGH STANDARDIZATION AND AUTOMATION OF PROTOCOLS. UW-PPG WILL EVALUATE THE PURITY, CONCENTRATION AND BIOPHYSICAL PROPERTIES (E.G. PROTEIN FOLDING, AGGREGATION, AND/OR STABILITY) OF THE PURIFIED SAMPLES TO ENHANCE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE STRUCTURE DETERMINATION EFFORTS. UW-PPG WILL LEAD AND SUPPORT SEVERAL HIGH VALUE TARGETS (HVTS), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECTS (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECTS (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM (SLT). B. LEAD ONE STRUCTURE-BASED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTIC DEVELOPMENT PROJECT. UW-PPG MEMBERS WILL LEAD ONE SVTD PROJECT ENTITLED “STUDIES ON CHEMICAL-GENETICALLY VALIDATED PLASMODIUM FALCIPARUM PROTEIN KINASES (TOUSLED-LIKE KINASE 1[TLK1] AND AURORA KINASE 2 [ARK2]).” C. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-PPG WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. UW-PPG WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. KEY UW-PPG STAFF WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID REQUIRED MEETINGS TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. UW-PPG WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION. UW-PPG WILL CONDUCT THEIR WORK WITH THE GOAL TO PUBLISH THEIR RESULTS IN HIGH IMPACT PUBLICATIONS

description: DIAGNOSIS OF LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACT INFECTIONS (LRTLS) OFTEN RELIES ON SAMPLE TYPES SUCH AS BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE OR ENDOTRACHEAL ASPIRATE, WHICH ARE HIGHLY INVASIVE, OR SPUTUM, WHICH IS MORE DIFFICULT TO OBTAIN IN CERTAIN PATIENTS. THESE SAMPLES ARE ESPECIALLY CHALLENGING TO COLLECT IN CHILDREN; WHERE RAPID DIAGNOSIS OF LRTLS IS CRUCIAL SINCE PNEUMONIA ACCOUNTS FOR 14% OF ALL DEATHS OF CHILDREN UNDER 5 YEARS OLD. BLOOD AS AN ALTERNATIVE SAMPLE TYPE WOULD BE MORE EASILY ACCESSIBLE IN ALL PATIENT GROUPS, INCLUDING NEWBORNS AND CHILDREN. DIAGNOSIS OF LRTLS IN CHILDREN REMAINS AN UNRESOLVED CHALLENGE AS THE DISEASE AETIOLOGY IS NOT ACHIEVED FOR THE MAJORITY OF CHILDREN, EVEN IN HIGH-INCOME COUNTRIES. CULTURE-BASED DIAGNOSTIC METHODS ARE SLOW AND HAVE POOR SENSITIVITY, WHILE MOLECULAR DIAGNOSTIC RESULTS LACK SPECIFICITY. WE DEMONSTRATED THAT BROAD APPLICATION OF MOLECULAR PATHOGEN DETECTION IN 4,611 FEBRILE PATIENTS IN THE EU-FUNDED PERFORM STUDY DID NOT ENABLE CONCLUSIVE DISCRIMINATION OF BACTERIAL OR VIRAL AETIOLOGY. VIRUSES ARE DETECTED IN MOST PATIENTS WITH BACTERIAL INFECTIONS, AND THE CLINICAL VALUE OF INDIVIDUAL PATHOGEN DETECTION IN DETERMINING TREATMENT IS LOW. NEW APPROACHES ARE NEEDED TO ACCURATELY AND RAPIDLY INFORM CLINICAL DECISIONS AND GUIDE ANTIBIOTIC THERAPY. WE ARE A MULTI-DISCIPLINARY TEAM OF MEDICAL DEVICE DEVELOPMENT ENGINEERS (PROTONDX), CLINICAL ACADEMIC DOCTORS WITH EXPERTISE IN PAEDIATRIC INFECTIOUS DISEASE, MOLECULAR BIOLOGISTS AND BIOINFORMATICIANS (IMPERIAL). OUR APPROACH - INSTEAD OF RELYING ON PATHOGEN DETECTION FROM LOWER RESPIRATORY SPECIMENS - RELIES ON QUANTIFICATION OF HOST BLOOD RNA BIOMARKERS, TO DISTINGUISH BETWEEN BACTERIAL AND VIRAL DISEASES WITH HIGH ACCURACY. HOST RESPONSE CAN ALSO DIFFERENTIATE BETWEEN ACTIVE BACTERIAL INFECTION AND COLONIZATION, AS COLONIZATION OR LATENT INFECTION DOES NOT GIVE RISE TO THE SAME INFLAMMATORY RESPONSES OBSERVED IN DISEASE. ADDITIONALLY, VIA RNA-SEQ STUDIES WE HAVE EXAMINED AND PUBLISHED PROOF OF PRINCIPLE THAT THE LEVELS OF EXPRESSION OF MULTIPLE RNA BIOMARKERS MEASURED SIMULTANEOUSLY CAN ACHIEVE MULTICLASS CLASSIFICATION AT THE PATHOGEN LEVEL WITH HIGH SENSITIVITY AND SPECIFICITY. OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO IDENTIFY SIGNATURES THAT CAN BE ASSESSED IN BLOOD VIA A LOOP MEDIATED ISOTHERMAL AMPLIFICATION (LAMP)-BASED HOST RESPONSE TEST TO DETECT INFECTIONS AND CLASSIFY THE MAJOR ORGANISMS CAUSING COMMUNITY ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA (CAP). THE WORK WILL DELIVER PROOF-OF-CONCEPT FOR BLOOD-BASED TESTING USING STANDARD QPCR PLATFORMS AND A TRANSFORMATIVE PORTABLE, ACCURATE, RAPID AND EASY-TO-USE SAMPLE-TO-RESULT DIAGNOSTIC TECHNOLOGY CALLED LACEWING. THE TEST WOULD PROVIDE A MULTI-OUTCOME PROBABILITY OF A PATIENT BELONGING TO EACH DIAGNOSTIC GROUP: BROAD LEVEL CLASSIFICATION (BACTERIAL, VIRAL, TB, OTHER CAUSES), AND DETAILED LEVEL CLASSIFICATION (IDENTIFICATION OF THE CAUSATIVE PATHOGEN). THE TESTING OUTPUTS WOULD ULTIMATELY INFORM CLINICAL DECISIONS IN EMERGENCY DEPARTMENTS (EDS) AND URGENT CARE CENTRES IN <20 MINS WITHOUT A LABORATORY AND SKILLED PERSONNEL. WE WILL FOCUS ON CHILDREN UNDER 2 YEARS OLD, WHICH ARE A HIGH-RISK POPULATION FOR CAP WHERE INVASIVE SAMPLE TYPES ARE EVEN LESS ACCESSIBLE. WE WILL LEVERAGE EXISTING RNA BIOMARKER DATA USING A NOVEL CROSS-PLATFORM BIOINFORMATIC FRAMEWORK FOR SIGNATURE DISCOVERY AND TRANSLATION THAT WILL BE COMPATIBLE WITH LAB-BASED OR POINT OF CARE DIAGNOSTIC TECHNOLOGIES AND PLATFORMS. OUR FRAMEWORK INCORPORATES PLATFORM-SPECIFIC CONSTRAINTS EARLY IN THE BIOMARKER DISCOVERY AND SELECTION PHASES TO ADDRESS PRECISION-RELATED CHALLENGES AND MAXIMISE TEST DEVELOPMENT FEASIBILITY. TESTING WILL BE CONDUCTED ON A REAL-TIME LAMP (QLAMP) PLATFORM WITH PRELIMINARY COMPARISON TO OUR LAB-ON-CHIP ELECTROCHEMICAL SENSING LACEWING PLATFORM IN SEMICONDUCTOR TECHNOLOGY FOR REAL-TIME ELECTRONIC LAMP (ELAMP), WHICH HAS ALREADY BEEN DEMONSTRATED WITH BLOOD AND OTHER SAMPLE TYPES FOR TARGETS INCLUDING SARS-COV-2, DENGUE, COLISTIN RESISTANCE AND KLEBSIELLA.

description: THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM WILL EVALUATE THE POTENTIAL OF BREATH ANALYSIS AS A NOVEL, NONINVASIVE DIAGNOSTIC APPROACH FOR LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACT INFECTIONS (LRTIS). THE GOAL IS TO ASSESS WHETHER MEASURING VOLATILE ORGANIC COMPOUNDS (VOCS) IN EXHALED BREATH CAN PROVIDE RAPID, ACCURATE, AND CLINICALLY USEFUL DIAGNOSTIC INFORMATION TO SUPPORT PATIENT CARE. THE PROJECT IS STRUCTURED AROUND A PROSPECTIVE, MULTI-SITE CLINICAL STUDY INVOLVING MULTIPLE PATIENT POPULATIONS INCLUDING BOTH CHILDREN AND ADULTS, IN CONVENTIONAL AND INTENSIVE CARE SETTINGS. BREATH SAMPLES AND MICROBIOLOGICAL SAMPLES WILL BE COLLECTED ALONGSIDE STANDARD CLINICAL AND BIOLOGICAL DATA TO DOCUMENT THE DIAGNOSTIC SIGNATURES ASSOCIATED WITH RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS USING REAL-TIME MASS SPECTROMETRY. THE PROGRAM WILL ASSESS WHETHER BREATH-BASED DIAGNOSTICS CAN DIFFERENTIATE INFECTION FROM COLONIZATION, HELP IDENTIFY THE PATHOGENS, AND REACH RELEVANT DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY COMPARED TO CURRENT REFERENCE METHODS. THE PROJECT IS PLANNED OVER 24 MONTHS AND AIMS TO GENERATE GENERALIZABLE EVIDENCE ON THE INTEREST AND FEASIBILITY OF BREATH ANALYSIS FOR RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS. THIS WORK WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE BROADER GOAL OF DEVELOPING NON-INVASIVE, RAPID, AND SCALABLE DIAGNOSTIC TOOLS THAT CAN ENHANCE PATIENT MANAGEMENT AND SUPPORT MORE EFFICIENT HEALTHCARE DELIVERY.
