description: THE WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY IN ST. LOUIS, UNDER THE DIRECTION OF CRAIG SMITH, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT (9/1/2025-8/31/2026). A. STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY TRAINING: WUSTL WILL TRAIN UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS HOW TO ANALYZE PROTEIN STRUCTURES. THE STUDENTS WILL WRITE MANUSCRIPTS DESCRIBING THE STRUCTURE AND (PREDICTED) FUNCTION OF SELECTED PROTEINS. IF POSSIBLE, ONE OR TWO STUDENTS WILL PARTICIPATE IN A SUMMER RESEARCH PROJECT FOCUSED ON CHARACTERIZING THE FUNCTION OF TARGET(S) USING A VARIETY OF LABORATORY METHODS. WUSTL WILL SUPPORT HIGH VALUE TARGETS (HVTS), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECTS (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECTS (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM (SLT). B. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: WUSTL WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. WUSTL WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. KEY STAFF MEMBERS FROM WUSTL WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. WUSTL STAFF WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION AND WILL CONDUCT THE PROJECT WORK WITH THE AIM OF PRODUCING IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS

description: THE WASHINGTON STATE UNIVERSITY GROUP (WSU), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF GARRY BUCHKO, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENTS. WSU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING AT LEAST ONE NMR STRUCTURE DURING THIS YEAR OF THE CONTRACT (SEPT 1, 2025 THROUGH AUG 31, 2026) WHICH MAY BE FROM THE SSGCID PIPELINE OR MAY BE ASSOCIATED WITH A SPECIAL PROJECT. WSU WILL LEAD ONE STRUCTURE-BASED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTIC DEVELOPMENT PROJECT AND MAY SUPPORT OTHER SPECIAL PROJECT STUDIES AS NEEDED, USING NMR-BASED METHODS (E.G.: DYNAMIC STUDIES, CHEMICAL SHIFT PERTURBATION, ENZYME KINETICS, SOLID-STATE NMR, STD-NMR). A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION BY NMR: WSU (DR. BUCHKO) WILL DETERMINE THE SOLUTION STRUCTURE OF AT LEAST ONE PROTEIN USING NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR)-BASED METHODS. THESE TARGETS WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASE, AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE WSU/PNNL-NMR WORK. THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25-30 KDA THAT FAIL TO PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL PRIMARILY BE IDENTIFIED BY THE SEATTLE CHILDREN’S RESEARCH TARGET SELECTION GROUP, HOWEVER, DR. BUCHKO WILL ALSO IDENTIFY RELEVANT COLLABORATORS WHO ARE WILLING TO NOMINATE TARGETS TO THE NMR PIPELINE AND COLLABORATE TO PUBLISH ANY RESULTS PRODUCED BY SSGCID. WSU MAY BE ASKED TO LEAD AND SUPPORT SEVERAL HIGH VALUE TARGETS (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECTS (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECTS (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM. CANDIDATES SUITABLE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION WILL BE IDENTIFIED FROM 1H-15N HSQC SPECTRA COLLECTED ON 15N-LABELED PROTEIN PREPARED BY WSU. STANDARD TRIPLE RESONANCE EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PERFORMED TO ASSIGN THE BACKBONE AND SIDE CHAIN 1H, 13C, AND 15N RESONANCES OF THE PROTEIN. ONCE THE RESONANCE ASSIGNMENTS ARE COMPLETE, NOE DATA CRUCIAL FOR OBTAINING DISTANCE RESTRAINTS WILL BE COLLECTED. NOE ASSIGNMENTS AND STRUCTURE CALCULATIONS WILL BE PERFORMED ITERATIVELY USING COMBINED AUTOMATED AND MANUAL METHODS. THE QUALITY OF THE FINAL SET OF STRUCTURES WILL BE ASSESSED AND ONCE THE FINAL ENSEMBLE OF STRUCTURES IS FOUND TO BE SATISFACTORY, THE COORDINATES OF THE ENSEMBLE WILL BE DEPOSITED IN THE PROTEIN DATA BANK (PDB; HTTP://WWW.PDB.ORG) AND IMMEDIATELY RELEASED TO THE WORLD. AT THE SAME TIME, ALL 1H, 13C, AND 15N CHEMICAL SHIFT DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED WITH THE BIOMAGNETIC RESEARCH BANK (BMRB; HTTP://WWW.BMRB.WISC.EDU/). MANUSCRIPTS THAT INCLUDE A DESCRIPTION OF THESE STRUCTURES WILL BE PUBLISHED IN AS TIMELY A FASHION AS IS POSSIBLE. B. LEAD ONE STRUCTURE-BASED VACCINE AND THERAPEUTIC DEVELOPMENT (SVTD) WSU WILL LEAD A SVTD PROJECT ENTITLED “CHARACTERIZATION OF NOVEL ANTIBIOTICS TARGETING HELICOBACTER PYLORI.” C. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION, AND REPORTING: WSU WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. WSU WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS, AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. BUCHKO WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUESTED MEETINGS AS REQUIRED TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. BUCHKO WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION. THE MAJOR AIM OF THE PROJECT WORK WILL BE IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS.

description: THE UNIVERSITY OF KANSAS (KU), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF SCOTT LOVELL, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT (9/1/2025-8/31/2026). KU WILL ACCEPT PROTEIN AND OTHER SAMPLES PRIMARILY GENERATED BY OTHER SSGCID SITES AND PREPARE THEM FOR X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY STRUCTURE DETERMINATION STUDIES, CONDUCT CRYSTALLIZATION EXPERIMENTS, COLLECT DIFFRACTION DATA, AND PERFORM STRUCTURE SOLUTION. KU WILL ALSO SUPPORT VARIOUS SPECIAL PROJECT STUDIES AS NEEDED AND LEAD ONE FUNCTIONAL STUDY. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES BY X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY: KU WILL ACCEPT PROTEIN SAMPLES PRIMARILY RECEIVED FROM THE OTHER TEAM SITES FOR X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY STRUCTURE DETERMINATION STUDIES AND CONDUCT HIGH THROUGHPUT CRYSTALLIZATION EXPERIMENTS, INCLUDING CRYSTALLIZATION TRIALS, OPTIMIZATION, DATA COLLECTION AND INTERPRETATION. WHEN NECESSARY, KU WILL CONDUCT CO-CRYSTALLIZATION SCREENS OF THE TARGET IN COMPLEX WITH SMALL MOLECULES AND LIGANDS. KU WILL IDENTIFY AND HARVEST CRYSTALS THAT ARE SUITABLE FOR DIFFRACTION SCREENING AND CONDUCT LARGE SCALE CRYSTAL DIFFRACTION SCREENS, COLLECT DIFFRACTION DATA AND MONITOR QUALITY METRICS OF THE SUITABLE CRYSTALS. WHERE APPROPRIATE, KU WILL ALSO LIAISE WITH KUMC’S CRYOEM CENTER TO HELP SOLVE STRUCTURES BY CRYOEM. KU WILL PERFORM STRUCTURE SOLUTION, MODEL REFINEMENT AND VALIDATION FOR X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY. A STRUCTURE DETERMINATION PROJECT WILL BE CONSIDERED COMPLETE WHEN THE REFINEMENT AND VALIDATION OF THE FINAL STRUCTURE MODELS DO NOT PROVIDE ANY CLEAR SIGNAL OF WHERE THE MODEL CAN BE IMPROVED OR WHEN 3D STRUCTURE QUALITY PARAMETERS SATISFY THE MINIMUM QUALITY REQUIREMENTS ESTABLISHED AND AGREED UPON IN COORDINATION WITH THE CENTER FOR STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY OF INFECTIOUS DISEASES. KU WILL SUPPORT HIGH VALUE TARGETS (HVTS), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECTS (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECTS (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM (SLT). FUNCTIONAL STUDIES KU WILL LEAD ONE FUNCTION STUDY, ENTITLED “STRUCTURE AND FUNCTIONAL STUDIES OF THE TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATOR, GNTR FROM ENTEROCOCCUS FAECALIS.” QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: KU WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. KU WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. KEY STAFF MEMBERS FROM KU WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. KU STAFF WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION AND WILL CONDUCT THE PROJECT WORK WITH THE AIM OF PRODUCING IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS. IT IS EXPECTED THAT SEVENTY-FIVE STRUCTURES WILL BE SOLVED THROUGH THIS WORK

description: SERES IS DEVELOPING A NOVEL LIVE BIOTHERAPEUTIC PRODUCT (LBP) OF HUMAN COMMENSAL BACTERIA FORMULATED FOR ORAL LIQUID DELIVERY, TO ADDRESS THE UNMET NEED FOR PREVENTION OF GUT-SEEDED AMR INFECTION IN THE MEDICAL ICU. INFECTIONS WITH PATHOGENIC (OFTEN MULTIDRUG RESISTANT, MDR) BACTERIA ARE THE LEADING CAUSE OF MORTALITY IN THE MEDICAL INTENSIVE CARE UNIT (ICU), CAUSING UP TO 9 DEATHS FOR EVERY 100 ICU PATIENTS ADMITTED (VINCENT, 2009). MOST PATIENTS ARE ADMITTED TO THE MEDICAL ICU WITH A KNOWN OR SUSPECTED INFECTION (I.E., SEPSIS) BUT, WITH TARGETED OR EMPIRIC ANTIBIOTICS, MOST RECOVER FROM THIS INITIAL INFECTION. WHAT CAUSES DEATHS—AND WHAT THIS PROJECT PROPOSES TO PREVENT—ARE THE SECONDARY, HEALTHCARE- ASSOCIATED INFECTIONS THAT FREQUENTLY DEVELOP DURING THE PROLONGED RECOVERY FROM SEPSIS. A NOVEL APPROACH THAT ADDRESSES BOTH GUT COLONIZATION AND SUBSEQUENT TRANSLOCATION BY E. COLI AND OTHER GUT SEEDED PATHOGENS COULD PREVENT A SIGNIFICANT PROPORTION OF THESE INFECTIONS. IF GUT COLONIZATION AND TRANSLOCATION BY E. COLI COULD BE AMELIORATED BY A LBP SUCH AS SER-155, A LARGE PROPORTION OF THESE INFECTIONS COULD BE PREVENTED. SER-155 IS CURRENTLY IN CLINICAL DEVELOPMENT AND HAS BEEN EVALUATED IN ALLOGENEIC HCT PATIENTS. DATA FROM OUR PHASE 1B STUDY SUPPORTS THE SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF SER-155 IN PREVENTING INFECTION IN IMMUNE COMPROMISED, HOSPITALIZED PATIENTS. THE PROPOSED WORK WILL EXTEND THESE FINDINGS BY DEVELOPING A LIQUID FORMULATION OF SER-155 (“SER-155-LF"), A NECESSARY STEP IN THE MEDICAL ICU AS PATIENTS ARE COMMONLY INTUBATED WITH NARROW-CALIBER GASTRIC OR DUODENAL FEEDING TUBES, PLACED FOR THE DELIVERY OF MEDICATIONS AND ENTERAL NUTRITION. UPON SUCCESSFUL DEVELOPMENT OF A LIQUID FORMULATION WHICH IS SUITED FOR DELIVERY IN THE ICU VIA NG TUBE, THE PROPOSED WORK PLAN WILL NEXT FOCUS ON GMP MANUFACTURING OF SER-155-LF FOR CLINICAL STUDY AND PREPARATION OF AN EARLY PHASE TRIAL IN ICU PATIENTS WITH A PRIMARY OUTCOME OF SAFETY AND ENGRAFTMENT, EXPLORATORY ENDPOINTS AROUND E. COLI COLONIZATION AND AMR, AND DENSE DOWNSTREAM CLINICAL AND MECHANISTIC ANALYSES.

description: THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT FRED HUTCHINSON CANCER CENTER (FHCC) WILL BE PERFORMING. NOTE THAT THE TASK NUMBERS BELOW REFLECT THE NUMBERING OF THE OVERALL ACTIVITIES IN THE PRIME CONTRACT. ALTHOUGH THIS SOW DETAILS THE COMPLETE SUITE OF PROPOSED WORK, THE TASKS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CONTRACT ITERATION ARE LIMITED TO THE SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES OUTLINED BELOW, DELIVERABLES FOR THIS CONTRACT PERIOD ARE HIGHLIGHTED. THROUGH THE EXECUTION OF THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL EXAMINE BASIC INDUCTION OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY FROM VACCINATION, INCLUDING STUDIES THAT ADDRESS NONTUBERCULOUS MYCOBACTERIA (NTM) INTERFERENCE, RNA VACCINE DELIVERY, PRIME-BOOST REGIMENS (INCLUDING BCG PRE-EXPOSURE), TRANSCRIPTOMIC HOST SIGNATURES, SYSTEMS BIOLOGY AND DURABLE IMMUNE MEMORY FOR THE FURTHER ADVANCEMENT OF THE EFFORT TO DESIGN AND EVALUATE AN EFFICACIOUS VACCINE AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (M.TB) THE WORK UNDER THIS CONTRACT MAY INCLUDE THE POSSIBLE DISTRIBUTION OF DE-IDENTIFIED HUMAN SUBJECT PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMC), SERUM, AND OTHER CLINICAL SAMPLES TO SCRI AND THE PHOENIX PARTNERS. NHP SAMPLES AND/OR DOWNSTREAM DATA MAY BE SHARED WITH THE PARTNERS ON THIS CONTRACT. OPTION 3 ACTIVITIES: EVALUATE OPTIMIZED M.TB VACCINE CANDIDATES FOR SAFETY, IMMUNOGENICITY AND EFFICACY IN THE NHP MODEL OF TB TASK 3.5 TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS OF NHP SAMPLES. FHCC WILL EXECUTE GENE EXPRESSION PROFILING WITH RNASEQ/NANOSTRING ASSAYS ON NHP SAMPLES GENERATED IN OPTION 3 AT UKHSA. TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS WILL BE FOCUSED ON IDENTIFYING A PERIPHERAL BLOOD SURROGATE ENDPOINT FOR THE M.TB ERDMAN ULDA CHALLENGE OUTCOMES. THE INITIAL UNBIASED RNA SEQUENCING APPROACH WILL USE WHOLE-BLOOD SAMPLES FROM PRE- AND POST-CHALLENGE TIME POINTS. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL LOOK FOR TRANSCRIPTS THAT ARE CORRELATED WITH M.TB COLONY FORMING UNITS (CFU) AND M.TB QPCR ASSAYS FROM BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE (BAL), THE PRIMARY CHALLENGE OUTCOMES. IN ADDITION TO ABSOLUTE ABUNDANCE AT POST-CHALLENGE TIME POINTS, WE WILL ALSO LOOK FOR CHANGES IN TRANSCRIPT ABUNDANCE RELATIVE TO THE DAY OF CHALLENGE AS A POTENTIAL CORRELATE OF CHALLENGE OUTCOME. AS WE BUILD A MODEL TO PREDICT CHALLENGE OUTCOME FROM THESE GENE EXPRESSION MEASURES WE WILL SPECIFICALLY CONSIDER TRANSCRIPTS THAT HAVE PREVIOUSLY BEEN IDENTIFIED AS PREDICTORS OF PROGRESSION TO TB DISEASE, SUCH AS TYPE I IFN-RELATED GENES WHOSE EXPRESSION INCREASES DURING DISEASE PROGRESSION. THE HUMAN EXPRESSION SIGNATURES WILL BE EVALUATED IN NHPS AND VICE VERSA; ADDITIONALLY, A JOINT MODEL WILL BE DEVELOPED, ALLOWING FOR DIFFERENCES IN NHP AND HUMAN ASSOCIATIONS, WHILE IDENTIFYING A COMMON GENE SIGNATURE. description: SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO PROVIDE RAPID DEPLOYMENT OF TECHNICAL, OPERATIONAL, AND CLINICAL RESEARCH RESOURCES AND EXPERTISE FOR THIS TIME-SENSITIVE INITIATIVE. THE PROTOCOL IS TITLED, ASSESSMENT OF IMMUNE RESPONSE TO EBOLA VIRUS DISEASE AS MODULATED BY VACCINES AND MEDICAL COUNTERMEASURES, AND IS ALSO KNOWN AS PALM 005. THE SCOPE OF WORK INCLUDES BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO: STRATEGIC AND OPERATIONAL PLANNING AND HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT; INFRASTRUCTURE OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCE; LOGISTICS AND PROCUREMENT MANAGEMENT; SITE DEVELOPMENT TO ENSURE ALL CLINICAL SITES REMAIN IN A STATE OF PREPAREDNESS AND COMPLIANCE WITH PROTOCOL REQUIREMENTS; INITIATING AND COMPLETING ENROLLMENT AND FOLLOW-UP FOR THE CLINICAL RESEARCH PROTOCOL; OVERALL MANAGEMENT AND OVERSIGHT OF THE CONDUCT OF THE MOBILIZATION, PSYCHOSOCIAL SUPPORT AND COMMUNICATIONS EFFORTS; AND OTHER ACTIVITIES SUCH AS LABORATORY SERVICES AND PHARMACY SUPPORT. THE SPECIFIC SUPPORT TO EBOLA OUTBREAK #14 IN THE EQUATOR PROVINCE IS TO COVER GAPS IN THE SAFE ADMINISTRATION OF INVESTIGATIONAL PRODUCT UNTIL SUPPORT OF OTHER EBOLA RESPONSE PARTNERS HAS BEEN ESTABLISHED IN THIS REGION. THE PALM 010 STUDY IS A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL TO TEST THE SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF MPOX VACCINES IN THE DRC. THE SCOPE OF WORK IS STRICTLY FOR THE TRIAL INITIATION PHASE WHICH INCLUDES PLANNING AND PREPARATION FOR THIS TRIAL, SUCH AS PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT, RESEARCH SITE ASSESSMENTS, AND SITE PREPARATION/RENOVATION ACTIVITIES AND ALL ACTIVITIES LEADING UP TO SITE ACTIVATION. THE PALM 007 EXTENSION STUDY IS A SINGLE-ARM, OPEN-LABEL EXTENSION TO THE PALM007 RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL FOR FURTHER CLINICAL CHARACTERIZATION OF THE NATURAL HISTORY OF MPOX WHICH FORMS PART OF THE INITIATION OF THE PALM 010 STUDY. ANALYSIS OBJECTIVES INCLUDE DESCRIPTIVE SUMMARIES OF BASELINE CHARACTERISTICS AND CHARACTERIZATION OF PARTICIPANT TRAJECTORIES AS MEASURED BY TARGETED SYMPTOM ASSESSMENTS, LONGITUDINAL PCR P.O. BOX B, FREDERICK, MD 21702-1201 • 301-846-1000 A SUBSIDIARY OF RCF-505 PAGE 4 OF 4 REV. AUGUST 2023 ASSESSMENTS, AND TIMING OF KEY CLINICAL MILESTONES SUCH AS LESION RESOLUTION AND DURATION OF VIREMIA. THE EXTENSION PHASE WILL ALSO PROVIDE AN OPPORTUNITY TO OBSERVE ADDITIONAL CASES OF RECRUDESCENT DISEASE TO SUPPORT CASE STUDY DESCRIPTIONS AND EXPLORATORY ANALYSES OF RISK FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH RECRUDESCENCE. THE SUBCONTRACTOR, AS THE KEY IMPLEMENTATION PARTNER IN THE DRC, SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR PROVIDING THE PREPARATION, IMPLEMENTATION AND EXECUTION FOR CLINICAL OPERATION ACTIVITIES ASSOCIATED WITH THESE CLINICAL RESEARCH EFFORTS AND WILL BE REQUIRED TO WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH OTHER PROJECT STAKEHOLDERS SUCH AS BUT LIMITED TO, PARTICIPATING COUNTRIES, STUDY SPONSORS, AND MINISTRIES OF HEALTH TO CONDUCT AND COMPLETE THESE CLINICAL RESEARCH STUDIES. THE SCOPE OF WORK INCLUDES, BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO ADMINISTRATIVE, FINANCIAL AND HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, CLINICAL RESEARCH SITE OPERATIONS, PROCUREMENT AND LOGISTICS SUPPORT, LABORATORY OPERATIONS, REGULATORY COMPLIANCE, DATA MANAGEMENT, INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (IT) SUPPORT, AND TRAVEL SUPPORT TO SUPPORT THE PALM PROTOCOL ACTIVITIES. IN ADDITION, THE SUBCONTRACTOR IS TASKED TO SUPPORT THE PALM BIOREPOSITORY LABOR REQUIREMENTS IN THE DRC.

description: THE PROPOSED RESEARCH FOCUSES ON EVALUATING A NONINVASIVE DIAGNOSTIC PLATFORM THAT USES EXHALED BREATH TO DIAGNOSE LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACT INFECTIONS (LRTIS) IN HIGH-RISK POPULATIONS WITHIN CRITICAL CARE ENVIRONMENTS, INCLUDING INTUBATED PATIENTS WITH MECHANICAL VENTILATION AND NON-INTUBATED INPATIENTS. THIS PLATFORM MEASURES HOST PROTEASE ACTIVITY, SPECIFICALLY NEUTROPHIL ELASTASE (HNE), MATRIX METALLOPROTEINASES (MMPS), AND CATHEPSINS, AS HOST IMMUNE RESPONSES TO DISTINGUISH BETWEEN RESPIRATORY COLONIZATION AND ACTIVE INFECTION, AS WELL AS DIFFERENTIATE BACTERIAL FROM VIRAL INFECTIONS. ADDITIONALLY, THE PLATFORM INCORPORATES THE MEASUREMENT OF SS-LACTAMASE ACTIVITY TO EVALUATE BACTERIAL RESISTANCE TO GUIDE ANTIBIOTIC SUSCEPTIBILITY ASSESSMENTS. THIS DIAGNOSTIC STRATEGY INTRODUCES TWO KEY INNOVATIONS. FIRST, THE EXHALED BREATH SAMPLING SYSTEM OFFERS HIGH EFFICIENCY IN CAPTURING PROTEIN MATERIALS FROM THE LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACT AND CAN BE FEASIBLY INTEGRATED INTO EXISTING CLINICAL WORKFLOWS IN INTENSIVE CARE SETTINGS. SECOND, THE PLATFORM INCLUDES A COST-EFFECTIVE AND RAPID MATRIX-ASSISTED LASER DESORPTION/IONIZATION MASS SPECTROMETRY (MALDI-MS) ASSAY THAT EMPLOYS CUSTOMIZED HIGH-SPECIFICITY SENSOR MOLECULES ALLOWING THE DETECTION OF MULTIPLE TARGETS IN A MULTIPLEXED FASHION, INCLUDING BOTH HOST PROTEASES AND BACTERIAL SS-LACTAMASES. THE INFORMATION PROVIDED BY THIS DIAGNOSTIC PLATFORM IS DIRECTLY RELEVANT TO CRITICAL CLINICAL DECISION-MAKING. SPECIFICALLY, SENSITIVE AND SPECIFIC QUANTIFICATION OF HOST PROTEASE ACTIVITY ALLOWS FOR THE DIFFERENTIATION OF BACTERIAL COLONIZATION FROM ACTIVE BACTERIAL OR VIRAL INFECTION, WHICH ENABLES CLINICIANS TO IDENTIFY PATIENTS WHO TRULY REQUIRE ANTIBIOTIC THERAPY. IN PARALLEL, FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS OF SS-LACTAMASE ACTIVITY WITHIN THE SAME SAMPLE ALLOWS THE DIFFERENTIATION AMONG MAJOR CLASSES OF RESISTANCE ENZYMES, BROAD-SPECTRUM SS-LACTAMASES (BSBL), EXTENDED-SPECTRUM SS-LACTAMASES (ESBL), AMPC SS-LACTAMASES, AND CARBAPENEMASES, THUS SUPPORTING PRECISE AND TARGETED ANTIMICROBIAL INTERVENTIONS. THIS APPROACH OFFERS SIGNIFICANT ADVANTAGES OVER CONVENTIONAL DIAGNOSTIC METHODS, WHICH OFTEN RELY ON BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE (BAL) AND MICROBIAL CULTURE WHICH ARE INVASIVE AND TYPICALLY REQUIRE SEVERAL DAYS TO DELIVER RESULTS. SIMILARLY, CURRENT CULTURE-BASED ANTIMICROBIAL SUSCEPTIBILITY TESTING (AST) SUFFERS FROM DELAYS AND LIMITED SENSITIVITY, WHILE GENOMIC METHODS SUCH AS POLYMERASE CHAIN REACTION (PCR) AND WHOLE GENOME SEQUENCING (WGS) MAY INCUR HIGH COSTS AND MAY NOT RELIABLY DETECT EMERGING OR UNKNOWN RESISTANCE MECHANISMS NOR CAN THESE METHODS RELIABLY DISTINGUISH BETWEEN COLONIZATION AND INFECTION. THE PROPOSED WORK HAS THE POTENTIAL TO SUBSTANTIALLY ADVANCE LRTI MANAGEMENT IN CRITICAL CARE SETTINGS, INCLUDING REDUCING UNNECESSARY ANTIBIOTIC USE, ENABLING EARLIER AND MORE EFFECTIVE TREATMENT OF INFECTIONS CAUSED BY ANTIBIOTIC-RESISTANT BACTERIA, AND ULTIMATELY IMPROVING PATIENT OUTCOMES. BEYOND THIS STUDY, BREATHBIOMICS™ WILL OFFER A NONINVASIVE ALTERNATIVE TO BAL OR SPUTUM COLLECTION FOR RESPIRATORY INFECTION DIAGNOSIS IN CHILDREN AND OTHER PATIENT POPULATIONS WHICH WOULD BENEFIT FROM NON-INVASIVE SAMPLING OF THE LOWER AIRWAYS.

description: QMAP (QUICK MULTIPLEXED ASSAY PLATFORM) IS A CHEAP, FAST, ACCURATE, AND HIGHLY SCALABLE FULLY AUTOMATED SYSTEM FOR NEONATAL SEPSIS SCREENING. IT CAN OFFER BROAD-SPECTRUM ANALYSIS OF MOLECULAR MARKERS REPRESENTING PATHOGEN SPECIES AND ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE THROUGH A SINGLE-POT REACTION. THIS ENABLES RAPID DIAGNOSIS, PROVIDING ACCURATE RESULTS WITHIN 6 HOURS FROM LESS THAN 2 ML OF WHOLE BLOOD. THE SYSTEM EMPLOYS GRAPHICALLY ENCODED MICRODISKS, EACH ENGINEERED TO DETECT SPECIFIC ID/AST GENE MOLECULES THROUGH THE ATTACHMENT OF COMPLEMENTARY DNA PROBES, WHICH ARE SUBSEQUENTLY POOLED FOR EACH ASSAY. THE SYSTEM IS HIGHLY SCALABLE AND MULTIPLEXED, ENABLING THE INTEGRATION OF BOTH PATHOGEN ID AND AST AT A SINGLE RUN. EACH ID OR AST SPECIFIC MICRODISKS CAN BE MASS-PRODUCED AT A LOW COST. THE ONE-POT APPROACH ALLOWS PARALLEL DETECTION OF 71 GENES(ID 44 GENES AND AST 27 GENES) WITH MINIMAL USAGE OF REAGENTS AND ASSOCIATED KITS. COMPARED TO EXISTING TECHNOLOGIES, OVERALL REAGENT COSTS CAN BE REDUCED BY 4 TO 5- FOLD, WHILE ACHIEVING 2 TO 10 TIMES GREATER ID/AST GENE COVERAGE, MAKING IT IDEAL FOR A COMPREHENSIVE NEONATAL SEPSIS SCREENING PLATFORM THAT IS ALSO AFFORDABLE FOR LMICS. WITH MINIMAL SAMPLE PREPARATION AND OUR ONE-POT REACTION DESIGN, EACH STEP IS SIMPLIFIED, MINIMIZING THE RISK OF SAMPLE DILUTION OR BACTERIAL LOSS DURING TRANSFER, DISTRIBUTION, OR REACTIONS. THIS CAN POTENTIALLY REDUCE THE REQUIRED BLOOD SAMPLE VOLUME BY MORE THAN 50% COMPARED TO CONVENTIONAL DIAGNOSTICS AND ALSO ENHANCE THE SENSITIVITY OF ASSAY. FURTHERMORE, THE SYSTEM ULTIMATELY ENABLES THE DETECTION OF OVER 100 DISTINCT PROBES BY INCORPORATING ADDITIONAL TYPES OF MICRODISKS. THIS FLEXIBILITY ALLOWS QMAP TO EXPAND ITS PANEL LIBRARY TO INCLUDE NEW PATHOGENS OR AMR GENES, PROVIDING AN ADAPTABLE SOLUTION FOR EVOLVING CLINICAL REQUIREMENTS. MANY COMPANIES HAVE DEVELOPED METHODS(FLUORESCENCE-BASED PRINCIPLE, NMR-BASED PRINCIPLE, ELECTROCHEMICAL-BASED PRINCIPLE) TO MAXIMIZE THE DETECTION COVERAGE FOR COMPREHENSIVE PROFILING OF PATHOGEN SPECIES AND ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE. HOWEVER, THE NUMBER OF MOLECULES BEING ANALYZED IN SINGLE WELL HAS BEEN SEVERELY LIMITED BY THE TYPE OF DETECTION SIGNAL, SPATIAL SEPARATION REQUIREMENTS (COMPARTMENTALIZATION), OR THE INCREASING CONSUMABLES AND EQUIPMENT COSTS. THE QMAP TECHNOLOGY OVERCOMES THE LIMITATIONS OF TARGET MULTIPLEXITY, OPERATING ENTIRELY IN A SINGLE WELL WHILE MINIMIZING SAMPLE LOSS, DILUTION, COMPLEXITY OF OPERATION, AND REAGENT USAGE. QMAP ENABLES ONE-POT SIMULTANEOUS SCREENING OF OVER 100 UNIQUE TARGETS, DEMONSTRATING STRONG POTENTIAL FOR NEONATAL SEPSIS DIAGNOSTICS, WHERE RAPID AND COMPREHENSIVE PATHOGEN IDENTIFICATION AND RESISTANCE PROFILING ARE CRITICAL.

description: PHIOGEN’S MISSION IS TO EXPLORE THE MICROBIAL WORLD FOR BACTERIOPHAGES WITH NOVEL THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA HIGHLIGHT A BREAKTHROUGH DISCOVERY WITH A FIRST-IN-CLASS SOLUTION OF DUAL ACTION THERAPEUTICS: A SERIES OF PHAGES THAT NOT ONLY DEMONSTRATE STRONG EFFICACY AGAINST ANTIMICROBIAL-RESISTANT (AMR) BACTERIA BUT ALSO CONFERRED LONG-TERM PROTECTION AGAINST REINFECTION WITHOUT REQUIRING A SECOND TREATMENT. THE LEADING HYPOTHESIS IS THAT CERTAIN PHAGES, BY UNIQUELY LYSING OUR BACTERIAL TARGETS, ELICIT A PROINFLAMMATORY RESPONSE THAT SUBSEQUENTLY ACTIVATES ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY AGAINST SPECIFIC BACTERIAL ANTIGENS. THIS IMMUNE PRIMING MAY PREVENT FUTURE INFECTIONS. TRADITIONALLY, MEDICAL INTERVENTIONS HAVE BEEN EITHER PROACTIVE (E.G., VACCINES) OR REACTIVE (E.G., THERAPIES). THE DISCOVERY AND INVESTIGATION PRESENTED HERE IS HIGHLY INNOVATIVE AND SIGNIFICANT, AS WE SUGGEST A NEW CLASS OF DUAL ACTION THERAPEUTICS, ONES THAT ACTS BOTH AS A TREATMENT AND INDUCES A PROTECTIVE RESPONSE AGAINST A SECOND INFECTION. GLOBALLY, SIX BACTERIAL SPECIES ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE MAJORITY OF THE 5 MILLION ANNUAL DEATHS DUE TO ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE, THE SO-CALLED "ESKAPE" SPECIES. WITH THE BACKING OF VARIOUS FUNDERS AND COLLABORATORS, PHIOGEN HAS ASSEMBLED A COLLECTION OF DOZENS OF NOVEL PHAGES TARGETING THESE HIGH-PRIORITY AMR PATHOGENS. FOR THESE PATHOGENS, THERAPEUTIC OPTIONS ARE SCARCE, AND NO VACCINES CURRENTLY EXIST. DEMONSTRATING THAT SOME OF THESE PHAGES POSSESS DUAL THERAPY-IMMUNIZATION PROPERTIES WOULD REPRESENT A PARADIGM SHIFT IN INFECTIOUS DISEASE TREATMENT AND PREVENTION.

description: KINVARD BIO AIMS TO BUILD UPON RESEARCH FROM THE LABORATORY OF PR. ANDY MYERS AT HARVARD UNIVERSITY WHICH HAS DELIVERED A HIGHLY PROMISING SERIES OF NEXT GENERATION LINCOSAMIDE ANTIBIOTICS, COLLECTIVELY TERMED THE OXEPANOPROLINAMIDES (OPPS). THIS RESEARCH UTILIZED CHEMICAL SYNTHESIS TO ACCESS LINCOSAMIDE ANALOGS WITH SIGNIFICANT SCAFFOLD MODIFICATIONS INACCESSIBLE BY SEMI-SYNTHETIC METHODS. THIS EFFORT SUCCESSFULLY DELIVERED LEAD COMPOUNDS THAT ARE HIGHLY ACTIVE IN BACTERIA EXPRESSING DIVERSE RESISTANCE MECHANISMS WHICH RENDER CLINDAMYCIN (AND OTHER RIBOSOME TARGETING ANTIBIOTICS) INEFFECTIVE. INFORMED BY THE DATA GENERATED BY THE PREVIOUS COLLABORATION BETWEEN CARB-X AND THE MYERS LAB AT HARVARD, OUR CURRENT PROGRAM AIMS TO FURTHER PROFILE THE MOST PROMISING LEAD COMPOUND WHILE CONDUCTING A FOCUSED LEAD OPTIMIZATION (LO) CAMPAIGN. WE WILL CHARACTERIZE KEY FEATURES OF THE OPP CLASS AND DEVELOP TOOLS TO MOST EFFECTIVELY EXECUTE THE LO EFFORT. THE LO PROGRAM AIMS TO PRODUCE NEW OPPS WITH INCREASED CHEMICAL DIVERSITY AND ENHANCED ANTIBACTERIAL ACTIVITY WHILE MAINTAINING THE FAVORABLE ATTRIBUTES OF THE CLASS. ULTIMATELY, THESE ACTIVITIES SEEK TO DELIVER A DEVELOPMENT CANDIDATE TO ADDRESS THE NEED FOR NEW ORAL THERAPIES IN THE TREATMENT OF COMMUNITY ACQUIRED BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA (CABP) AND ACUTE SKIN AND SKIN STRUCTURE INFECTIONS (ABSSSI).

description: STATEMENT OF WORK MY GROUP WILL BE ENGAGED IN TWO MAJOR ACTIVITIES AS PART OF THIS CEIRR CENTER: 1. LONGITUDINAL, EPIDEMIOLOGICAL, AND EVOLUTIONARY MODELING AS PART OF THE “PATHOGENESIS AND IMMUNE RESPONSE RESEARCH” COMPONENT, PROJECTS 1 AND 3. IN PROJECT 1, WE WILL DEVELOP INDIVIDUAL, LONGITUDINAL MODELS TO UNDERSTAND THE DEVELOPMENT OF IMMUNITY AND PROTECTION TO INFLUENZA OVER TIME, WITH A PARTICULAR FOCUS ON UNDERSTANDING THE EVOLUTION OF ANTIBODY SPECIFICITY AND CONSEQUENCES FOR PROTECTION AND TRANSMISSION. WE WILL ALSO PROVIDE BROAD STATISTICAL SUPPORT FOR THE WORK CONDUCTED IN PROJECT 1. DR. COBEY WITH CO-LEAD ALL ACTIVITIES IN PROJECT 3, WHICH FOCUSES ON PREDICTING VIRAL EVOLUTIONARY AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL DYNAMICS ON A GLOBAL SCALE. HER FOCUS WILL BE ON INTEGRATING AIMS 2 AND 3, WHICH INVOLVES FORECASTING THE DYNAMICS OF CLADES, SUBTYPES, AND TYPES USING POPULATION-LEVEL TIMES SERIES OF CASES AND IMMUNE PROFILES. THESE MODELS WILL FURTHER BE RECONCILED WITH THOSE IN PROJECT 1. 2. MY GROUP WILL LEAD THE COMPUTATIONAL CORE. THE CORE’S MAJOR ACTIVITIES WILL BE EXPANDED ANALYSES USING DATA FROM MULTIPLE CENTERS TO (1) FORECAST VIRAL EVOLUTION AND EPIDEMIOLOGY, (2) UNDERSTAND IMMUNE CORRELATES OF RISK, PROTECTION, VACCINE FAILURE, AND TRAMISSION, AND (3) ANALYZE OTHER ASPECTS OF THE IMMUNE RESPONSE TO INFLUENZA, INFLUENZA DYNAMICS, AND VACCINATION. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL DEVELOP NOVEL BIOINFORMATIC TOOLS TO (4) INFER ANTIBODY SPECIFICITY, (5) ASSESS SELECTION USING MUTANT LIBRARIES, (6) VISUALIZE VIRAL EVOLUTION, AND (7) DEVELOP NEW ANTIGENIC MAPS GIVEN HOSTS’ COMPLEX IMMUNE HISTORIES. MY GROUP WILL COORDINATE THESE ACTIVITIES AND TAKE THE LEAD ON SEVERAL, ESPECIALLY (2), (3), (4), AND (7). IN ADDITION, WE WILL IDENTIFY MODELING OPPORTUNITIES AND COORDINATE MODELING EFFORTS BETWEEN THE CENTERS, INCREASE MODELING CAPACITY, AND ASSIST WITH STUDY DESIGN AND DATA INTEGRATION. WE WILL ALSO SUPPORT MODELING EFFORTS IN OTHER COMPONENTS OF THE CENTER, FOR INSTANCE, RELATED TO PROJECT 2 OR PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS.

description: THE MEDICINAL CHEMISTRY FOCUS ON PI4K IS TO IDENTIFY A NOVEL SERIES OF BACK-UP COMPOUNDS THAT ARE DIVERSE WITH OFF-TARGET TOXICITY AS WELL AS PHARMACOKINETIC PROPERTIES. ACME IS BEST SITED TO PERFORM THIS WORK GIVEN THEIR PREVIOUS EXPERIENCE IN SYNTHESIZING A LARGE A RANGE OF PI4K MOLECULES IN A TIMELY FASHION. THE COMPANY WILL SYNTHESIZE CHEMICALS THAT ARE DESIGNED BY THE STANFORD MEDICINAL CHEMISTS. THE SCOPE OF CHEMISTRY ACTIVITIES: TYPICAL ACTIVITIES INCLUDE SYNTHESIS OF FOCUSED COMPOUND LIBRARIES (TYPICALLY 20-200 COMPOUNDS PER LIBRARY) ON A SCALE OF 10-50 MG AND PURITY OF >95%. PROVIDE RELEVANT ANALYTICAL DATA INCLUDING 1H, 13C NMR AND LCMS. SYNTHESIS (TYPICALLY >50 MG) OF ANALOGS OF EACH STRUCTURE TO SUPPORT LEAD OPTIMIZATION AND LEAD SERIES IDENTIFICATION ACTIVITIES. SYNTHESIS OF KEY REFERENCE COMPOUNDS IN THE 0.5-5 G RANGE AND A PURITY OF ~95-98% (>98% WHEN RELEVANT). SYNTHESIS OF KEY INTERMEDIATES ON 5-50 G SCALE AND A PURITY OF ~95%. SCALE-UP OF SELECTED COMPOUNDS FOR ADVANCED IN-VIVO STUDIES ON A SCALE OF 5-50 G AND PURITY OF 95% (>98% WHEN RELEVANT). DEVISING CHEMICAL SYNTHETIC ROUTES WHEN NECESSARY. TECHNICAL JUSTIFICATION WHEN FACTORING IN THE ANTICIPATED EXTRA FEES AND LACK OF CLOSE PROXIMITY, COMBINED WITH A LONG- STANDING TRACK RECORD OF PRODUCTIVE AND COST-EFFECTIVE WORK DONE BY ACME ON OUR BEHALF, THEY WERE FELT TO BE THE OVERALL BEST VALUE.

description: SCOPE OF WORK STATEMENT THE SCOPE OF WORK STATEMENT MUST INCLUDE THE PROJECT TITLE, START/END DATES, PI NAME, AND PROJECT DESCRIPTION (INCLUDING OBJECTIVES, TASKS, AND DELIVERABLES). WHILE EXACT EXPERIMENTAL OR PROCEDURAL INFORMATION IS NOT NECESSARY, THE SCOPE OF WORK STATEMENT SHOULD PROVIDE SUFFICIENT DETAIL ABOUT THE PROPOSED WORK TO ALLOW SOMEONE REVIEWING THE STATEMENT AND WHO WAS FAMILIAR WITH THE PROJECT TO DETERMINE WHETHER OR NOT THE WORK AGREED TO WAS ACTUALLY PERFORMED PROJECT TITLE: TUBERCULOSIS EPIDEMIOLOGIC STUDIES CONSORTIUM III (TBESCIII) ESTIMATED DATES: 9/29/2021 TO 3/28/2026 SUBCONTRACTOR PI NAME: AMY SHEN TANG, MD, DIRECTOR OF IMMIGRANT HEALTH, NORTH EAST MEDICAL SERVICES PROJECT DESCRIPTION (INCLUDING OBJECTIVES, TASKS, AND DELIVERABLES AS APPLICABLE): OBJECTIVE: IDENTIFY INTERVENTIONS THAT ARE COST-EFFECTIVE IN INCREASING TB TESTING AND LTBI TREATMENT AND COMPLETION AMONG FOREIGN-BORN PERSONS SEEKING PRIMARY CARE IN A COMMUNITY HEALTH SETTING TASKS: IF AWARDED TBESCIII FUNDS, NORTH EAST MEDICAL SERVICES (NEMS) WILL EXECUTE A MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING AND/OR DATA USE AGREEMENT WITH UCSF AT THE START OF THE PROJECT PERIOD. NEMS WITH THEN WORK WITH DR. PRIYA SHETEÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S TEAM AT UCSF TO DESIGN A STUDY PROTOCOL FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF NEW OR ENHANCED SYSTEMS-, PROVIDER-, AND PATIENT-LEVEL INTERVENTIONS THAT PROMOTE TB SCREENING, TESTING AND LTBI TREATMENT AT NEMSÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ VARIOUS CLINIC SITES. NEMS WILL INVOLVE KEY PERSONNEL IN IT, INFORMATICS, AND ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS (EHR) DEPARTMENTS TO HELP WITH DATA EXTRACTION AND MAKE EHR MODIFICATIONS THAT WILL IMPROVE AND OPTIMIZE LTBI CARE CASCADE WORKFLOWS. NEMS WILL RECRUIT ADMINISTRATIVE PERSONNEL TO ENSURE COMPLIANCE WITH STUDY PROTOCOLS AND SMOOTH IMPLEMENTATION OF MULTIPHASE STUDY INTERVENTIONS AT VARIOUS SITES. NEMS WILL ALSO RECRUIT KEY CLINICAL STAFF INCLUDING PHARMACISTS AND MID-LEVEL PRACTITIONERS FOR IMPLEMENTING CLINICAL INTERVENTIONS, AND PATIENT OUTREACH COORDINATORS/COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS WHO WILL CONDUCT CULTURALLY SENSITIVE TB OUTREACH AND EDUCATION AND OTHER SERVICES ADDRESSING SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH. DELIVERABLES: 1. EXECUTE MOU (WITHIN 2 MONTHS OF AWARD) AND DUAS AS NEEDED 2. IMPLEMENT AGREED UPON STUDY PROTOCOLS/INTERVENTIONS ACCORDING TO STUDY TIMELINE 3. SUBMIT BASELINE AND QUARTERLY EHR DATA REPORTS TO UCSF FOR ANALYSIS

description: THE ADJUVANT DISCOVERY CONTRACT WILL IDENTIFY, CHARACTERIZE, AND ADVANCE NOVEL SYNTHETIC CLR-BASED ADJUVANTS FOR USE IN COMBINATION WITH BACTERIAL AND FUNGAL ANTIGENS TO INDUCE A SAFE AND DURABLE TH17 AND/OR TH17/TH1 IMMUNITY. THIS PROPOSAL BRINGS TOGETHER HIGHLY EXPERIENCED RESEARCH TEAMS FROM THE UNIVERSITY OF MONTANA, INIMMUNE CORPORATION, UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO, AND UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS AT SAN ANTONIO, EACH WITH UNIQUE EXPERTISE AND PREVIOUS EXPERIENCE IN THE DISCOVERY AND DEVELOPMENT OF INNOVATIVE VACCINES AND ADJUVANTS. DRS. EVANS AND RIEL, AND COLLEAGUES AT UM WILL LEAD THE DISCOVERY EFFORTS AND COORDINATE ACTIVITIES OF ALL SUBCONTRACTORS. THE RESEARCH TEAM AT UM WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR COMPOUNDS LIBRARY SYNTHESIS, SAR STUDIES, MECHANISM OF ACTION STUDIES, RECEPTOR IDENTIFICATION, EARLY LIFE IMMUNITY (CORD BLOOD AND NEONATAL MICE), FORMULATION, MULTIVALENT DISPLAY, SAFETY ASSESSMENTS AND IMMUNOGENICITY STUDIES. DR. RASHEED AND COLLEAGUES AT INIMMUNE CORPORATION WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH THE TEAM FROM UM TO COMPLETE THE PRIMARY HTRF HIGH THROUGHPUT SCREEN OF COMPOUND LIBRARIES AND ASSIST WITH MEDICINAL CHEMISTRY SAR AND ANALYTICAL CHEMISTRY WITH LEAD SCAFFOLDS. DR. KHADER AND COLLEAGUES AT UCHICAGO WILL PROVIDE M72 ANTIGEN IN SUFFICIENT QUANTITY AND QUALITY TO SUPPORT FORMULATION OPTIMIZATION AND PRE-CLINICAL IMMUNOLOGY. THE TEAM AT UCHICAGO WILL ALSO CONDUCT MURINE VACCINATION AND MTB CHALLENGE STUDIES IN C57BL/6 MICE AND EVALUATE ADJUVANT SAFETY AND MECHANISMS OF CLR-MEDIATED EFFICACY, PROTECTION, AND DURABILITY. THE TEAM AT UCHICAGO ALSO BRINGS SPECIALIZED EXPERTISE IN THE MECHANISM OF PROTECTION AND A WIDE ARRAY OF ANTIGENS AND MULTIOMICS APPROACHES FOR EVALUATING NOVEL ADJUVANTS. DR. CHIUNG-YU HUNG AND COLLEAGUES AT UTSA ARE EXPERTS IN FUNGAL DISEASE MODELS AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF VACCINES FOR INVASIVE FUNGAL DISEASE. DR. HUNG WILL PROVIDE RCPA1 ANTIGEN IN SUFFICIENT QUANTITY AND QUALITY TO SUPPORT FORMULATION OPTIMIZATION AND PRE-CLINICAL IMMUNOLOGY AND CONDUCT MURINE COCCIDIOIDES VACCINATION AND CHALLENGE STUDIES IN BOTH C57BL/6 AND HUMAN HLA-DR4 TRANSGENIC MICE. INDEPENDENTLY, AND NOT AS AN AGENT OF THE GOVERNMENT, THE SUBCONTRACTOR (INIMMUNE) SHALL FURNISH ALL NECESSARY SERVICES, QUALIFIED PROFESSIONAL, TECHNICAL, AND ADMINISTRATIVE PERSONNEL, MATERIAL, EQUIPMENT AND FACILITIES, NOT OTHERWISE PROVIDED BY THE GOVERNMENT UNDER THE TERMS OF THIS CONTRACT, AS NEEDED TO PERFORM THE TASKS SET FORTH BELOW.

description: LE SAGE SCOPE OF WORK FOR PENN-CEIRR OPTION 18.L THIS CEIRR CONCEPT PROPOSAL HAS TWO DISTINCT AIMS THAT WILL ENABLE CHARACTERIZATION OF H5N1 HIGHLY PATHOGENIC AVIAN INFLUENZA (HPAI) VIRUS IN TERMS OF HOST AND ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS THAT AFFECT TRANSMISSIBILITY. H5N1 HPAI STRAINS THAT ARE IMPORTANT TO THE DAIRY CATTLE OUTBREAK WILL BE ASSESS IN THE FOLLOWING AIMS. THERE ARE MANY IN VITRO CHARACTERISTICS THAT HAVE AN IMPACT ON EFFICIENT TRANSMISSION OF INFLUENZA VIRUS. IN AIM 1, I WILL CHARACTERIZE H5N1 HPAI STRAINS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND HOST TROPISM AND ENVIRONMENTAL STABILITY. THE FOLLOWING TASKS WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED: 1. EXAMINE REPLICATION KINETICS OF H5N1 HPAI IN PRIMARY HUMAN AIRWAY EPITHELIAL CELLS AND COMPARE IT TO A SEASONAL INFLUENZA VIRUS. 2. PERFORM SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING ON THE INFECTED PRIMARY HUMAN AIRWAY EPITHELIAL CELLS TO COMPARE HOST TROPISM BETWEEN H5N1 HPAI AND SEASONAL INFLUENZA VIRUS. 3. COMPARE THE SECRETED CYTOKINES AND CHEMOKINES FROM H5N1 HPAI OR SEASONAL INFLUENZA VIRUS INFECTED PRIMARY HUMAN AIRWAY EPITHELIAL CELLS USING LUMINEX ASSAY. 4. DETERMINE THE ENVIRONMENTAL STABILITY UNDER A RANGE OF RELATIVE HUMIDITIES IN STATIONARY DROPLETS THAT CONTAIN MUCUS, COLLECTED FROM PRIMARY HUMAN AIRWAY EPITHELIAL CELLS. PRE-EXISTING IMMUNITY IS AN IMPORTANT BARRIER TO INFLUENZA VIRUS TRANSMISSION. IN AIM 2, I WILL ASSESS THE IMPACT OF SEASONAL VACCINATION IN FERRETS PRIOR TO CHALLENGE WITH H5N1 HPAI. THE FOLLOWING TASKS WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED: 1. PERFORM FERRET PATHOGENESIS AND SURVIVAL STUDIES IN FERRETS THAT HAVE BEEN VACCINATED WITH A SEASONAL INFLUENZA VIRUS THREE MONTHS PRIOR TO INTRANASAL CHALLENGE. 2. AS AIRBORNE TRANSMISSION IS NOT EFFICIENT FOR HPAI STRAINS, I WILL LEVERAGE THE AEROBIOLOGY CORE AT THE UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH TO COMPARE THE SUSCEPTIBILITY OF VACCINATED FERRETS TO AEROSOL CHALLENGE OF H5N1 HPAI CHALLENGE. 3. PERFORM SEROLOGICAL ASSAYS TO DETERMINE THE LEVELS OF CROSS-REACTIVE HA AND NA ANTIBODIES GENERATED BY THESE VACCINATED FERRETS BEFORE AND AFTER CHALLENGE.

description: LAKDAWALA STATEMENT OF WORK IN THIS CEIRR APPLICATION, THE LAKDAWALA LAB AT THE UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH WILL LEVERAGE OUR INFLUENZA TRANSMISSION AND PATHOGENESIS EXPERTISE TO ASSIST IN MULTIPLE PROJECTS. IN ADDITION, WE USE OUR EXTENSIVE KNOWLEDGE OF VIRAL PROPERTIES THAT PROMOTE AIRBORNE TRANSMISSION OF INFLUENZA VIRUSES TO CHARACTERIZE EMERGING ZOONOTIC STRAINS EACH YEAR. OUR SPECIFIC STATEMENT OF WORK FOR EACH ELEMENT OF THE CEIRR APPLICATION IS DETAILED BELOW. REQUIRED #3: INFLUENZA SURVEILLANCE, RISK ASSESSMENT AND RESPONSE TASKS: 1. ASSESS THE REPLICATION OF EMERGING SWINE AND AVIAN VIRUSES IN PRIMARY HUMAN BRONCHIAL EPITHELIAL CELLS. 2. ASSIST IN MOLECULAR CHARACTERIZATION OF EMERGING SWINE AND AVIAN VIRUSES. REQUIRED #4: PRE-PANDEMIC AND PANDEMIC RESPONSE TASKS: 1. PERFORM FERRET PATHOGENESIS STUDIES FOR 1-3 INFLUENZA VIRUSES PER YEAR. (UP TO 12 ANIMALS PER YEAR) 2. THE WORK UNDER THIS CONTRACT MAY INCLUDE THE POSSIBLE DISTRIBUTION OF DE-IDENTIFIED HUMAN SUBJECT PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMC), SERUM, AND OTHER CLINICAL SAMPLES TO SCRI AND THE PHOENIX PARTNERS. NON-HUMAN PRIMATE (NHP) SAMPLES AND/OR DOWNSTREAM DATA MAY BE SHARED WITH THE PARTNERS ON THIS CONTRACT. RYAN MCNAMARA, WHO HAS PREVIOUSLY BEEN EMPLOYED AT THE RAGON INSTITUTE, TO DEVELOP A WORKPLAN FOR THE SYSTEM SEROLOGY ENDPOINTS FOR BOTH CLINICAL AND PRECLINICAL EVALUATIONS. WE HAVE CONFIRMED THAT A LIST OF 207 M.TB ANTIGENS THAT WERE RECENTLY PUBLISHED ARE NOT PROPRIETARY TO RAGON AND ARE AN APPROPRIATE SET FOR OUR INVESTIGATIONS. SYSTEMS SEROLOGY CAPTURES LARGE NUMBERS OF DISTINCT ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC SERUM-BASED ANTIBODY PROFILE FEATURES THAT COMPREHENSIVELY AND OBJECTIVELY PROBES THE ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC FC-ANTIBODY-OME AT UNPRECEDENTED DEPTH. DISPARATE 53 DATA POINTS WILL BE INTEGRATED AND A SPECTRUM OF COMPUTATIONAL METHODS FOR CONSTRUCTING MULTI-VARIATE MODELS AND THEN APPLIED TO ASCERTAIN PREDICTIVE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN COMBINATIONS OF SYSTEM VARIABLES (STRUCTURE:FUNCTION, TRANSFER, ETC.) TO DEFINE NOVEL AND OFTEN UNEXPECTED INSIGHTS INTO THE ANTIBODY CHARACTERISTICS THAT DRIVE UNIQUE AND DISTINCT BIOLOGICAL OUTCOMES. description: 3.1 SCOPE IN THIS PROJECT, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP NEW IMMUNE-ENHANCING FORMULATIONS BY DISCOVERING AND OPTIMIZING SMALL MOLECULE MODULATORS THAT IMPROVE INNATE IMMUNE ACTIVATION TO SUPPORT ENHANCED T-CELL RESPONSES DURING VACCINATION. BUILDING ON PRELIMINARY WORK THAT IDENTIFIED PME-564 AS A POTENT MODULATOR OF NF RELATED COMPOUNDS THAT ACHIEVE AN OPTIMAL BALANCE OF IMMUNE ACTIVATION AND SAFETY. THESE COMPOUNDS WILL BE TESTED IN MULTIPLE FORMULATION TYPES TO ASSESS THEIR ABILITY TO POTENTIATE VACCINEINDUCED T-CELL RESPONSES WITHOUT INDUCING EXCESSIVE INFLAMMATION. WE HAVE TWO GOALS: (1) IDENTIFY A FORMULATION CANDIDATE THAT CAN BE RAPIDLY ADMIXED WITH EITHER CURRENT QUADRIVALENT VACCINES OR VACCINES. PAIRING THESE FORMULATIONS WITH THE HIGHEST PERFORMING VACCINE PLATFORM TO DEVELOP VACCINE CANDIDATES. IMPROVING REACTOGENICITY, REDUCING DOSAGE, AND INCREASING DURABILITY OF EACH VACCINE. PRE-CLINICAL NEXT-GENERATION VACCINES VACCINES, DETERMINING AN APPROPRIATE TOXICITY AND SAFETY PROFILE FOR BOTH THE INDEPENDENT AND MIXED FORMULATION. THIS NEW APPROACH ADDRESSES A LIMITATION IN CURRENT ADJUVANT TECHNOLOGY. ADJUVANTS TRANSITIONING OUT OF BASIC DISCOVERY HAVE LIMITED METHODS TO CONTROL EXCESS INFLAMMATION IN THE FORM OF INCREASED CYTOKINES – REPRESENTED BY EXCESS TNF 6 PRODUCTION. THE FOCUS OF THIS SUPPLEMENTAL PROGRAM WILL BE THE CO-FORMULATION OF THESE MOLECULES WITH VACCINES, SPECIFICALLY IN THE CONTEXT OF NEXT-GENERATION VACCINES. FORMULATIONS DO HELP ADDRESS THIS PROBLEM TO SOME EXTENT, BUT THEY DO NOT ADDRESS THE FUNDAMENTAL ACTIVITY OF THE COMPOUND, WHICH GENERATES A LARGE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE AT THE CELLULAR LEVEL. OUR APPROACH DIRECTLY TARGETS THE PATHWAY THAT CAUSES THIS EXCESSIVE AND OFTEN SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION AND REDUCES IT. THE ADDED BENEFIT IS THAT BECAUSE THE MODULATION OCCURS INDEPENDENTLY OF THE AGONIST, IT CAN PROVIDE AN ADDED BENEFIT NOT JUST TO A SPECIFIC AGONIST BUT TO ANY , QUADRIVALENT, OR FLU VACCINE. THE RESULT IS COUNTER-INTUITIVE BUT EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED, A BROAD INCREASE IN ANTIBODY RESPONSES FOR THESE VACCINES. AS WELL, EXPERIMENTS IN FORMULATION, DOSAGE, AND CONCENTRATION WILL PROVIDE ESSENTIAL INFORMATION FOR DEFINING HOW IMMUNE-MODULATORS SUCH AS PME-564 ARE CONSIDERED IN USE IN VACCINE FORMULATIONS. WE WILL ALSO EXPLORE THE USE OF OUR IMMUNOMODULATOR IN THE CONTEXT OF DOSE SPARING FOR NEXTGENERATION VACCINES VACCINES. IF NEEDED, SEPARATE VIALS OF IMMUNOMODULATOR CAN BE CO-MIXED ON SITE OF VACCINATION WHICH WILL ENABLE DOSE SPARING FOR AVAILABLE VACCINES. WE WILL EXPLORE MAXIMAL AND MINIMAL DOSES OF IN COMBINATION WITH OUR IMMUNOMODULATORS TO SELECT THE BEST BALANCE BETWEEN DURABILITY, IMMUNOGENICITY, AND REACTOGENICITY. OUR PRIMARY OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP AN ADJUVANT FORMULATION THAT INCREASES THE T-CELL RESPONSES AND DURABILITY OF THOSE LEVELS FOR A PLATFORM OF VACCINES WITH A FOCUS ON FLU SYSTEMS WHILE MINIMIZING THE INFLAMMATORY EFFECTS UPON INJECTION. OUR SECONDARY OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP A NOVEL DERIVATIVE OF IMMUNOMODULATORY COMPOUND PME-564 AND RELATED DERIVATIVES AS A BROAD-SPECTRUM VACCINE ENHANCING OR DOSE SPARING EXCIPIENT THAT CAN BE USED AS PART OF MULTIPLE FORMULATIONS. TO IMPROVE THE OUTCOME OF THE FORMULATION AND TO DEVELOP A NOVEL DERIVATIVE OF PME-564 AND RELATED DERIVATIVES, WE WILL EXPLORE THE MECHANISM OF A SERIES OF CHEMICALLY SYNTHESIZED DERIVATIVES, OPTIMIZE THEIR STRUCTURE AND FORMULATION, AND TEST THEM AS ADJUVANTS WITH MULTIPLE FLU VACCINATION PLATFORMS. THESE VACCINE CANDIDATES WILL THEN BE TESTED FOR SAFETY, TOXICITY, AND THE ABILITY TO PROVIDE PROTECTION IN MOUSE CHALLENGE BEFORE BEING USED IN HIGHER ANIMAL MODELS.

description: STATEMENT OF WORK – PROJECT 3 OBJECTIVES. WE WILL TARGET HUMAN-SWINE INTERFACES IN MAJOR SWINE PRODUCTION REGIONS IN THE US, EUROPE, AND ASIA. COORDINATED SURVEILLANCE WITH SWINE AND HUMAN SAMPLE COLLECTION THAT LEVERAGES EXISTING SURVEILLANCE [E.G., US DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE (USDA) NATIONAL IAV IN SWINE (IAV-S) SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM AND VETERINARY DIAGNOSTIC LABS] WILL ALLOW US TO QUANTIFY DRIVERS OF IAV EVOLUTION IN THE SWINE HOST. OUR OVERALL OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP A RISK FRAMEWORK THAT ARTICULATES HOW ANTIGENIC DIVERSITY AND OTHER PHENOTYPIC PROPERTIES OF CIRCULATING SWINE IAVS AFFECT HUMAN PANDEMIC POTENTIAL AND INTERSPECIES TRANSMISSION. WE WILL DETERMINE THE PUBLIC HEALTH RISK OF CIRCULATING AND EMERGING IAVS IN GLOBAL SWINE POPULATIONS BY A COORDINATED AND SYSTEMATIC PIPELINE OF IN SILICO, IN VITRO, AND IN VIVO TESTING AND ANALYSES. SWINE IAV ISOLATES IDENTIFIED AS UNIQUE THROUGH SURVEILLANCE AND IN VIVO ANALYSES WILL BE CHARACTERIZED BY A IN VIVO AND IN VITRO PANDEMIC POTENTIAL PIPELINE AMONG CEIRR INVESTIGATORS. APPROACH. THIS OBJECTIVE WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED WITH 4 STREAMS OF SWINE VIROLOGIC DATA: 1) ACTIVE SURVEILLANCE IN CAMBODIA; 2) ACTIVE AND PASSIVE SURVEILLANCE IN THE UK; 3) ACTIVE AND PASSIVE SURVEILLANCE IN THE USA; AND 4) LEVERAGING THE USDA SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM AND ESTABLISHED SWINE INFLUENZA NETWORKS. HUMAN SAMPLING WILL OCCUR AT THE SWINE INTERFACE IN CAMBODIA AND THE USA. SEROLOGIC SPECIMENS WILL BE USED FROM OCCUPATIONALLY EXPOSED HUMAN COHORTS TO EVALUATE ANTIBODY RESPONSES TO SWINE IAV AND COMPARE TO URBAN HUMAN COHORTS. SEQUENCE ANALYSIS OF IAV-S WILL BE SUPPORTED BY DEDICATED SWINE COMPUTATIONAL EXPERTISE AND ANTIGENIC AND PHENOTYPIC CHARACTERIZATION OF SWINE IAV FOR ASSESSMENT OF RISK TO HUMANS CONDUCTED IN AND IN VIVO AND IN VITRO PANDEMIC POTENTIAL PIPELINE. EACH OF THESE COMPONENTS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO DEVELOPMENT OF A RISK RANKING METHOD FOR SWINE IAV. METHODS. AIM 1. INVESTIGATE DYNAMICS OF IAV AT HUMAN-SWINE INTERFACES THROUGH: A) LONGITUDINAL SURVEILLANCE FROM RELEVANT SWINE POPULATIONS AND HUMAN-SWINE INTERFACES TO INCLUDE CHARACTERIZATION OF IAV GENETIC DIVERSITY; AND B) COLLECTION OF OCCUPATIONALLY EXPOSED HUMAN COHORT SERA AND VIROLOGIC ASSESSMENT OF INTERSPECIES TRANSMISSION. AIM 2. DEVELOP PHYLOGENETIC ALGORITHMS THAT RAPIDLY IDENTIFY NOVEL REASSORTED VIRUSES, QUANTIFY VIRAL DIVERSITY BETWEEN SWINE AND HUMAN IAV, AND IDENTIFY SWINE IAV STRAINS TO TEST FOR ANTIGENIC ADVANCE OR INCREASED REPLICATION AND TRANSMISSION IN SWINE. AIM 3. ANTIGENIC AND PHENOTYPIC CHARACTERIZATION OF SWINE IAV FOR RISK TO HUMANS BY CHARACTERIZING VIRAL PROPERTIES IN THE SWINE HOST, SWINE-TO-FERRET TRANSMISSION, KEY PREDICTORS OF THE PANDEMIC RISK OF SWINE IAV, AND OTHER DOWNSTREAM MEDIATORS VIA COLLABORATION WITH CEIRR INVESTIGATORS. SCHEDULE. EACH OF THE INVESTIGATORS AND SITE LEADERS IN THIS PROJECT HAVE ESTABLISHED PROGRAMS TO QUICKLY IMPLEMENT SAMPLE FLOW FOR OUR CEIRR PROJECT. CLINICAL SAMPLES FROM LONGITUDINALLY SAMPLED SWINE WILL BE EVALUATED PERIODICALLY THROUGHOUT EACH YEAR, WHEREAS PASSIVE SURVEILLANCE BASED ON ROUTINE SUBMISSIONS TO THE VETERINARY DIAGNOSTIC LABORATORIES PARTICIPATING IN THIS PROPOSAL WILL IMMEDIATELY BEGIN TO ENTER THE PROJECT. VIRAL EVOLUTION AT THE GENETIC AND ANTIGENIC LEVELS WILL BE ASSESSED AT LEAST BI-ANNUALLY TO SELECT STRAINS FOR FURTHER CHARACTERIZATION. AUTOMATED SEQUENCE AND DATA ANALYSIS ALGORITHMS WILL BE DEVELOPED AND IMPLEMENTED TO ASSIST IN THE SELECTION PROCESS. EACH YEAR, SWINE AND FERRET SERA WILL BE RAISED FOR ANTIGENIC CHARACTERIZATION OF UP TO 6 UNIQUE SWINE IAV AND TO TEST AGAINST HUMAN POPULATION SERA, UP TO 3 STRAINS WILL BE ASSESSED FOR PHENOTYPING IN THE SWINE HOST, AND UP TO 2 STRAINS WILL BE ASSESSED FOR AEROSOL TRANSMISSION BETWEEN SWINE AND FERRETS. SWINE IAV RANKED AS HIGHER RISK FOR HUMANS WILL BE SHARED AMONG CEIRR INVESTIGATORS FOR DOWNSTREAM RISK ASSESSMENT STUDIES AND POTENTIAL PUBLIC HEALTH ACTION.

description: SCOPE OF WORK EVOLUTIONARY ALGORITHMS FOR PRIORITIZING INFLUENZA A VIRUSES FOR PANDEMIC RISK ASSESSMENT PI NAME: TAVIS ANDERSON START/END DATES: SEPTEMBER 2024 – SEPTEMBER 2026 PROJECT DESCRIPTION (INCLUDING OBJECTIVES, TASKS, AND DELIVERABLES AS APPLICABLE): WE WILL DEVELOP AN INTEGRATED COMPUTATIONAL PLATFORM FOR RAPIDLY ASSESSING THE ZOONOTIC AND PANDEMIC POTENTIAL OF A WIDE RANGE OF INFLUENZA A VIRUSES (IAV). THE COMPUTATIONAL PLATFORM WILL RANK THE IAV STRAINS FROM GENOMIC SURVEILLANCE IN NON-HUMAN POPULATIONS BASED ON THEIR ZOONOTIC RISK AND WILL ACCOUNT FOR (I) GENETIC AND ANTIGENIC DIVERSITY, (II) GEOGRAPHIC SPREAD, (III) DETECTION FREQUENCY, (IV) HOST BREADTH, (V) REASSORTMENT HISTORY, AND (VI) PHENOTYPIC PROPERTIES. THE PLATFORM AND DERIVED LISTS OF REPRESENTATIVE VIRUSES AND THEIR PREDICTED PHENOTYPIC PROPERTIES WILL BE AVAILABLE AS A RESOURCE TO ALL CEIRR RESEARCHERS. DELIVERABLES: 1. AN ACCURATE METHOD FOR REASSORTMENT ANALYSIS ON LARGE IAV DATASETS. AS REASSORTMENT PLAYS AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN THE EMERGENCE OF PANDEMIC IAV, WE WILL DEVELOP AND DEPLOY A METHOD FOR AUTOMATIC DETECTION OF REASSORTMENT FROM THE GENOMIC SURVEILLANCE DATA. WE WILL USE THE DETECTED REASSORTMENT EVENTS TO INFORM THE ZOONOTIC RISK ASSESSMENT AND IAV STRAIN RANKING, AND STUDY THE IMPACT OF REASSORTMENT ON PHENOTYPIC EVOLUTION OF IAV. 2. MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS FOR PREDICTING ZOONOSIS-ASSOCIATED PHENOTYPES. A. WE WILL DESIGN EFFECTIVE MACHINE LEARNING MODELS TO PREDICT THE ANTIGENIC NOVELTY OF NON-HUMAN IAV RELATIVE TO THE EXISTING VACCINE AND CANDIDATE VACCINE STRAINS. THE MODELS WILL BE TRAINED ON THE EXISTING HEMAGGLUTININ INHIBITION ASSAY (HI) DATA FOR SWINE AND AVIAN IAV. B. AN INTERPRETABLE MACHINE LEARNING METHOD FOR PREDICTING THE PH STABILITY OF THE IAV HEMAGGLUTININ PROTEIN WILL BE DEVELOPED, LEVERAGING THE PUBLISHED PH STABILITY AND PH OF INACTIVATION ASSAY DATA. 3. AN ALGORITHM FOR SELECTING MOST REPRESENTATIVE SETS OF NON-HUMAN IAV IN TERMS OF GENETIC AND/OR ANTIGENIC DIVERSITY AND RANKING THE REPRESENTATIVE STRAINS BASED ON THE ASSOCIATED ZOONOTIC RISK FACTORS. A. AN EFFICIENT ALGORITHMIC PIPELINE FOR CLUSTERING GENETICALLY AND/OR ANTIGENICALLY SIMILAR IAV WILL BE DEVELOPED WITH MOST REPRESENTATIVE STRAINS BEING SELECTED FROM WITHIN EACH CLUSTER. B. WE WILL DESIGN A ZOONOTIC RISK METRIC THAT INTEGRATES THE PREDICTED PHENOTYPIC PROPERTIES FOR EACH IAV, REASSORTMENT STATUS, DETECTION FREQUENCY, GEOGRAPHIC AND HOST SPREAD. C. A USER-FRIENDLY INTERFACE WILL BE DEVELOPED TO ALLOW RESEARCHERS TO SELECT MOST REPRESENTATIVE IAV STRAINS FOR CONSEQUENT IN VITRO AND IN VIVO STUDIES, AND VIEW THE RISK SCORES OF INDIVIDUAL STRAINS TOGETHER WITH A DETAILED BREAKDOWN OF EACH FACTOR CONTRIBUTING TO THE OVERALL RISK SCORE.

description: IOWA STATE UNIVERSITY SCOPE OF WORK THIS IS A 7 YEAR PROJECT INVOLVING SURVEILLANCE FOR INFLUENZA A VIRUS IN SWINE. SAMPLING WILL OCCUR ON BOTH PIGS AND HUMANS. WE WILL IDENTIFY AND TARGET UP TO 4 BREEDING/FARROWING AND NURSERY SWINE FARMS EVERY YEAR FOR MONTHLY SAMPLE COLLECTION. THE FARMS WILL HAVE A HISTORY OR KNOWN STATUS OF INFLUENZA A INFECTION OR OUTBREAKS IN THE PIGS. AT EACH FARM, WE WILL COLLECT, 32 NASAL SWABS, 10 UDDER WIPES, 4 ORAL FLUIDS, 7 HUMAN NASAL MUCOUS WIPES, AND ONE VETERINARIAN NASAL MUCOUS WIPE. ONCE PER YEAR, A PHLEBOTOMIST WILL COLLECT A HUMAN SERUM SAMPLE, WHICH WILL INCLUDE 32 SERA FROM THE 4 PRODUCTION SYSTEMS AND 50 VETERINARIAN SERA AT A MAJOR SWINE MEETING. THE HUMAN SUBJECTS WILL ALSO ANSWER AN INFLUENZA RELATED QUESTIONNAIRE PROVIDED BY ISU. ALL SAMPLES WILL BE TESTED VIA PCR FOR INFLUENZA H1 & H3. VIRUS ISOLATION WILL BE ATTEMPTED ON POSITIVE SAMPLES. ALL TESTING WILL OCCUR IN THE LABORATORY OF THE PRIMARY INVESTIGATOR (GAUGER) OR THROUGH THE ISU VDL. THE ULTIMATE GOAL IS TO ISOLATE AN AVERAGE OF 4 INFLUENZA A VIRUSES OR MORE PER MONTH (336 OVER THE 7 YEAR PERIOD). THESE SAMPLES WILL BE SHARED WITH THE UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE (USDA) FOR FURTHER CHARACTERIZATION AND TESTING.

description: SCOPE OF WORK IN THIS CONTRACT, THE BOYD LAB WILL CARRY OUT THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES: PROJECT 1: CREATE ANTIBODY GENE SEQUENCE LIBRARIES FROM A MICHIGAN HUMAN COHORT AND, SUBJECT TO AVAILABILITY, A HONG KONG HUMAN SUBJECT COHORT, FROM PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS OF SAMPLES TAKEN DURING SURVEILLANCE FOR INFLUENZA INFECTION, OR PRIOR TO AND FOLLOWING INFLUENZA VACCINATION. THESE LIBRARIES WILL BE SEQUENCED USING THE ILLUMINA MISEQ INSTRUMENT. DATA WILL BE ANALYZED TO EVALUATE B CELL CLONAL POPULATIONS AND CANDIDATE VACCINE-RESPONSIVE B CELLS. PROJECT 2: FROM A HUMAN COHORT IN PENNSYLVANIA, CREATE ANTIBODY GENE SEQUENCE LIBRARIES FROM PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS OF SAMPLES TAKEN DURING SURVEILLANCE FOR INFLUENZA INFECTION, OR PRIOR TO AND FOLLOWING INFLUENZA VACCINATION. THESE LIBRARIES WILL BE SEQUENCED USING THE ILLUMINA MISEQ INSTRUMENT. DATA WILL BE ANALYZED TO EVALUATE B CELL CLONAL POPULATIONS AND CANDIDATE VACCINE-RESPONSIVE B CELLS. IN ADDITION, INFLUENZASPECIFIC B CELLS WILL BE ISOLATED BY FLOW CYTOMETRIC SORTING FOLLOWING INFLUENZA VACCINATION, AND SINGLE-CELL PCR WILL BE CARRIED OUT TO AMPLIFY ANTIBODY HEAVY AND LIGHT CHAINS. WE WILL THEN SEQUENCE THOSE PCR AMPLICONS AND CLONE THEM INTO EXPRESSION VECTORS FOR GENERATION OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES. MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES WILL BE SHARED WITH OTHER PROJECT INVESTIGATORS FOR CHARACTERIZATION FOR BINDING TO INFLUENZA VACCINE COMPONENTS IN ELISA ASSAYS AND WITH HEMAGGLUTININ INHIBITION ASSAYS. WE WILL ANALYZE THE ANTIBODY GENE SEQUENCE DATA AND CORRELATE IT WITH THE BINDING AND OTHER PROTEIN ASSAY DATA FROM THE MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES GENERATED. IN ADDITION WE WILL SEQUENCE ANTIBODY GENE LIBRARIES GENERATED FROM FERRETS IN THIS PROJECT, AND ATTEMPT TO CLONE THE HEAVY AND LIGHT CHAIN GENE SEQUENCES FROM FERRET CELLS THAT BIND INFLUENZA ANTIGENS, TO EXPRESS THE ANTIBODIES AS PROTEIN FOR FURTHER CHARACTERIZATION BY OTHER PROJECT INVESTIGATORS. WE WILL ANALYZE THE FERRET ANTIBODY GENE SEQUENCE DATA BY COMPARING THEM TO THE HUMAN ANTIBODY DATA GENERATED IN PROJECTS 1 AND 2. ALL DATA GENERATED IN THE PROJECT WILL BE SHARED WITH THE OTHER PROJECT AND CORE INVESTIGATORS FOR JOINT ANALYSIS AND CORRELATION OTHER DATA INCLUDING CLINICAL AND VIRAL ANALYSES.

description: THE PURPOSE OF STUDIES AT THE HENNEPIN HEALTHCARE RESEARCH INSTITUTE (HHRI) SITE IS TO TEST LEAD VACCINES TARGETING HEROIN AND FENTANYL FOR THEIR ABILITY TO REDUCE THE ADDICTIVE EFFECTS OF THESE DRUGS IN RATS. IN ADDITION, HHRI WILL EXAMINE WHETHER COMBINING THESE VACCINES INTO A BIVALENT FORMULATION WILL ALTER THEIR EFFICACY. THE WORK REQUIRED TO ACCOMPLISH THIS INVOLVES A SERIES OF FIVE STUDIES IN WHICH THE EFFECTS OF VACCINATION ON HEROIN AND FENTANYL SELF-ADMINISTRATION AND WITHDRAWAL WILL BE EXAMINED IN RATS. THE FIRST EXPERIMENT WILL TEST THE EFFICACY OF A LEAD HEROIN AND BIVALENT VACCINE AT REDUCING HEROIN SELF-ADMINISTRATION (HSA). THE SECOND EXPERIMENT WILL TEST THE EFFICACY OF A LEAD FENTANYL AND BIVALENT VACCINE AT REDUCING FENTANYL SELF-ADMINISTRATION (FSA). THE THIRD EXPERIMENT WILL TEST THE EFFICACY OF THE BIVALENT VACCINE AT REDUCING COCAINE SELFADMINISTRATION TO CONFIRM THE BEHAVIORAL SPECIFICITY OF THE VACCINE. THE FOURTH AND FIFTH EXPERIMENTS WILL TEST WHETHER THE BIVALENT VACCINE PRECIPITATES HEROIN OR FENTANYL WITHDRAWAL, RESPECTIVELY, USING AN INTRACRANIAL SELF-STIMULATION ASSAY.

description: CENTAURI IS A PRIVATELY-OWNED BIOTECH COMPANY DEVELOPING NOVEL IMMUNOTHERAPEUTICS TO TREAT LIFE-THREATENING DISEASES. CENTAURI HAS A DEVELOPED AN IMMUNOTHERAPEUTIC PLATFORM (ALPHAMERS) THAT REDIRECTS PRE-EXISTING NATURAL ANTIBODIES TO TARGET SPECIFIC DISEASES WITH APPLICATIONS FOR CANCER AND INFECTIOUS DISEASE. ALPHAMERS ARE PART OF A LARGER FAMILY OF ANTIBODY RECRUITING MOLECULES (ARMS) DESIGNED TO REDIRECT A POTENT PRE-EXISTING IMMUNE RESPONSE AND THEREBY BRING ABOUT AN IMMEDIATE (WITHIN MINUTES) IMMUNOTHERAPEUTIC BENEFIT TO PATIENTS. THE ALPHAMER PLATFORM COMPRISES A TARGETING DOMAIN, THAT BINDS TO SPECIFICALLY TO THE BACTERIA, AN ANTIBODY-RECRUITING EFFECTOR DOMAIN THAT RECRUITS PRE-EXISTING NATURAL ANTI-GAL ANTIBODIES, AND PROPRIETARY LINKER TECHNOLOGY. ANTI-GAL ANTIBODIES ARE THE MOST ABUNDANT ANTIBODIES IN HUMANS, CONSTITUTING ABOUT 1% OF ALL IMMUNOGLOBULINS. THE ALPHAMER IS INTENDED TO RE-DIRECT THESE NATURALLY OCCURRING EFFECTOR ANTIBODIES WHICH ARE ALREADY PRESENT AT HIGH CONCENTRATIONS IN ALL PEOPLE TO TARGET BACTERIA FOR IMMUNE-MEDIATED DESTRUCTION, BY ACTIVATING THE COMPLEMENT CASCADE AND DESTROYING THE PATHOGEN THROUGH DIRECT LYSIS AND OPSONOPHAGOCYTOSIS. OUR LEAD PROGRAM (CTL-ABX01) TARGETS DRUG-SENSITIVE AND MULTI-DRUG RESISTANT (MDR) GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA, INCLUDING CLINICALLY RELEVANT STRAINS OF ENTEROBACTERIACEAE, PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA, AND ACINETOBACTER BAUMANNII. IN ADDITION TO RECRUITING THE IMMUNE SYSTEM, THE TARGETING DOMAIN OF THE ALPHAMER OF THE ABX01 PROGRAM HAS ALSO A DIRECT ANTIBACTERIAL EFFECT IN COMBINATION WITH ITS IMMUNOMODULATOR FUNCTION. AS SUCH, THE ALPHAMER SERVES AS A METHOD TO COMBINE THE POWER OF THE IMMUNE SYSTEM WITH DIRECT ANTIBACTERIAL ACTION IN ONE DRUG. THE AIM OF THIS PILOT PROJECT IS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE IMMUNE-MEDIATED TRANSLATION AND EFFICACY OF THE ALPHAMER IN VIVO BY EXECUTING APPROPRIATE DISEASE MODELS IN ORDER TO PREDICT AN EFFICACIOUS DOSE FOR HUMAN. PROJECT SUCCESS WOULD ENABLE US TO SELECT LEAD COMPOUNDS FOR CLINICAL CANDIDATE SELECTION STUDIES, COMPLETION OF PRE-IND-ENABLING STUDIES, AND CONDUCT OF A FIRST-IN-HUMAN STUDY.

description: STATEMENT OF WORK – FRED HUTCHINSON CANCER RESEARCH CENTER BLOOM LAB THE BLOOM LAB WILL PERFORM EXPERIMENTAL AND COMPUTATIONAL WORK TO CHARACTERIZE INFLUENZA VIRUS EVOLUTION. IN PROJECT 3, THEY WILL USE MUTATIONAL ANTIGENIC PROFILING TO EXPERIMENTALLY MAP THE EFFECTS OF VIRAL MUTATIONS ON IMMUNE RECOGNITION. IN THE COMPUTATIONAL CORE, THEY WILL DEVELOP TOOL TO ANALYZE AND VISUALIZE THE EFFECTS OF VIRAL MUTATIONS. BEDFORD LAB THE BEDFORD LAB AT THE FRED HUTCH WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF PROJECT 3, AIM 2 (PREDICT AND VISUALIZE WHICH CIRCULATING CLADES OF INFLUENZA WILL DOMINATE USING PHYLOGENETIC ANALYSES, AGE-STRUCTURED SEROLOGY, MUTATIONAL ANTIGENIC PROFILING, AND VACCINATION COVERAGE). FOR THIS, THE BEDFORD LAB WILL DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A PREDICTIVE MODEL THAT INCORPORATES DATA GENERATED BY THE BLOOM LAB FOR PROJECT 3, AIM 1 AS WELL AS OTHER SEROLOGICAL DATA GENERATED BY THE CENTER. THE BEDFORD LAB WILL INTEGRATE THIS SEROLOGICAL DATA WITH PUBLICLY AVAILABLE INFLUENZA GENETIC SEQUENCE DATA. THIS MODEL WILL ESTIMATE THE EVOLUTIONARY TRAJECTORY OF THE INFLUENZA VIRUS POPULATION. THE BEDFORD LAB WILL ALSO BE RESPONSIBLE FOR CONTRIBUTING KEY COMPONENTS TO THE MODELING AND COMPUTATIONAL CORE. THIS PRIMARILY CONSISTS OF USING THE EXISTING NEXTSTRAIN FRAMEWORK TO SUPPORT ANALYSIS AND SHARING OF DATA GENERATED BY THE CENTER. THE BEDFORD LAB ALREADY WORKS CLOSELY WITH WHO COLLABORATING CENTERS TO INTEGRATE AND ANALYZE INFLUENZA SEROLOGICAL AND SEQUENCE DATA. THE INTERACTION WITH THE CENTER SHOULD BE SIMILAR. THE BEDFORD LAB WILL DEVELOP A COMPUTATIONAL PREDICTIVE MODEL TO (1) ESTIMATE THE HUMAN POPULATION IMMUNE LANDSCAPE AGAINST DIFFERENT STRAINS OF SEASONAL INFLUENZA AND (2) PREDICT UPCOMING STRAIN DYNAMICS FOR THE INFLUENZA VIRUS POPULATION. DATA TO INFORM (1) WILL BE INTEGRATED FROM THE DEEP MUTATIONAL SCANNING (DMS) EXPERIMENTS CONDUCTED BY THE BLOOM LAB ALONGSIDE OTHER SEROLOGICAL DATA GENERATED BY OTHER STUDIES IN THE CENTER. WITH AN ESTIMATE OF POPULATION IMMUNITY IN HAND, WE WILL INFER FITNESS VALUES FOR CIRCULATING VIRUSES AND USE THESE FITNESS VALUES TO PREDICT WHETHER STRAINS INCREASE IN FREQUENCY OR DECLINE. THIS MODEL WILL BE IMPLEMENTED IN AN OPEN SOURCE PYTHON FRAMEWORK FOLLOWING OUR EXISTING STRAIN FORECASTING CODEBASE. THE PRIMARY ADDITIONS FOR THE CURRENT PROJECT ARE TO: (1) INTEGRATE HUMAN POPULATION IMMUNITY THROUGH DMS AND SEROLOGICAL DATA AND (2) INCORPORATE A GEOGRAPHICALLY STRUCTURED VIRUS POPULATION. THIS MODEL WILL BE RUN CONTINUALLY AS NEW DATA BECOMES AVAILABLE AND UP-TO-DATE FORECASTS PROVIDED FROM THE NEXTSTRAIN.ORG WEBSITE. THE BEDFORD LAB WILL EXTEND THE NEXTSTRAIN PLATFORM TO INTEGRATE AND SHARE DATA GENERATED BY THE CENTER. THE BEDFORD LAB WILL CREATE A NEW CEIRR NEXTSTRAIN GROUP THAT WILL HOUSE ALL THE CEIRR ANALYSES. THIS GROUP ALLOWS FOR BOTH PUBLIC DATASETS AND FOR PRIVATE DATASETS, BOTH OF WHICH SHOULD BE USEFUL FOR THESE PURPOSES. THE BEDFORD LAB WILL ALSO HOUSE A DATABASE OF SEROLOGICAL AND SEQUENCE DATA FOR CENTER PROJECTS CORRESPONDING TO THE WAY THE BEDFORD LAB CURRENTLY HOUSES WHO COLLABORATING CENTER DATA.

CORE LABORATORY FUNCTIONS: MHRI WILL PERFORM THE MINIMAL PROFICIENCY TESTING ASSAYS AND DOCUMENTATION REQUIRED TO MAINTAIN THE CAP ACCREDITATION FOR SHS ASSAYS, AS REQUIRED BY OUR TRIBAL AND SHS PARTNERS UNTIL ALL ASSAYS ARE COMPLETE AND RESULTS REPORTED.

description: STATEMENT OF WORK PI: MAƩHEW FRIEMAN UNIVERSITY OF MARYLAND, BALƟMORE PENN CEIRR OPƟON 18.L SEPTEMBER 11, 2024 IN THESE STUDIES, WE WILL DEVELOP AND USE A NOVEL PHAGE DISPLAY CORONAVIRUS SPIKE LIBRARY, SPIKE-SCAN, TO DETERMINE HOW VACCINE PLATFORM, FORMULATION OR COMBINATION SCHEME AƯECTS EPITOPE PRESENTATION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE DEVELOPMENT OF THIS DATA WILL AID IN OUR FUTURE VACCINE DEVELOPMENT TO DETERMINE HOW EACH OF THESE PARAMETERS AƯECTS EPITOPE SPREAD AND ULTIMATELY FUTURE PROOFING OF VACCINES. THIS NEW “SPIKE-SCAN” PLATFORM WILL BE USED TO ASSESS ANTIBODIES PRODUCED ACROSS MULTIPLE VACCINE PLATFORMS INCLUDING VARIANT SPIKE PROTEINS, NOVEL ADJUVANTS AND HUMAN MIX AND MATCH VACCINE STUDIES CONTROLLED CLINICAL TRIALS TO DETERMINE HOW VACCINE PLATFORM AND FORMULATION AƯECTS BREADTH OF COVERAGE. THE SPIKE-SCAN RESULTS COMBINED WITH TRADITIONAL ELISA AND NEUTRALIZATION STUDIES WILL BE USED TO INFORM FUTURE VACCINE DEVELOPMENT TO PRODUCE WIDER BREADTH AND QUANTIFIABLY HIGHER ANTIBODY RESPONSES. OUR GOAL IS TO DETERMINE AN OPTIMIZED COMBINATION OF ANTIGEN, ADJUVANT AND PLATFORM FOR FUTURE VACCINE DEVELOPMENT FOR CORONAVIRUSES. IN THIS PROJECT WE WILL FIRST PRODUCE A SPIKE DIRECTED CORONAVIRUS “SPIKE-SCAN” LIBRARY THAT INCLUDES ANIMAL AND HUMAN CORONAVIRUS SPIKE PROTEINS INCLUDING CURRENT SARS-COV-2 VARIANT SPIKE SEQUENCES. WE HAVE IDENTIFIED A BROAD SPECTRUM OF SPIKE PROTEINS ACROSS CORONAVIRUS LINEAGES THAT WILL ALLOW FOR DEEP PROFILING OF SERA FROM VACCINE STUDIES. UPON SUCCESSFUL CREATION OF THE SPIKE-SCAN LIBRARY, WE WILL ANALYZE SERUM FROM THE FOLLOWING SUBSETS: 1. NOVAVAX VARIANT SPIKE VACCINES, INCLUDING MULTIPLE SARS-COV-2 VARIANT SPIKES 2. HEXAPRO-WU1 SPIKE WITH VARIOUS ADJUVANTS TO EVALUATE CHANGES IN BREADTH OF COVERAGE 3. IMPRINTING MODELS TO ASSESS IMPACT OF PREVIOUS EXPOSURE 4. description: STATEMENT OF WORK FOR WILSON AND WARD LABS IN THIS PROJECT, WE WILL STRUCTURALLY AND BIOPHYSICALLY CHARACTERIZE NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES AND IMMUNE SERA DERIVED FROM NATURAL INFECTION BY INFLUENZA VIRUS AND FROM VACCINATION. THE WILSON LAB WILL EXPRESS AND PURIFY ANTIBODIES, ANTIGENS AND IMMUNOGENS FROM MAMMALIAN CELL LINES, INCLUDING 293S, 293T AND 293F CELLS, DROSOPHILA CELLS, OR E. COLI FOR STRUCTURAL AND BIOPHYSICAL STUDIES. WE WILL THEN STRUCTURALLY AND BIOPHYSICALLY ANALYZE THESE NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES WITH INFLUENZA ANTIGENS [HEMAGGLUTININ (HA), AND NEURAMINIDASE (NA)], AS WELL AS IDENTIFIED RESISTANCE MUTANTS, TO DETERMINE ANTIBODY AFFINITIES AND MODE OF BINDING, STABILITY, STOICHIOMETRY, EPITOPES AND 3D STRUCTURES. WE WILL USE X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY TO DETERMINE THE HIGH-RESOLUTION STRUCTURES OF ANTIBODIES AND ANTIBODY-ANTIGEN COMPLEXES. OTHER BIOPHYSICAL METHODS INCLUDING BIO-LAYER INTERFEROMETRY (BLI), ISOTHERMAL TITRATION CALORIMETRY ITC), DIFFERENTIAL SCANNING CALORIMETRY (DSC) AND SURFACE PLASMON RESONANCE (SPR), WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE BINDING AFFINITIES AND PROTEIN/IMMUNOGEN STABILITY. WE WILL DESIGN, MODIFY AND CHARACTERIZE IMMUNOGENS AS VACCINES CANDIDATES USING STRUCTURE-ASSISTED VACCINE DESIGN METHODS THAT WE HAVE PREVIOUSLY SUCCESSFULLY UTILIZED FOR HIV, INFLUENZA VIRUS AND HEPATITIS C VIRUS. THE WARD LAB WILL UTILIZE THEIR RECENTLY DEVELOPED NOVEL EM IMAGING METHOD OF POLYCLONAL EPITOPE MAPPING (EMPEM) TO ANALYZE POLYCLONAL ANTIBODY RESPONSES IN SERA TO IDENTIFY PATTERNS OF EPITOPE UTILIZATION AND FREQUENCY IN HA AND NA IN HUMAN LONGITUDINAL COHORTS. THE HA OR NA PROTEIN PROBES IN THESE ANALYSES WILL BE PRODUCED IN THE WILSON LAB AND SERA PROVIDED BY OUR COLLEAGUES IN THIS CEIRR PROJECT.

description: SCOPE OF WORK FOR BLOOM LAB (FRED HUTCH CANCER CENTER) FOR SAVE OPTION “DEEP MUTATIONAL SCANNING OF HOW MUTATIONS TO THE SARS-COV-2 SPIKE AƯECT ACE2 BINDING” SARS-COV-2’S EVOLUTION OVER THE LAST 4.5 YEARS HAS INVOLVED THE REPEATED EMERGENCE OF NEW VARIANTS WITH AMINO-ACID MUTATIONS IN THE SPIKE, ESPECIALLY IN THE RECEPTOR-BINDING DOMAIN (RBD) AND N-TERMINAL DOMAIN (NTD). THIS EVOLUTION IS DRIVEN IN SUBSTANTIAL PART BY TWO FORCES: PRESSURE FOR ANTIGENIC MUTATIONS THAT ESCAPE ANTIBODY NEUTRALIZATION AND THEREBY ENABLE THE VIRUS TO REINFECT INDIVIDUALS WITH IMMUNITY FROM PRIOR INFECTIONS/VACCINATIONS, AND PRESSURE FOR THE SPIKE TO MAINTAIN THE BINDING TO ACE2 RECEPTOR THAT IS CRUCIAL FOR VIRAL CELL ENTRY. THE WORK IN THE BLOOM LAB WILL USE A FULL-SPIKE PSEUDOVIRUS DEEP MUTATIONAL SCANNING SYSTEM TO MEASURE HOW ALL MUTATIONS TO THE SPIKE OF RECENT SARS-COV-2 VARIANTS AƯECT ACE2 BINDING (FOR DETAILS ON THE APPROACH THAT WILL BE USED, SEE DADONAITE ET AL, NATURE, 631:617-626, 2024). BRIEFLY, WE WILL CHOOSE THE DOMINANT SARS-COV-2 VARIANT, CONSTRUCT A LIBRARY CONTAINING ALL TOLERATED AMINO-ACID MUTATIONS THAT VARIANT’S SPIKE, GENERATE PSEUDOVIRUSES CARRYING THOSE MUTANTS, AND ASSAY THEM TO DETERMINE HOW THE MUTATIONS AƯECT ACE2 BINDING. WE WILL THEN ANALYZE THE DATA TO CREATE INTERACTIVE MAPS OF THE MUTATIONAL EƯECTS ON ACE2 BINDING, AND SHARE THESE DATA PUBLICLY ALONG WITH PUBLISHING THEM. INITIAL WORK WILL BEGIN WITH THE SPIKE OF THE KP.3.1.1 VARIANT, WHICH IS CURRENTLY THE GLOBALLY DOMINANT VARIANT. WE ALSO ANTICIPATE STUDYING A SECOND VARIANT THAT IS DOMINANT IN THE SUMMER OF 2025. SO OVERALL MILESTONES ARE: - CREATE PSEUDOVIRUS MUTANT LIBRARY WITH KP.3.1.1 SPIKE (LAST QUARTER OF 2024) - MEASURE HOW ALL MUTATIONS TO KP.3.1.1 SPIKE AƯECT ACE2 BINDING, ANALYZE DATA, AND PUBLISH RESULTS ALONGSIDE INTERACTIVE VISUALIZATIONS OF DATA (FIRST HALF OF 2025). - CHOOSE A SECOND SARS-COV-2 VARIANT THAT IS DOMINANT IN THE SPRING OF 2025 AND REPEAT THE ABOVE PROCESS

description: THIS PROJECT IS DESIGNED TO UNRAVEL THE DETERMINANTS OF CROSS-PROTECTIVE T-CELL IMMUNITY AGAINST INFLUENZA BY EMPLOYING A CUTTING-EDGE MULTI-OMICS SYSTEMS IMMUNOLOGY APPROACH. THE OBJECTIVES OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO DEFINE THE MEMORY CD8 T CELL SUBSETS THAT OFFER CROSS-PROTECTIVE IMMUNITY AGAINST DIVERSE INFLUENZA STRAINS, UNCOVER THE INNATE IMMUNE MECHANISMS—PARTICULARLY TYPE I INTERFERON (IFN) SIGNALING—THAT SHAPE THESE RESPONSES, AND IDENTIFY THE KEY FACTORS DRIVING PROTECTIVE T CELL IMMUNITY. SPECIFICALLY, WE AIM TO MAP THE T-CELL SIGNATURES ASSOCIATED WITH BROAD IMMUNITY, EXPLORE HOW INNATE IMMUNE SIGNALS, INCLUDING IFN PATHWAYS, INFLUENCE T CELL ACTIVATION AND MEMORY FORMATION, AND DEVELOP INTEGRATIVE MODELS THAT LINK INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSES, T CELL BEHAVIOR, AND VIRAL CHARACTERISTICS TO PREDICT PROTECTIVE IMMUNITY. WE WILL START BY CHARACTERIZING MEMORY CD8 T CELL SUBSETS THAT ARE CROSS-REACTIVE AGAINST MULTIPLE INFLUENZA STRAINS USING HIGH-DIMENSIONAL CYTOMETRIC ANALYSIS (AIM 1). OUR SYSTEMS CYTOMICS PLATFORM WILL ENABLE DETAILED IMMUNOPHENOTYPING, WHILE FUNCTIONAL ASSAYS WITH EX VIVO INFECTION MODELS WILL ASSESS T CELL RESPONSES IN PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT CONDITIONS. THE EX VIVO MODELS WILL USE PRIMARY HUMAN CELLS, INCLUDING MONOCYTE-DERIVED DENDRITIC CELLS, TO EVALUATE THE FUNCTIONAL CAPACITY OF T CELLS AGAINST VARIOUS INFLUENZA STRAINS. WE WILL UTILIZE A COMPREHENSIVE PANEL OF INFLUENZA STRAINS PROVIDED BY THE GARCIA-SASTRE LAB AT MOUNT SINAI, INCLUDING BOTH WILD-TYPE VIRUSES AND GENETICALLY MODIFIED STRAINS SUCH AS ΔNS1 VIRUSES THAT LACK IMMUNE-EVASIVE PROTEINS. THIS WILL ALLOW US TO EXAMINE CROSS-REACTIVITY ACROSS DIVERSE VIRAL STRAINS, INCLUDING HIGHLY PATHOGENIC VARIANTS LIKE H5N1 AND H2N2 (ADAPTED FOR WORK UNDER BSL2 CONDITIONS). NEXT, WE WILL INVESTIGATE HOW VARIATIONS IN TYPE I INTERFERON SIGNALING DURING INFECTION INFLUENCE THE DEVELOPMENT AND FUNCTIONALITY OF CROSS-REACTIVE MEMORY CD8 T CELLS (AIM 2). USING THE SAME EX VIVO INFECTION MODELS COMBINED WITH TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS OF APCS, WE WILL EXAMINE HOW IFN-DRIVEN CHANGES IN GENE EXPRESSION WITHIN THESE CELLS AFFECT T-CELL PRIMING AND MEMORY DEVELOPMENT. INCLUDING THE ΔNS1 VIRUSES PROVIDED BY THE GARCIA-SASTRE LAB WILL ENABLE US TO DISSECT THE ROLE OF IFNS IN SHAPING CROSS-REACTIVE T-CELL MEMORY AND UNDERSTAND HOW THE ABSENCE OF IMMUNE EVASION AFFECTS THE IMMUNE RESPONSE. FINALLY, WE WILL INTEGRATE THE HIGH-DIMENSIONAL DATA FROM T-CELL PROFILING AND APC TRANSCRIPTOMICS USING OUR AI-POWERED PLATFORM, SIMON, TO CREATE PREDICTIVE MODELS (AIM 3). THESE MODELS WILL HELP IDENTIFY BASELINE IMMUNE SIGNATURES, PARTICULARLY WITHIN THE APC TRANSCRIPTOME, THAT PREDICT ROBUST CROSS-PROTECTIVE T-CELL RESPONSES. THESE MODELS WILL BE VALIDATED USING BOTH IN SILICO DATASETS FROM FLU-INFECTED INDIVIDUALS AND REAL-WORLD DATA FROM THE FLUPRINT STUDY AND HUMAN INFLUENZA CHALLENGE MODELS. THE PROJECT WILL COMPREHENSIVELY CHARACTERIZE FLU-SPECIFIC CROSS-REACTIVE CD8 T CELL RESPONSES, PROVIDING INSIGHTS INTO HOW IFN SIGNALING SHAPES T CELL IMMUNITY AND PREDICTIVE MODELS CAPABLE OF FORECASTING CROSS-PROTECTIVE T CELL RESPONSES BASED ON PRE-EXISTING IMMUNE STATES. BY LEVERAGING THE UNIQUE VIRAL STRAINS PROVIDED BY MOUNT SINAI, INCLUDING GENETICALLY MODIFIED STRAINS FROM DR. ADOLFO GARCIA-SASTRE, THIS WORK WILL FURTHER CONTRIBUTE TO OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW DIFFERENT INFLUENZA VARIANTS DRIVE IMMUNE RESPONSES. ULTIMATELY, THE FINDINGS WILL ADVANCE THE DEVELOPMENT OF UNIVERSAL INFLUENZA VACCINES BY IDENTIFYING IMMUNE MARKERS THAT PREDICT BROAD T CELL-MEDIATED PROTECTION ACROSS DIVERSE INFLUENZA STRAINS.

description: THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT UK HEALTH SECURITY AGENCY (UKHSA), PREVIOUSLY KNOWN AS PUBLIC HEALTH ENGLAND (PHE), WILL BE PERFORMING. NOTE THAT THE TASK NUMBERS BELOW REFLECT THE NUMBERING OF THE OVERALL ACTIVITIES IN THE PRIME CONTRACT. THROUGH THE EXECUTION OF THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL EXAMINE BASIC INDUCTION OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY FROM VACCINATION, INCLUDING STUDIES THAT ADDRESS NONTUBERCULOUS MYCOBACTERIA (NTM) INTERFERENCE, RNA DELIVERY, PRIME-BOOST REGIMENS (INCLUDING BCG PRE-EXPOSURE), TRANSCRIPTOMIC HOST SIGNATURES, SYSTEMS BIOLOGY AND DURABLE IMMUNE MEMORY FOR THE FURTHER ADVANCEMENT OF THE EFFORT TO DESIGN AND EVALUATE AN EFFICACIOUS VACCINE AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (M.TB). THE WORK UNDER THIS CONTRACT MAY INCLUDE THE POSSIBLE DISTRIBUTION OF DE-IDENTIFIED HUMAN SUBJECT PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMC), SERUM, AND OTHER CLINICAL SAMPLES TO SCRI AND THE PHOENIX PARTNERS. NHP-DERIVED SAMPLES AND/OR DOWNSTREAM DATA MAY BE SHARED WITH THE PARTNERS ON THIS CONTRACT. OPTION 2 ACTIVITIES: OBJECTIVE: EVALUATE OPTIMIZED M.TB VACCINE CANDIDATES FOR SAFETY, IMMUNOGENICITY AND EFFICACY IN GUINEA PIG MODEL OF TB TASK 2.1 EVALUATE IMMUNE RESPONSE OF TB CANDIDATE VACCINES IN GUINEA PIGS GUINEA PIG IMMUNOLOGY THE ABILITY TO STUDY IMMUNE RESPONSES IN GUINEA PIGS IS SLOWLY IMPROVING. METHODOLOGY FOR DETERMINING A VARIETY OF CELL- SURFACE MARKERS, CYTOKINES AND CHEMOKINES HAS BEEN DEVELOPED AND STUDIES HAVE BEEN PERFORMED ON BCG-VACCINATED AND M.TB-INFECTED GUINEA PIGS. RELATED SOPS DEVELOPED AT PARTNER INSTITUTES LIKE CSU WILL BE SHARED WITH UKHSA FOR PERFORMANCE OF GUINEA PIG ENDPOINTS AND ASSAY HARMONIZATION. THE NUMBER OF ANTIBODY REAGENTS REMAINS RESTRICTIVE BUT SOME KEY FEATURES OF THE IMMUNE RESPONSE HAVE BEEN DESCRIBED. USING FLOW CYTOMETRY, IT IS POSSIBLE TO MONITOR CD4 AND CD8 T CELLS IN THE LUNGS AND STAINING WITH CD62L PLUS GATING VERSUS CD45 CAN IDENTIFY ACTIVATED T CELLS. FURTHER DEVELOPMENT OF ANTIBODIES TO DETECT IFN-Γ WILL ENABLE INTRACELLULAR STAINING PROTOCOLS TO BE ESTABLISHED. FLOW CYTOMETRY STUDIES HAVE SHOWN THAT CELL ACCUMULATION PATTERNS CHANGE IN BCG VACCINATED GUINEA PIGS AFTER AEROSOL CHALLENGE AND THAT THESE PATTERNS DIFFER FROM THOSE OF THE UNVACCINATED CONTROLS; FOR EXAMPLE, ACTIVATED CD4+ RESPONSES HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO APPEAR MORE RAPIDLY AND THERE WAS A FASTER AND LARGER MACROPHAGE RESPONSE POST-INFECTION IN BCG VACCINATED ANIMALS THAN IN UNVACCINATED CONTROLS. SUCH FINDINGS OFFER THE POTENTIAL FOR IDENTIFICATION OF IMMUNE CORRELATES OF PROTECTION BOTH PRE- AND POST- CHALLENGE. THERE IS NOW A LARGE PANEL OF CYTOKINES (IL-1, IL-4, IL-10, IL-12P40, IFN-Γ, AND TNFΑ) AND CHEMOKINES (IL- 8, MCP-1, TGFΒ, AND RANTES) THAT CAN BE MEASURED BY PCR. THERE ARE A SMALL NUMBER OF ANTIBODY REAGENTS SPECIFIC FOR SOME OF THESE CYTOKINES BEING DEVELOPED BY OUR GROUP AND OTHERS WHICH WILL INCREASE THE SOPHISTICATION OF THESE STUDIES. WORK BY OTHER GROUPS USED MOUSE ANTIBODIES IN A MULTIPLEX ASSAY TO DETECT GUINEA PIG CYTOKINES AND WE PROPOSE TO EVALUATE THIS SYSTEM ON SERA AND ANTIGEN-STIMULATED CELL SUPERNATANTS. CYTOKINES AND CHEMOKINES: WE HAVE RECENTLY DEVELOPED AN IFN-Γ ELISPOT. INITIATIVES TO FURTHER OPTIMIZE THIS ASSAY ARE ON- GOING. IF SUCH ASSAYS BECOME AVAILABLE, THEY WILL BE USED TO DETECT IFNΓ SECRETION BY CELLS IN WHOLE BLOOD, PMBC OR SPLENOCYTES STIMULATED WITH APPROPRIATE ANTIGENS. OTHER CYTOKINES CAN BE DETECTED USING MOUSE-SPECIFIC ANTIBODIES WHICH CROSS-REACT WITH GUINEA PIG PROTEINS (IL-8 AND TGFΒ), AND GUINEA PIG-SPECIFIC ANTI TNF IS ALSO AVAILABLE. A MULTIPLEX CYTOKINE ASSAY FOR MICE HAS ALSO BEEN SHOWN TO CROSS-REACT WITH GUINEA PIG PROTEINS AND WE WILL INVESTIGATE THESE REAGENTS FOR USE IN A LUMINEX ASSAY FOR GUINEA PIGS. A TNFΑ BIOASSAY HAS ALSO BEEN DESCRIBED TO DETECT ACTIVE TNFΑ, AND THIS ASSAY IS ESTABLISHED AT UKHSA. LUNG AND SPLEEN TISSUE WILL BE COLLECTED FOR HISTOPATHOLOGICAL EXAMINATION AT POST-MORTEM. OPTION 3.M72 ACTIVITIES: THE ANIMALS USED IN THESE STUDIES WILL BE RHESUS MACAQUES OF INDIAN GENOTYPE OBTAINED FROM ESTABLISHED UK BREEDING COLONIES AND WILL BE BETWEEN 3 AND 6 YEARS OF AGE (TYPICALLY BETWEEN 4 – 12 KG). ABSENCE OF PREVIOUS EXPOSURE TO MYCOBACTERIAL ANTIGENS AND/OR NTM RECOGNITION WILL BE CONFIRMED BY EX VIVO IFN-Γ ELISPOT TO MEASURE RESPONSES TO PURIFIED PROTEIN DERIVATIVE (PPD) FROM M.TB, POOLED 15-MER PEPTIDES OF ESAT-6 AND CFP-10 AND NTM MEGA PEPTIDE POOLS FOR SCREENING TIMEPOINTS AND MTB300 FOR POST VACCINATION AND M.TB CHALLENGE TIMEPOINTS AS AVAILABLE. THE PROJECT LICENSE ENABLING THESE STUDIES WILL BE APPROVED BY THE ANIMAL WELFARE AND ETHICAL REVIEW BODY AT UKHSA PORTON AND GRANTED BY THE HOME OFFICE, UK. ANIMALS WILL BE HOUSED IN SOCIALLY COMPATIBLE GROUPS AND ACCORDING TO THE CODE OF PRACTICE FOR THE HOUSING AND CARE OF ANIMALS BRED, SUPPLIED OR USED FOR SCIENTIFIC PURPOSES, DECEMBER 2014, THE NC3RS, AND THE GUIDELINES ON PRIMATE ACCOMMODATION, CARE AND USE, AUGUST 2006 (NC3RS, 2006). ANIMALS WILL BE MONITORED DAILY FOR BEHAVIORAL AND CLINICAL CHANGES. BEHAVIOR WILL BE EVALUATED FOR CONTRA-INDICATORS INCLUDING DEPRESSION, WITHDRAWAL FROM THE GROUP, AGGRESSION, CHANGES IN FEEDING PATTERNS, BREATHING PATTERN, RESPIRATION RATE AND COUGH. BLOOD SAMPLE COLLECTION (PAXGENE) FOR TRANSCRIPTOMICS WILL BE COLLECTED TWO DAYS AFTER EACH IMMUNIZATION OR CHALLENGE. BLOOD SAMPLE COLLECTION FOR M.TB ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC IMMUNE RESPONSES WILL BE EVALUATED AT REGULAR INTERVALS THROUGHOUT THE STUDY (HIGH PRIORITY TIMEPOINTS TO INCLUDE: TWO WEEKS POST PRIME AND BOOST IMMUNIZATIONS, ONE WEEK PRE-CHALLENGE, ONE, TWO, FOUR AND EIGHT WEEKS POST CHALLENGE), AEROSOL CHALLENGE AND EUTHANASIA; ANIMALS WILL BE WEIGHED, EXAMINED FOR GROSS ABNORMALITIES AND BODY TEMPERATURE MEASURED. RED BLOOD CELL (RBC) HEMOGLOBIN LEVELS WILL BE MEASURED TO IDENTIFY THE PRESENCE OF ANEMIA, AND ERYTHROCYTE SEDIMENTATION RATES (ESR) WILL BE MEASURED TO DETECT AND MONITOR INFLAMMATION INDUCED BY INFECTION WITH M.TB. TASK 3.M72: USE ULDA MODEL TO EVALUATE THE EFFICACY OF NEW TB VACCINE CANDIDATES NOTE: AFTER REVIEW OF ALL UPCOMING EXPERIMENTS, THE NIH, SCRI AND UKHSA AGREED THAT THE FOLLOWING EXPERIMENT COMBINING BOTH ID93 AND M72 VACCINE GROUPS IS PREFERRED GIVEN IT IS BOTH COST SAVING (SHARED CONTROLS) AND SCIENTIFICALLY MORE ROBUST (DIRECT HEAD TO HEAD) THAN THE EXPERIMENTAL DESIGNS AS SEPARATE TASKS. description: THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP AN IV + ORAL AGENT WITH A NOVEL MECHANISM OF ACTION (MOA) FOR THE TREATMENT OF COMPLICATED URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS (CUTI) CAUSED BY MDR ENTEROBACTERALES. ARREPATH HAS IDENTIFIED A SERIES OF INHIBITORS OF A HIGHLY CONSERVED ENZYME IN GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA WITH NO HUMAN HOMOLOG THAT HAS NEVER BEEN CLINICALLY EXPLOITED AND IS THEREFORE CONSIDERED A NOVEL MOA. IF SUCCESSFULLY DEVELOPED, AN ANTIBIOTIC THAT INHIBITS THIS ENZYME WOULD BE ACTIVE AGAINST THE VAST MAJORITY OF ANTIBIOTIC-RESISTANT INFECTIONS CAUSED BY TARGET PATHOGENS, REPRESENTING AN IMPORTANT NEW TOOL IN THE FIGHT AGAINST ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE. THE CURRENT PROPOSAL SEEKS TO OPTIMIZE PROPERTIES OF OUR INHIBITORS TO ALLOW FOR THE SELECTION OF A DEVELOPMENT CANDIDATE SUITABLE FOR IND-ENABLING STUDIES.

description: SCOPE OF WORK: THE CENTER FOR VACCINE DEVELOPMENT AND GLOBAL HEALTH (CVD) WILL FURNISH THE NECESSARY SCIENTIFIC, CLINICAL, ADMINISTRATIVE AND LABORATORY PERSONNEL, AND THE MATERIALS, EQUIPMENT, AND FACILITIES TO EVALUATE A RABIESVECTORED MONOVALENT LASSA FEVER VACCINE IN HUMANS. THIS WORK INCLUDES THE REGULATORY PHASE, THE TRIAL PREPARATORY PHASE, THE EXECUTION PHASE OF THE CLINICAL TRIAL, AND THE ANALYSIS AND RESULTS PHASE. IN THE REGULATORY PHASE, WE WILL COORDINATE ASSEMBLY OF THE PRE-IND BRIEFING PACKAGE, SCHEDULE THE PRE-IND MEETING AND PARTICIPATE IN THE PRE-IND MEETING. WE WILL COORDINATE THE DEVELOPMENT AND FILING OF THE IND PACKAGE, INCLUDING PROVIDING OVERSIGHT OF OUTSIDE VENDORS, AS NEEDED. CVD WILL ACT AS STUDY SPONSOR FOR THE CLINICAL TRIAL. WE WILL DESIGN THE CLINICAL TRIAL PROTOCOL, WITH INPUT FROM ALL PARTNERS. PRIOR TO STARTING THE TRIAL, WE WILL OBTAIN ALL NECESSARY APPROVALS, INCLUDING FROM NIH AND INSTITUTIONAL REVIEW BOARDS; TRAIN STUDY STAFF; DELINEATE ROLES AND TIMELINES; AND ENSURE ADEQUATE FACILITIES AND RESOURCES ARE AVAILABLE TO CONDUCT THE TRIAL ACCORDING TO GOOD CLINICAL TRIAL (GCP) STANDARDS, STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES AND OTHER GUIDELINES. WE WILL PERFORM THE CLINICAL TRIAL AS DESIGNED IN THE PROTOCOL, ACCORDING TO ALL ETHICAL, QUALITY AND GCP STANDARDS. THIS WILL INCLUDE STUDY INITIATION; RECRUITMENT, INFORMED CONSENT AND RETENTION OF THE STUDY POPULATION; CONDUCT OF STUDY VISITS PER SCHEDULE; DATABASE CLEANING AND CLOSURE; AND WRITING OF REPORTS AND PUBLICATIONS. WE WILL COMPLY WITH REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS INCLUDING SERIOUS ADVERSE EVENTS (SAES) REPORTING REQUIREMENTS. WE WILL COMMUNICATE AS REQUIRED WITH FUNDERS, AND PARTNERS, AND CONVENE A SAFETY MONITORING COMMITTEE PER THE DETAILS IN THE PROTOCOL. CVD WILL PERFORM ALL DATA RECORDING PROCESSES AND FUNCTIONS, INCLUDING CASE REPORT FORM DESIGN, DATA COLLECTION AND ENTRY, SOURCE DOCUMENTATION. WE WILL ENSURE THAT CLINICAL DATA ARE ACCURATE, COMPLETE AND TIMELY. WE WILL ENSURE THE QUALITY, SECURITY, SAFETY AND RELIABILITY OF ALL DATA ACCORDING TO OUR QUALITY MANAGEMENT PLAN. AFTER DATA LOCK, CVD WILL ANALYZE TRIAL RESULTS ACCORDING TO THE PROTOCOL AND THE STATISTICAL ANALYSIS PLAN, AND PRODUCE A FINAL CLINICAL STUDY REPORT. WE WILL COMPLY WITH ALL NECESSARY REPORTING TO CLINICALTRIALS.GOV, THE FUNDER, AND THE FDA, AS RELEVANT.

description: THE OH LAB AT DUKE UNIVERSITY WILL DEVELOP AND VALIDATE A METAGENOMIC PIPELINE FOR PATHOGEN DETECTION AND MICROBIAL LOAD ESTIMATION. THIS PIPELINE SIMULTANEOUSLY GENERATES DEEP METAGENOMIC DATA THAT MAY CONTAIN RELEVANT INFORMATION ABOUT INFECTION RISK AS WELL AS ACCURATELY DETECT, AT THE STRAIN LEVEL, MOST LIKELY STRAIN LEVELS OF PATHOGENS OF INTEREST. THIS PIPELINE WILL BE COMPLEMENTED BY QPCR TO CALCULATE MICROBIAL LOAD, DATA WHICH WILL THEN BE USED TO EXTRAPOLATE BIOBURDEN AS A FUNCTION OF CFUS PER GRAM OF STOOL OR SKIN SWAB. THE OH LAB WILL RETURN 1) A DETAILED WORKFLOW FOR SAMPLE ACQUISITION, PREPARATION, AND ANALYSIS, 2) ALGORITHMS AND DATABASES FOR PATHOGEN DETECTION IN METAGENOMIC DATA, AND 3) BENCHMARK TESTING FOR THIS PIPELINE.

description: OUR PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP A NEW DRUG EFFECTIVE AGAINST MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT (MDR) GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA. OUR EARLY LEAD COMPOUNDS ARE DERIVED FROM A NATURAL PRODUCT AND REPRESENT A NOVEL CLASS OF COMPOUNDS FEATURING A NOVEL MODE OF ACTION. THE AGENTS ARREST THE FUNCTION OF BAMA, AN ESSENTIAL COMPONENT FOR BACTERIAL SURVIVAL, WHICH NO CURRENT DRUGS TARGET. BAMA, IS AN ESSENTIAL COMPONENT OF THE ÃƑÅ¸-BARREL ASSEMBLY MACHINERY (BAM), LOCATED IN THE OUTER MEMBRANE (OM) OF GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA; THE TARGET IS NOT PRESENT IN HUMANS (SPECIFIC). BAMA FOLDS AND INTEGRATES OM-PROTEINS INTO THE OM; INHIBITION LEADS TO OM BLEBBING AND ULTIMATELY CELL LYSIS (ESSENTIAL). SINCE BAMA HAS NOT BEEN TARGETED BY ANY EXISTING DRUGS, BACTERIA HAVE NOT DEVELOPED TARGET-BASED RESISTANCE. HENCE, OUR PROGRAM CAN BE REGARDED AS THE FOUNDATION FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A FIRST IN CLASS BAMA INHIBITOR. WE WILL FOCUS ON TREATING HOSPITAL-ACQUIRED INFECTIONS SUCH AS PNEUMONIA CAUSED BY MDR BACTERIA. THESE INFECTIONS ARE CLASSIFIED AS A Ã¢Â‚¬Å“CRITICAL PRIORITYÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ BY THE WORLD HEALTH ORGANIZATION (WHO) DUE TO THEIR SEVERITY AND LIMITED TREATMENT OPTIONS.
