description: IN THIS CARB-X PROJECT, WE AIM AT DEVELOPING OUR NOVEL CLASS OF COMPOUNDS TARGETING THE BACTERIAL SLIDING CLAMP (DNAN) AS ANTIBIOTIC LEAD CANDIDATES FOR THE TREATMENT OF GRAM-POSITIVE BACTERIAL INFECTIONS. IT WILL BE GUIDED BY A PRIMARY TPP OF A STANDALONE THERAPY FOR THE TREATMENT OF COMMUNITY ACQUIRED BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA (CABP) CAUSED BY SUSCEPTIBLE AS WELL AS MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT (MDR) STREPTOCOCCUS PNEUMONIAE. WITHIN THE FRAME OF CARB-X FUNDING FOR THIS HIT-TO-LEAD BASE STAGE, WE WILL FOCUS IN THE FIRST PLACE ON THREE GOALS, NAMELY OPTIMIZATION OF TARGET AFFINITY AND ANTIBACTERIAL ACTIVITY AGAINST MAINLY TWO KEY GRAM-POSITIVE TPP PATHOGENS (STREPTOCOCCUS PNEUMONIAE AND STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS), DEMONSTRATION OF TARGET ENGAGEMENT IN A GRAM-POSITIVE BACTERIAL STRAIN, AND PROOF-OF-CONCEPT IN A MURINE INFECTION MODEL. IF THESE AIMS ARE ACHIEVED, WE WILL THEN CONCENTRATE ON OPTIMIZATION OF BOTH THE PHARMACOKINETIC (PK) PROPERTIES AND THE ANTIBIOTIC SPECTRUM OF OUR COMPOUND CLASS IN ORDER TO COVER OTHER GRAM-POSITIVE TPP-RELEVANT GERMS, INCLUDING MDR CLINICAL ISOLATES, AS WELL AS OPPORTUNISTIC GRAM-NEGATIVE PATHOGENS INVOLVED IN CABP INFECTIONS. MOREOVER, WE WILL IMPLEMENT IN VITRO SAFETY PHARMACOLOGY AGAINST HUMAN OFF-TARGETS AND IN VIVO SAFETY AND EFFICACY PROFILING TO IDENTIFY THE MOST PROMISING 2Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ3 LEAD CANDIDATES. THE ENVISAGED LEAD COMPOUNDS WILL DEMONSTRATE POTENT ANTIBIOTIC ACTIVITY AGAINST MULTIPLE GRAM-POSITIVE STRAINS, IN VITRO AND IN CELLUO TARGET ENGAGEMENT, PROMISING IN VITRO ADME-TOX PROFILE, AS WELL AS FAVORABLE IN VIVO PK AND PHARMACODYNAMICS (PD) PROPERTIES.

description: THE KEY GOALS OF THIS PROGRAM ARE TO DEMONSTRATE DETECTION OF GONORRHEA FROM CRUDE VAGINAL SWAB AND URINE SAMPLES AND DEMONSTRATE PROOF-OF-FEASIBILITY FOR THE STI SCOUT, A PRODUCT INTENDED FOR AT HOME AND POINT-OF-NEED TESTING FOR GONORRHEA AND CHLAMYDIA. THE TARGET PATHOGENS ARE NEISSERIA GONORRHOEAE AND CHLAMYDIA TRACHOMATIS. THE KEY CLINICAL INDICATIONS ARE SYMPTOMATIC AND ASYMPTOMATIC INFECTIONS OR SUSPECTED INFECTIONS OF THE UROGENITAL TRACT BY CHLAMYDIA OR GONORRHEA, THE TWO MOST COMMON, TREATABLE SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS IN THE UNITED STATES. SCOUT IS TARGETING DIFFERENTIATION AGAINST OTHER APPROACHES BY OFFERING PCR-LEVEL ACCURACY WITH THE CONVENIENCE AND COST OF RAPID ANTIGEN TESTING. UNLIKE COLLECT-AT-HOME AND SEND-IN TESTING OPTIONS, STI SCOUT DELIVERS RESULTS IMMEDIATELY TO THE USER (WITHIN 30 MINUTES). THE SCOUT HUB IS A REUSABLE DEVICE THAT ENABLES TESTING FOR MULTIPLE INDICATIONS, NOT JUST STIS, ADDING A VALUABLE TOOL TO INDIVIDUALSÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ OR CLINICSÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ TOOLKIT FOR DIAGNOSING COMMON, TREATABLE ILLNESSES OR INFORMING ON OVERALL WELLNESS. A MOBILE APPLICATION, SCOUT CONNECT, PERMITS RESULT TRACKING, SHARING, AND FOLLOW-ON CARE VIA TELEHEALTH AND E-PRESCRIPTIONS FROM QUALIFIED HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS. A PLANNED REFLEX TEST FOR NG AMR WILL ENABLE BETTER STEWARDSHIP OF ANTIBIOTICS.

description: PNEUMONIA IS A COMMON CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS THAT OFTEN LACKS A MICROBIOLOGICAL DIAGNOSIS BECAUSE NO PATHOGEN IS IDENTIFIED. WITHOUT A MICROBIOLOGICAL DIAGNOSIS, ANTIBIOTICS TARGETING A BROAD RANGE OF PATHOGENS ARE USED, INCREASING THE RISKS FOR RESISTANCE ALONG WITH POOR OUTCOMES IF INAPPROPRIATE ANTIBIOTICS ARE CHOSEN. THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM PROPOSES TO DIAGNOSE LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACT BACTERIAL INFECTIONS AND THEIR ASSOCIATED ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE IN FOUR HOURS, MUCH FASTER THAN CURRENT CULTURE TECHNIQUES. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM IS TO DEVELOP RAPID DIAGNOSTIC TESTS THAT WILL BE INDICATED IN ALL PATIENTS WITH A CLINICAL SUSPICION FOR PNEUMONIA. THE SHORT-TERM OBJECTIVE WILL FOCUS ON PNEUMONIAS CAUSED BY STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS, PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA, AND HAEMOPHILUS INFLUENZAE, WITH THE GOAL OF HAVING RESULTS AVAILABLE IN 4 HOURS. THE STRATEGY USED IN THIS DIAGNOSTIC TEST DISTINGUISHES IT FROM COMPETITORS AND ALTERNATIVES. THIS DIAGNOSTIC IS BASED ON DETECTING RNA SEQUENCE(S) SPECIFIC FOR THE PATHOGEN CAUSING PNEUMONIA IN A HUMAN PATIENT. TESTING WILL BE DONE ON BLOOD DRAWN DIRECTLY FROM THE PATIENT, MAKING IT LESS INVASIVE THAN OTHER METHODS THAT OBTAIN SAMPLES FROM THE AIRWAYS, SUCH AS BRONCHOSCOPY OR DEEP SUCTIONING. THIS TEST WILL NOT REQUIRE THE SPECIMEN TO BE CULTURED, ALLOWING FOR FASTER RESULTS THAN TRADITIONAL MICROBIOLOGICAL METHODS. THE RNA TARGETED BY THE TEST IS IDENTIFIED VIA RNA SEQUENCING OF BLOOD FROM PATIENTS WITH THE INFECTION. RNA SEQUENCING DATA SHOWS RNA SPECIFIC TO THE PATHOGEN OF INTEREST (S. AUREUS., P. AERUGINOSA, AND H. INFLUENZAE) THAT IS ALSO SPECIFIC FOR AN ACTIVE INFECTION. TARGETING RNA ALSO ENSURES THAT THE INFECTION IS CURRENT SINCE RNA IS LESS STABLE THAN DNA, LASTING MINUTES TO HOURS WHEN FROM A BACTERIUM. THE METHOD, HOWEVER, IMMEDIATELY STABILIZES THE RNA FOR TESTING. RNA ALSO IDENTIFIES BACTERIA THAT ARE ACTIVELY MAKING RESISTANCE PROTEINS, RATHER THAN BACTERIA WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR RESISTANCE BASED ONLY ON GENOMIC DNA. AT THE END OF THIS PROJECT, PCR BASED TESTS WILL BE CREATED THAT ARE INFORMED BY RNA SEQUENCING DATA. THESE WILL DIAGNOSE PNEUMONIA DUE TO S. AUREUS., P. AERUGINOSA, AND H. INFLUENZAE, ALONG WITH RELEVANT ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE, USING BLOOD FROM THE PATIENT. THIS PCR TESTING PLATFORM USES FDA-APPROVED INSTRUMENTATION TO FACILITATE TRANSITIONING FROM A RESEARCH LABORATORY TO A CLINICAL MICROBIOLOGY LABORATORY.

description: OPTION 23C: 0258-A485-4609 OPTION 23D: 0258-A486-4609 THE UNIVERSAL INFLUENZA VACCINE TECHNOLOGY LANDSCAPE IS A UNIQUE, OPEN-ACCESS DATABASE OF INFORMATION ON UNIVERSAL, BROADLY PROTECTIVE, AND NEXT-GENERATION INFLUENZA VACCINES, AS DEFINED IN THE INFLUENZA VACCINES R&D ROADMAP, IN CLINICAL AND PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT. AS OF MAY 2024, THE LANDSCAPE PROFILED MORE THAN 200 VACCINE CANDIDATES IN THE R&D PIPELINE IN ACADEMIC, GOVERNMENT, AND INDUSTRY LABORATORIES, INCLUDING COVID-INFLUENZA COMBINATION VACCINES IN CLINICAL DEVELOPMENT, ACROSS SIX DIFFERENT VACCINE PLATFORMS. DATA ON EACH VACCINE CANDIDATE ARE SUMMARIZED BY PHASE, PLATFORM, TECHNICAL APPROACH, GOAL, AND STATUS OF DEVELOPMENT. THE LANDSCAPE IS ONLINE AND OPEN ACCESS, AND THE ENTIRE DATASET CAN BE DOWNLOADED AS A CSV FILE. A SMALL GROUP OF SUBJECT-MATTER EXPERTS IN INFLUENZA VACCINE R&D AND/OR VACCINE DATABASE DEVELOPMENT PROVIDES ADVICE ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE LANDSCAPE. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO CONTINUE DEVELOPING AND MAINTAINING INFORMATION ON THE LANDSCAPE TO INCLUDE AN UP-TO-DATE, COMPREHENSIVE, AND ACCURATE OVERVIEW OF VACCINE CANDIDATES IN PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT FOR UNIVERSAL, BROADLY PROTECTIVE, AND NEXT-GENERATION INFLUENZA VACCINES. SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES: 1. COLLECT AND CURATE INFORMATION ON UNIVERSAL, BROADLY PROTECTIVE, AND NEXT-GENERATION INFLUENZA VACCINES TECHNOLOGIES IN PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT FROM A WIDE RANGE OF PUBLICLY AVAILABLE SOURCES. CONTINUE RESEARCH ON UNIVERSAL, BROADLY PROTECTIVE, AND NEXT-GENERATION INFLUENZA VACCINE TECHNOLOGIES; MONITOR KEY SOURCES OF INFORMATION FROM THE SCIENTIFIC LITERATURE, PREPRINT SERVERS, AND INDUSTRY WEBSITES AND NEWS SOURCES; AND CROSSCHECK DATA ON VACCINE TECHNOLOGIES IN THE DATABASE. 2. UPLOAD NEW OR REVISED INFORMATION ON THE IVR LANDSCAPE WEBSITE ON A WEEKLY BASIS, FOR DISPLAY IN THE SNAPSHOT GRAPHIC AND DATABASE TABLE, AND MONITOR DATA FOR COMPLETENESS AND ACCURACY. 3. DISSEMINATE INFORMATION ON R&D OF INFLUENZA CANDIDATE VACCINES IN PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT VIA PRESENTATIONS AND PUBLICATIONS IN THE PEER-REVIEWED LITERATURE; ENCOURAGE FEEDBACK FROM DEVELOPERS, RESEARCHERS, AND FUNDING ORGANIZATIONS. 4. CONSULT WITH ADVISORY WORKING GROUP MEMBERS FOR GUIDANCE AND REVIEW. COMMUNICATE WITH DEVELOPERS TO VERIFY ACTIVITIES AND ACCURACY OF DATA. 5. MODIFY THE ONLINE DATABASE FORMAT AS NEEDED, WITH SUPPORT FROM CIDRAPÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S IT CONSULTANTS, AND IN COMMUNICATION WITH NIAID AND CIVICS-SEM. THE LANDSCAPE WILL PROVIDE A COMPREHENSIVE, UP-TO-DATE RESOURCE ON THE R&D PIPELINE FOR VACCINE CANDIDATES IN PRECLINICAL DEVELOPMENT FOR RESEARCHERS, DEVELOPERS, AND NIAID LEADERSHIP. THE LANDSCAPE SUPPORTS THE NIAID/CIVICS PROGRAMÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S GOAL OF ADVANCING INFLUENZA VACCINE SCIENCE AND IDENTIFYING POTENTIAL VACCINE CANDIDATES THAT MAY OFFER BROAD AND LONG-LASTING PROTECTION AGAINST SEASONAL AND PANDEMIC INFLUENZA.

description: THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO EVALUATE VARIOUS ADJUVANTS AND COMBINATIONS OF THESE ADJUVANTS FOR USE IN MUCOSAL IMMUNOTHERAPY FOR PEANUT ALLERGY. DR. KULIS AND HIS TEAM AT UNC CHAPEL HILL WILL PERFORM IN VIVO MOUSE STUDIES, ASSAY HUMAN PERIPHERAL BLOOD CELLS, AND QUANTIFY IMMUNOLOGIC RESPONSES TO ADJUVANTS AND PEANUT FROM BOTH MOUSE AND HUMAN BLOOD. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL EVALUATE SIX ADJUVANT FORMULATIONS IN CELL CULTURE ASSAYS WITH HUMAN T AND B CELLS FROM BLOOD, PRIMARILY INVESTIGATING CYTOKINE RESPONSES AND THEN SENDING CELLS FROM THESE EXPERIMENTS TO DUKE FOR OMICS EXPERIMENTS. FOR THE MOUSE STUDIES, WE WILL EVALUATE THE SAME SIX ADJUVANTS PLUS PEANUT BY ADDING THE ADJUVANTS TO SPLEEN AND LYMPH NODE CELLS IN CULTURE. WE WILL ALSO ADMINISTER THE ADJUVANTS AND PEANUT BY THE SUBLINGUAL ROUTE TO LIVE MICE THAT ARE EITHER NOT SENSITIZED TO PEANUT OR IN MICE THAT HAVE AN ESTABLISHED PEANUT ALLERGY. WE WILL PERFORM THESE EXPERIMENTS AT UNC, AND ALSO SAVE VARIOUS SAMPLES (SPLEEN, LYMPH NODE, SERUM, SALIVA, AND FECAL PELLETS) TO SHIP TO DUKE FOR OMICS STUDIES. ULTIMATELY, THE SIX ADJUVANTS WILL BE EVALUATED FOR THEIR SAFETY AND EFFICACY IN THE PEANUT ALLERGIC MICE. description: THE TTIMS LRCC FUNCTIONS ARE TO SERVE AS THE BIOSTATISTICAL AND ANALYTICAL CENTER FOR ANALYSES RELEVANT TO THE EVALUATION AND MONITORING OF INFECTIONS INCLUDING THOSE IN HIV (INCIDENT AND PREVALENT), HCV (INCIDENT), HBV (INCIDENT) AND SYPHILIS (RECENT) TEST-POSITIVE BLOOD DONORS BY COLLECTING AND ANALYZING DATA FOR RISK FACTORS, MOLECULAR SURVEILLANCE AND ANTI- RETROVIRAL DRUG USE THAT MAY IMPACT THE DETECTION OF HIV. SPECIFICALLY, THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVES OF THIS CONTRACT ARE TO: Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ EVALUATE AND MONITOR RISK FACTOR CHARACTERISTICS OF DONATIONS CONFIRMED POSITIVE FOR TTIS AS STATED ABOVE, AND COMPARISON TO UNINFECTED US ALLOGENEIC BLOOD DONORS. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ INTEGRATE RISK FACTOR DATA AND DISEASE MARKER SURVEILLANCE INFORMATION ACROSS DIFFERENT BLOOD COLLECTION ORGANIZATIONS. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ MONITOR ARV AND PREP/PEP USE IN US ALLOGENEIC BLOOD DONOR POPULATION BASED ON TESTING OF BOTH HIV-POSITIVE AND INFECTION-NEGATIVE DONATIONS FOR THE PRESENCE OF ARV DRUGS. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ EXPLORE THE CHARACTERISTICS OF BLOOD DONORS WHO USE ARV/PREP/PEP TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THEIR RISKS, KNOWLEDGE, AND MOTIVATIONS FOR DONATING WHILE USING THESE THERAPIES. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ EVALUATE WELL-CHARACTERIZED US BLOOD DONOR SAMPLES FROM TTIMS AND OTHER SOURCES FOR THE REFINEMENT OF EXISTING ANALYTICAL METHODS SUCH AS THE SEDIA LAG AVIDITY ASSAY TO DERIVE ESTIMATES OF RECENT INFECTION WITH HIV WITH A GOAL OF RAPIDLY OBTAINING MORE ACCURATE AND TIMELY RESULTS. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ PROVIDE LOGISTICAL SUPPORT FOR THE TTIMS PROJECT AND FOR THE COMMITTEE/SUBCOMMITTEE MEETINGS, CONFERENCES, AND DONATION(S) TRANSFER/SHIPMENT. IN SUPPORT OF THESE OBJECTIVES, ARC WILL RECRUIT, ENROLL AND INTERVIEW ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS, PROVIDE DATA AS REQUIRED IN THE TTIMS LRCC STATEMENT OF WORK, PROVIDE BIOSPECIMENS FOR RESEARCH TESTING AT VRI, AND WILL ACTIVELY COLLABORATE IN THE ANALYSIS, INTERPRETATION, AND REPORTING OF FINDINGS IN TTIMS. SUSAN STRAMER, PHD, WILL SERVE AS THE PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR (PI) AT ARC. SHE WILL OVERSEE ALL ASPECTS OF ARCÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S PARTICIPATION IN THE LRCC PORTION OF TTIMS INCLUDING ACQUISITION OF DONOR DATA AND BIOSPECIMENS AND WILL PARTICIPATE IN CALLS AND MEETINGS FOR THE TTIMS PROJECT. IN ADDITION, ROGER DODD, PHD, WILL SERVE AS THE CO-PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR AT ARC. HE WILL ASSIST IN THE OVERSIGHT OF THE ACQUISITION OF DONOR DATA AND WILL PARTICIPATE IN CALLS AND MEETINGS FOR THE TTIMS PROJECT WHEN NECESSARY. ARC WILL RECRUIT DONORS WITH QUALIFYING TEST RESULTS; ADMINISTER THE WEB-BASED QUESTIONNAIRE AND ENTER RISK FACTOR DATA INTO AN ELECTRONIC DATABASE; PERFORM QUALITY CONTROL (QC) ON ALL DATA ENTERED INTO THE DATABASE; RESPOND TO REQUESTS FROM THE LRCC REGARDING DATA QUALITY ASSURANCE AND QC; DEVELOP AND SUBMIT TO THE LOCAL IRB DOCUMENTS AND AMENDMENTS FOR APPROVAL. ARC STAFF WILL PROVIDE TO VRI 5 X 1 ML PLASMA CRYOVIALS AND A SINGLE 5 ML PLASMA CRYOVIAL FOR EACH PARTICIPANT. IN COLLABORATION WITH THE LRCC, ARC WILL COORDINATE SAMPLE SHIPMENT WITH DESIGNATED VRI STAFF. IN ADDITION, ARC WILL WORK WITH THE LRCC AND CTS TO SOURCE SPECIMENS FOR ARV/PEP/PREP TESTING. ARC WILL ALSO WORK THE LRCC TO FACILITATE SURVEYS AND QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS OF ARV/PEP/PREP TEST-POSITIVE BLOOD DONORS. ARC WILL BE A COLLABORATOR IN THE COLLECTION OF THESE SURVEY AND QUALITATIVE INTERVIEW DATA AND WILL ASSIST IN IDENTIFYING AND RECRUITING PARTICIPANTS FOR THESE ACTIVITIES. ADDENDUMS TO THIS SOW WILL BE DEVELOPED AFTER THE RESEARCH PROTOCOLS TO SUPPORT EXPANDED ART/PEP/PREP STUDIES ARE FULLY DEFINED AND APPROVED BY THE TTIMS STEERING COMMITTEE.

Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ EVALUATE WELL-CHARACTERIZED US BLOOD DONOR SAMPLES FROM TTIMS AND OTHER SOURCES FOR THE REFINEMENT OF EXISTING ANALYTICAL METHODS SUCH AS THE SEDIA LAG AVIDITY ASSAY TO DERIVE ESTIMATES OF RECENT INFECTION WITH HIV WITH A GOAL OF RAPIDLY OBTAINING MORE ACCURATE AND TIMELY RESULTS. Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ PROVIDE LOGISTICAL SUPPORT FOR THE TTIMS PROJECT AND FOR THE COMMITTEE/SUBCOMMITTEE MEETINGS, CONFERENCES, AND DONATION(S) TRANSFER/SHIPMENT. IN SUPPORT OF THESE OBJECTIVES, NYBC WILL RECRUIT, ENROLL AND INTERVIEW ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS, PROVIDE DATA AS REQUIRED IN THE TTIMS LRCC STATEMENT OF WORK, PROVIDE BIOSPECIMENS FOR RESEARCH TESTING AT VRI, AND WILL ACTIVELY COLLABORATE IN THE ANALYSIS, INTERPRETATION, AND REPORTING OF FINDINGS IN TTIMS. DEBRA KESSLER, WILL SERVE AS THE PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR (PI) AT NYBC. SHE WILL OVERSEE ALL ASPECTS OF NYBCÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S PARTICIPATION IN THE LRCC PORTION OF TTIMS INCLUDING ACQUISITION OF DONOR DATA AND BIOSPECIMENS AND WILL PARTICIPATE IN CALLS AND MEETINGS FOR THE TTIMS PROJECT. IN ADDITION, CARLOS DEL VALLE, WILL SERVE AS THE STUDY MANAGER AT NYBC. HE WILL ASSIST IN THE OVERSIGHT OF THE ACQUISITION OF DONOR DATA, AND WILL PARTICIPATE IN CALLS AND MEETINGS FOR THE TTIMS PROJECT WHEN NECESSARY. NYBC WILL RECRUIT DONORS WITH QUALIFYING TEST RESULTS; ADMINISTER THE WEB-BASED QUESTIONNAIRE AND ENTER RISK FACTOR DATA INTO AN ELECTRONIC DATABASE; PERFORM QUALITY CONTROL (QC) ON ALL DATA ENTERED INTO THE DATABASE; RESPOND TO REQUESTS FROM THE LRCC REGARDING DATA QUALITY ASSURANCE AND QC; DEVELOP AND SUBMIT TO THE LOCAL IRB DOCUMENTS AND AMENDMENTS FOR APPROVAL. NYBC STAFF WILL FORWARD PLASMA BAGS AND/OR PILOT TUBES TO CREATIVE TESTING SOLUTIONS (CTS) SO THAT CTS CAN CREATE UP TO 5 X 2 ML PLASMA CYROVIALS AND A SINGLE 15 ML PLASMA CRYOVIAL FOR EACH PARTICIPANT AND PREPARE ALIQUOTS FOR SHIPMENT TO THE REPOSITORY AND ADDITIONAL TESTING AT VRI FOR ALL INFECTIONS OF INTEREST AS DEFINED BY THE TTIMS STEERING COMMITTEE. IN COLLABORATION WITH THE LRCC, NYBC WILL COORDINATE SAMPLE SHIPMENT WITH DESIGNATED CTS STAFF. IN ADDITION, NYBC WILL WORK WITH THE LRCC AND CTS TO SOURCE SPECIMENS FOR ARV/PEP/PREP TESTING. NYBC WILL ALSO WORK THE LRCC TO FACILITATE SURVEYS AND QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS OF ARV/PEP/PREP REACTIVE BLOOD DONORS. NYBC WILL NOT BE EXPECTED TO LEAD THE COLLECTION OF THESE SURVEY AND QUALITATIVE INTERVIEW DATA BUT WILL ASSIST IN IDENTIFYING AND RECRUITING PARTICIPANTS FOR THESE ACTIVITIES. ADDENDUMS TO THIS SOW WILL BE DEVELOPED AFTER THE RESEARCH PROTOCOLS TO SUPPORT EXPANDED ART/PEP/PREP STUDIES ARE FULLY DEFINED AND APPROVED BY THE TTIMS STEERING COMMITTEE. description: STATEMENT OF WORK: DEFINING THE ROLE OF CD8 T CELLS INDUCED BY A NOVEL LIPOSOMAL NANOPARTICLE MRNA VACCINE IN PREVENTING MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. THE GOAL OF IMPAC-TB IS TO IDENTIFY MECHANISMS OF PROTECTIVE IMMUNITY AGAINST TB, AND OUR OVERALL STRATEGY FOR THE CASCADE IMPAC-TB ANIMAL PROGRAM IS TO START WITH GOLD-STANDARDS OF VACCINE-MEDIATED PROTECTION (I.E, CMV/TB AND IV BCG IN NHP; BCG IN MICE) AND THEN DISSECT HOW PROTECTION IS MEDIATED. THE AKAGERA MRNA VACCINE REPRESENTS A NEW GOLD STANDARD FOR PREVENTION OF INFECTION Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ THE BEST VACCINE-MEDIATED PROTECTION EVER OBSERVED IN MICE. TO ACHIEVE OUR GOAL OF IDENTIFYING MECHANISMS OF TB IMMUNITY, CASCADE IMPAC-TB WOULD LIKE TO IDENTIFY THE ANTIGENS AND T CELL SUBSETS THAT MEDIATE THE PROTECTION PROVIDED BY THE NEW AKAGERA MRNA VACCINE, WHICH SHOWS THE BEST VACCINE-MEDIATED PROTECTION EVER OBSERVED IN MICE. THE SPECIFIC WORK TO BE PERFORMED IS DETAILED BELOW. UNDER ALL THREE AIMS, AKAGERA MEDICINES WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR CREATING THE MRNA VACCINE CONSTRUCTS REQUIRED FOR EACH EXPERIMENT. IN ADDITION, SCIENTISTS AT AKAGERA MEDICINES WILL ALSO MEET REGULARLY WITH SCIENTISTS AT SCRI TO EVALUATE PROGRESS, DESIGN NEW CONSTRUCTS, AND TROUBLE-SHOOT, AS NECESSARY. AIM 1: IDENTIFY PROTECTIVE ANTIGENS IN THE AKAGERA MRNA VACCINE. AKAGERA MEDICINES WILL PREPARE SEPARATE MRNA VACCINE CONSTRUCTS FOR 4 ORFS (TB10.4, MTB39, AND ESAT-6 WHICH ARE THE MOST IMMUNOGENIC ANTIGENS IN THE MRNA VACCINE, AND MTB32, WHICH ALONG WITH MTB39 IS PART OF THE M72 VACCINE). THESE WILL BE SENT TO SCRI FOR TESTING IN MICE, TO COMPARE THE PROTECTIVE EFFICACY OF THE PARENTAL MRNA VACCINE, EACH OF THESE 4 CONSTRUCTS INDIVIDUALLY, POOLED ADMINISTRATION OF TB10.4, MTB39, ESAT-6 MRNA CONSTRUCTS, AND THAT SAME POOL WITH THE ADDITION OF MTB32. SCRI WILL MEASURE THE THREE METRICS OF IMMUNITY THAT WERE PREVIOUSLY DEFINED IN THE ULD MODEL: REDUCTION OF LUNG BACTERIAL BURDENS, PREVENTION OF DISSEMINATION TO THE CONTRALATERAL LUNG, AND PREVENTION OF DETECTABLE INFECTION. COLONIES WILL BE COLLECTED, DNA ISOLATED, AND BAR-CODES AMPLIFIED AND SEQUENCED TO DETERMINE THE NUMBER OF FOUNDING MTB STRAINS IN EACH LUNG. BECAUSE THE GROUP SIZES WILL HAVE TO BE REDUCED TO 15 MICE (RATHER THAN OUR MORE STANDARD 20) TO ACCOMMODATE THE NUMBER OF VACCINES TESTED SIMULTANEOUSLY, THE EXPERIMENT WILL BE REPEATED FOUR TIMES TO ASSURE REPRODUCIBILITY AND STATISTICAL RIGOR. IF PROTECTION CONFERRED BY THE THREE OR FOUR POOLED ANTIGENS IS NOT SIMILAR TO THAT CONFERRED BY THE PARENT VACCINE, AKAGERA MEDICINES WILL SYNTHESIZE ADDITIONAL ANTIGENS UNTIL A COCKTAIL OF ANTIGENS THAT CONFERS SIMILAR PROTECTION IS FOUND. AIM 2: IDENTIFY AND ELIMINATE CD8 EPITOPES FROM MRNA VACCINE CONSTRUCTS. THIS AIM WILL FOCUS ON EACH ANTIGEN THAT CONFERRED SOME DEGREE OF PROTECTION AGAINST ESTABLISHING SUSTAINED INFECTION IN AIM 1. ANTIGENS THAT DID NOT PREVENT DETECTABLE INFECTION WILL NOT BE EXAMINED FURTHER IN AIM 2. IN PRIOR CD8 EPITOPE MAPPING STUDIES, TB10.4 IS KNOWN TO HAVE TWO EPITOPES, TB10.4 ON THE H-2B BACKGROUND (C57BL/6) AND TB10.4 ON THE H-2D BACKGROUND (BALB/C), AND MTB32A IS KNOWN TO HAVE ONE EPITOPE ON THE H-2B BACKGROUND (C57BL/6) (MTB32). THUS, IF THESE ANTIGENS ARE FOUND TO CONTRIBUTE TO PREVENTION OF INFECTION IN AIM 1, AKAGERA MEDICINES WILL MAKE A TRUNCATED TB10.4 OR MTB32A CONSTRUCT THAT LACKS THE RESPECTIVE CD8 EPITOPES, BUT WHICH WOULD STILL CONTAIN KNOWN CD4 EPITOPES. FOR MTB39 AND ESAT6, THE CD8 EPITOPES HAVE NOT BEEN MAPPED, BUT IF EITHER MTB39 OR ESAT-6 WERE SHOWN IN AIM 1 TO CONTRIBUTE TO PREVENTING INFECTION, AKAGERA WOULD GENERATE OVERLAPPING PEPTIDES FOR EACH ANTIGEN AND MAP THE EPITOPE(S) RESPONSIBLE USING STIMULATIONS ASSAYS WITH SPLENOCYTES FROM IMMUNIZED B6XBALB/C F1 MICE. AFTER IDENTIFYING THE EPITOPES, AKAGERA MEDICINES WOULD GENERATE NEW CONSTRUCTS THAT SPECIFICALLY LACKED THE CD8 EPITOPES, EITHER VIA TRUNCATION OR POINT MUTATION OF AMINO ACID RESIDUES PREDICTED TO BE CRITICAL FOR THE RESPONSE. description: THE PURPOSE OF THIS SUBAWARD IS TO STUDY HOW THE BASELINE STATE AND FUNCTION OF ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES CAN BE ALTERED BY VACCINATION AND OTHER HOST FACTORS, IN THE CONTEXT OF MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL INVESTIGATE THE MECHANISMS THAT DRIVE INNATE CELL REPROGRAMMING BY VACCINATION AND ITS IMPACT ON THE HOST IMMUNE RESPONSE AND BACTERIAL CONTROL. THE SUBAWARD WILL ALSO PERFORM A CROSS-SPECIES ANALYSIS OF ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES BY ANALYZING EPIGENETIC STATES ACROSS MOUSE AND HUMAN SAMPLES AND LINKING MACROPHAGE EPIGENETIC STATES TO TRANSCRIPTIONAL RESPONSES. 1) ANALYZE EPIGENETIC PROFILES GENERATED BY ATAC-SEQ AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL PROFILES GENERATED BY RNA-SEQ FOR UNTREATED VERSUS INTERFERON-TRAINED MURINE ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES. 2) PERFORM ATAC-SEQ EPIGENETIC PROFILING ON FROZEN HUMAN ADHERENT BAL SAMPLES FROM ACTIVE TB, RESISTER, HEALTHY CONTROLS, AND SUBCLINICAL TB INDIVIDUALS. PROFILING INCLUDES: CELL PREPARATION, TRANSPOSITION REACTION AND PURIFICATION, PCR AMPLIFICATION, LIBRARY PURIFICATION, AND LIBRARY QC. 3) COMPARE AND CONTRAST MOUSE AND HUMAN ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGE TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND EPIGENETIC PROFILES. 4) GENERATE BULK RNA-SEQUENCING SAMPLES FOR MTB-INFECTED B6 AND C3H ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGES FOLLOWING SA161 HIGH DOSE AEROSOL INFECTION. 5) PERFORM IN VITRO MTB INFECTIONS AND IN VIVO AEROSOL INFECTIONS AFTER AM TRANSFER USING WT, SP140-/-, AND SP140-/-IFNAR-/- MURINE EX VIVO ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGE (MEXAM) PRIMARY CELL LINES TO STUDY ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGE RESPONSE TO VACCINATION AND INTERFERON EXPOSURES.

description: SERVING AS PROXIMAL SPOKES, THE NATIONAL SMART IRB AMBASSADORS ARE ESSENTIAL CONTRIBUTORS TO BI-DIRECTIONAL COMMUNICATION BETWEEN THE CTSAS, TINS, IRBS, RESEARCH TEAMS, INSTITUTIONS AND THE SMART IRB TEAM. DURING THE FIRST PHASE OF SMART IRB, THE AMBASSADORS SUCCESSFULLY BUILT TRUST WITH CONSTITUENTS, DROVE AND ENABLED SIGN-ON TO THE SMART IRB AGREEMENT, AND SERVED AS AN ESSENTIAL RESOURCE FOR TRAININGS, WORKFLOW DEVELOPMENT, AND DISSEMINATION OF RESOURCES. THE SMART IRB AMBASSADORS WILL CONTINUE TO REPRESENT THEIR HOME INSTITUTIONS AND OTHER CTSAS AS ASSIGNED AS WELL AS WILL WORK WITH OTHER AMBASSADORS TO BRING POSITIVE CHANGE TO ALL INSTITUTIONS INVOLVED. IN ADDITION, SMART IRB AMBASSADORS WILL SERVE AS DOMAIN EXPERTS, RESPECTED BY THEIR PEERS, AND WORK COLLABORATIVELY TO COLLECT FEEDBACK FROM USERS, REPRESENT SMART IRB ON NATIONAL COMMITTEES, AND DESIGN AND CONDUCT PILOT STUDIES OF POTENTIALLY HARMONIZED POLICIES AND PROCESSES. IMPORTANTLY, SMART IRB AMBASSADORS WILL ALSO IDENTIFY A CADRE OF EXPERIENCED SUPER USERS TO ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF TRAININGS AND MATERIALS ORIENTED TOWARD PREPARING STUDY TEAMS FOR A SMOOTH TRANSITION TO SINGLE IRB REVIEW. IN TURN, THE SMART IRB AMBASSADORS WILL BE A KEY COMPONENT TO DEVELOPING MATERIALS FOR, AND ENCOURAGE THE ADOPTION OF, THE SMART IRB RELIANCE LEARNING COMPENDIUM AND THE NATIONAL COMMON REGULATORY PORTFOLIO.

description: THE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES OF DTU AS PART OF IEDB & AR PROGRAM ARE TO MAINTAIN, ENHANCE AND UPDATE THE EXISTING SET OF EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS, AND DEVELOP NEW TOOLS FOR THE ANALYSIS RESOURCE. DTU WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN PERIODIC TELECONFERENCES AND MEETINGS, AND PROVIDE TASK STATUS FOR THE QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS. SPECIFICALLY, DTU WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS: A. ANALYSIS RESOURCE TASKS 1. MAINTAIN AND UPDATE THE EXISTING MHC CLASS I AND II BINDING PREDICTION TOOLS. THIS WILL INCLUDE RE-TRAINING THE PREDICTION TOOLS AS SUFFICIENT NEW DATA BECOMES AVAILABLE. 2. DEVELOP NEW MHC CLASS I AND II EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS INCLUDING DEVELOPMENT OF TCR BASED EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS USING THE TCR SEQUENCE AND STRUCTURE INFORMATION. 3. MAINTAIN AND UPDATE MHC PROCESSING PREDICTION TOOLS. THIS WILL INCLUDE RE-TRAINING THE PREDICTION TOOLS AS SUFFICIENT NEW DATA BECOMES AVAILABLE. 4. UPDATE EVALUATIONS OF THE MHC BINDING AND T CELL PROCESSING PREDICTION TOOLS. 5. MAINTAIN EXISTING B CELL TOOLS DEVELOPED BY DTU. 6. DEVELOP NEW B CELL EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS INCLUDING DEVELOPMENT OF ANTIBODY SPECIFIC EPITOPE PREDICTION TOOLS USING BCR SEQUENCE INFORMATION. 7. ESTABLISH AUTOMATED BENCHMARKING SYSTEMS FOR PROCESSING PREDICTION TOOLS AS WELL AS PREDICTION TOOLS NOT HOSTED IN THE IEDB. 8. PROVIDE UPDATED BENCHMARK DATASETS WITH RESPECT TO THESE TASKS, DTU WILL DEVELOP CODE IN THEIR LOCAL ENVIRONMENT AND ENSURE THAT IT CAN BE EXECUTED APPROPRIATELY IN THE IEDB PRODUCTION ENVIRONMENT AND WORK WITH THE LJI TEAM TO UPDATE WEB SERVERS EXECUTING THE CODE AS NECESSARY. THIS INCLUDES RETRAINING, BUG FIXES, AND FEATURE ENHANCEMENTS AS THEY OCCUR. FOR ANY NEW TOOL OR SUBSTANTIAL TOOL UPDATE DEVELOPED WITH FUNDING FROM THE IEDB BY DTU, THE PRIMARY PUBLICATION WILL INCLUDE A LINK TO THE WORKING TOOL ON THE IEDB WEBSITE. B. MEETINGS AND REPORTS 1. MEETINGS/TELECONFERENCES/VIDEOCONFERENCES DTU WILL PARTICIPATE IN MEETINGS WITH LJI AT A MINIMUM OF TWICE PER MONTH, EITHER IN PERSON OR VIA TELECONFERENCE/VIDEOCONFERENCE. THE PURPOSE OF THESE MEETINGS WILL BE TO COORDINATE EFFORTS AND REPORT PROGRESS. DTU WILL ALSO BE EXPECTED TO PARTICIPATE IN 1-2 US BASED PROGRAM MEETINGS PER CONTRACT YEAR FOR THE PURPOSE OF PROVIDING FEEDBACK TO NIH AND FURTHER PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT. 2. QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL REPORTS DTU WILL PROVIDE INPUT FOR THE QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL REPORTS ON A TIMELY BASIS SO THEIR CONTENT CAN BE INCORPORATED IN ADVANCE OF THE SPECIFIED DELIVERY DATE TO NIAID.

description: THE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY OF LEIDOS AS PART OF THE IEDB & AR PROGRAM IS TO MAINTAIN AND IMPROVE THE EXISTING IEDB DATABASE AND CURATION SYSTEMS. IN ADDITION, LEIDOS SHALL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN PERIODIC MEETINGS, PROVIDE PROGRESS REPORTS ON THE WORK AND RESPOND TO IEDB HELP DESK TICKETS IF REQUIRED. AN OVERVIEW OF TASKS TO BE ACCOMPLISHED BY LEIDOS ARE LISTED BELOW: A. IMMUNE EPITOPE DATABASE TASKS 1. ASSIST LJI IN THE MAINTENANCE, CONTINUED IMPROVEMENT AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXISTING IEDB DATABASE SYSTEM AND MAKING IT AVAILABLE TO END USERS. THE SYSTEM SHOULD INCLUDE COLLECTION, STORAGE, ANALYSIS, ARCHIVE AND EXCHANGE OF IMMUNE EPITOPE DATA AND ACCOMPANYING INFORMATION. 2. ASSIST LJI IN MAINTENANCE AND ENHANCEMENT OF THE IEDB WEB PORTAL INCLUDING: A. FURTHER OPTIMIZATION, DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF UNIFORM, INTELLIGENT WEB-BASED INTERFACES FOR MAKING DATA ACCESSIBLE TO END USERS. THE INTERFACE SHALL MINIMALLY INCLUDE COMPLEX QUERY; SEMANTIC QUERY; DOWNLOAD; EPITOPE SUBMISSION; LINKS TO RELATED RESOURCES; AND REPORTS, MANUSCRIPTS, NEWSLETTERS, AND COMPENDIA. B. UPDATE EXISTING FEATURES AND IMPLEMENT NEW FEATURES IN THE IEDB WEB PORTAL AS NEEDED. C. ASSIST IN ESTABLISHING AND TRACKING PERFORMANCE METRICS TO DETERMINE UTILIZATION AND UTILITY OF THE WEB PORTAL WITHIN THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. RELEVANT METRICS SHALL FREQUENCY OF DATA DOWNLOADS, CHARACTERIZATION OF USERS AND USER QUERY STATISTICS. AT A MINIMUM, THIS ACTIVITY SHOULD BE CONDUCTED BI-ANNUALLY (EVERY 2 YEARS). 3. UPON REQUEST, ASSIST LJI IN THE MAINTENANCE AND UPDATING OF SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION INCLUDING: A. DOCUMENT ALL SYSTEM COMPONENTS, SOFTWARE AND DATABASES IN ACCORDANCE WITH INDUSTRY BEST PRACTICES AND IN A MANNER THAT WILL ALLOW ANOTHER CONTRACTOR OR USER TO UNDERSTAND AND UTILIZE THE SYSTEM. B. PROVIDE A HIGH LEVEL OVERVIEW OF FUNCTIONS AND FEATURES OF THE SYSTEM, INCLUDING SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE, HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE DESIGN, DATABASE DESIGN AND DATA MODELS. THIS COMPENDIUM OF FUNCTIONS AND FEATURES SHALL BE UPDATED SEMI-ANNUALLY OR AS REQUESTED BY THE COTR OR CONTRACTING OFFICER. C. WORK WITH LJI TO ESTABLISH AND DOCUMENT A SCHEDULE OF SYSTEM UPDATES AND RELEASES. 4. COMPLY WITH SECTION 508 OF THE REHABILITATION ACT (29 U.S.C. 794D), (SEE HTTP://WWW.SECTION508.GOV/) IN TERMS OF DATABASE/WEBSITE USE AND DIRECT EPITOPE/DATA SUBMISSION BY THE BROADER RESEARCH COMMUNITY. B. CURATION SYSTEM TASKS 1. ASSIST LJI IN THE MAINTENANCE, CONTINUED IMPROVEMENT AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EXISTING IEDB CURATION SYSTEM. THE SYSTEM SHOULD INCLUDE COLLECTION, TRACKING, AND ASSIGNMENT OF PUBLISHED MANUSCRIPTS AND ACCOMPANYING INFORMATION. C. MEETINGS AND REPORTS PARTICIPATE IN WEEKLY MEETINGS TO COORDINATE SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT EFFORTS. ADDITIONALLY, PROVIDE QUARTERLY AND ANNUAL REPORTS SUMMARIZING WORK PERFORMED. D. COMMUNITY OUTREACH 1. IF REQUESTED, ASSIST WITH ADDRESSING ANY HELP DESK TICKETS RELATED TO ANY IEDB SYSTEMS INFRASTRUCTURE. 2. ASSIST LJI WITH PREPARING A COMPENDIUM OF THE DATA IN THE IMMUNE EPITOPE DATABASE ON AN ANNUAL BASIS.

description: THE DU PLESSIS/WALZL LABORATORY AT STELLENBOSCH UNIVERSITY (SU) WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE CLINICAL AND IMMUNOLOGICAL WORK (INCLUDING ON-SITE DATA MANAGEMENT) OF THE PROJECT. SU WILL COORDINATE THE STUDY DESIGN, PARTICIPANT SCREENING AND ENROLLMENT FOR THE CASCADE HOUSEHOLD CONTACT STUDY, PERFORM BRONCHOSCOPIES AND MANAGE SAMPLE SHARING TO PARTICIPATING SITES. SU WILL PROVIDE INPUT IN THE DESIGN, EXECUTION AND DATA ANALYSIS OF IMMUNOLOGICAL STUDIES AND PARTICIPATE IN THE LEADERSHIP TEAM OF Ã¢Â‚¬Å“CASCADE IMPAC-TBÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ CENTER. SU WILL INTERACT AND COORDINATE ALL PROJECT ACTIVITIES WITH THE PI OF THE PROJECT. DR. DU PLESSIS AND DR. WALZL, THE SU CO-PIÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S WILL REVIEW ALL RAW DATA GENERATED BY THE SU TEAM, AND SUPERVISE THE LABORATORY WORK, AND THE RESEARCH TECHNICIANS. SPECIFIC DELIVERABLES FOR YEAR 6 OF THE CONTRACT AT SU INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING: A. RECRUITMENT: THE ANTICIPATED SCREENING AND RECRUITMENT GOALS HAVE BEEN ACHIEVED AND EXCEEDED. WHILE THE INITIAL RECRUITMENT TARGET WAS SET AT 20 PARTICIPANTS FOR EACH OF THE 8 CLINICAL GROUPS (N=160 TOTAL), WE EXCEEDED THIS TO ACHIEVE AND ENROLL A TOTAL NUMBER OF 185 STUDY PARTICIPANTS ACROSS ALL GROUPS FOR THE MAIN STUDY. THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC HAS RESULTED IN A REQUEST FOR A SOMEWHAT ALTERED CLASSIFICATION AND ENROLLMENT TARGET OF CLINICAL GROUPS, WHICH WAS APPROVED BY THE NIH IN 2021. THE SU HHC STUDY NOW CONSISTS OF GROUPS STRATIFIED NOT ONLY BY IGRA RESULTS OR PET/CT READOUT, BUT ALSO BY SARS-COV-2 SEROLOGY STATUS. THE BUDGET FOR PERIOD 6 WILL INCLUDE LIMITED PARTICIPANT RECRUITMENT AND BRONCHOSCOPIES, AS ORIGINALLY PROPOSED, WHICH WILL INCLUDE ONLY STUDY PARTICIPANTS FROM SELECTED Ã¢Â‚¬Å“BIOLOGICALLY INTERESTINGÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ CLINICAL PHENOTYPES FOR FURTHER TARGETED FUNCTIONAL ANALYSES THROUGH GRANULOMA MODEL MANIPULATION. SU HAS BUDGETED FOR N=12 BRONCHOSCOPIES. B. END-ASSAYS: IMMUNOPHENOTYPING EXPERIMENTS Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ ONE OF THE DELIVERABLES AT SU IS TO CONDUCT DEEP PHENOTYPING OF PAIRED BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE (BAL) AND PBMC FROM THE VARIOUS CASCADE HOUSEHOLD CONTACT STUDY CLINICAL GROUPS. SU HAS EVALUATED THE ASSAY PRIORITY LIST, AS WELL AS THE BAL AND PBMC SAMPLES COLLECTED FROM PARTICIPANTS ENROLLED IN THE CASCADE HOUSEHOLD CONTACT STUDY, TO ENUMERATE THE NUMBER OF STORED SAMPLES AVAILABLE FOR THE OBJECTIVES RELATED TO THE PROPOSED PLANS FOR THIS END-ASSAY. OF ALL MAIN STUDY PARTICIPANTS FROM WHICH PAIRED BAL AND PBMC HAVE BEEN COLLECTED (N=190), SUFFICIENT CELL NUMBERS WERE OBTAINED FROM 88% OF PARTICIPANTS, WHICH INCLUDES MAKING USE OF RESIDUALLY STORED BAL CELLS. THIS ALSO INCLUDES REPLACEMENT OR REPEATING OF BRONCHOSCOPIES FOR N=5 OF THE PARTICIPANTS WITH LOW CELL YIELDS. WHILE THE BAL CELL AUTOFLUORESCENCE IS LIKELY TO RESULT IN A SMALLER NUMBER OF AVAILABLE FLUORESCENT CHANNELS FOR OUR BAL MYELOID FLOW CYTOMETRY IMMUNE PHENOTYPING PANEL, THE OPTIMIZATION OF THE 24 MARKER MYELOID PANEL FOR PBMC HAS BEEN COMPLETED WHILE OPTIMIZATION OF THE 27 MARKER LYMPHOID PANEL FOR PBMC WILL BE FINALIZED IN OCTOBER 2024. SU EXPECTS TO COMPLETE IMMUNE PHENOTYPING OF ALL SU HHC PBMC SAMPLES BY JUNE 2025. IMMUNE PHENOTYPING OF ALL SU HHC BAL SAMPLES USING THE LYMPHOID FLOW CYTOMETRY PANEL WILL BE COMPLETED BY DECEMBER 2025. GRANULOMA MODEL/KILLING ASSAYS Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ SU WILL MAKE USE OF THE IN VITRO GRANULOMA MODEL ALONG WITH PARALLEL ASSESSMENTS IN MONOLAYER CULTURE AND UNFRACTIONATED PBMC AND BAL, TO ASSESS MTB KILLING AMONGST THE VARIOUS CLINICAL GROUPS. INTERESTING FINDINGS RELATED TO MTB CONTROL WILL BE TESTED IN FUTURE IN GRANULOMA MODEL EXPERIMENTS. BY USING CLINICAL SAMPLES FROM PARTICIPANTS NOT ELIGIBLE ACCORDING TO THE CASCADE HHC STUDY CRITERIA, SU HAS OPTIMIZED THE MODEL AND ALSO IMPLEMENTED CHANGES TO STREAMLINE BACTERIAL LOAD ASSESSMENT THROUGH MGIT CULTURE. SU EXPECTS TO COMPLETE THE KILLING ASSAY EXPERIMENTS FOR AT LEAST A QUARTER OF ALL SU HHC SAMPLES BY THE END OF PERIOD 6. description: MPHI IS A NON-PROFIT PUBLIC HEALTH INSTITUTE MADE UP OF RESEARCHERS, EVALUATORS, AND CONTENT DEVELOPERS AIMED AT PROMOTING HEALTH AND WELLBEING. MPHI WILL CONTINUE TO CONTRIBUTE ITS EXPERTISE IN RESEARCH AND PROJECT EVALUATION TO SUPPORT PLANNING AND EVALUATION ACTIVITIES FOR THE S-TAC PROJECT. AS LEAD EVALUATOR FOR THIS PROJECT YEAR, THE GOAL OF THIS PARTNERSHIP IS TO SUPPORT THE S-TAC AND ITS PARTNERS IN CONDUCTING EVALUATION AND QUALITY IMPROVEMENT ACROSS ALL S-TAC TA ACTIVITIES AND DELIVERABLES PROVIDED THROUGHOUT OPTION YEAR 1 OF THE S-TAC'S CONTRACT. CCBHC S-TAC IS FUNDED THROUGH A CONTRACT BY THE SUBSTANCE USE AND MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES ADMINISTRATION (SAMHSA), WHICH REQUIRES PROJECT EVALUATION ACTIVITIES AND REPORTING DURING EACH PROJECT YEAR. MPHI IS MADE UP OF OVER 1,000 CONTENT AND PROCESS EXPERTS ACROSS MULTIPLE TOPIC AREAS, BRINGING TOGETHER DIVERSE KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERTISE. EXPERTS FROM MPHI WORK WITH STAKEHOLDERS FROM ACADEMIA, GOVERNMENT, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, AND HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS ACROSS TO U.S. TO STRENGTHEN PUBLIC HEALTH AND MENTAL WELLBEING AND INFLUENCE POLICY AND PRACTICE THROUGH RESEARCH, CONTENT DEVELOPMENT, AND EVALUATION ACTIVITIES. IN LINE WITH THEIR EXPERTISE, THE MPHI WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT TASK 4 IN ADDITION TO TASK 2 OF THE CCBHC STAC PROJECT WITH EVALUATION PLAN DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT, INCLUDING WORKING IN PARTNERSHIP WITH KEY STAKEHOLDERS TO ENSURE THE EVALUATION QUESTIONS, METHODOLOGY AND DATA COLLECTED ARE APPLICABLE AND USEFUL IN ASSESSING KEY OUTCOMES OF INTEREST AND INFORMING QUALITY IMPROVEMENT AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS. MPHI IS A CRITICAL PARTNER TO S-TAC IN THIS WORK BECAUSE OF THEIR HISTORICAL INVOLVEMENT IN THIS EFFORT IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE NATIONAL COUNCIL. MPHI IS THE EVALUATION LEAD FOR THE TWO OTHER SAMHSA FUNDED TA CENTERS AT THE NATIONAL COUNCIL, NTTAC AND THE COE-IHS. S-TAC WOULD LIKE TO BUILD THEIR PARTNERSHIP WITH MPHI AS THEIR EVALUATION LEAD ON EFFORTS MOVING FORWARD TO ENSURE BETTER ALIGNMENT IN DATA COLLECTION AND EVALUATION EFFORTS ACROSS ALL THREE TA CENTERS FUNDED BY SAMHSA HOSTED BY THE NATIONAL COUNCIL. TASK 2 – 396 HOURS PROVIDE EVALUATION CONSULTATION AND STRATEGY TO THE NATIONAL COUNCIL STAC EVALUATION TEAM AND SOLIDIFY AN EVALUATION PLAN FOR YEARS 2 AND 3 OF THE STAC PROJECT. – 183 HOURS TASK ORDER 4 – 136 HOURS CONTINUE TO WORK WITH THE NATIONAL COUNCIL AND THEIR IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE PARTNERS TO SUPPORT THE EVALUATION OF THE EBP IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE PILOT ACTIVITIES. THESE ACTIVITIES MAY INCLUDE ATTENDING MEETINGS AND PROVIDING FEEDBACK, DEVELOPING A DISSEMINATING AND EVALUATION SURVEY TOOL, WORKING WITH NATIONAL COUNCIL AND OTHER KEY PROJECT PARTNERS TO IDENTIFY OTHER KEY EVALUATION QUESTIONS, PARTICIPATE IN AND CONDUCT PRELIMINARY QUALITATIVE ANALYSIS OF LISTENING SESSIONS WITH CCBHC-E GRANTEES AND SUPPORTING THE USE OF DATA TO INFORM FUTURE TTA PROGRAMMING AND ACTIVITIES.

description: THIS STAKEHOLDER RESEARCH WILL SERVE AS A FOUNDATIONAL STEP IN DEVELOPING A COMPREHENSIVE STRATEGIC ENGAGEMENT PLAN AND A THEORY OF CHANGE AIMED AT PROMOTING THE ADOPTION OF FAIR DATA MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, ESPECIALLY WITHIN MINORITY SERVING INSTITUTIONS (MSIS) AND HISTORICALLY BLACK COLLEGES AND UNIVERSITIES (HBCUS). BY DEEPLY ANALYZING THE FACTORS THAT INFLUENCE RESEARCHERSÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ DECISIONS TO EITHER SUPPORT, ADOPT, REJECT, OR OVERLOOK FAIR PRINCIPLES, THE RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHTS INTO THE BARRIERS AND MOTIVATORS SPECIFIC TO THESE COMMUNITIES. UNDERSTANDING THESE DYNAMICS WILL ALLOW US TO TAILOR ENGAGEMENT STRATEGIES THAT ADDRESS UNIQUE CHALLENGES FACED BY RESEARCHERS AT MSIS AND HBCUS, ENSURING THAT THE INITIATIVES ARE NOT ONLY RELEVANT BUT ALSO CULTURALLY AND CONTEXTUALLY APPROPRIATE. THIS APPROACH WILL HELP FOSTER A MORE INCLUSIVE AND EQUITABLE ENVIRONMENT FOR THE WIDESPREAD ADOPTION OF FAIR DATA MANAGEMENT AND SHARING PRACTICES.

description: OPTION SAMPLE AND DATA 6 Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ GALE THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE IMPAC-TB PROGRAM IS TO INFORM THE RATIONAL DESIGN OF AN EFFECTIVE TB VACCINE BY IDENTIFICATION OF IMMUNE RESPONSES THAT ARE CAPABLE OF CONTROLLING AND POTENTIALLY EVEN ERADICATING MTB. WE WILL ACHIEVE THIS GOAL BY IDENTIFYING AND DISSECTING PROTECTIVE PATHWAYS IN NATURAL AND VACCINE-INDUCED IMMUNITY THROUGH INTEGRATED ANALYSES OF TISSUE-SPECIFIC AND SYSTEMIC IMMUNITY IN MICE, NON-HUMAN PRIMATES (NHP), AND HUMANS. THE TASKS COVERED IN OUR OPTION 6 BUDGET ARE DESIGNED TO AUGMENT THE TASKS THAT WE ARE PERFORMING THROUGH OUR YEAR 6 BASE BUDGET. SPECIFICALLY: 1. THE GALE LABORATORY WILL CONDUCT RNA-SEQ ASSAYS FOR THE NHP IMMUNOLOGIC STUDIES. OUR YEAR 6 BASE BUDGET COVERS PERFORMING RNA-SEQ ASSAYS ON THE MAJORITY OF THE SAMPLES FROM NHP EXPERIMENTS BUT NOT ALL OF THEM. UNDER OUR OPTION 6 BUDGET, WE WILL PROCESS THE REMAINING SAMPLES FROM THESE STUDIES. TASKS INCLUDE 1) RECEIVING THESE ADDITIONAL SAMPLES AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MINNESOTA FROM THE PICKER LAB (OHSU), 2) ISOLATING RNA FROM THESE SAMPLES AND PERFORMING RNA QC, 3) CONSTRUCTING RNA-SEQ LIBRARIES AND PERFORMING LIBRARY QC USING THE ISOLATED RNA, AND 4) GENERATING RNA SEQUENCE DATA FROM THE RESULTING MRNA-SEQ LIBRARIES. 2. THE GALE LABORATORY WILL CONDUCT COMPUTATIONAL DATA ANALYSIS AND MODELING ON RNA-SEQ DATA SETS. OUR YEAR 6 BASE BUDGET COVERS DATA ANALYSIS ON THE MAJORITY OF THE SAMPLES FROM NHP EXPERIMENTS BUT NOT ALL OF THEM. UNDER OUR OPTION 6 BUDGET, WE WILL PERFORM DATA ANALYSIS ON DATA GENERATED FROM THE REMAINING SAMPLES. THIS ANALYSIS WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO INITIAL DATA QC, GENERATION OF NORMALIZED EXPRESSION MATRIXES, DIFFERENTIAL GENE EXPRESSION ANALYSIS, FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS, CO-EXPRESSION ANALYSIS AND WHEN APPROPRIATE RULE-BASED MODELING.

description: THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW GERNER) WILL BE PERFORMING. NOTE THAT THE TASK NUMBERS BELOW REFLECT THE NUMBERING OF THE OVERALL ACTIVITIES IN THE PRIME CONTRACT. ALTHOUGH THIS SOW DETAILS THE COMPLETE SUITE OF PROPOSED WORK, THE TASKS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CONTRACT ITERATION ARE LIMITED TO THE SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES OUTLINED BELOW, DELIVERABLES FOR THIS CONTRACT PERIOD ARE HIGHLIGHTED. YEAR 6 (BASE) Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ HAWN THE HAWN LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW) WILL HAVE SEVERAL ROLES IN THIS SUBCONTRACT IN YEAR 6. EACH ACTIVITY FROM YEARS 1-5 IS ONGOING. 1. UW WILL OVERSEE GENOTYPING AND ANALYSIS OF CANDIDATE GENE POLYMORPHISMS IN HEALTHY CONTROLS IN SEATTLE. GENOTYPING IS COMPLETED EXCEPT FOR NEW ENROLLEES. ANALYSIS IS ONGOING WITH NEW CANDIDATE GENES THAT HAVE RECENTLY BEEN SELECTED FOR WORK IN YEAR 6. POLYMORPHISMS WILL BE ANALYZED FOR THEIR ASSOCIATION WITH MTB-INFECTED MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES. CANDIDATE GENES WILL BE SELECTED BASED ON STUDIES FROM DRS. URDAHL, PICKER, LEWINSOHN, AND WALZL. 2. UW WILL ORGANIZE AND FACILITATE THE ISOLATION OF PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONOCYTES AND MONOCYTE-DERIVED MACROPHAGES FOR EX VIVO MTB INFECTION FROM HEALTHY CONTROLS IN SEATTLE. MONOCYTES WILL BE ISOLATED FROM CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS, WHICH ARE AVAILABLE FROM AN ESTABLISHED SEATTLE COHORT OF HEALTHY SUBJECTS. ANALYSES ARE UNDERWAY TO EXAMINE THE ASSOCIATION OF GENETIC VARIANTS IN CANDIDATE GENES WITH MTB-INDUCED MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES IN A COHORT OF 100 HEALTHY DONORS. . 3. UW WILL OVERSEE THE MACROPHAGE EXPERIMENTS INCLUDING CRISPR/CAS9 GENE SILENCING IN THP1 AND U937 CELLS AND STUDIES OF PRIMARY MONOCYTES FROM SEATTLE AND CAPE TOWN. STUDIES WILL INCLUDE INFECTION OF MACROPHAGES WITH MTB AND ANALYSIS OF IMMUNE PATHWAYS AND CONTROL OF MTB REPLICATION. CELL SUPERNATANTS WILL BE HARVESTED FOR CYTOKINE/CHEMOKINE ELISA AND RNA EXTRACTED FROM CELLS, QUANTIFIED, AND ANALYZED. 4. UW WILL COLLABORATE WITH INVESTIGATORS ON THE ANALYSIS OF WHETHER POLYMORPHISMS IN CANDIDATE GENES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPES AND PREPARE IT FOR PUBLICATION WITH OTHER INVESTIGATORS.

description: THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON (UW GERNER) WILL BE PERFORMING. NOTE THAT THE TASK NUMBERS BELOW REFLECT THE NUMBERING OF THE OVERALL ACTIVITIES IN THE PRIME CONTRACT. ALTHOUGH THIS SOW DETAILS THE COMPLETE SUITE OF PROPOSED WORK, THE TASKS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CONTRACT ITERATION ARE LIMITED TO THE SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES OUTLINED BELOW, DELIVERABLES FOR THIS CONTRACT PERIOD ARE HIGHLIGHTED. EXPANSION OF MICROSCOPY CAPABILITIES IN IMPACTB CASCADE WORK WITH IBEX IMAGING OF HUMAN SAMPLES AN EXTENSION OF WORK UNDER THE 75N93019C00070 CASCADE IMPAC-TB CONTRACT. ONGOING IMPACTB CASCADE STUDIES USING 10-13-PLEX IMAGING HAVE PROVIDED MANY KEY INSIGHTS INTO CELL TYPE COMPOSITION AND LESION ORGANIZATION DURING MTB INFECTION ACROSS ANIMAL MODELS, AND MOST RECENTLY IN HUMAN LESIONS OF PATIENTS WITH END-STAGE DISEASE. THE SUPPLEMENT WILL PROVIDE SUPPORT FOR THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES: AIM 1: THE ULTRA-HIGH PLEX (IBEX) IMAGING APPROACH DEVELOPED BY DR. RONALD GERMAINÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S LAB AT THE NIH WILL BE USED TO BETTER CHARACTERIZE HUMAN LUNG LESIONS DURING MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS INFECTION. THIS WILL LEAD TO IMPROVED DEFINITION OF CELLULAR COMPOSITION AND HETEROGENEITY. ADOPTION OF THIS TECHNOLOGY WILL INITIALLY BE IMPLEMENTED ON AND APPLIED TO ALREADY AVAILABLE SAMPLES PROVIDED THROUGH THE ONGOING POST-MORTEM IMPACTB STUDIES IN UGANDA WITH STEVE COSE. AIM 2: OBTAIN AND INCLUDE IN OUR WORKFLOW ADDITIONAL SAMPLES FROM A BROADER SPECTRUM OF LESION TYPES AND DISEASE STAGES. TO THIS END WE WILL ESTABLISH A COLLABORATION WITH DR. ADRIE STEYNÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S GROUP AT THE AFRICA HEALTH RESEARCH INSTITUTE (AHRI), LEVERAGING THEIR EXTENSIVE HUMAN LUNG TISSUE REPOSITORY AT THE ALBERT LUTHULI CENTRAL HOSPITAL AS PART OF THE HUMAN LUNG PROJECT. THROUGH THIS COLLABORATION, WE WILL OBTAIN HUMAN LUNG GRANULOMA SAMPLES AND LINKED DRAINING AND NON-DRAINING LNS FROM INDIVIDUALS WITH VARIOUS STAGES OF TB DISEASE. THESE SAMPLES WILL THEN BE ANALYZED USING THE IBEX IMAGING PIPELINE IN THE GERNER LAB. USING IBEX ULTRA-HIGH PLEX IMAGING ON THESE UNIQUE AND PRECIOUS SAMPLES, WE WILL NOT ONLY BETTER DEFINE THE HETEROGENEITY OF HUMAN DISEASE AT A HIGH LEVEL OF CELLULAR AND SPATIAL RESOLUTION, BUT ALSO LINK HOW LUNG DISEASE AFFECTS PROCESSES TAKING PLACE IN ASSOCIATED LUNG DRAINING LYMPH NODES.

description: SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE TASKED TO PROVIDE RAPID DEPLOYMENT OF TECHNICAL, OPERATIONAL, AND CLINICAL RESEARCH RESOURCES AND EXPERTISE FOR THIS TIME-SENSITIVE INITIATIVE. THE PROTOCOL IS TITLED, ASSESSMENT OF IMMUNE RESPONSE TO EBOLA VIRUS DISEASE AS MODULATED BY VACCINES AND MEDICAL COUNTERMEASURES, AND IS ALSO KNOWN AS PALM 005. THE SCOPE OF WORK INCLUDES BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO: STRATEGIC AND OPERATIONAL PLANNING AND HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT; INFRASTRUCTURE OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCE; LOGISTICS AND PROCUREMENT MANAGEMENT; SITE DEVELOPMENT TO ENSURE ALL CLINICAL SITES REMAIN IN A STATE OF PREPAREDNESS AND COMPLIANCE WITH PROTOCOL REQUIREMENTS; INITIATING AND COMPLETING ENROLLMENT AND FOLLOW-UP FOR THE CLINICAL RESEARCH PROTOCOL; OVERALL MANAGEMENT AND OVERSIGHT OF THE CONDUCT OF THE MOBILIZATION, PSYCHOSOCIAL SUPPORT AND COMMUNICATIONS EFFORTS; AND OTHER ACTIVITIES SUCH AS LABORATORY SERVICES AND PHARMACY SUPPORT. THE SPECIFIC SUPPORT TO EBOLA OUTBREAK #14 IN THE EQUATOR PROVINCE IS TO COVER GAPS IN THE SAFE ADMINISTRATION OF INVESTIGATIONAL PRODUCT UNTIL SUPPORT OF OTHER EBOLA RESPONSE PARTNERS HAS BEEN ESTABLISHED IN THIS REGION. THE CURRENT PORTFOLIO OF PALM RESEARCH STUDIES TO SUPPORT IN THIS SOW INCLUDES: PALM 010 MPOX VACCINE RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL INITIATION PHASE PALM 007 EXTENSION: A SINGLE-ARM, OPEN-LABEL EXTENSION TO THE PALM007 RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL FOR FURTHER CLINICAL CHARACTERIZATION OF THE NATURAL HISTORY OF MPOX.

description: THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO COMPLETE PHASE 1 CLINICAL TRIALS WITH A NEW VACCINE FORMULATION THAT PREVENTS INVASIVE DISEASE CAUSED BY ESCHERICHIA COLI. DIFFERENT PATHOGENIC BACTERIA, INCLUDING E. COLI, POSSESS AN EXTRACELLULAR FORM OF GLYCERALDEHYDE-3-PHOSPHATE DEHYDROGENASE (GAPDH) THAT HAS A POTENT IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE ACTIVITY IN THE MAMMALIAN HOSTS. HOST IMMUNOSUPPRESSION IS MEDIATED BY THE ABILITY OF GAPDH TO BIND TO TLR2 AND TO TRIGGER A FAST PRODUCTION OF INTERLEUKIN-10. EXCRETION OF BACTERIAL GAPDH THROUGHOUT THE BLOOD STREAM OF THE HOST OCCURS IMMEDIATELY AFTER INFECTION AND INHIBITS EARLY EVENTS OF THE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE, ALLOWING THE BACTERIA TO SPREAD SYSTEMICALLY WITHIN FEW HOURS. NEUTRALIZATION OF BACTERIAL GAPDH IS ESSENTIAL TO PROMOTE A PROTECTIVE RESPONSE AGAINST E. COLI INFECTIONS. ACKNOWLEDGING THE IMPORTANCE OF EXTRACELLULAR GAPDH IN THE PATHOGENICITY OF E.COLI CAN EXPLAIN WHY OTHER ATTEMPTS TO DEVELOP VACCINES THAT TARGET ONLY STRUCTURAL EPITOPES HAVE FAILED. AS IT IS WIDELY KNOWN, GAPDH IS AN UBIQUITOUS ENZYME THAT, IN ITS INTRACELLULAR FORM IS ESSENTIAL FOR GLYCOLYSIS. HOWEVER, E. COLI POSSESS TWO DIFFERENT GENES THAT CODE FOR TWO DIFFERENT GAPDH: I) THE INTRACELLULAR GLYCOLYTIC ENZYME CODED BY GAPA GENE AND II) THE EXTRACELLULAR VIRULENCE FACTOR CODED BY GAPC GENE. THE ABROGATION OF GAPC GENE DOES NOT INFLUENCE THE METABOLIC RATE OF THE BACTERIA BUT REDUCES DRAMATICALLY THE ABILITY OF BACTERIA TO CAUSE DISEASE. HUMANS DO NOT POSSESS GAPC-ENCODED GAPDH, BUT THERE IS STILL A SIGNIFICANT DEGREE OF IDENTITY BETWEEN GAPC- AND GAPA-ENCODED GAPDH (APPROX. 50%). TO OVERCOME ANY REACTIVITY TO HUMAN GAPDH, WE IDENTIFIED REGIONS (PEPTIDES) EXPOSED TO SOLVENT ON BACTERIAL GAPDH THAT ARE COMPLETELY ABSENT FROM HUMAN GAPDH. WITHIN THIS PROJECT WE INTEND TO DEVELOP AN IMMUNOGENIC FORMULATION THAT TARGETS THE IDENTIFIED REGIONS. DIFFERENT FORMULATIONS WILL BE TESTED FOR THEIR IMMUNOGENICITY AND ABILITY TO PREVENT INVASIVE DISEASE CAUSED BY E. COLI IN IN VIVO CHALLENGING ASSAYS IN THE MOUSE MODEL. THE BEST COMBINATION OF POLYPEPTIDE + CARRIER PROTEIN WILL PROCEED TO PRECLINICAL STUDIES AND PHASE 1 STUDIES.

description: PEARL DIAGNOSTICS INC. (PEARLDX) DEVELOPS NOVEL IN VITRO DIAGNOSTIC (IVD) TESTS THAT AID NON-INVASIVE DIAGNOSIS OF LIFE-THREATENING LUNG INFECTIONS. PEARLDXÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S TECHNOLOGY LEVERAGES THE DISCOVERY THAT MICROBIAL EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES (EVS) RELEASED FROM ORGANISMS GROWING IN THE LUNGS ARE EXCRETED IN URINE. IDENTIFICATION OF SPECIFIC LUNG PATHOGENS SUCH AS PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA (PSA) AS A CAUSE OF PNEUMONIA IS CRITICAL IN MITIGATING THE IMPACT OF ANTIMICROBIAL DRUG RESISTANCE. WHILE A LESS COMMON CAUSE OF COMMUNITY-ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA (CAP), THIS GRAM-NEGATIVE ROD (GNR) IS INTRINSICALLY RESISTANT TO SEVERAL ANTIBIOTIC CLASSES, INCLUDING B-LACTAMS, AND EXHIBITS FREQUENT MULTIDRUG RESISTANCE (MDR). THE PREVALENCE OF PSA IN CAP IS REPORTED AS VARIABLE, RANGING FROM 0 TO 23%, WITH A POOLED PREVALENCE OF 8.6% IN PEOPLE WITH IDENTIFIED RISKS FOR MDR INFECTIONS. IDENTIFICATION OF PSA IN CULTURES ENABLES SUSCEPTIBILITY TESTING AND TAILORING OF EMPIRIC THERAPY FOR BOTH CAP AND HOSPITAL- AND VENTILATOR-ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA (HAP, VAP) IN HIGH-RISK PATIENTS. HOWEVER, THIS FREQUENTLY REQUIRES BAL SAMPLING AND CULTURE YIELD IS VARIABLE. IDENTIFICATION OF THE ORGANISM IS NOT AN ASSURANCE OF ACUTE DISEASE ETIOLOGY, AS COLONIZATION IS COMMON IN PEOPLE WITH POOR AIRWAY CLEARANCE, SUCH AS IN THOSE WITH BRONCHIECTASIS AND CYSTIC FIBROSIS (CF). VARIABLE PERFORMANCE, NON-SPECIFICITY OF CLINICAL FINDINGS, RELIANCE ON INVASIVE SAMPLING, AND TIME TO CULTURE DRIVE A HIGH AMOUNT OF ANTIBIOTIC EMPIRICISM, ULTIMATELY GENERATING AND PROPAGATING ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE (AMR). PEARLDXÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S PRODUCTS PROVIDE ADVANTAGES WITH REGARD TO ACCESS (REFERENCE LABS VS. LOW-RESOURCE SETTINGS), COSTS (> $2000/TEST VS. < $20), AND TIME TO RESULT (3-5 DAYS VS. < 2 HR.). OTHER TECHNOLOGIES TYPICALLY RELY ON LARGE INSTRUMENTS AND/OR REFERENCE TESTING. THEREFORE, THERE REMAIN CRITICAL UNMET NEEDS AND OPPORTUNITIES TO IMPROVE PATIENT OUTCOMES WITH EASIER-TO-DEPLOY, LESS EXPENSIVE IVDS USING URINE AS AN ADJUNCT DIAGNOSTIC AID FOR PNEUMONIA. THE AVAILABILITY OF ADJUNCTIVE NON-CULTURE-BASED TESTS (NCBT) TO AID IN THE DIAGNOSIS OF PNEUMONIA IS A LONG-APPRECIATED PRIORITY. PEARLDX, WITH SUPPORT FROM CARB-X, INTENDS TO DEVELOP A LOW-COST, LOW TURNAROUND TIME (TAT) URINE ASSAY FOR THE DETECTION OF PSEUDOMONAS PNEUMONIA (PMA). THE INITIAL AIM OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP A PROTOTYPE ASSAY. ALL ASSAYS DEVELOPED BY PEARLDX, INCLUDING THE PROPOSED CARB-X-SUPPORTED PSA ASSAY, ARE ADVANCED USING CLINICAL SAMPLES FROM PATIENTS, WITH ITERATIVE IMPROVEMENTS OF THE ASSAY INFORMED BY THE CHARACTERIZATION OF URINARY ANTIGENS AND BY REDUCING MATRIX INTERFERENCE.

description: MELIO IS COMMITTED TO REVOLUTIONIZING THE HEALTHCARE INDUSTRY BY OFFERING RAPID INFECTIOUS DISEASE DIAGNOSTIC SOLUTIONS. BY REDEFINING STANDARDS OF CARE, MELIO AIMS TO DRIVE A SHIFT TOWARD PRECISION HEALTHCARE, EMPOWERING CLINICIANS TO MAKE INFORMED, TIMELY DECISIONS FOR TREATMENT FOR INFECTIONS, REDUCING HEALTHCARE COSTS, AND THE OVERPRESCRIPTION OF ANTIBIOTICS. MELIO’S FIRST PRODUCT FOCUSES ON PROVIDING A BREAKTHROUGH IN BOTH SPEED AND PATHOGEN COVERAGE FOR DIAGNOSING BLOOD STREAM INFECTIONS DIRECTLY FROM A PATIENT’S BLOOD SAMPLE FOR NEONATES. UNLIKE THE STANDARD CULTURE METHOD, WHICH SERVES AS A BOTTLENECK BY TAKING DAYS TO DELIVER RESULTS, MELIO’S TECHNOLOGY OFFERS AN EXPEDITED ALTERNATIVE THAT COULD TRANSFORM PATIENT CARE.

description: PNEUMONIA IS A COMMON CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS THAT OFTEN LACKS A MICROBIOLOGICAL DIAGNOSIS BECAUSE NO PATHOGEN IS IDENTIFIED. WITHOUT A MICROBIOLOGICAL DIAGNOSIS, ANTIBIOTICS TARGETING A BROAD RANGE OF PATHOGENS ARE USED, INCREASING THE RISKS FOR RESISTANCE ALONG WITH POOR OUTCOMES IF INAPPROPRIATE ANTIBIOTICS ARE CHOSEN. THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM PROPOSES TO DIAGNOSE LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACT BACTERIAL INFECTIONS AND THEIR ASSOCIATED ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE IN FOUR HOURS, MUCH FASTER THAN CURRENT CULTURE TECHNIQUES. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM IS TO DEVELOP RAPID DIAGNOSTIC TESTS THAT WILL BE INDICATED IN ALL PATIENTS WITH A CLINICAL SUSPICION FOR PNEUMONIA. THE SHORT-TERM OBJECTIVE WILL FOCUS ON PNEUMONIAS CAUSED BY STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS, PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA, AND HAEMOPHILUS INFLUENZAE, WITH THE GOAL OF HAVING RESULTS AVAILABLE IN 4 HOURS. THE STRATEGY USED IN THIS DIAGNOSTIC TEST DISTINGUISHES IT FROM COMPETITORS AND ALTERNATIVES. THIS DIAGNOSTIC IS BASED ON DETECTING RNA SEQUENCE(S) SPECIFIC FOR THE PATHOGEN CAUSING PNEUMONIA IN A HUMAN PATIENT. TESTING WILL BE DONE ON BLOOD DRAWN DIRECTLY FROM THE PATIENT, MAKING IT LESS INVASIVE THAN OTHER METHODS THAT OBTAIN SAMPLES FROM THE AIRWAYS, SUCH AS BRONCHOSCOPY OR DEEP SUCTIONING. THIS TEST WILL NOT REQUIRE THE SPECIMEN TO BE CULTURED, ALLOWING FOR FASTER RESULTS THAN TRADITIONAL MICROBIOLOGICAL METHODS. THE RNA TARGETED BY THE TEST IS IDENTIFIED VIA RNA SEQUENCING OF BLOOD FROM PATIENTS WITH THE INFECTION. RNA SEQUENCING DATA SHOWS RNA SPECIFIC TO THE PATHOGEN OF INTEREST (S. AUREUS., P. AERUGINOSA, AND H. INFLUENZAE) THAT IS ALSO SPECIFIC FOR AN ACTIVE INFECTION. TARGETING RNA ALSO ENSURES THAT THE INFECTION IS CURRENT SINCE RNA IS LESS STABLE THAN DNA, LASTING MINUTES TO HOURS WHEN FROM A BACTERIUM. THE METHOD, HOWEVER, IMMEDIATELY STABILIZES THE RNA FOR TESTING. RNA ALSO IDENTIFIES BACTERIA THAT ARE ACTIVELY MAKING RESISTANCE PROTEINS, RATHER THAN BACTERIA WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR RESISTANCE BASED ONLY ON GENOMIC DNA. AT THE END OF THIS PROJECT, PCR BASED TESTS WILL BE CREATED THAT ARE INFORMED BY RNA SEQUENCING DATA. THESE WILL DIAGNOSE PNEUMONIA DUE TO S. AUREUS., P. AERUGINOSA, AND H. INFLUENZAE, ALONG WITH RELEVANT ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE, USING BLOOD FROM THE PATIENT. THIS PCR TESTING PLATFORM USES FDA-APPROVED INSTRUMENTATION TO FACILITATE TRANSITIONING FROM A RESEARCH LABORATORY TO A CLINICAL MICROBIOLOGY LABORATORY.

description: OUR PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP A NEW DRUG EFFECTIVE AGAINST MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT (MDR) GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA. OUR EARLY LEAD COMPOUNDS ARE DERIVED FROM A NATURAL PRODUCT AND REPRESENT A NOVEL CLASS OF COMPOUNDS FEATURING A NOVEL MODE OF ACTION. THE AGENTS ARREST THE FUNCTION OF BAMA, AN ESSENTIAL COMPONENT FOR BACTERIAL SURVIVAL, WHICH NO CURRENT DRUGS TARGET. BAMA, IS AN ESSENTIAL COMPONENT OF THE ÃƑÅ¸-BARREL ASSEMBLY MACHINERY (BAM), LOCATED IN THE OUTER MEMBRANE (OM) OF GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA; THE TARGET IS NOT PRESENT IN HUMANS (SPECIFIC). BAMA FOLDS AND INTEGRATES OM-PROTEINS INTO THE OM; INHIBITION LEADS TO OM BLEBBING AND ULTIMATELY CELL LYSIS (ESSENTIAL). SINCE BAMA HAS NOT BEEN TARGETED BY ANY EXISTING DRUGS, BACTERIA HAVE NOT DEVELOPED TARGET-BASED RESISTANCE. HENCE, OUR PROGRAM CAN BE REGARDED AS THE FOUNDATION FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A FIRST IN CLASS BAMA INHIBITOR. WE WILL FOCUS ON TREATING HOSPITAL-ACQUIRED INFECTIONS SUCH AS PNEUMONIA CAUSED BY MDR BACTERIA. description: URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS (UTIS) ARE AN INCREASING CLINICAL PROBLEM, HAVING INCREASED BY 60% BETWEEN 1990 AND 2019 AND ACCOUNTING FOR 40% OF ALL NOSOCOMIAL INFECTIONS. APPROXIMATELY 65% OF COMPLICATED OR RECURRENT UTIS (RUTIS) ARE DUE TO UROPATHOGENIC E. COLI (UPEC), ALTHOUGH SEVERAL OTHER GRAM-NEGATIVE AND GRAM-POSITIVE PATHOGENS ARE ALSO IMPLICATED. CLARAMETYX BIOSCIENCES, INC. (CLARAMETYX) IS DEVELOPING A VACCINE CANDIDATE, CMTX-301, TO PREVENT RUTIS. CMTX-301 IS A PATHOGEN-AGNOSTIC VACCINE CANDIDATE FOR THE PREVENTION OF BACTERIAL BIOFILMS, A KEY COMPONENT OF MANY RECALCITRANT AND/OR RECURRENT BACTERIAL INFECTIONS, SUCH AS RUTIS. IMMUNIZATION WITH CMTX-301 FOCUSES THE HOST IMMUNE RESPONSE ON SPECIFIC PROTECTIVE EPITOPES WITHIN COMPONENTS OF THE BACTERIAL BIOFILM RESPONSIBLE FOR ITS STRUCTURAL STABILITY, THEREBY PREVENTING BIOFILM FORMATION. GIVEN THAT BIOFILMS ARE A SIGNIFICANT DEFENSE MECHANISM AGAINST DISEASE RESOLUTION, PREVENTING DEVELOPMENT OF THESE PROTECTIVE STRUCTURES SHOULD REDUCE DISEASE OCCURRENCE AND THUS PROVIDE SIGNIFICANT BENEFITS. . UNLIKE OTHER BACTERIAL VACCINES THAT TARGET SPECIFIC BACTERIAL SPECIES, CMTX-301 IMMUNIZATION TO PREVENT BACTERIAL BIOFILM FORMATION WILL ALLOW THE HOST’S NATURAL IMMUNE RESPONSE TO CLEAR INFECTION IN A PATHOGEN-AGNOSTIC MANNER. THE PROGRAM PROPOSED HEREIN WILL ESTABLISH PROOF-OF-CONCEPT PRECLINICAL STUDIES AGAINST RUTI DUE TO E. COLI , DEVELOP A LAB-SCALE MANUFACTURING PROCESS THAT CAN SCALE FOR NEED, AND SEEK FDA GUIDANCE ON THE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM TO ADVANCE CMTX-301 TO CLINICAL EVALUATION.

description: THE I LEAD PROGRAM IS A LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVE DESIGNED TO ENHANCE PARTICIPANTS' SKILLS IN NAVIGATING CHANGE AND COMPETING PRIORITIES. IT FOCUSES ON A VARIETY OF KEY LEADERSHIP TOPICS (E.G., INTEREST-BASED NEGOTIATION, RESULTS-BASED ACCOUNTABILITY, SITUATIONAL LEADERSHIP, EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE, AND OTHERS). THE PROGRAM SPANS UP TO 12 MONTHS AND INCLUDES FIVE GROUP TRAINING SESSIONS, EACH 6 HOURS IN LENGTH. THROUGHOUT THE PROGRAM, PARTICIPANTS SHALL REFINE AND APPLY THEIR LEADERSHIP SKILLS THROUGH NINE ONE-ON-ONE COACHING SESSIONS AND NINE FOUR COLLABORATIVE SKILLS TEAM MEETINGS, WHICH SHALL BE CONDUCTED IN SMALL GROUPS. THE PROGRAM INCLUDES UP TO 25 FEDERAL EMPLOYEES AT GS 14 AND 15 LEVELS, AND T42 (OR EQUIVALENT). DPCPSI OVERSEES THE APPLICATION AND SELECTION PROCESS FOR THE 25 PARTICIPANTS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE TWO COACHES FOR THE I LEAD PROGRAM. YOSI WILL COACH FOUR COACHEES, AND PATTY WILL COACH FIVE COACHEES. SPECIFICALLY, THE CONTRACTOR COACHES SHALL: Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ ATTEND THE TWO-HOUR PROGRAM ORIENTATION SESSION FROM 8-10 ET ON 01/14/25 Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ CONDUCT NINE ONE-HOUR INDIVIDUAL COACHING SESSIONS BEGINNING IN JANUARY 2025 FOR EACH COACHEE (36 TO 45 TOTAL SESSIONS) Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ DEBRIEF 360 SURVEY RESULTS WITH EACH COACHEE DURING ONE OF THE COACHING SESSIONS (FMP WILL ADMINISTER THE 360 AND PROVIDE THE COACH THE REPORT) Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢ LEAD FOUR GROUP "SKILLS TEAM" MEETINGS WHERE THE COACH MEETS WITH THEIR FOUR COACHEES TO HELP THEM APPLY CONCEPTS FROM THE TRAINING PROGRAM (4 TOTAL HOURS).

description: THE ADJUVANT DISCOVERY CONTRACT PROPOSED HEREIN WILL IDENTIFY, CHARACTERIZE, AND ADVANCE NOVEL SYNTHETIC IL-1R-BASED ADJUVANTS FOR USE IN COMBINATION WITH AN INFLUENZA VACCINE TO INDUCE RAPID AND SUSTAINED BROADLY PROTECTIVE IMMUNITY TO SEASONAL AND/OR PANDEMIC INFLUENZA VIRUS. THIS PROPOSAL BRINGS TOGETHER HIGHLY EXPERIENCED RESEARCH TEAMS FROM THE UNIVERSITY OF MONTANA, DUKE UNIVERSITY, THE ICAHN SCHOOL OF MEDICINE AT MOUNT SINAI AND INIMMUNE CORPORATION, EACH WITH UNIQUE EXPERTISE AND PREVIOUS EXPERIENCE IN NIAID ADJUVANT DISCOVERY AND DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS. DR. EVANS, DIRECTOR OF THE CTM, AND COLLEAGUES AT UM WILL LEAD THE DISCOVERY EFFORTS AND COORDINATE ACTIVITIES OF ALL SUBCONTRACTORS. THE RESEARCH TEAM AT UM WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR HIGH THROUGHPUT IN SILICO SCREENING, PEPTIDE LIBRARY PRODUCTION, COMPOUNDS SYNTHESIS AND SAR, MECHANISTIC STUDIES, FORMULATION, SAFETY ASSESSMENTS AND EFFICACY STUDIES. DR. STAATS, PROFESSOR OF PATHOLOGY, ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR OF IMMUNOLOGY AND MEDICINE, DUKE, AND COLLEAGUES WILL WORK CLOSELY WITH THE TEAM FROM UM TO COMPLETE THE HTS SCREENING OF SYNTHETIC PEPTIDE LIBRARIES, APTAMER LIBRARY PRODUCTION AND SCREENING, CONFIRMATION SCREEN OF SELECTED HITS USING IL-1R REPORTER CELLS, EVALUATION OF BINDING AND INTERNALIZATION, CRITICALLY EVALUATE THE INTRACELLULAR SIGNALING PATHWAYS OF LEAD IL- 1R AGONISTS AND ASSESS THE ROUTE OF ADMINISTRATION AND SCHEDULE TO OPTIMIZE BOTH PARENTERAL (IM) AND MUCOSAL (IN, SL) VACCINATION THROUGH ADJUVANT SELECTION AND FORMULATION. DR. KRAMMER, ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR OF MICROBIOLOGY, AND COLLEAGUES AT THE ICAHN SCHOOL OF MEDICINE AT MOUNT SINAI BRING EXPERTISE AND CONSIDERABLE KNOWLEDGE IN INFLUENZA VIRUS ANIMAL MODELS AND THE PRODUCTION OF RECOMBINANT INFLUENZA ANTIGENS. DR. KRAMMER WILL PROVIDE RECOMBINANT INFLUENZA ANTIGENS AND LEAD EFFORTS TOWARDS THE IN VIVO INFLUENZA CHALLENGE MODELS (MOUSE AND FERRET) FOR EVALUATION OF IL-1 ADJUVANTED INFLUENZA VACCINES. THE TEAM AT MOUNT SINAI ALSO BRINGS SPECIALIZED EXPERTISE IN THE SEROLOGICAL MECHANISM OF PROTECTION AND A WIDE ARRAY OF ANTIGENS AND VIRUSES TO ASSESS HETEROSUBTYPIC PROTECTION AGAINST SELECTED SEASONAL AND HIGHLY PATHOGENIC INFLUENZA VIRUS STRAINS. DR. BAZIN-LEE, VICE PRESIDENT OF DISCOVERY RESEARCH, ALONG WITH HER COLLEAGUES AT INIMMUNE CORPORATION, WILL OVERSEE ANALYTICAL ASSAY DEVELOPMENT, PHYSIOCHEMICAL CHARACTERIZATION, STABILITY AND SCALE-UP SYNTHESIS OF LEAD IL-1R ADJUVANTS IDENTIFIED IN RESEARCH AREAS 1-3.

description: [THE MATIC-2 TRIAL IS A BAYESIAN, RANDOMIZED, MULTICENTER, ADAPTIVE PLATFORM PHASE III TRIAL. THE TRIAL WILL INCLUDE INJURED CHILDREN WITH HEMORRHAGIC SHOCK ANTICIPATED TO REQUIRE MASSIVE BLOOD TRANSFUSION, WHO WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO RECEIVE EITHER LTOWB OR CT AND TRANEXAMIC ACID OR PLACEBO. IT'S HYPOTHESIZED THAT THE USE OF LTOWB IS NON-INFERIOR AND/OR SUPERIOR FOR 24-HOUR MORTALITY AND THAT LTOWB DOES NOT INCREASE THE RISK OF ADVERSE EVENTS OR OUTCOMES, SUCH AS THROMBOTIC EVENTS, COMPARED TO CT. IT'S ALSO HYPOTHESIZED THAT THE USE OF TXA IS SUPERIOR FOR 24-HOUR MORTALITY AND DOES NOT INCREASE THE RISK OF ADVERSE EVENTS OR OUTCOMES, SUCH AS THROMBOTIC EVENTS, COMPARED TO PLACEBO. THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVES ARE TO 1. DETERMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF LTOWB TO REDUCE ALL-CAUSE 24-HOUR MORTALITY COMPARED TO CT IN CHILDREN WITH TRAUMATIC LIFE-THREATENING HEMORRHAGE. 2. DETERMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF TXA TO REDUCE ALL-CAUSE 24-HOUR MORTALITY COMPARED TO PLACEBO IN CHILDREN WITH TRAUMATIC LIFE-THREATENING HEMORRHAGE. SECONDARY OBJECTIVES ARE TO DETERMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS AND SAFETY OF LTOWB AND TXA TO IMPROVE SECONDARY AND EXPLORATORY OUTCOMES (OR ENDPOINTS) IN CHILDREN WITH TRAUMATIC LIFE-THREATENING HEMORRHAGE. SAFETY OBJECTIVES ARE TO DETERMINE THE EFFECT OF LTOWB AND TXA ON SAFETY RELATED OUTCOMES/ENDPOINTS. MECHANISTIC OBJECTIVES ARE TO: 1. DEFINE TRAUMA INDUCED COAGULOPATHY (TIC) ACCORDING TO MEASURES OF SHOCK, HEMOSTASIS, AND ENDOTHELIAL AND IMMUNE FUNCTION. 2. TO DETERMINE IF MEASURES OF SHOCK, ENDOTHELIAL, IMMUNE, AND HEMOSTASIS FUNCTION UPON ADMISSION (TIC ENDOTYPE) PREDICTS WHICH HEMOSTATIC RESUSCITATION THERAPIES OR COMBINATIONS OF THERAPIES (LTOWB, CT, LTOWB + TXA, CT+TXA) FOR EACH STUDY GROUP IMPROVES OUTCOMES WITHOUT INCREASING THE RISK OF ADVERSE EVENTS. 3. TO DETERMINE THE MECHANISMS OF HOW HEMOSTATIC RESUSCITATION THERAPIES OR COMBINATIONS OF THERAPIES (LTOWB, CT, LTOWB + TXA, CT+TXA) IMPROVE TIC ENDOTYPES AND OUTCOMES. PHARMACOKINETIC OBJECTIVES ARE TO EVALUATE THE PK AND PD PROPERTIES OF TXA IN A POPULATION OF CHILDREN WITH LIFETHREATENING TRAUMATIC BLEEDING. ]

description: THE MISSION OF THE NIH OFFICE OF DATA SCIENCE STRATEGY IS TO ENHANCE BIOMEDICAL DATA SCIENCE BY LEADING AND COORDINATING EFFORTS ACROSS NIH TO MODERNIZE DATA RESOURCES, DEVELOP A SKILLED DATA SCIENCE WORKFORCE, AND BUILD STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS FOR ADVANCING TECHNOLOGIES AND METHODS. NIH EMPHASIZES THE MANAGEMENT AND SHARING OF RESEARCH DATA ACCORDING TO THE FAIR PRINCIPLES, ENSURING DATA IS FINDABLE, ACCESSIBLE, INTEROPERABLE, AND REUSABLE. ACHIEVING THESE PRINCIPLES RELIES ON WELL-DOCUMENTED SEMANTIC RESOURCES LIKE STANDARDS AND ONTOLOGIES. WHILE TOP-DOWN APPROACHES TO CREATING THESE RESOURCES MAY FAIL, COMMUNITY-DRIVEN, CO-DEVELOPED RESOURCES ARE MORE LIKELY TO BE WIDELY ADOPTED. THIS APPROACH BENEFITS KEY NIH STAKEHOLDERS, INCLUDING NIH-FUNDED BIOMEDICAL RESEARCHERS, DATA AND COMPUTER SCIENTISTS, AND EARLY CAREER RESEARCHERS AND STUDENTS, PARTICULARLY THOSE FROM UNDERREPRESENTED GROUPS AND MINORITY-SERVING INSTITUTIONS.

description: OVERALL RESPONSIBILITIES: • PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE ACTIVITIES FOR 5 HRSA RURAL HEALTH GRANTEES IN THE DIRECT SERVICES PROGRAM, 2 QUALITY GRANTEES AND 3 OUTREACH GRANTEES. ALL WORK WILL BE PROVIDED BY CATHERINE LIEMOHN, PRINCIPAL. RURAL HEALTH NETWORK DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM TASK 3: EXECUTE TA PROVIDE TA TO 5 DIRECT SERVICES GRANTEES. TARGETED TA INCLUDES THE FOLLOWING: O SCHEDULE REGULAR MEETINGS WITH GRANTEES: SET UP THE MEETING, INVITE GRANTEE AND FORHP PROJECT OFFICER TO PARTICIPATE. CONDUCT HOUR-LONG, MONTHLY CALLS WITH RHND GRANTEES. BEFORE BEGINNING CALLS WITH EACH GRANTEE, TA PROVIDERS WILL REVIEW ALL DOCUMENTATION RELATED TO EACH GRANTEE. TA PROVIDERS WILL SUBMIT CALL AGENDAS FIVE DAYS IN ADVANCE OF EACH CALL TO BOTH THE GRANTEE AND PO AND WILL INCLUDE WORK PLAN PROGRESS, CURRENT ISSUES AND CHALLENGES, TA SUPPORT NEEDS, REVIEW OF DELIVERABLES, AND ANY RELEVANT FORHP OR TA ANNOUNCEMENTS. O TAKE NOTES OF THE CALL ON TEMPLATE PROVIDED AND SUBMIT THEM ELECTRONICALLY TO THE PO AND GRANTEE WITHIN FIVE DAYS. O UPLOAD FINAL MEETING SUMMARIES TO ONE DRIVE, NO LATER THAN FIVE (5) BUSINESS DAYS AFTER EACH CALL. GHPC WILL COMPILE ALL SUMMARIES FOR SUBMISSION TO THE COR. O LOG MONTHLY MEETINGS CONDUCTED INTO HTTPS://GHPC-CHSD.ORG/LOGIN/. TASK 3: TAAPS: COMPLETE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE ACTION PLANS FOR THREE OUTREACH GRANTEES IN THE 2025 COHORT AFTER USING THE FIRST MONTHLY CALL AS AN INTAKE CALL. O INFORMED BY INTRODUCTORY CALLS WITH GRANTEES, THE TA TEAM WILL DOCUMENT GRANTEE NEEDS AND SUPPORTS USING A TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE ACTION PLAN (TAAP). BUILDING ON AN ESTABLISHED TEMPLATE AND PROCEDURES DEVELOPED FOR OTHER FORHP GRANTEES, THE TAAP WILL INCLUDE BACKGROUND INFORMATION ON THE GRANTEE PROGRAM AND NETWORK, PERCEIVED STRENGTHS AND POTENTIAL BARRIERS, GRANTEE NEEDS, TA STRATEGIES, EXPECTED OUTCOMES, AND TIMELINE. IN ADDITION, ESTABLISH THE ROUTINE MONTHLY CALL TIME AND DOCUMENT IT IN THE TAAP. O TA PROVIDERS WILL ELECTRONICALLY SUBMIT DRAFT TAAPS AND CALL SUMMARIES PREVIOUSLY DRAFTED TO GHPC, GRANTEES AND POS WITHIN THREE WEEKS OF EACH CALL. THE ASSOCIATED PO AND GRANTEE WILL REVIEW THE TAAP AND SUBMIT REVISIONS TO THE TA PROVIDER. WITHIN FIVE DAYS OF RECEIVING REVISIONS, THE TA PROVIDER WILL ELECTRONICALLY SUBMIT THE REVISED TA PLAN TO THE PO AND GRANTEE AS A FINAL TAAP. O UPLOAD CALL SUMMARIES AND FINAL TAAPS TO ONE DRIVE. GHPC WILL COMPILE ALL SUMMARIES FOR SUBMISSION TO THE COR. O LOG FINAL TAAPS INTO CHSDTEAM.COM. description: PEPTILOGICS IS A BIOTECHNOLOGY COMPANY THAT UTILIZES AN INNOVATIVE PLATFORM TO DEVELOP NOVEL PEPTIDE THERAPEUTICS TO ADDRESS UNMET MEDICAL NEEDS. OUR PIPELINE INCLUDES A NOVEL CLASS OF ENGINEERED CATIONIC ANTIBIOTIC PEPTIDES. OUR LEAD CANDIDATE, PLG0206, BASED ON NATURALLY OCCURRING ANTIMICROBIAL PEPTIDES, EXHIBITS BROAD-SPECTRUM ACTIVITY AGAINST CLINICALLY IMPORTANT MDR GRAM-POSITIVE (S. AUREUS, INCLUDING MRSA, AND E. FAECIUM, INCLUDING VRE) AND GRAM-NEGATIVE (P. AERUGINOSA, E. COLI, AND A. BAUMANNII) PATHOGENS. PLG0206 EXHIBITS THE ABILITY TO RAPIDLY INACTIVATE BOTH PLANKTONIC AND BIOFILM PATHOGENS. THIS WITH ITS BROAD-SPECTRUM ACTIVITY MAKE IT AN IDEAL DEVELOPMENT CANDIDATE FOR PREVENTING INVASIVE INFECTIONS. PLG0206 TARGETS AND DISRUPTS THE BACTERIAL MEMBRANE, CAUSING RAPID BACTERIAL DEATH VIA CELLULAR CHEMICAL IMBALANCE. SINCE BACTERIAL MEMBRANES ARE A CONSERVED EVOLUTIONARY TARGET, THIS MOA APPEARS TO LIMIT THE RISK FOR RESISTANCE COMPARED TO OTHER ANTIBIOTICS. WITH RAPID BACTERICIDAL AND ANTI-BIOFILM ACTIVITY ON CONTACT, PLG0206 IS BEING DEVELOPED FOR THE PREVENTION OF TRAUMATIC FRACTURE-RELATED INFECTIONS (FRI) VIA LOCAL ADMINISTRATION IN CONJUNCTION STANDARD SURGICAL CARE. FRI IS A SERIOUS, LIFE-THREATENING INFECTION WITH SIGNIFICANT ECONOMIC BURDEN. FRI TREATMENT REQUIRES HOSPITALIZATION AND ONE OR MORE REPEAT SURGICAL PROCEDURES. MICROORGANISMS THAT CAUSE FRI INCLUDE S. AUREUS, COAGULATE-NEGATIVE STAPHYLOCOCCUS SPP., ENTEROCOCCUS SPP., AND AEROBIC GRAM-NEGATIVE BACILLI. THE POTENTIAL INFECTING PATHOGEN IS UNKNOWN AT THE TIME OF TRAUMATIC INSULT AND INITIAL SURGERY. CLINICAL PRACTICE GUIDELINES RECOMMEND 2-5 DAYS OF SYSTEMIC ANTIBIOTICS FOLLOWING TRAUMATIC INJURY TO PREVENT FRI. DESPITE THIS, TRAUMATIC FRACTURES HAVE A HIGH INFECTION RATE (UP TO 40%). FRI OFTEN REQUIRES MULTIPLE SURGICAL PROCEDURES, LEADING TO SUBSTANTIAL MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY WITH AN UP TO 25% 5-YEAR MORTALITY RISK. CURRENT STRATEGIES DO NOT ADEQUATELY PREVENT THE INFECTIONS THAT LEAD TO FRI'S HIGH MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY BURDEN, AND FRI REMAINS AN UNMET MEDICAL NEED AND REQUIRES A DIFFERENT APPROACH TO THAT CURRENTLY EMPLOYED. PLG0206, ADMINISTERED AT THE TIME OF INJURY, THROUGH ITS RAPIDLY ACTING BROAD-SPECTRUM ACTIVITY AGAINST THE PATHOGENS COMMONLY CAUSING FRI HAS THE POTENTIAL TO ADDRESS THIS UNMET NEED. PLG0206 WILL BE ADMINISTERED FOLLOWING TRAUMATIC INJURY IN THE OPERATING THEATER AFTER SURGICAL DEBRIDEMENT AND BONE FIXATION AS A LONG-ACTING CONTROLLED RELEASE FORMULATION. IT IS EXPECTED TO BE MORE EFFECTIVE THAN THE CURRENT STANDARD OF CARE BY PROVIDING LONG-LASTING PATHOGEN-INACTIVATING DRUG LEVELS TO PREVENT INFECTION NIDI (DEVITALIZED AND CONTAMINATED BONE AND SOFT TISSUE AND METAL FIXATION DEVICES) THAT LEAD TO INVASIVE INFECTION. THE EXPECTED LIMITED SYSTEMIC EXPOSURE WITH LOCAL DRUG DEPOT SHOULD ENSURE A GOOD SAFETY PROFILE. THE DEVELOPMENT PLAN WILL ASSESS THE IN VITRO AND IN VIVO RELEASE CHARACTERISTICS OF VARIOUS PLG0206 CONTROLLED-RELEASE FORMULATIONS ALONG WITH PK, TOLERABILITY, AND EFFICACY IN ANIMAL MODELS OF FRI. ADDITIONAL STUDIES WILL IDENTIFY THE MOST EFFECTIVE, WELL-TOLERATED CONCENTRATION TO BE USED IN HUMAN TRIALS TO ESTABLISH SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF LOCAL ADMINISTRATION IN THE PREVENTION OF FRI IN CONJUNCTION WITH CURRENT STANDARD OF CARE.

description: THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON NMR GROUP (UW-NMR), UNDER THE DIRECTION OF GABRIELE VARANI, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT. UW-NMR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SOLVING 1 NMR STRUCTURE DURING THIS ONE YEAR SUBCONTRACT PERIOD, 9/1/2024 Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ 8/31/2025) AND FOR LEADING ONE PROJECT ON PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS AND RAPID RESPONSE TO OUTBREAKS/EPIDEMIC/PANDEMICS. A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR RNA MOLECULE BY NMR: UW-NMR WILL DETERMINE THE SOLUTION STRUCTURE OF PROTEINS OR RNA MOLECULES USING NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR)-BASED METHODS. THESE TARGETS WILL ORIGINATE FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASES AND ONCE APPROVED BY NIAID WILL ENTER INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE FOR TRACKING THE UW-NMR WORK. THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25 KDA THAT FAIL TO PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL PRIMARILY BE IDENTIFIED FROM COMMUNITY REQUESTS AND INTERNAL BATCHES; SPECIFICALLY, THESE WILL BE TARGETS OF INTEREST TO THE CENTER THAT COULD NOT BE DETERMINED USING CRYSTALLOGRAPHY. HOWEVER, DR. VARANI WILL ALSO IDENTIFY RELEVANT COLLABORATORS HIMSELF WHO ARE WILLING TO NOMINATE TARGETS TO THE NMR PIPELINE AND ARE WILLING TO COLLABORATE TO PUBLISH ANY RESULTS PRODUCED BY SSGCID, ESPECIALLY IN THE AREA OF BACTERIAL AND VIRAL NON CODING RNAS. UW-NMR MAY ALSO BE ASKED TO LEAD AND SUPPORT HIGH VALUE TARGET (HVT), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECT (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECT (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM, WHENEVER OPPORTUNITIES ARISE FOR ADVANCING SCIENTIFIC PROBLEMS THAT MIGHT BEST BE ADDRESSED BY NMR. CANDIDATES SUITABLE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION WILL BE IDENTIFIED FROM 1H-15N HSQC SPECTRA COLLECTED ON 15N-LABELED PROTEIN PREPARED BY UW-NMR. STANDARD TRIPLE RESONANCE EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PERFORMED TO ASSIGN THE BACKBONE AND THE SIDE CHAIN RESONANCES OF THE PROTEIN. ONCE THE RESONANCE ASSIGNMENTS ARE COMPLETE, NOE DATA CRUCIAL FOR OBTAINING DISTANCE RESTRAINTS WILL BE COLLECTED. NOE ASSIGNMENTS AND STRUCTURE CALCULATIONS WILL BE PERFORMED ITERATIVELY USING COMBINED AUTOMATED AND MANUAL METHODS. THE QUALITY OF THE FINAL SET OF STRUCTURES WILL BE ASSESSED AND ONCE THE FINAL ENSEMBLE OF STRUCTURES IS FOUND TO BE SATISFACTORY, THE COORDINATES OF THE ENSEMBLE AND THE MEAN STRUCTURE WILL BE DEPOSITED IN THE PROTEIN DATA BANK (PDB; HTTP://WWW.PDB.ORG) AND IMMEDIATELY RELEASED TO THE WORLD. AT THE SAME TIME, ALL 1H, 13C AND 15N CHEMICAL SHIFT DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED WITH THE BIOMAGNETIC RESEARCH BANK (BMRB; HTTP://WWW.BMRB.WISC.EDU/). MANUSCRIPTS THAT INCLUDE A DESCRIPTION OF THESE STRUCTURES WILL BE PUBLISHED IN AS TIMELY A FASHION AS IS POSSIBLE. B. LEAD ONE PANDEMIC PREPAREDNESS AND RAPID RESPONSE TO OUTBREAKS/EPIDEMIC/PANDEMICS PROJECT. THE UN-NMR GROUP WILL LEAD A PROJECT ON STRUCTURAL CHARACTERIZATION OF AN ESSENTIAL RNA PACKAGING ELEMENT FROM THE INFLUENZA A VIRUS. C. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: UW-NMR WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH QUALITY DATA ON WELL-DEFINED PROTEIN AND RNA SAMPLES. UW-NMR WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. DR. VARANI WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DR. VARANI WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION AND WILL CONDUCT THE PROJECT WORK WITH THE AIM OF PRODUCING IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS. UW-NMR IS EXPECTED TO SOLVE AT LEAST 1 NMR STRUCTURE FROM THESE STUDIES DURING THIS CONTRACT YEAR.

description: DARTMOUTH COLLEGE, UNDER THE DIRECTION OF OLUWATOYIN ASOJO, PH.D., WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING WORK TO SUPPORT THE BASIC PROJECT REQUIREMENT (9/1/2024-8/31/2025). A. STRUCTURE DETERMINATION OF PROTEINS OR PROTEIN COMPLEXES BY X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY: DARTMOUTH WILL TRAIN UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS IN THE USE OF STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY TO CHARACTERIZE THE FUNCTION OF SELECTED TARGETS. THE STUDENTS WILL WRITE MANUSCRIPTS DESCRIBING THE STRUCTURE AND (PREDICTED) FUNCTION OF SELECTED PROTEINS. IF POSSIBLE, ONE OR TWO STUDENTS WILL PARTICIPATE IN RESEARCH PROJECTS FOCUSED ON CHARACTERIZING THE FUNCTION OF TARGET(S) USING A VARIETY OF LABORATORY METHODS. DARTMOUTH WILL SUPPORT HIGH VALUE TARGETS (HVTS), COMMUNITY REQUEST PROJECTS (CRP), HIGHEST IMPACT PROJECTS (HIP) AND OTHER SPECIAL STUDIES WITHIN THE SSGCID PIPELINE, AS DECIDED BY THE SSGCID SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP TEAM (SLT). B. QUALITY CONTROL, DATA COLLECTION AND REPORTING: DARTMOUTH WILL ESTABLISH AND CONDUCT QUALITY CONTROL PROCEDURES AS NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE PRODUCTION OF HIGH-QUALITY DATA. DARTMOUTH WILL ENSURE THAT THE STATUS OF ALL WORK PERFORMED FOR SSGCID IS UPDATED IN A TIMELY FASHION, THROUGH THE CENTRAL TARGET TRACKING DATABASE (CTTDB), TRACKING SPREADSHEETS AND/OR ANY OTHER TRACKING SYSTEM REQUIRED BY THE PROJECT. KEY STAFF MEMBERS FROM DARTMOUTH WILL PARTICIPATE IN SSGCID PROJECT MEETINGS AND NIAID-REQUIRED MEETINGS TO ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THE PROJECT. DARTMOUTH STAFF WILL CONTRIBUTE TO QUARTERLY AND SEMI-ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS AND ANY OTHER NIAID REQUIRED REPORTS AS NEEDED AND IN A TIMELY FASHION AND WILL CONDUCT THE PROJECT WORK WITH THE AIM OF PRODUCING IMPACTFUL PUBLICATIONS.

description: THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) OUTLINES THE ACTIVITIES THAT COLORADO STATE UNIVERSITY (CSU) WILL BE PERFORMING THROUGHOUT THE PROPOSED WORK PERIOD. THE TASK NUMBERS BELOW REFLECT THE NUMBERING OF ACTIVITIES IN THE M72-SPECIFIC PACKAGE OF THE PRIME CONTRACT. THROUGH THE EXECUTION OF THIS CONTRACT, WE WILL EXAMINE PREVENTION OF DISEASE OUTCOMES AND ARCHIVE SAMPLES FOR ANALYZING BASIC INDUCTION OF INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY FROM VACCINATION, TO BE COMPLETED IF FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE. THIS WORK WILL INCLUDE STUDIES THAT ADDRESS BCG PRIME AND BOOSTS WITH M72 COMBINED WITH 3 DIFFERENT ADJUVANT SYSTEMS IN THE GUINEA PIG MODEL. PBMC WILL BE COLLECTED AND ARCHIVED FOR IMMUNOGENICITY AND POST-INFECTION ANALYSIS WITH MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (M.TB) ERDMAN, IF FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE, IN AN EFFORT TO DESIGN AND EVALUATE AN EFFICACIOUS VACCINE AGAINST MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (M.TB). THE WORK UNDER THIS CONTRACT MAY INCLUDE THE POSSIBLE DISTRIBUTION OF DE-IDENTIFIED HUMAN SUBJECT PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS (PBMC) AND OTHER CLINICAL SAMPLES TO SCRI AND THE PHOENIX PARTNERS. OPTION 2.M72 ACTIVITIES TASK 2.M72. EVALUATE IMMUNOGENICITY AND POD EFFICACY OF M72 COMBINED WITH DIFFERENT ADJUVANT FORMULATIONS AGAINST M.TB IN GUINEA PIGS SOME OF THE HARVESTED SAMPLES IN THIS M72 TASK OUTLINED BELOW WILL BE DISTRIBUTED TO COLLABORATOR SITES. CSU WILL PROVIDE THESE SAMPLES TO COLLABORATORS AS NEEDED AND PREDETERMINED BY THE NEEDS OF SOPS. THIS WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: SERUM OR BLOOD FOR ENDPOINT ANTIBODY ELISAS (SCRI), SYSTEMS SEROLOGY (HSPH) AND TRANSCRIPTOMIC (FHCC) ASSAYS ACROSS SPECIES. FURTHERMORE, DATA GENERATED IN THIS OPTION WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO CSU AND FHCC SYSTEMS BIOLOGISTS IN THE CORRECT FORMAT, AS DEFINED IN THE BASE PERIOD, FOR INTEGRATED ANALYSIS. ITERATIVE ANALYSIS WILL INVOLVE PRECLINICAL BIOLOGISTS AND SYSTEMS BIOLOGISTS FOR OPTIMAL DATA INTEGRITY AND IMPACT. GUINEA PIG STUDIES WILL BE PERFORMED IN PARALLEL IMMUNOPATHOLOGIC STUDIES, USING THE LABORATORY ISOLATE, M.TB ERDMAN. GUINEA PIGS WILL BE BCG OR MOCK VACCINATED AND AFTER 120 DAYS, GUINEA PIGS WILL BE MOCK BOOSTED, OR BOOSTED WITH TWO INTERVALS OF THE M72 CANDIDATE VACCINE + 3 CANDIDATE ADJUVANTS, INCLUDING GLA-SE, GLA-LSQ, OR UM-1098. GUINEA PIGS WILL BE INFECTED WITH 20-50 BACILLI OF M.TB ERDMAN AND SAMPLES WILL BE HARVESTED AT VARIOUS INTERVALS. WE WILL DETERMINE THE COURSE OF THE INFECTIONS BY MEASURING CFU LEVELS IN THE LUNGS AND BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE CELLS, AND DETERMINE PROTECTIVE EFFICACY OF VACCINE STRATEGIES USING QUANTITATIVE HISTOPATHOLOGY. SAMPLES WILL BE COLLECTED AND ARCHIVED FOR DOWNSTREAM USE, BUT NOT FULLY ANALYZED, INCLUDING: PBMC TO MEASURE VACCINE IMMUNOGENICITY STUDIES PRE-INFECTION AND PERIPHERAL RESPONSE POST-INFECTION, SERUM FOR SYSTEMS SEROLOGY AND CYTOKINE ELISA, LUNG AND SPLEEN CELL SUSPENSIONS FOR ANTIGEN STIMULATION AND CYTOKINE ANALYSIS, LUNG TISSUE FOR CYTOKINE ELISA, AND BAL FLUID FOR CYTOKINE ELISA. PARAFORMALDEHYDE-FIXED LUNG TISSUE WILL BE ARCHIVED IN PARAFFIN BLOCKS. IN SITU ANALYSIS OF BACTERIAL RESPONSE WILL BE ANALYZED BY RNASCOPE ISH ON FORMALIN-FIXED PARAFFIN-EMBEDDED LUNG TISSUE AND ON CELLS ISOLATED BY BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE TO DETECT BACTERIA-SPECIFIC TRANSCRIPTS, WHICH HAS THE POTENTIAL TO REVEAL THEIR PRECISE LOCATION AND REPLICATIVE STATE IN LESIONS. LUNG AND SPLEEN TISSUE WILL BE COLLECTED FOR HISTOPATHOLOGICAL EXAMINATION AT POST-MORTEM. THE SAMPLES FOR HISTOLOGY WILL BE COLLECTED INTO 4% PARAFORMALDEHYDE IN LABELLED POTS PROVIDED BY THE STUDY DIRECTOR FROM THE HISTOLOGY DEPARTMENT. THE TISSUES COLLECTED AT NECROPSY WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO THE HISTOLOGY DEPARTMENT WHERE THEY WILL BE PROCESSED TO PARAFFIN FOR ROUTINE SECTIONING AND THEN HEMATOXYLIN AND EOSIN (H&E) STAINING WILL BE PERFORMED. THE INITIAL UNBIASED RNA SEQUENCING APPROACH WILL USE WHOLE-BLOOD SAMPLES FROM PRE- AND POST-CHALLENGE TIME POINTS. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL LOOK FOR TRANSCRIPTS THAT ARE CORRELATED WITH M.TB COLONY FORMING UNITS (CFU) AND M.TB QPCR ASSAYS FROM BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE (BAL), THE PRIMARY CHALLENGE OUTCOMES. IN ADDITION TO ABSOLUTE ABUNDANCE AT POST-CHALLENGE TIME POINTS, WE WILL ALSO LOOK FOR CHANGES IN TRANSCRIPT ABUNDANCE RELATIVE TO THE DAY OF CHALLENGE AS A POTENTIAL CORRELATE OF CHALLENGE OUTCOME. AS WE BUILD A MODEL TO PREDICT CHALLENGE OUTCOME FROM THESE GENE EXPRESSION MEASURES WE WILL SPECIFICALLY CONSIDER TRANSCRIPTS THAT HAVE PREVIOUSLY BEEN IDENTIFIED AS PREDICTORS OF PROGRESSION TO TB DISEASE, SUCH AS TYPE I IFN-RELATED GENES WHOSE EXPRESSION INCREASES DURING DISEASE PROGRESSION. THE HUMAN EXPRESSION SIGNATURES WILL BE EVALUATED IN NHPS AND VICE VERSA; ADDITIONALLY, A JOINT MODEL WILL BE DEVELOPED, ALLOWING FOR DIFFERENCES IN NHP AND HUMAN ASSOCIATIONS, WHILE IDENTIFYING A COMMON GENE SIGNATURE. ONCE TRANSCRIPTS OR GENES HAVE BEEN IDENTIFIED, A TARGETED CROSS-SPECIES NANOSTRING PANEL WILL BE DEVELOPED FOR EVALUATION IN THE SMALL ANIMAL MODELS AS WELL AS IN FUTURE NHP AND CLINICAL TRIALS. WE PLAN TO DEVELOP A NANOSTRING NCOUNTER GENE PANEL WHICH CAN ACCOMMODATE UP TO 800 GENES AND WOULD BE SIGNIFICANTLY MORE COST EFFECTIVE THAN RNA SEQUENCING. ALTERNATIVELY, DEPENDING ON THE COMPLEXITY OF THE GENE PANEL, IT COULD BE DEVELOPED AS A 96 TRANSCRIPT/GENE (INCLUDING HOUSEKEEPING GENES) QPCR BIOMARK FLUIDIGM ASSAY. TASK 3.7 COMPARE IMMUNE PROFILES IN NHP, SMALL ANIMAL MODELS AND HUMANS TO IDENTIFY CORRELATES OF PROTECTION. SUBTASK 3.7.4 INTEGRATED ANALYSIS AND DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS MODELING OF EXPERIMENTAL IMMUNOLOGY DATA ACROSS ALL SPECIES EXPERIMENTAL DATA WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO THE STATISTICAL CENTER AND A FORMAL INTER-SITE AND INTER-SPECIES VARIABILITY ASSESSMENT WILL BE PERFORMED. VARIABILITY WILL BE DETERMINED USING COEFFICIENTS OF VARIATION (CV), MEAN AND STANDARD DEVIATION OF RESPONSES. DESIRED CUT-OFFS FOR ACCEPTABLE CVS WILL BE PRE-SPECIFIED FOR EACH ASSAY. EFFORT IN THE BASE PERIOD WILL HAVE BEEN MADE TO STANDARDIZE THE ASSAYS AND HARMONIZATION ASSESSMENTS WILL HAVE BEEN REPEATED IF CVS DID NOT MEET THE CUT OFF.
